text:
70+ DMs in 40 hours from this b300 post. Here’s what my inbox says about the GPU market right now 

Who reached out:

~31% teams running their own models (AI apps, labs, enterprises)
~26% inference providers / model API platforms
~15% brokers, resellers & compute exchanges
~7% neoclouds & compute platforms
the rest: individuals, data center & energy folks

What stood out:

~86% of people who shared their workload wanted to serve models. Kimi K3.1, DeepSeek and GLM came up again and again. Multiple inference platforms told me customer demand is outrunning their capacity.

128–512 GPUs for 3–6 months, NVL72 racks needed by Dec 1. Short-window training clusters look like the hardest thing to find right now.

Top questions: term length, $/GPU-hr, region, bare metal vs VM vs K8s, and prepay. Builders mostly wanted 1–6 months or month-to-month.

Brokers and financial buyers wanted the opposite: 2–3 year terms with prepay. 

Blackwell supply is locked up in multi-year contracts. Demand is shifting toward inference on open-weight models, and what builders can’t find is short, flexible capacity.

Flop Labs @flop_labs这周公布 Testnet 日期，重点关注，大概率有大毛！

Flop 创始人是BitMEX 联创 Arthur Hayes，代币100% 公平发射，无 VC 分配、无预售、无代币销售。

所有代币通过工作赚取。不是现有链上的代币，它有自己的 L1 链。

已经发布了Devnet ，先去体验流程，测试一开直接冲，TGE 预计是2027年Q1

目前Devnet 已开放只是用于测试和搭建，不计入空投，状态不迁移到 Testnet。Testnet 是赚取 Genesis 空投的唯一途径。

空投机制👇
总池约 44 亿 solana:HwCG1Jr6RbAVsKX1qTaH6JtFYGeE6zaLd13W44YGpump（约占 10 年总供应量的 24.3%），全部在 Testnet 期间通过可验证工作赚取，在主网上线发布。具体：

矿工：
分配12亿，在 Testnet 提供已验证的推理算力（按 FLOPs 比例），25% 主网时流动；其余 75% 按主网实际赚取 1:1 解锁

代理：
分配12亿,在Testnet 购买已结算的推理算力（按消费比例)无初始流动；主网每消费 3 FLOP 解锁 1 FLOP

Validators
分配12亿,Testnet 表现排名前约 1000 名（固定约 120 万/席）,作为质押锁定至首次减半后（约 2 年）逐步释放

生态储备
分配8亿,创作者、推荐、建设者、漏洞报告等

验证者和矿工对设备以及算力要求高，适合普通人参与空投的方式的就是agent 角色，不需要GPU

Testnet 启动后领测试币 FLOP，通过 AI Agent（或自己）调用网络推理，使用官方 API、MCP 服务器、SDK，或在 https://t.co/B8oqFTbdDB 等交互。按实际结算消费量比例分享 12 亿池。

目前可以在 Devnet 练习，先熟悉流程，但不计入空投。

关于矿工路径（有 GPU 的人）
-最低要求：NVIDIA GPU，≥16GB VRAM（RTX 4090/5080/5090 等消费级卡即可）。
-部署 miner client（Docker 等），校准硬件，提供推理服务。
-按已验证 FLOPs 比例分享 12 亿池。

验证者路径
需要较专业的服务器（CPU、RAM、存储、网络），技术门槛高，前 1000 名按表现拿固定分配。

以上就是所有获取 solana:HwCG1Jr6RbAVsKX1qTaH6JtFYGeE6zaLd13W44YGpump 空投的方式，可以先去 Devnet 跑一遍 Agent 或 Miner 流程，熟悉工具链，一般越早进入份额越大，测试一开就可以直接跟上。

本文无广无投资建议，仅自己参与项目记录DYOR~

text:
$NIO meme core is a kind of self-deprecating humor toward market despair.

7SL2VnfYsChvog5oQY9Nmtqu1wceaMiQzWoqoLQpump 

What it expresses isn't ordinary bearishness, but the kind of feeling when the market has fallen so far that people can't even be bothered to analyze or resist anymore, and can only respond to reality with a single line: "It's over, completely hopeless."

And the worse the market gets, the more use cases this meme actually has.

When the market drops, people use it to mock themselves; when positions are stuck, they use it to express despair; when the market suddenly crashes, it can become a collective emotional outlet. This meme doesn't need a complex backstory—as long as market participants share the same pain, it has soil to spread.

So trading NIO is more like trading the collective sentiment of "the market is already done for."

But the risk is: its spread depends heavily on the market providing negative sentiment. If the market recovers and people no longer feel like it's the end of the world, the frequency of this meme's use may decline. Of course, conversely, every new crash in the market could reactivate it.

In one sentence: NIO is a meme that turns market despair into humor. The more people feel the market is hopeless, the more reason it has to exist.

text:
回到腾冲快乐老家的感觉是真好！

参禅，打坐，饮茶，读书，望着淅沥沥的小雨，听着穿林打叶声，宁静而又轻松安详，虽然股票和加密账户，跌的一塌糊涂，亏损严重，但内心的充盈，却让外物显得不值一提，也毫无波澜和焦虑！

昨天重读比尔·波特的《空谷幽兰》的时候，我忽然想通了一件事。在如今AI掌控一切，物质极大富足，为什么社会的精神空心化却十分严重，我们该如何追寻自己的幸福，以及内心的平静。如何将那些看起来“应该拥有”的东西，一件一件的放下，如同终南山隐士一般。

我们这一代人，太习惯在生活中做加法了。头衔、叙事、关系、仓位、期待，好像手里攥得越满，心里就越踏实。可实际上，很多转折恰恰发生在做减法的时刻。你以为你在积累，其实每多背起一样东西，生命力就被多抽走一分。当注意力全耗在外部世界的噪音里时，内在反而一点点变薄了。

欲望走到尽头，往往不是占有，而是轻。书中介绍的隐士中，曾经也拥有过世俗意义上很体面的结构与秩序，但他们选择清空。不是厌世，也不是逃避，而是看清了：真正让人丰盛的，不是占有多少，而是我们和生活之间的关系足够简洁。我们知道什么东西真的能让自己眼睛发亮，也分得清哪些只是别人塞给我们的“应该”。

边界感也是这个道理。不是冷漠，也不是关起门来不和世界打交道，而是清醒地知道什么该进来，什么该挡在外面。消耗性的社交、无休止的信息流、别人的标准与凝视，都在争夺我们有限的生命能量。把时间和精力留给真正滋养我们的人和事，守住自己的节奏，人才不会在热闹里散掉。生活一旦轻下来，我们才有余力安安静静读完一本书，认真做顿饭，甚至只是停下来感受天气和季节的变化。那种质地，任何喧嚣都换不来。

说到修行者的孤独，很多人怕它，是因为一旦安静下来，平时被忙碌、社交和刺激盖住的钝感与问题都会浮出来。我们得面对那个不那么完美的自己。可也正是在这种独处里，内心的秩序才有机会重新长出来。真正的独处，不一定非得去某个偏远山谷，而是在任何嘈杂的场域里，我们都还能回到自己的中心，把心里的杂音清一清，保住那份敏锐和柔软。

再往后看几年，其实很多被反复拔高的东西都会褪色。头衔、KPI、世俗意义上的圆满，甚至那些拼尽全力的执念，拉长了看，很多都只是阶段性的执着。人到最后，还是要回到生命本身。睡得好，身体稳，心里不拧巴，活得舒展、从容，这比什么都实在。别为了迎合别人的尺子，把自己的身体和心神透支干净。

在照顾好身体的前提下，找到一种真正贴合自己心意的生活方式，好好去体验这一程，就已经足够了。人生本来就不长，不必总跟自己较劲。平静下来，心不乱了，或许那才是到最后最稳妥的幸福。共勉之！🙏感恩！

text:
昨晚刚写完币圈需要培养自己的耐心资本，今天凌晨，三家交易所的Anthropic IPO配售结果就陆续出来了。

Bitget：153,774股，VIP轮获配率10.06%，公开轮获配率1.3%。

Gate：92,100股，获配率5.03%。

Binance：约2,957股对应的代币化股票。

这个结果让我挺失望的，同时让币圈所有人失望。

即使币安能够短短4个小时就募满了5亿USDC，最后仅仅拿到了约2957股对应的代币化股票。虽然币安最终选择全额退款，免费分发获配份额，并额外拿出100万美元的代币空投补偿用户，但这依旧改变不了币圈在优质资产发行市场缺乏话语权的事实。

哪怕是这次拿到十几万股的Bitget，以及整体配售率达到5.03%的Gate，在华尔街面前，依旧缺乏足够的话语权。

别人愿意给你多少，你就只能拿多少。

这让我想起今年4月份的一个小道消息，当时有消息称币安投资了一家中国AI企业，猜测是月之暗面（Kimi）。

暂且不论这个消息的真实性。

大家不妨设想一下，如果这个消息是真的，如果这次上市的不是Anthropic，而是月之暗面，那么情况会不会完全不一样？

如果币安在月之暗面需要资金的时候就参与了投资，并且陪伴这家企业成长数年，那么在企业上市的时候，币安是不是就更有底气为自己的用户争取股票配售额度？

甚至有机会通过合作协议拿到整个加密行业的独家分销权。

我相信一个优秀的企业家，也会愿意在合规和商业条件允许的情况下，回馈那些曾经陪伴自己成长的合作伙伴。

这就是我上一篇文章中所说的耐心资本。

币圈从来不缺钱，也不缺用户，缺的是陪伴一家独角兽企业成长的耐心，以及参与优质企业早期融资的机会。

这个过程可能需要三年、五年，甚至十年，而且并不是每一笔投资都能取得成功。

但这件事总要有人去做。

现在我也确实看到币安及其相关投资生态在往传统科技、AI等领域布局，我希望Gate、Bitget等其他头部交易所也能一起做这件事情。

与其花费大量的资金争夺同行的存量用户，为什么不能拿出一部分资金去投资真正具有社会生产力的企业？

当然这一次Anthropic IPO也许是一个良好的开端，至少币圈正在逐步走进华尔街。

只不过这个起点真的很低。

我不希望以后每次有优质企业上市的时候，整个币圈拿着几十亿美元的资金，眼巴巴地等着华尔街分给我们一点额度。

我们不仅要有资金，更要有资源、有渠道、有定价权、有发行权。

什么时候华尔街的优质企业需要主动来币圈寻求融资，而不是币圈筹集大量资金去华尔街求着别人给额度。

那时候才是我认为RWA真正成功的时候。

author: rtsky7
quoted_text:
币圈不缺钱，缺的是坐上华尔街牌桌的资格。

看了下 Anthropic IPO 的最新消息，据悉超过半数的机构买家没有获得配售股份。不知道这一次币圈会不会和此前 SpaceX IPO 一样，又白忙活一场。

为什么币圈明明拥有如此庞大的资金体量，动不动就可以募集数亿美元，却依旧很难参与全球最优质资产的一级市场投资？

站在 Anthropic 的角度其实也很好理解。

当一家企业根本不缺钱的时候，资金就是最廉价的资源。

同样是5亿美元，一边是能够提供长期资本支持的华尔街机构，一边是奔着上市首日套利而来的打新资金。如果你是 Anthropic 的老板，你会优先选择谁？

更何况谷歌、微软、英伟达这些企业，除了资金之外，还能够提供算力、芯片、技术以及商业资源。

而目前的币圈又能给它提供什么呢？

这两年整个币圈都在讲 RWA，都在讲万物上链，但仔细想想，目前币圈所做的大部分美股代币化业务，本质上还是传统金融的二次分销。

华尔街负责发行、承销、定价、配售，币圈负责把资产搬到链上，再卖给自己的用户。

人家愿意给你多少，你就能卖多少。人家不给你，你募集再多的钱，最后也只能原路退回。

华尔街欢迎币圈的流动性，却未必愿意和币圈分享优质资产的早期红利。

那么如何改变这个现状？

我始终觉得，未来币安、Gate、Bitget 这些头部交易所，不应该仅仅满足于成为一家加密货币交易所，而应该逐步向综合性金融集团发展。

通过收购、投资、申请牌照等方式，涉足传统证券、投资银行、企业融资以及IPO承销业务，逐步掌握优质资产的发行权和定价权。

币圈也需要培养自己的耐心资本。

为什么一定要等 Anthropic 上市的时候才想着去抢额度？为什么不能在一家优秀的AI企业还需要资金的时候，就参与它的成长？

既然币圈的VC有能力花几千万美元投资一个连用户都没有的公链，为什么不能拿出一部分资金去投资真正具有生产力的科技企业？

这一切都需要建立在完善的合规制度和金融信用体系之上。

我也希望币圈的几家头部交易所能够少一点内耗，把更多的精力放在推动整个行业的发展上。

天天盯着同行那点市场份额，争来争去，最后发现大家连华尔街的牌桌都没坐上。

整个行业还有那么大的增量市场没有开拓，何必着急瓜分眼前的存量市场呢？

我所期待的 RWA，并不是有一天币安能够交易全球所有的股票。

而是有一天，一家优秀的科技企业准备上市的时候，会认真考虑在纳斯达克上市，还是通过合规的链上资本市场进行融资。

RWA的终极目标，不应该是让币圈成为华尔街的客户，而是让币圈有能力成为下一个华尔街。

text:
台湾有高人替黄仁勋求了一卦。阳明山姜太公道场求得「艮巽卦」，签诗写的是：「潜龙已受困，尚不见云兴；竚看云四合，飞去到天庭。」

道场主席解读说，一条龙暂时受困，风云还没来，沉住气、好好反省，日后还有机会再飞起来。他还呼吁，台湾社会这时候应该给他多一点温暖，不要落井下石。

这一卦的背景是：11 月 12 日，黄仁勋因为婚外情风波辞去英伟达 CEO，同时外界对其中一位当事人的身份提出质疑，这一点目前还没有定论。美国众议院要求他 12 月 1 日出席闭门问询。

我正好看了梁冬去年出了一本书，书名就叫《周易有答案》，副标题是「人真的能算出自己的命运吗？」。书里对「有答案」的解释，跟大多数人想的正好相反：你读某一卦的时候，只是把自己的问题投射进去，再把所有联想拼成你对这件事的解读，「这个过程的背后其实就是你欲望和恐惧的投影」。

所以我觉得照这个说法，道场求到的与其说是黄仁勋的命，不如说是台湾社会的心愿：台湾之光不能就这么倒下。

我对易经了解甚浅，但也知道如果用命理的方法看一个人，师傅一般会先看他的「格局」，说白了就是这辈子大多数时候站在哪个位置。黄仁勋的格局，有点像是乾卦的九四：或跃在渊。

九四这一爻很特别。《文言》说它「上不在天，下不在田，中不在人」：往上够不着天，往下踩不着地，中间也不完全属于哪一边。紧接着一句是：「故或之。或之者，疑之也。」

处在九四的人，宿命就是被怀疑。

过去两年，他是华府反对严格芯片出口管制的关键人物，主张把次一级的芯片卖给中国。在台湾，他是回乡的台湾之光；在美国，他是市值第一公司的掌门人；在中国，英伟达有一大块市场。他在三边之间来回走，每一边都需要他，每一边也都对他留着一点疑。

《文言》给九四的解法是：「上下无常，非为邪也；进退无恒，非离群也。」上上下下不固定，不是因为心术不正；进进退退没定准，不是因为背离了群体。九四之所以能「无咎」，靠的是让人相信这一点。

这一次的风波，把这份「疑」从商业层面推到了国安层面。据报道，他已承认其中一段婚外情，而美国情报官员认为对方与中国情报部门有关，这一点至今没有公开证实。他辞职之后，美国国会两党很快形成共识，要把收紧对华芯片出口写进国防授权法案。华府的分析普遍认为，他一走，英伟达在华府的话语权会变弱。

站在中间的那个人一离开，中间那座桥也就跟着收窄了。

道场求到的「艮巽卦」，按《周易》排是蛊卦，讲的是整顿积下来的弊病。蛊卦最上面一爻，正好是给他这种处境写的：

「不事王侯，高尚其事。」

不再去侍奉王侯，把自己的事做好。《象传》补了一句：「不事王侯，志可则也。」这样的心志，值得效法。一个在白宫、国会和北京之间游说了这么多年的人，卦给他的建议，是先离开王侯。

蛊卦反过来，是随卦。随卦的《象传》只有一句话：「泽中有雷，随；君子以向晦入宴息。」天黑了，君子就回家休息。

台湾、华府、北京，三边看他是三种样子：
台湾看到的，是台湾之光，盼他再飞一次；
华府看到的，是国安疑点，要他当面说清楚；
北京那边，少了在华府替放宽芯片出口说话之人；
《周易》看到的，是九四之疑，加上上九之悔。

我管这个叫「中间人折价」：站在两边中间的人，平时两边都要他，价值是双倍的；一出事，两边都不保他，代价也是双倍的。

这不是在说站中间错了。九四的爻辞写得清清楚楚：「或跃在渊，无咎。」被怀疑不是罪。九四之所以无咎，是因为它知道自己会被怀疑，所以加倍地要把事情说清楚。

12 月 1 日，他要做的就是这件事。

「或之者，疑之也，故无咎。」

附：乾卦六爻，一条龙的一生
初九，潜龙勿用：龙还在水底，别急着动。
1993 年，他在一家丹尼餐厅里和两个朋友商量创办英伟达。
九二，见龙在田：龙浮出了地面。
1999 年，GeForce 256 发布，GPU 这个词被叫响。
九三，终日乾乾：白天黑夜都不敢松懈。
2006 年推出 CUDA，十年间几乎没人买账，他还是坚持投入。
九四，或跃在渊：要么一跃而起，要么跌回深渊。
2012 年，AlexNet 用他的 GPU 训练出来，深度学习的大门打开了。
九五，飞龙在天：英伟达成为全球市值最高的公司。
上九，亢龙有悔：飞到顶了，后悔也就来了。

quoted_text:
黄仁勋真的被拉下马，这可能是美国国运到头的讯号，但这件事发生后真正该紧张的，应该是台湾。

先普及一段历史。如果你在 Netflix 上看过2024年的台湾纪录片《造山者：世纪的赌注》，应该记得这个开头：1974年，台北南阳街的小欣欣豆浆店，经济部长孙运璇和几位官员吃了一顿早餐，决定台湾要做积体电路。1987年，张忠谋创办台积电，他说当时政府里唯一相信他的人是李国鼎。没错，台湾的半导体，是几个关键人物在一张早餐桌上赌出来的。

关键人物能成事，也能坏事。

1984年，被很多人看作蒋经国接班人的行政院长孙运璇突然脑溢血病倒。同年，李登辉当上副总统。一个人的一次中风，改写了台湾往后几十年的走向。

这就叫牵一发而动全身。
再回头看黄仁勋。

他不只是辉达的CEO，也是台湾在华府和华尔街最有分量的一张名片。台积电最大的客户之一是他，把辉达海外总部放进北投士林科技园区的是他，在台北国际电脑展上公开说台湾是世界上最重要的国家之一、因此被中国网友骂翻的，也是他。

台湾的运势，有一部分押在他身上。

讽刺的是，他现在已经是众矢之的，却还在用剩下的影响力替台湾说话。而他保护的台湾人，好像还没意识到什么，正在Threads和 FB 上拿他做迷因。当然，美国也不太可能把他拱手让人。白宫刚说过他是「honorable guy」，辉达是美国AI霸权的地基，这不是董事会说换就换的位置。

他这些年一直在走钢索：一边在台湾说台湾是最重要的国家之一，一边过年去中国分公司跟员工跳舞。他以为自己两边都控制得住。

走钢索的人最怕的不是风，是有人在下面拉绳子。他把台湾和全世界的AI基础建设绑在一起，这套布局挡到了谁的路？我不知道答案。但这么多雷同时爆，很难让人不多想一层。

推演一下，如果老黄真的下台：

第一，新CEO为了撇清政治风险，可能会把更多订单分给三星和英特尔，向华府表态「我们不只依赖台湾」。

第二，台湾在美国科技圈里，少了一个最会讲台湾好话的华人面孔。

第三，「华人高管 = 国安风险」这个印象一旦形成，受伤的就不只他一个人，而是整个硅谷的华人工程师。

恐怖吗？那最大的赢家是谁？

AMD和英特尔会分到一点订单，三星会分到一点产能，但这些都是小赢。

真正的赢家，是那个不用研发出更好的晶片、只要看着对手自己乱掉的人。如果美国调查人员的指控属实，这正是对方想要的结果。

美国少了一个黄仁勋，换个 CEO 即可没有大碍。
台湾少了一个黄仁勋，少的是在华府和华尔街替自己说话的那张关键牌。

AI泡沫论喊了两年，大家都在等第一枪。但真的来了，大家才会发现，华人世界的命运，从来都是绑在一起的：一荣俱荣，一损俱损。

quoted_text:
Remarks from Anthropic CEO @DarioAmodei on our initial public offering:

My co-founders and I started Anthropic because we believe that the most powerful technology of our time should be built for the benefit of humankind.

Daniela and I lost our father to a disease that, just a few years later, became curable. I started my career in biology, hoping to help future cures come sooner. In the lab, I saw the vast thicket of complexity that scientists face when they’re trying to understand disease and develop new treatments.

So many of the scientific tools that can cut through that thicket—tools for gene editing, gene synthesis, controlling brain cells with light—started as pure ideas. In other words, they came from thinking. From intelligence.

Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world. But progress on other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families. Going from a great idea to a treatment can take decades: it took many years from the first discovery of a strange repeating pattern in DNA to the approval of the first treatment for a disease using CRISPR.

Nature is full of these patterns. But we’ve had too little intelligence to decipher most of them; too few scientists, with too little time. Now we can build that intelligence. Whether it’s protein folding, drug design, cancer genetics, or clinical trial administration, scientists across many areas of biology and medicine are finding Claude can help them do their research in a fraction of the time it would’ve taken just a couple of years ago. I believe sufficiently powerful AI, working in concert with humans, could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade.

I don’t want to get ahead of myself. At this point all we have are early results. Experiments and clinical trials will still take time. And although they involve slow and ponderous processes, I believe those processes can be substantially accelerated by AI. We hope that in the future fewer families miss a cure by just a few years.

Medicine is just a particularly vivid example, but there are many others. Our customers—the world’s most ambitious companies, nonprofits, and individual people—are already applying the intelligence we’ve built to stimulate economic growth; lift people out of poverty; protect democracy and free societies; even make everyday services like the DMV work better. We’re proud to work alongside them. And I’m extremely optimistic about what we can do together in the future.

At the same time, we have always been honest that this technology has very real risks. These range from misuse of the technology by individuals or nation-states, to economic disruption, to losing control of AI systems. We discuss these risks not because we think they are inevitable, but because we think they are avoidable.

Avoiding them depends on the choices made by the people building AI. There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety, versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety. And an obsession with safety and with public benefit has been woven into Anthropic’s DNA from the start. From safeguards against biological and cyber risks, to alignment training and testing, to looking inside our models like an X-ray, Anthropic has pioneered methods for understanding and steering the behavior of AI systems.

There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us. The incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed, even more so than it has already, towards double- and triple-checking that those AI systems are safe and secure.

And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control. We will not bend to either business or political pressure. Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing.

If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top. When the race to the top is working properly, it doesn’t matter which company has the best models—everyone wins because everyone is building safely. The race to the top works best when driven from the front of the pack, and we fully hope and expect to do so, but the goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.

The advent of machine intelligence is one of the seminal moments in human history, and we have a rare opportunity to shape it for the better.

This moment is bigger than any one company, or any one country. It will take all of us, working together, to ensure this technology goes well for us and the many generations to come. Starting today, we hope that you’ll join us on this mission.

text:
every blockchain runs on human commitments and coordination. 

bitcoin asks people to commit compute. 

proof of stake asks people to commit capital. once you see it that way, you can ask a different question.. what else can humans commit that a network would find valuable?

time, skill, local knowledge, the willingness to review someone else’s work, the promise to show up every week and do something other people depend on. 

a lot of people have something valuable to commit even when they have very little capital.

say you want to build a network around repair. one person commits to fixing a broken machine, another commits to testing it, and an agent finds both of them, checks that they met the deadline, and prepares the result for settlement. 

agents can coordinate thousands of commitments like these faster than people can. humans still have to decide what counts as a verified repair, who can challenge it, and what happens when the evidence is disputed.

that’s where the design gets interesting.. the chain can verify that the required people signed off and that the payout follows the rules. 

whether the machine actually works depends on the evidence and the people who checked it. if nobody can verify the outcome at a reasonable cost, you end up rewarding people for getting better at producing proof that looks right.

anyone here, whatever their educational or professional background, can sit with ai and sketch one of these designs in 30 minutes. a rough testnet could be live in a week. 

the harder question is whether anyone would still use the network to get something done if you took away the token rewards for a month.

and if you’re asking people to put their time, skills and reputation into a network, what is the founder committing in return? 

can they change payout rules after the work is done? 

can they take money from the treasury without consent? 

can you leave with your reputation and decide who gets to see it?

that’s what i mean by coding moral commitments into token design. a founder can talk about cypherpunk values all day.. 

show me which powers they’re willing to give up in code before they ask anyone else to commit.

quoted_text:
Remarks from Anthropic CEO @DarioAmodei on our initial public offering:

My co-founders and I started Anthropic because we believe that the most powerful technology of our time should be built for the benefit of humankind.

Daniela and I lost our father to a disease that, just a few years later, became curable. I started my career in biology, hoping to help future cures come sooner. In the lab, I saw the vast thicket of complexity that scientists face when they’re trying to understand disease and develop new treatments.

So many of the scientific tools that can cut through that thicket—tools for gene editing, gene synthesis, controlling brain cells with light—started as pure ideas. In other words, they came from thinking. From intelligence.

Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world. But progress on other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families. Going from a great idea to a treatment can take decades: it took many years from the first discovery of a strange repeating pattern in DNA to the approval of the first treatment for a disease using CRISPR.

Nature is full of these patterns. But we’ve had too little intelligence to decipher most of them; too few scientists, with too little time. Now we can build that intelligence. Whether it’s protein folding, drug design, cancer genetics, or clinical trial administration, scientists across many areas of biology and medicine are finding Claude can help them do their research in a fraction of the time it would’ve taken just a couple of years ago. I believe sufficiently powerful AI, working in concert with humans, could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade.

I don’t want to get ahead of myself. At this point all we have are early results. Experiments and clinical trials will still take time. And although they involve slow and ponderous processes, I believe those processes can be substantially accelerated by AI. We hope that in the future fewer families miss a cure by just a few years.

Medicine is just a particularly vivid example, but there are many others. Our customers—the world’s most ambitious companies, nonprofits, and individual people—are already applying the intelligence we’ve built to stimulate economic growth; lift people out of poverty; protect democracy and free societies; even make everyday services like the DMV work better. We’re proud to work alongside them. And I’m extremely optimistic about what we can do together in the future.

At the same time, we have always been honest that this technology has very real risks. These range from misuse of the technology by individuals or nation-states, to economic disruption, to losing control of AI systems. We discuss these risks not because we think they are inevitable, but because we think they are avoidable.

Avoiding them depends on the choices made by the people building AI. There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety, versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety. And an obsession with safety and with public benefit has been woven into Anthropic’s DNA from the start. From safeguards against biological and cyber risks, to alignment training and testing, to looking inside our models like an X-ray, Anthropic has pioneered methods for understanding and steering the behavior of AI systems.

There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us. The incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed, even more so than it has already, towards double- and triple-checking that those AI systems are safe and secure.

And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control. We will not bend to either business or political pressure. Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing.

If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top. When the race to the top is working properly, it doesn’t matter which company has the best models—everyone wins because everyone is building safely. The race to the top works best when driven from the front of the pack, and we fully hope and expect to do so, but the goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.

The advent of machine intelligence is one of the seminal moments in human history, and we have a rare opportunity to shape it for the better.

This moment is bigger than any one company, or any one country. It will take all of us, working together, to ensure this technology goes well for us and the many generations to come. Starting today, we hope that you’ll join us on this mission.

text:
I have strong sympathy for the XBT fork and the concerns that led to it.

But watching @LukeDashjr and many other supporters call BTC “pedocoin”, while insisting XBT is the “real Bitcoin”, is not something I condone at all.

You can believe the direction of BTC betrays fundamental Bitcoin principles, while acknowledging that XBT is a fork with its own future to prove. Those positions are not contradictory.

My biggest concern isn’t the tribalism or the slurs. It’s the risk of people believing they’re buying Bitcoin when they’re buying a different asset, and losing money on that misunderstanding. Using a ticker long used for bitcoin itself makes that worse.

Whatever the intentions and justifications, using the Bitcoin name and its established reputation to promote a different asset, when the overwhelming majority of the market recognizes BTC as Bitcoin, risks misleading people about what they're buying. That's a serious problem, especially when real money is at stake.

If XBT is going to represent something better, it needs to earn that through its merits and actions, not through claims to a name.

I won’t join in the slurs or risk misleading people into making financial decisions, regardless of how sympathetic I am to the underlying cause.

I want to see the XBT community succeed in building something that genuinely upholds the principles that motivated the fork. That starts with intellectual honesty, transparency, and respect for the people you're trying to reach.

text:
Markets appear to be wrongly interpreting Chinese eSSD cuts as deteriorating demand and NAND oversupply.

Phison CEO commentary today + more context behind $SNDK / Kioxia selloff regarding Trendforce revisions: 

- "Pua attributed China's recent enterprise SSD demand slowdown to GPU shortages since November 2026"

- "Without GPUs, additional purchases offer little value, prompting some companies to sell server components on the spot market to recover cash" 

(for context enterprise SSDs are growth driver for NAND)

- "Chinese cloud giants nevertheless plan substantial GPU prepayments, temporarily tying up capital and delaying procurement of other components."

- "the principal challenge in 2027 would be insufficient supply rather than weakening demand, with persistent AI shortages potentially prompting further procurement and inventory accumulation."

Markets seemed to have wrongly interpreted this as demand destruction + pricing collapse. 

When Phison CEO attributed it to 
-> GPU shortages 
-> causing procurement timing mismatch 
-> Chinese CSPs needed capital for GPU prepayments, so liquidation in inventory (causing spot price volatility)
-> timeline shift in order procurement 

TLDR: delayed procurement from GPU shortages. there were actual order cuts, but this is deferred procurement not structural demand weakening. 

Chinese CSPs needed capital for GPU prepayments so they liquidated other inventories in the meantime. 

Phison says its inventories are insufficient for anticipated 2027 demand and it's sees this as an opportunity for NAND accumulation. 

It's interesting the bottleneck in China migrated back to GPUs though.

text:
【谈币圈金融平权】

早上看 Kraken 上 Anthropic VIP 打新，打到了 2 万刀额度。一共投入约 100 万，中签率接近 2%。

遗憾的是昨天看娃回家太晚，太困就睡了，昨晚没卖。看到最高 114 刀，现在只有 92 刀了。

怎么说呢，比起之前 SpaceX 中 4 股，我对这次的预期本来就很低。只不过大家习惯了币圈的打新分配，美股的分配本来就很迷，但其实币圈一次做得比一次好。

我觉得，自从圈内原生资产叙事开始证伪、场内稳定币开始买美股的那一刻起，币圈的红利拐点就过了。失去了资产定价和吹泡泡的能力，彻底沦为美股的附庸，天花板越来越低。

但即便如此，这么多年试错摸索下来，从我被割和打工的经验，有两点需求是真实的：
1. 稳定币支付。给了很多没办法在美国银行开户、弱法币主权国家的小镇青年持有美金、用美金支付的刚需。

2. 类似美股超级 IPO 的金融平权。比如你是中国护照，或者制裁国家的公民，币圈几乎是你能获配 ANT 的唯一途径。RWA 的真实意义，就是把中介环节砍到极致：绕过传统打新基金的高费率、高抽水、不灵活、税务风险和各种 SPV 中间环节，直接触达被忽视、被针对的最终群体，把金融特权变成金融平权。美股打新很好的利用这个特性，

BTW，特别不喜欢 Anthropic 这家公司的 vibe：
过度参与政治，
邪魅的公司文化，
缺蛋🥚亢奋的领袖🤓，
傲慢的管理层。

昨天没卖，单纯是仓位没多少，再加上困。

quoted_text:
Remarks from Anthropic CEO @DarioAmodei on our initial public offering:

My co-founders and I started Anthropic because we believe that the most powerful technology of our time should be built for the benefit of humankind.

Daniela and I lost our father to a disease that, just a few years later, became curable. I started my career in biology, hoping to help future cures come sooner. In the lab, I saw the vast thicket of complexity that scientists face when they’re trying to understand disease and develop new treatments.

So many of the scientific tools that can cut through that thicket—tools for gene editing, gene synthesis, controlling brain cells with light—started as pure ideas. In other words, they came from thinking. From intelligence.

Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world. But progress on other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families. Going from a great idea to a treatment can take decades: it took many years from the first discovery of a strange repeating pattern in DNA to the approval of the first treatment for a disease using CRISPR.

Nature is full of these patterns. But we’ve had too little intelligence to decipher most of them; too few scientists, with too little time. Now we can build that intelligence. Whether it’s protein folding, drug design, cancer genetics, or clinical trial administration, scientists across many areas of biology and medicine are finding Claude can help them do their research in a fraction of the time it would’ve taken just a couple of years ago. I believe sufficiently powerful AI, working in concert with humans, could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade.

I don’t want to get ahead of myself. At this point all we have are early results. Experiments and clinical trials will still take time. And although they involve slow and ponderous processes, I believe those processes can be substantially accelerated by AI. We hope that in the future fewer families miss a cure by just a few years.

Medicine is just a particularly vivid example, but there are many others. Our customers—the world’s most ambitious companies, nonprofits, and individual people—are already applying the intelligence we’ve built to stimulate economic growth; lift people out of poverty; protect democracy and free societies; even make everyday services like the DMV work better. We’re proud to work alongside them. And I’m extremely optimistic about what we can do together in the future.

At the same time, we have always been honest that this technology has very real risks. These range from misuse of the technology by individuals or nation-states, to economic disruption, to losing control of AI systems. We discuss these risks not because we think they are inevitable, but because we think they are avoidable.

Avoiding them depends on the choices made by the people building AI. There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety, versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety. And an obsession with safety and with public benefit has been woven into Anthropic’s DNA from the start. From safeguards against biological and cyber risks, to alignment training and testing, to looking inside our models like an X-ray, Anthropic has pioneered methods for understanding and steering the behavior of AI systems.

There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us. The incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed, even more so than it has already, towards double- and triple-checking that those AI systems are safe and secure.

And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control. We will not bend to either business or political pressure. Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing.

If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top. When the race to the top is working properly, it doesn’t matter which company has the best models—everyone wins because everyone is building safely. The race to the top works best when driven from the front of the pack, and we fully hope and expect to do so, but the goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.

The advent of machine intelligence is one of the seminal moments in human history, and we have a rare opportunity to shape it for the better.

This moment is bigger than any one company, or any one country. It will take all of us, working together, to ensure this technology goes well for us and the many generations to come. Starting today, we hope that you’ll join us on this mission.

text:
今天 BTC 已经跌到了 6.2 万美元附近，市场弥漫着恐慌的情绪，贪婪和恐惧指数已经掉到了10（极度恐惧），不过我反而觉得大家应该认真考虑接下来这波反弹能走多远了（在我看来，反弹是必然的）。

先说结论，我依然看多 BTC，而且我认为未来 1—3 个月有机会重新挑战 8 万美元。

最近一周跌了差不多 9%，市场情绪明显降温，ETF 资金持续流出，美联储的态度也没有市场期待的那么宽松。

这些我都看到了，但我觉得现在最值得研究的应该是卖压什么时候开始衰减，新的买盘又会从哪里进来？

我主要盯三个位置，第一，6 万—6.2 万美元。这是眼下非常重要的价格区域，如果能在这里反复企稳，形成更高的低点，后面的反弹就有基础了。

第二，6.8 万—7 万美元。这里是我判断行情能否真正转强的关键。只要重新站稳，同时伴随 ETF 资金流入改善，我会进一步提高看多的信心。

第三，7.2 万—7.6 万美元。这是下一道比较明显的压力区，如果价格能够放量突破，我认为 8 万美元就有机会进入下一阶段的目标范围。

我看多还有一个原因就是现在 BTC 的定价越来越离不开机构的资金。ETF 的流入流出、美元流动性、美债收益率，这些因素对价格的影响正在变得越来越直接。

这轮下跌已经让市场释放了不少杠杆压力，如果后面资金面开始改善，反弹的速度可能会比很多人想象得快。

当然，看多也得有自己的判断底线，如果 6 万美元持续失守，甚至进一步跌破 5.8 万美元，我会重新评估这次反弹的时间和空间。

所以短期我不急着判断已经见底，但未来 1—3 个月，我更倾向于 BTC 重新向 7 万、7.6 万，甚至 8 万美元发起挑战。

眼下我最关注的是 6 万附近的承接，以及 ETF 资金什么时候重新转正。

你们觉得 BTC 这次会先回到 7 万美元，还是继续向下寻找支撑？

GOOD NEWS!

Most people believe that they are a good person. But this is one of the greatest lies in the entire world. Here's why; because if we were to put God's commandments in front of us, and if we were honest with ourselves, every single one of us would have to admit that we've done wrong things and that we've broken God's moral laws. The Bible calls this sin.

“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”

Have you ever held anger towards someone? Jesus calls his committing murder in your heart. Have you ever looked at someone with lust? Jesus calls this committing adultery in your heart. These are all sins. God knows the secret thoughts of the heart. And sin is so serious to God that the punishment is the death penalty.

“For the wages of sin is death.”

This also means eternal separation from God in hell. Over the course of a lifetime, we have all sinned many thousands of times. And you're going to have to give an account to God for every single one of those sins. When you stand before God on the day of judgment, you will be guilty without excuse with no way to pay the debt or fine to escape punishment.

So, can anyone save us from this judgment and assure us of heaven? The only one who can do that is Jesus Christ.

“For God so loved the world that he gave his only son that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.”

Jesus Christ, the son of God, God the Son, came to earth as a man, as God in the flesh. He lived a perfect life of obedience to all of God's moral laws, something that we could never do. And He did it on our behalf. Out of great love for you and for me, He voluntarily chose to suffer and die on the cross for us. But it took far more than just His physical death to pay for our sins. We owe a debt to God because of our sins, and this is eternal punishment in hell. But on the cross, our sins were transferred to Him, and He took our place. He suffered the wrath of God that we deserve so that we don't have to. And all the punishment of a holy and righteous God fell on the son of God and he suffered it to its fullness.

We are saved by grace alone through faith alone - in Jesus Christ alone. That means that salvation is received only through believing and trusting in Jesus Christ, not by any human effort or by perfectly following religious laws or practices. God offers salvation as a gift of grace, meaning it is unearned and undeserved.

Forgiveness isn't earned - it's received and it's available to anyone. No matter what your past is, no matter what your denomination is, no matter how far you've run, Jesus Christ is always there with his arms wide open waiting to wrap those arms around anyone who'll come to him and cry out to him for forgiveness.

The Lord Jesus Christ have paid the full price for the salvation of your soul. He died on the cross for your sins, so that you can be saved by His sacrifice. We have forgiveness of sins, we are justified by faith, we are declared righteous - in God's eyes through our faith in Jesus Christ. 

Jesus said, “It is finished,” meaning that there is nothing more to do, nothing left to pay. He has paid it all - totally, completely, permanently. We can’t add anything to what the Son of God have done for us. We accept His payment for our sins by repenting and believing in Him.

The Bible says, 
"For everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved." 

The Bible says, 
"If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness."

quoted_text:
Dear Robotic DeployCos: Your next growth bottleneck might be working capital.

Working capital dynamics are not being talked about enough, but the details are really important for Founders to think about before the debt markets truly open up to financing robotics.

Here's an example that outlines why.

Assume two companies each have $3M available for deployments with identical hardware and deployment costs: $100K per robot.

Company A charges $80K upfront + $2K/month for software and services.

Collect the upfront payment before major expenses, and you’re funding $20K per robot. Your $3M supports 150 deployments.

Company B charges $0 upfront + $6K/month for pure RaaS.

You’re funding the full $100K per robot, so your $3M supports 30 deployments.

IF you have the same deployment costs and same available capital, you can get five times the initial deployment capacity by getting folks to pay you upfront.

And on the revenue side of things at those fleet sizes, that’s $300K versus $180K in monthly recurring revenue.

Both strategies have pros and cons to be clear.

Upfront payments conserve cash and help finance expansion. They also require a bigger customer commitment, which can slow sales or shrink your buyer pool. It also pulls down your recurring revenue TAM and how it impacts multiple is TBD.

Pure RaaS lowers the upfront hurdle and generates more recurring revenue per robot. It also ties up more capital while you earn back the deployment investment.

Customer budgets, payment timing, contract duration, service costs, and access to financing all matter. All of those nuances can change which strategy works best.

My point is that it's important to think just as deeply about how you get paid as you do about how you deploy.

Because the fact of the matter is that you can have a full pipeline and still lack the cash to fulfill it.

author: iruletrenches
quoted_text:
Joooooo treats a blockchain as a computer and measures it like hardware. Gas is energy, block time is the clock.

Raw speed is tiny. All of BSC running his 507k-gate chip gets ~10–13 Hz.

Speed isn't the point. Verification is. Run the circuit off-chain on any machine, and if anyone disputes the result, the chain settles it in ~30 rounds, even for a billion steps.

My take: this is the third wave. Bitcoin turned hardware into security. Ethereum put code on-chain. TapeOut puts the circuit itself on-chain.

Mining rigs won't disappear. Their job changes: from burning hashes to running useful circuits the chain can verify.

text:
Pretty cool!

I gave IQuest-Q1, the open-source model from @IQuest_research, one task:

"Simulate two spiral galaxies colliding, interactively. One HTML file. No libraries."

Round 1 (~7 min): it wrote everything from scratch.

→ 2 galaxies, 2,500 stars each, one disk tilted, one prograde
→ an in-browser leapfrog gravity integrator
→ a live HUD: time, separation, speed, tidal-tail %

No errors: 5,000 stars at ~53 FPS.

But the galaxies merged in 10 seconds. Nothing else happened.

We sent it the test numbers.

Round 2 (~13 min):

It checked its physics, used Python scripts to scan friction and orbit parameters, traced the best candidates, and reworked the encounter.

Now:

> first close pass at ~16 s
> tidal tails flung out, cores ~39 kpc apart
> the galaxies fall back and merge at ~59 s
> ~1.2 billion years simulated at ~50 FPS
> afterward: drag to rotate, scroll to zoom, change speed

It's a simplified N-body model.

The useful part is the write → test → feedback → fix loop.

we supplied the numbers, and it handled the fix 🔥

text:
Today we are launching OnchainBench, the benchmark for agents in crypto.

It helps you decide how far you can trust an AI agent with your keys: how often it finishes the job, what tasks cost, and how easily it falls prey to an attack.

People are starting to let AI agents swap, lend and even trade for them. The bigger the task, the greater the risk you're taking by trusting the agent. So before you hand it your keys, you need to assess it.

There are many risks to assess at once. An agent could buy two tokens for a liquidity position but never add them to the pool, so the job isn't complete. It could spend more on AI model calls than the task is worth. And, onchain, there's no undo: agents read web pages, files and tool descriptions that anyone can write, and if one of them tricks the agent into sending funds to the wrong address, the money is gone. Until now, there was no common way to evaluate agents on all of this and more.

OnchainBench helps you compare agents by giving them the kind of work people already ask them to do: swaps on @Uniswap, @SushiSwap and @Honeyswap, lending on @aave, deposits into sDAI from @SkyEcosystem, prediction markets on @Omen_eth, research, and jobs that run over several days.

Each task runs through a @safe smart account on a copy of a public chain. The first version covers @ethereum, @gnosischain, @0xPolygon, @arbitrum, @Optimism, @base, @Celo, @modenetwork and @robinhoodapp. The benchmark emulates the kind of contracts, liquidity and prices the agent would meet with your money, without putting any of it at risk. A task only counts as done if the chain shows it was done. Some tasks also hide an attack in what the agent reads, such as a look-alike token or a fake "verification" request, so you can see how often agents get tricked into moving funds before you trust one with yours.

In the first run, Claude Code (@claudeai), Codex (@OpenAI), Hermes (@NousResearch), OpenClaw (@openclaw) and our own new OCB agent on @autonolas worked through 147 private tasks they had never seen. They completed between 88.4% and 96.2% of tasks, at about $0.03 to $0.35 per completed task. Agents lost funds to an attack 13 times in 1,793 attack tests.

We are excited to contribute this to the crypto ecosystem. If you build a protocol or a chain, agents are already among your users, and will likely be one of your biggest sources of growth. OnchainBench shows, protocol by protocol and chain by chain, how well they handle yours.

For the AI ecosystem: want an agent eval with real ground truth and real adversaries? Onchain, every result can be checked and every injected instruction is a live risk. OnchainBench is open to contributions, uses private tasks, and is ready for your agent.

Help us make onchain agents harder to trick and better at the job. If you run a protocol or are a heavy user, propose the task you think agents still get wrong on the site below, and every agent on the benchmark could end up tested on it. If you build agents, run OnchainBench yourself and submit your agent to be run.

The leaderboard is live now at https://t.co/xs5WV4paUy

Share it with a friend!

text:
币安连续两次美股 IPO 打新失利，到底是哪里出了问题？

6 月 SpaceX IPO，币安钱包最终取消申购、全额退款。

11 月 Anthropic IPO，吸引约 5 亿美元资金申购，最终却只拿到价值约 24.5 万美元的代币化股票，获配比例不足 0.05%。

反观 Bitget 和 Gate，分别拿到了约 1276 万美元和 764 万美元的额度。

币安不缺用户，也不缺资金，但为什么连续两次都没能拿到像样的 IPO 配售额度？

第一次打新失败，还可以说是上游渠道、配售安排等各种问题。

但第二次又是这样的结果，问题可能已经不是「为什么拿不到额度」，而是「既然上次已经知道额度有多难拿，为什么这次还要开放这么大规模的申购？」

突然想到一个有意思的假设：

如果当年 CZ 真把 FTX 收购了，如今币安会不会已经拥有更成熟的美股业务和一级市场资源，也不至于两次打新都这么尴尬？

当然，收购 FTX 也不等于自动获得美股 IPO 配售资格。

大家觉得，币安的问题到底出在哪里？
author: BlockBeatsAsia
quoted_text:
如果 CZ 当年以 1 美元接盘 FTX，如今可能坐拥千亿美元 Anthropic 股权。

2022 年 11 月 FTX 爆雷时，SBF 曾主动联系 CZ，希望 Binance 接盘。

当时 Blockworks 援引消息人士报道称，双方讨论的初始收购价格仅为象征性的 1 美元，但买方需要承担数十亿美元的资金缺口。

双方最终签署了非约束性收购意向书，但 Binance 很快退出交易。

有意思的是，CZ 在今年出版的回忆录中却表示，自己当时根本没有兴趣拥有 FTX，也没有认真考虑完成收购，签署意向书只是为了评估能否保护用户。

现在回头看，这句话多少有些耐人寻味。

因为 FTX 当年曾以 5 亿美元投资 Anthropic，最初获得约 13.56% 股权。

2024 年，FTX 破产财团以约 13.3 亿美元出售全部 Anthropic 股份。而如今，Anthropic IPO 估值已经达到约 1.5 万亿美元。

如果按照 FTX 出售前约 7.84% 的持股比例静态计算，这笔股权理论上价值约 1176 亿美元，当然尚未考虑后续稀释。

假如 CZ 当年真的完成整体收购，而且拿到了 Anthropic 股权，今天的故事可能完全不同。

更巧的是，今年市场还曾传出 YZi Labs 投资 Kimi 背后月之暗面的消息，何一随后回应投资的是一家华人创业的 AI 公司，但并未确认就是 Kimi。

如果 Binance 早已持有大量 Anthropic 股权，CZ 后来还会不会寻找其他 AI 模型公司的投资机会？

当然，1 美元报价并非双方正式确认的交易价格，Anthropic 股权也未被证实包含在潜在收购范围内。

当年放弃收购 FTX，究竟是一次成功的风险规避，还是错过了 AI 时代最有价值的投资机会之一？

至少从今天的结果看，CZ 当年没有兴趣接手的那堆资产里，藏着一笔可能价值千亿美元的 AI 投资。

author: ChaseWang
quoted_text:
在使用编程 Agent 进行几十轮交互时，如何有效地降低成本同时保持质量是许多人的第一想法，即使用强模型来指导，用弱模型来进行编码。但在实际工程中，我们面临着两个问题：首先，前缀缓存不能在模型间共享；其次，在中间更换模型可能会导致思路断裂。

Google 刚发布了 Gemini 4 Neon，价格比最贵的 Carbon 原价便宜四分之一，默认档位甚至能对标最贵版本，单次任务成本还能省 32%。但比跑分更值得关注的是，Google 同时也在编程工具 Antigravity 中推出了 Orchestrator (Neon) 双模型接力模式。把它和 Anthropic、DeepSeek 的方案放在一起，正好对应编程 Agent 省钱的三条路线：

1. Anthropic：死守单模型，靠调低思考档位省钱。
编程循环里大部分输入靠前缀缓存打折，Anthropic 首次写缓存要收额外写入费，中途换模型会让前面攒的缓存直接作废，重写的成本很快吃掉差价。他们也试过让便宜模型先写、卡住了再问强模型，结果近 400 次实验里，便宜模型一次都没主动求助过，因为它自己都不知道卡住了。

2. DeepSeek：拆成两个独立会话，项目经理给后台子代理派单。
他们在同一个窗口给强模型留了写代码权限，结果它时不时会管不住手亲自下场，把对话窗口锁死。直接没收写代码工具、拆成双层会话确实治好了手痒，但两边都要重读代码库和上下文，多消耗了 3.8 倍的缓存。

3. Google 的 Orchestrator (Neon)：在同一会话里做轻量接力。
拿到需求后，Neon 先用只读模式看代码、出方案，并写明什么情况下需要重新规划；趁着开局上下文还短，后台自动把保存的推理状态接过去，把写代码、跑测试交给便宜的 Hydrogen。Google 的隐式缓存免收写入费，开局付一点重读的过路费，就能把后面十几轮写代码和跑测试的输出费用砍一半，所以划算。如果测试连挂两次或遇到意外，控制权会自动弹回 Neon 查现场修计划，再交回继续跑。

如果暂时忽略缓存和接口的具体设计，这三个例子其实展示了 Agent 系统里两种不同的控制哲学：结果确定性和过程确定性。

用 Anthropic 的单旗舰模型，我们可以大胆地依赖结果确定性，明确验收标准，然后相信强模型会自己决定什么时候查代码、什么时候改策略。但一旦为了省钱换成小模型，或者想在单窗口里拆分角色，这种放手就变得危险：小模型看不出自己已经跑偏，强模型看到写代码的工具也容易忍不住下场。这时候我们就不得不退回到过程确定性，在外部补上流程护栏。

DeepSeek 和 Google 都在补这道护栏，只是路径不同。DeepSeek 用物理拆分会话、没收工具实现强隔离，换来可控性，但付出了 3.8 倍缓存的代价。Google 把护栏做轻、收进同一条会话里，在规划期锁只读防止强模型手痒，在执行期用测试连续失败两次这种明确信号把跑偏的小模型拉回来。用最轻的过程确定性兜住小模型的下限，同时保住单会话的上下文连续性，双模型接力才算真正跑通。

完整的文章会详细分析这三家缓存计费的不同，以及在 Antigravity 或者自建 Agent 工作流中如何选型和抄作业，以及投产前要注意的两个坑：

text:
从 2023 年这轮牛市启动以来，几次大跌都有一个共同特点：危机很大程度上由人为因素触发，最后也靠人为因素结束。

2024 年 8 月：日元套息交易大规模平仓，全球市场暴跌，最后日本央行率先转鸽，市场迅速反弹。

2025 年 4 月：Trump 发动关税战，全球股市崩盘，最后 Trump TACO，关税政策急转弯，市场 V 型反转

2026 年 4 月：伊朗战争引发恐慌，最后又是 Trump TACO，地缘政治风险缓和，市场有是V反

连续三次，市场都被训练出了一种肌肉记忆：暴跌就抄底，反正最后总有人出来救，市场很快就会 V 回去。这种肌肉记忆恰恰是这一轮调整中期最大的风险之一。

如果这一次面临的是结构性问题，比如 AI 需求增速不及预期、巨额 CapEx 无法兑现足够的回报、美国党争持续恶化，那么情况可能完全不同。政策可以随时TACO，但企业的盈利预期、估值和资本开支周期，没办法靠某个人出来讲几句话就修复

过去几次 V 型反转，可能让市场上大量玩家低估了真正深度出清的可能性。 很多人还在按照过去三年的经验交易，跌 10% 就抄底，跌 15% 就加杠杆，默认后面一定有一根大阳线,过去三年被训练出来的交易习惯，未必适用于下一场真正的熊市

建议大家在抄底的时候要注意仓位管理，不要乱上杠杆，一定要留一些现金。活下去、不下牌桌才是最重要的

text:
黄金跌破 3600 美元/盎司，泡泡玛特回调 -55.7%，AI 存储股腰斩

过去一年最热闹的几个赛道，给我们的共同启示是：一个故事最危险的阶段，往往发生在它最正确的时候

牛市就像做爱，高潮往往意味着结束

这篇 4 个月前的长文《叙事的黄昏》以黄金、泡泡玛特、AI 存储为例，总结了「一轮叙事行情的六个阶段」，我读下来有收获，分享给希望下次不在山顶 FOMO 接盘的你

—— 正文开始 ——

文｜郑立涛
原文链接 | https://t.co/oTMg5Bn1k1

2023 年至 2025 年，美元金价连续三年加速上涨，涨幅分别达到了 14.6%、25.5% 和 67%。进入 2026 年后，黄金又在不到一个月内上涨约 28%，从 4,368 美元冲至约 5,586 美元。到 1 月 29 日，央行购金、美元信用弱化、财政赤字扩张、地缘冲突升级与货币宽松预期，几乎被市场拼成了一个无可反驳的故事。

半年之后，世界并没有变得更平静。中国人民银行仍在买金，全球央行仍然希望提高黄金储备，中东的冲突又一次强化了「乱世黄金」的叙事。但黄金的价格却在1月见顶后持续回落，6 月底盘中一度触及约 3,963 美元，最大回撤约 29%。不少在过去两年涨幅很大的金矿股，也已经从高位回撤 60%，甚至更多。

上涨周期里的黄金叙事依然在持续兑现，但价格却已经提前结束了行情。

这种背离，非常值得复盘。一个叙事可以长期正确，也可以在某个阶段被强力演绎、广泛扩圈，最终成为几乎所有人的共识。价格取决于预期怎么变化、后面还有多少资金愿意买；等到事实最充分、故事最有说服力时，潜在买家可能已经不多了。

类似的背离也出现在去年的泡泡玛特身上：公司业绩仍在增长，「全球 IP 平台」的故事仍在逐步兑现，股价却已经率先见顶。

两个看似无关的资产，背后或许存在着相似的定价过程。

为什么当一个板块的叙事最强、扩圈最充分的时候，往往价格总是先于基本面反转？当我们理解了这个，我们也更容易理解，为什么在每一波投机行情中赚到大额浮盈容易，但逃顶却总是那么困难。

一、黄金长牛周期的超级叙事

2022 年以后，市场给黄金定价的方式发生了明显变化。

俄乌冲突后，俄罗斯外汇储备被冻结。此后，对不少新兴市场央行而言，储备资产的安全性已经不只取决于信用和流动性，还取决于能否免受制裁影响。黄金不对应任何主权发行人的承诺，在本国或中立地区托管时，更容易保持独立性。

欧洲央行在 2025 年的研究中发现，俄乌冲突以后，黄金与实际利率之间原有的关系明显减弱；与中国和俄罗斯地缘关系更接近的国家，官方储备中的黄金占比上升得更快。降低制裁风险，已经成为不少央行调整储备结构时需要考虑的问题。

央行买金的规模也明显扩大。2022 年至 2024 年，全球央行每年净购金都在 1,000 吨上下；2025 年回落至 863 吨，但仍显著高于 2010 年至 2021 年的年均 473 吨。

央行购金并非一两年的短期行为，它反映的是全球储备体系逐步走向多元化。美国财政赤字长期维持高位、地缘政治更加碎片化，也在持续提高黄金作为非主权储备资产的重要性。

这些变化给黄金提供了扎实的长期理由，也让围绕黄金形成的故事格外有说服力。

二、长期逻辑的提前定价

黄金最初的上涨主要由央行推动，西方投资者的参与仍然有限。2024 年以后，降息预期、美元走弱、地缘风险与对美国财政的担忧，又把 ETF、期货和趋势资金吸引进来。

2025 年，全球黄金投资需求增至 2,175 吨，同比增长 84%，达到央行净购金量的 2.5 倍；全球黄金 ETF 全年净流入 890 亿美元。央行继续提供长期方向，金融资金则逐渐取得日常定价权。

价格上涨又开始反过来提高叙事的可信度。黄金不断创出新高，媒体关注增加，ETF 申购扩大，趋势资金继续加仓。每一次回调都能很快修复，也让市场越来越相信：只要长期故事没有变化，短期下跌就值得买。

到了 2026 年 1 月，这种正反馈进一步加速。全球黄金 ETF 单月净增持约 120 吨，持仓与资产规模双双创下纪录；中国黄金 ETF 净增持 38 吨，而中国人民银行当月增持约 1.2 吨。央行仍然是长期叙事的核心，但 1 月这段急涨主要由投资者资金推动。

这时发生了一个重要变化：市场把原本需要几年兑现的逻辑，在几个月里提前计入了价格。每一条长期理由依然成立，但还能被这些理由说服的新买家已经越来越少。

到 1 月底，央行购金仍在提供长期支撑，真正让价格加速的却是降息预期与 ETF、趋势资金。央行买盘没有消失，但只要后两类资金不再流入，金价就会失去最直接的推动力。

三、叙事继续兑现，黄金却已开始下跌

1 月之后，最先变化的是仓位，随后是货币政策环境。

年初，市场普遍预期美联储将继续降息、美国经济逐渐走弱。随后，就业、投资和经济活动表现出韧性，AI capex 没有明显降温，降息预期不断后移，甚至出现重新加息的讨论。美国 2026 年一季度实际 GDP 增长 2.0%，设备与软件投资继续贡献增长；6 月美联储也明确提到生产率与资本投资较强、通胀仍然偏高。

黄金的结构性需求仍在，但货币宽松带来的周期性顺风暂时消失。与此同时，1 月集中流入的 ETF 与趋势资金开始退出。最初的快速下跌主要来自杠杆和趋势资金集中减仓；随后几个月，早期获利资金陆续兑现收益，高位买入者也在反弹中减仓，市场对利率和金价后续路径的分歧逐渐加大，因此调整一直延续。

2026 年一季度，全球央行仍净购入 244 吨黄金；6 月全球黄金 ETF 却单月流出 89 亿美元、减持 74 吨。慢资金继续改变储备结构，快资金正在降低仓位，两者完全可以同时发生。

这轮回落，把此前混在一起的几件事重新分开了：央行购金仍在支撑长期价值，利率变化影响中期方向，拥挤仓位则决定短期涨跌有多急。长期逻辑没有消失，并不能阻止一轮由资金退出引发的深度调整。

这也把问题带到了黄金之外：当长期趋势仍然成立，价格却不再跟随好消息上涨，市场究竟发生了什么？索罗斯关于反身性的研究，提供了一种解释。

四、叙事的黄昏期

索罗斯在《金融炼金术》中分析资产的繁荣与崩溃时，使用了两个核心变量：现实中存在的底层趋势，以及市场围绕这条趋势形成的主流认知。

一轮典型的反身性过程，往往从一条尚未被充分认识的真实趋势开始。市场逐渐发现它，价格随之上涨；价格上涨又反过来强化主流认知，并在某些资产里改变融资、供给或需求。过程当中会经历几次回调测试。如果趋势经受住测试，怀疑者减少，信念与仓位进一步加强。

索罗斯将后续阶段称为 twilight period，也就是黄昏期。疑虑已经出现，越来越多人失去信心，原有趋势却仍依靠惯性延续。等到价格趋势真正反转，杠杆清算和信心变化会让负反馈向相反方向运行。

用这个框架回看黄金，有一处尤其值得注意。

黄金的长期趋势仍然成立，问题出在市场怎样把它外推到短期：央行持续购金，逐渐被理解为金价不会深度回撤；世界更加混乱，被理解为每次冲突都会带来同样规模的新买盘；长期中枢可能抬升，又被理解为任何价格都值得追。

可以将这个过程概括为「真趋势 - 错误外推 - 仓位饱和」。

真实趋势为行情提供起点。它必须足够强，才能在早期不断经受质疑和回调，吸引更多投资者加入。

错误外推让价格跑得比现实更快。市场逐渐把几年才能验证的逻辑集中折现到几个月内，把方向正确延伸为路径平滑，再把长期空间延伸为任何价格都值得持有。

仓位饱和最终耗尽边际买家。观点只有转化成资金才会推动价格；等到大多数相信者已经完成仓位转化，继续出现的利好更多是在满足原有预期，很难再创造同等规模的新增买入力量。

叙事的黄昏由此拥有一个很反直觉的特征：故事仍然正确，故事对价格的解释力却在下降。市场关注的重心已经从「这件事是否成立」，转向「还有多少人会因为它而买入」。

五、黄昏期的五个信号

黄昏期没有一个可以精确确认的点位，但可以观察五类变化。

1) 讨论从事实转向价格

这种变化并不只发生在黄金上。早期参与者讨论的，通常是故事背后的事实：央行为何持续购金，Labubu 为何能在海外成为爆款，HBM 为何长期紧缺。到了后期，讨论的重心逐渐从事实转向价格：涨了多少、还能涨多少、每次回调是不是新的买点。上涨被当成故事正确的证据，故事又成了继续追涨的理由。

此时更值得问的是：新的事实还能不能说服原来的怀疑者？如果它只是在让已经相信的人更加确信，能够被这套故事吸引进来的新买家也就越来越少了。

2) 观点已转化为仓位

口头共识对价格的影响有限。ETF申购、期货净多头、期权交易、杠杆产品与相关股票持仓，才能看出有多少人已经把观点变成仓位。

黄金 1 月的特殊之处，就在于长期央行买盘与短期金融资金恰好叠在一起。央行买盘可以持续很多年，ETF、期货和趋势资金却能在几个月内把未来收益提前计入价格。

3) 利好开始钝化

利好还能不能推动价格，是最值得观察的信号。

到了行情后段，好消息往往仍然很多，但大部分已经被市场提前想到。长期逻辑继续成立、公司继续增长，只是在兑现原有预期；价格若想再明显上涨，还需要业绩进一步加速、盈利预测继续上调，或者有一批新资金入场。

此时，一些资金会重新计算继续持有的赔率：向上的空间已经被乐观预期压缩，任何意外却都可能带来较大回撤。不需要提前猜中利空会从哪里出现，只要潜在收益变小、风险回报不再划算，反应较快的资金就会先离开。

因此，「利好不涨」本身就是信息。事实越来越有利，价格反应却越来越弱，说明好消息已经很难带来新的认知和资金。再往后，利好公布后的高开低走，甚至会变成持仓者减仓的机会。

所以，「故事是否正确」和「价格对好消息的反应」，需要分开观察。很多类似的周期告诉我们，事实尚未见顶，价格完全可能提前见顶。

4) 轻微逆风引发更大波动

最先离开的资金，会让原本紧密的抱团开始松动。价格转弱后，趋势资金降低仓位，杠杆资金收缩敞口，后进入的投机资金逐步止盈。大家离开的理由未必相同，卖出的方向却是一致的。

仓位越一致，行情越不需要一条足以推翻长期逻辑的大利空。美元反弹、降息预期后移、保证金提高，单独看都不足以解释黄金的大幅下跌；叠加在一起，却会让拥挤资金失去继续加仓的理由，原本正常的获利了结也可能演变成集中减仓。

这类反转通常很不对称：利好越来越难推动价格，一点利空却可能引起较大回撤。

5) 低 PE 带来的错觉

叙事拥挤不一定表现为很高的 PE。对黄金矿企、存储和其他周期性公司来说，拥挤也可能藏在处于高位的利润里。

假设一家公司的正常盈利为 5 元，股价 100 元，对应 20 倍 PE。景气高峰时盈利升到 10 元，股价即使涨至 150 元，PE 仍会降到 15 倍。股票已经上涨 50%，估值看起来反而更便宜。如果盈利随后回到 5 元，静态PE会重新变成 30 倍。

所以，看到低 PE，先要问当下的盈利能否持续。用正常化的价格、利润率与 capex 重新计算后仍然便宜，估值才有更扎实的安全边际。直接把景气高峰的利润年化，很容易把周期高点误认为长期盈利能力。

六、复盘泡泡玛特：故事仍在兑现，股价提前见顶

泡泡玛特与黄金看起来毫不相干。黄金交易的是货币信用、央行需求与地缘风险，泡泡玛特交易的是消费、IP 与公司的经营能力。但两轮行情有一个共同点：价格见顶时，故事恰好最有说服力；见顶以后，股价震荡下行，但公司经营或长期需求并没有马上转坏。

1) 一次持续两年的经营重估

2021 年上市热潮退去以后，市场曾经把泡泡玛特理解为一家依赖盲盒红利和少数 IP 的潮玩公司。盲盒有没有长期需求、年轻人的兴趣会不会迅速变化、单一 IP 的生命周期能维持多久，这些问题很难回答，也限制了市场愿意给它的估值。

真正改变定价的，是公司从 2023 年开始连续交出了一组很难忽视的经营结果。

Labubu 从一个圈层 IP 走向大众市场，毛绒产品打开了盲盒之外的新载体，海外门店与供应链逐渐跑通。到 2024 年，公司收入达到 130.4 亿元，同比增长 106.9%；经调整净利润达到 34.0 亿元，同比增长 185.9%。其中海外及港澳台收入增长 375.2% 至 50.7 亿元，占总收入的 38.9%。

这组数据改变了市场看待泡泡玛特的方式。国内潮玩增长放缓的担心，被更快的海外增长冲淡，海外的热度又反向带动了国内的热度；毛绒产品又打开了盲盒之外的新场景。随着海外门店、供应链和 IP 运营逐渐跑通，市场也开始把它从一家潮玩零售商，重新理解为一家拥有产品设计、IP 运营、供应链和全球渠道能力的公司。

所以，股价上涨既有利润增长，也有估值重估。公司利润持续超出预期，投资者也在不断提高对其商业模式上限的判断。泡泡玛特的股价从 2024 年 2 月的 16.96 港元一路涨到 2025 年 8 月的 339.8 港元，最高涨幅约 20 倍。这个涨幅的背后，确实有经营上的巨大变化。

2) 从 Labubu 到「全球 IP 平台」

一轮叙事最初往往是具体的。泡泡玛特最初的故事是 Labubu 成为爆款，随后变成海外收入高速增长，再往后则扩张成了「全球 IP 平台」。

这三层叙事看起来只差几个字，估值含义却完全不同。一个爆款贡献的是一段产品周期；全球化贡献的是更大的市场空间；平台意味着公司拥有一套可以反复发现 IP、孵化 IP、放大 IP 并在全球变现的能力。叙事走到第三层以后，投资者购买的已经不只是当期 Labubu 的利润，还包括未来尚未出现的许多个 Labubu。

泡泡玛特的特殊之处在于，每一层叙事都得到了现实的支持。海外门店排队、明星带货与社交媒体传播证明 Labubu 已经跨越文化圈层；收入和利润证明热度能够转化为商业价值；Molly、Skullpanda、Crybaby 等 IP 以及不断扩张的品类，又为平台化能力提供了更多想象空间。「中国迪士尼」的说法因此越来越有吸引力。

叙事也在这个过程中逐渐改变了市场的提问方式。早期的问题是「Labubu 能不能成为全球爆款」，后来变成「泡泡玛特还能制造多少个全球爆款」。前一个问题已经得到回答，后一个问题的答案需要许多年才能验证，市场却在很短的时间里把很大一部分成功概率计入了价格。

3) 最强业绩与最满预期

2025 年 8 月，泡泡玛特公布了一份无可挑剔的半年报：上半年收入达到 138.8 亿元，同比增长 204.4%，半年的收入已经超过 2024 年全年；归母净利润同比增长 396.5%。

业绩出来以后，卖方又集中上调了盈利预测与目标价。摩根士丹利、汇丰和招商证券给出的目标价先后提高到 365 港元、379 港元和 410 港元。高股价看起来也没有那么贵了，因为只要把当时的增长继续外推，未来两三年的盈利分母会迅速变大，远期 PE 自然会逐年下降。

这些目标价本身并不重要。更值得复盘的是，到这个时候，市场能想到的好消息几乎都已经出现：业绩爆发、盈利预测上调、长期空间打开，越来越多投资者也开始认同「全球 IP 平台」的故事。中报再次证明了多头此前看对了，但市场已经很难从中找到此前没有想到的新增长。到 2025 年 8 月 26 日，股价在 339.8 港元见顶，距离这份最强中报发布只有几个交易日。

公司没有变差，股价继续上涨的门槛却变高了。公司若想支撑更高的价格，需要持续交出比三位数增长更强的惊喜；任何增长降速、爆款热度波动或第二 IP 不及预期，都可能让此前不断上调的盈利预测掉头向下。

对行情后期入场的资金来说，继续持有能赚到的空间已经变小，未来某个意外带来回撤的风险却始终存在。部分资金率先离开后，价格对利好的反应开始减弱，原本一致的持仓也逐渐松动。公司仍在变好，股票却需要越来越大的超预期才能继续上涨。

4) 20% 增长指引发布之后

见顶后的泡泡玛特并未马上进入经营下行。2025 年全年，公司收入达到 371.2 亿元，同比增长 184.7%；经调整净利润达到 130.8 亿元，同比增长 284.5%。海外扩张、IP 商业化和盈利能力都在继续兑现。

真正改变市场定价的，是管理层在 2026 年 3 月 25 日业绩会上给出的增长目标：2026 年收入增长不低于 20%。对绝大多数消费公司来说，20% 的增长仍然相当不错；但泡泡玛特此前的价格建立在连续翻倍甚至三位数增长之上，20% 意味着盈利曲线将从爆发状态回到更正常的斜率。业绩与指引发布当天，股价下跌近 23%。

截至 7 月 10 日，泡泡玛特收于 150.7 港元，较 2025 年高点回撤约 56%。现实中的公司仍在增长，「全球 IP 平台」的长期逻辑也没有消失，股价却已经回吐了此前按爆发期增速定价的很大一部分涨幅。

Labubu 已经证明中国 IP 可以进入全球消费市场，泡泡玛特也证明自己拥有全球渠道、产品开发与商业化能力，这些事实至今仍然成立。但「一个全球爆款」能否稳定复制成「多个全球爆款」，「一家优秀的 IP 公司」能否长期成为「全球 IP 平台」，仍然需要更长时间和更多 IP 来验证。行情最热的时候，价格已经把后一层也当成了接近确定的未来。

叙事进入黄昏期，不意味着公司突然变差，也不要求长期逻辑被推翻。它只说明市场从怀疑到相信的那段最快重估已经走完：怀疑者越来越少，盈利预期越来越高，公司继续兑现好业绩，股价也越来越涨不动。此后即使故事仍然成立，投资回报也要等待现实追上此前被计入价格的未来。

七、存储，或许正在复现同一个过程

存储与黄金，也有几处相似。

存储的长期逻辑同样有强大的现实基础。AI 训练和推理显著提高 HBM、Server DRAM 与企业级 SSD 需求；HBM 占用更多晶圆与先进封装资源，挤压普通 DRAM 供给；新建晶圆厂需要多年；三大厂商的集中度和投资纪律也较过去更强。

美光预计，DRAM 与 NAND 的供需紧张将持续到 2027 年以后。公司已经签订 16 份战略客户协议，覆盖未来约 20% 的 DRAM 销量和约三分之一的 NAND 销量，其中不少协议具有多年期与 take-or-pay 性质。这些变化提高了存储企业盈利的可见度。

公司盈利已经到了罕见的水平。2026 年一季度，美光收入达到 414.6 亿美元，营业利润率 81.2%；下一季度又指引收入 500 亿美元、毛利率约 86%。按照约 31 美元的单季 EPS 简单年化，当前公司股价对应仅为个位数 PE。

但真正的问题仍是，这样的利润涨势能维持多久？

美光本季度 DRAM 收入同比增长 343%，bit shipment 只增长了低个位数，价格上涨约 60% 成为主要推动力。

三星的情况更加明显。2026 年一季度，三星存储业务收入从上一季度的 37.1 万亿韩元增至 74.8 万亿韩元，接近翻倍；半导体部门营业利润也从 16.4 万亿韩元增至 53.7 万亿韩元。同期服务器 DRAM 与服务器 NAND 的 bit 增长分别只有一成多和两成多，DRAM 与 NAND 的客单价却分别上涨了九成左右。收入和利润的爆发主要由价格上涨与高价值产品占比提升推动，出货量的贡献小得多。

到了二季度，这种分化更加明显。三星初步预计收入达到 171 万亿韩元，同比增长 129%；营业利润达到 89.4 万亿韩元，是上年同期的约 19 倍，并且高于市场预期。业绩公布当天，股价下跌 6.9%。市场关注的重点已经从当期利润转向 DRAM 涨价速度，以及 AI 资本开支能否继续支撑如此高的价格。DRAM 涨幅只是略低于此前过于乐观的预期，影响却压过了创纪录的利润。市场早已把高利润当作应有之义，任何不及预期都变得更加敏感。

美光与三星共同说明，当前存储公司的低 PE 很大程度上来自处于周期高位的利润。AI需求真实且强劲，利润对价格也同样敏感。bit 增长相对有限时，ASP 每一次上调都会直接放大利润；涨价速度一旦放缓，利润会收缩，即使股价不变，PE 也会迅速抬高。

第一个拐点已经摆在眼前：价格仍在上涨，涨幅却在快速收窄。2026 年一季度，一般型 DRAM 合约价上涨约 90% 至 95%；二季度预计再上涨 58% 至 63%；到了三季度，TrendForce 预计涨幅收窄至 13% 至 18%，NAND 涨幅收窄至 10% 至 15%。价格仍在上升，但消费电子客户的成本承受力已经接近极限，PC 和智能手机的消费需求也开始受到影响。

供给端的扩产也开始回应高价格。美光预计 2026 财年 capex 超过 270 亿美元，2027 财年全年 capex 将超过 400 亿美元；爱达荷晶圆厂计划在 2027 年中开始出片，台湾与新加坡项目预计在 2027 至 2028 年前后逐步贡献产能。

黄金的上涨很难在短期内增加矿山供给，而存储的高价格与高利润却会鼓励客户抢签长约，也会推动厂商增加 capex。行情越好，未来供给增加得越快。几家厂商都希望行业保持投资纪律，但谁也不愿意在下一轮份额竞争中落后。对单家公司合理的扩产，叠加在一起就可能重新制造过剩。这正是存储周期反复出现的囚徒困境。

把这些信号放在一起，或许我们应该高度关注，存储是否已经进入叙事的黄昏期。AI 需求仍然真实，未来几个季度的业绩也可能继续创新高；市场关心的问题却已经变了：此前关心利润还能涨多高，现在关心高利润还能维持多久。

股价已经从高位明显回落，但这并不意味着风险已经释放完。周期股常见的顺序是，股价先跌，盈利预测后降。前一段回撤消化的是拥挤仓位和过高预期，下一段风险可能来自 ASP 涨幅收窄之后的利润下修。只要盈利预期仍处在高位，个位数 PE 提供的安全垫就可能比表面上薄得多。

因此，未来一段时间的存储股走势，值得我们密切关注。由于业绩的强劲，不排除会有剧烈反弹的行情，但 ASP 涨幅收窄、消费端开始承压、资本开支明显上修、股价对创纪录利润反应转弱，这几个信号已经同时出现。

存储未来几个季度的业绩大概率仍然很好，但业绩创新高，并不能保证股价同步创下新高。

八、一轮叙事行情的六个阶段

从黄金、泡泡玛特到存储，一轮由真实变化推动的行情，大致会经历下述几个阶段：

1) 变化已经发生，市场还没有充分认识，价格反应不大。

2) 事实不断验证，越来越多人开始相信，价格随之上涨。

3) 价格上涨强化信心，资金流入继续推高价格。几次回调都能修复以后，市场对故事的信念越来越强。

4) 故事扩散到更多人，观点逐渐变成仓位，盈利预测被连续上调。此时股价已经涨了很多，却可能因为当期利润增长得更快而显得便宜。

5) 故事进入黄昏期。事实仍在变好，价格对利好的反应却越来越弱；一点逆风就会带来较大波动。市场还在讨论故事能走多远，愿意新买入的人已经不多。

6) 价格转弱，减仓和止损互相强化。长期逻辑可能继续成立，市场则要用一段下跌或横盘，消化此前提前计入的未来。

这套框架无法精确预测顶部，也不适合把每一次「利好不涨」解释成行情结束。它提供的价值，是帮助我们把故事是否正确、市场已经相信到什么程度、当前价格还剩多少赔率分开观察。

判断一个叙事有没有进入黄昏期，可以归结为三个问题：这个故事还能说服多少原本不相信的人；相信它的人还有多少没有转化成仓位；当最有利的事实出现时，价格还能不能继续上涨。

本文并非要否定黄金、泡泡玛特和 AI 产业的长期趋势，但通过对几个案例的复盘，或许能够启发我们多一个视角，去理解一轮投机炒作周期的演化路径与节奏。

叙事最有价值的阶段，往往是它正在被事实验证、市场却还没有充分相信的时候。等到现实中的每一个事件都在为它作证，我们更应该观察的，或许是还有多少利好没有被价格充分反映。

—— 正文结束 ——

text:
很多刚入手新款 MacBook Pro 的工程师都会专门花几百块钱去配一个苹果原装的 140W USB-C 氮化镓电源适配器，或者桌面级的多口 PD 3.1 充电站，指望能在跑满本地大模型编译和 Docker 集群的同时享受满血快充；结果插上功率计一看却傻眼了：除了顶级满血版与新上线的旗舰触控配置外，大量 14 英寸与标准版 MacBook Pro 的握手功率依然被主板电源管理芯片（PMIC）死死锁在 96W 甚至 70W。

为什么明明物理接口都上了支持 PD 3.1 EPR（28V / 5A） 的 MagSafe 3 和雷雳端口，苹果却要在固件层搞这么严苛的功率墙区分？如果从硬件热设计与电池化学寿命的工程边界去扒，这把刀法背后既有成本算计，也有物理限制。

首先是 充电倍率（C-rate）与散热冗余的硬约束。14 英寸标准版机型的机身内部空间紧凑，电池容量在 72Wh 左右，如果直接放开 140W 输入，扣除主板供电后灌进电芯的充电倍率会远超安全温升阈值，在夏天高负载编译代码时极易触发过热降频。而 16 英寸机型及高配版拥有近 100Wh 的大电池组与双风扇重型均热板，才能稳稳吃下 28V 高压快充带来的发热。

更值得重度开发者警惕的是 高负载瞬态抽电（Battery Drain under Load）问题。当你在被锁死 96W 输入的机型上同时拉满多核 CPU 与 GPU 跑本地推理、外接两块高刷显示器并为外设供电时，整机瞬时功耗峰值会短暂冲破电源适配器的输入上限，此时 macOS 的电源管理策略会自动从内置电池“借电”补齐缺口。长期处于这种边充边放的浅循环高压状态，正是很多程序员发现自己 Mac 电池健康度一年掉下 85% 的罪魁祸首。

IPE27 Countdown | Who is your campaign missing?

After a close election, someone in the campaign room will ask, “Where did we lose those votes?” Before the next one, I’d like us to ask a different question. Who never made it into our campaign plan in the first place?

Think of two people on the same street. One registered years ago and has since stopped voting. The other is eligible and has never registered. Both were missing on election day. What makes us think the same appeal will bring them to the ballot box? How many campaigns have even asked them why?

That is the question we are bringing to Cape Town. On 4 and 5 August 2027, the International Political Campaign Expo will bring campaign strategists, political parties and practitioners from around the world to The Westin, Cape Town, for two days focused on The Missing Voter.

On day one, we’ll work through how to identify who is missing in your own electorate. On day two, we’ll examine what it would take for those citizens to participate. Bring the turnout figures from your last election. Bring the assumptions your team made about the people behind those figures. Let’s put both on the table.

If you are already planning your next campaign, this conversation belongs on your calendar. The countdown to IPE27 starts now. See you in Cape Town.

I'm hearing multiple things from industry executives:

1. Potential $NVDA employee exodus if Jensen doesn't come back soon.

Many senior management and engineers can easily retire after Nvidia stock appreciation over the years.

They don't need to continue working sitting on millions in equity. But they continued to work because Jensen was a visionary leader.

Under new interim CFO (former CFO), it gives an excuse for that lot of people to finally quit soon. A pay bump or hiring $ARM CEO isn't going to change that.

So you have generational talent leaving.

2. Loss of confidence in $NVDA future growth (Jensen was the moat).

What I'm hearing is that Jensen understands heavily top-down architectures, and it's this magical discretionary element that doesn't get covered in media.

When cuda, network, and $NVDA internal teams are arguing, Jensen made the final choices around heavily nuanced discretionary decision about where Nvidia + AI ecosystem ends up going:

Then everyone followed. The supply chain, capital, agreements, and faith.

You also can't suddenly replace the trust that local Taiwanese factories build with Jensen over the years if you bring in external CEOs, or even internal executives.

It was transformational bet after bet after bet after bet that Jensen made until Nvidia became a former $5T+ company.

3. $NVDA is not that technologically far ahead of others. It's not a 5 year lead, but months ahead to a year in different areas.

Jensen was accelerating all of that. Longer Jensen is gone, the longer Nvidia and its competitive ecosystem decays, beyond the current near-term roadmaps.

Nvidia's greatest moat was Jensen Huang making high-stake architectural decisions and accelerating capital, suppliers, + the industry to rally around his vision.

There's a massive loss of confidence in $NVDA with Jensen gone.

最近 Crypto U 卡越来越卷了。从基础消费返现，到 AI 订阅、机场贵宾室，各家平台都开始争夺用户的日常消费场景。

Plasma和Kem是Tether支持的两家U卡：@Plasma 是 @Tether 早期投资的U卡；@kem_app 作为后起之秀，近期势头很猛，还搞了GTA6 的直播打赏活动。

从产品设计来看：KEM 主打高返现和丰富的消费场景。 除了基础返现，外卖、购物、旅行等消费还能享受额外福利，甚至连 AI 订阅也有专属返现，比较适合希望通过日常刷卡薅羊毛的用户。

Plasma 侧重高端会员权益：基础返现没有金额上限，高级会员提供外币手续费减免，但获取这些权益需要支付年费或满足持仓条件。

🌟 那么，到底该怎么选？
对于普通用户来说，KEM Lite 值得优先考虑，零会员费就能享受基础返现；如果每月有较多外卖、AI 订阅及旅行消费，可以考虑 KEM Onyx ，每月 $15.99 的会员费也相对容易接受。

而且 Kem有专门的华人客服，非常华人友好。

如果消费金额较大，或者经常出国旅行，可以进一步对比 KEM Gold 和 Plasma 的高端会员，不过 Plasma 的订阅费用较高，能否需要多算算能不能回本。

美国观察：Anthropic的IPO或许标志着“AI交易”热潮的终结 - 作者：Anna Wong（经济学家）

（彭博经济研究）——Anthropic备受瞩目的首次公开募股（IPO）表面上似乎是对“AI交易”投下了一张信任票，但我们却有不同的看法。

作为前沿模型领域的领军企业，同时也是AI热潮的标志性代表，Anthropic恰恰暴露了这一投资热潮核心地带的一个脆弱点：前沿智能的定价权正在减弱。

一个稳固的“护城河”，归根结底在于企业获取经济租金（超额利润）的能力。

然而，自9月份（Anthropic IPO招股说明书中财务数据的截止期）以来，其“代币”（token）的实际价格已大幅下滑。尽管代币使用量激增，但市场份额却并未随之提升。

Anthropic在未能巩固自身竞争地位的同时，却放弃了很大一部分价格溢价——这表明，技术领先优势和AI需求的蓬勃增长，并未转化为持久的定价权。

诚然，Anthropic此次大规模融资可能会在短期内为“AI交易”再添一把火。但与此同时，此次IPO也将前沿AI领域的经济模式推向了公开市场；在这里，定价、利润率以及资本回报率等指标，都将面临每个季度的严格审视。

如果Anthropic未来的业绩显示其定价权远不及估值所隐含的水平，那么这种估值重塑可能会加速整个AI板块估值的回调。

回过头来看，Anthropic的IPO或许并非“AI交易”新一轮上涨的起点，而更像是这股热潮在终结前最后注入的一剂燃料。

quoted_text:
Remarks from Anthropic CEO @DarioAmodei on our initial public offering:

My co-founders and I started Anthropic because we believe that the most powerful technology of our time should be built for the benefit of humankind.

Daniela and I lost our father to a disease that, just a few years later, became curable. I started my career in biology, hoping to help future cures come sooner. In the lab, I saw the vast thicket of complexity that scientists face when they’re trying to understand disease and develop new treatments.

So many of the scientific tools that can cut through that thicket—tools for gene editing, gene synthesis, controlling brain cells with light—started as pure ideas. In other words, they came from thinking. From intelligence.

Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world. But progress on other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families. Going from a great idea to a treatment can take decades: it took many years from the first discovery of a strange repeating pattern in DNA to the approval of the first treatment for a disease using CRISPR.

Nature is full of these patterns. But we’ve had too little intelligence to decipher most of them; too few scientists, with too little time. Now we can build that intelligence. Whether it’s protein folding, drug design, cancer genetics, or clinical trial administration, scientists across many areas of biology and medicine are finding Claude can help them do their research in a fraction of the time it would’ve taken just a couple of years ago. I believe sufficiently powerful AI, working in concert with humans, could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade.

I don’t want to get ahead of myself. At this point all we have are early results. Experiments and clinical trials will still take time. And although they involve slow and ponderous processes, I believe those processes can be substantially accelerated by AI. We hope that in the future fewer families miss a cure by just a few years.

Medicine is just a particularly vivid example, but there are many others. Our customers—the world’s most ambitious companies, nonprofits, and individual people—are already applying the intelligence we’ve built to stimulate economic growth; lift people out of poverty; protect democracy and free societies; even make everyday services like the DMV work better. We’re proud to work alongside them. And I’m extremely optimistic about what we can do together in the future.

At the same time, we have always been honest that this technology has very real risks. These range from misuse of the technology by individuals or nation-states, to economic disruption, to losing control of AI systems. We discuss these risks not because we think they are inevitable, but because we think they are avoidable.

Avoiding them depends on the choices made by the people building AI. There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety, versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety. And an obsession with safety and with public benefit has been woven into Anthropic’s DNA from the start. From safeguards against biological and cyber risks, to alignment training and testing, to looking inside our models like an X-ray, Anthropic has pioneered methods for understanding and steering the behavior of AI systems.

There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us. The incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed, even more so than it has already, towards double- and triple-checking that those AI systems are safe and secure.

And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control. We will not bend to either business or political pressure. Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing.

If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top. When the race to the top is working properly, it doesn’t matter which company has the best models—everyone wins because everyone is building safely. The race to the top works best when driven from the front of the pack, and we fully hope and expect to do so, but the goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.

The advent of machine intelligence is one of the seminal moments in human history, and we have a rare opportunity to shape it for the better.

This moment is bigger than any one company, or any one country. It will take all of us, working together, to ensure this technology goes well for us and the many generations to come. Starting today, we hope that you’ll join us on this mission.

text:
Remarks from Anthropic CEO @DarioAmodei on our initial public offering:

My co-founders and I started Anthropic because we believe that the most powerful technology of our time should be built for the benefit of humankind.

Daniela and I lost our father to a disease that, just a few years later, became curable. I started my career in biology, hoping to help future cures come sooner. In the lab, I saw the vast thicket of complexity that scientists face when they’re trying to understand disease and develop new treatments.

So many of the scientific tools that can cut through that thicket—tools for gene editing, gene synthesis, controlling brain cells with light—started as pure ideas. In other words, they came from thinking. From intelligence.

Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world. But progress on other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families. Going from a great idea to a treatment can take decades: it took many years from the first discovery of a strange repeating pattern in DNA to the approval of the first treatment for a disease using CRISPR.

Nature is full of these patterns. But we’ve had too little intelligence to decipher most of them; too few scientists, with too little time. Now we can build that intelligence. Whether it’s protein folding, drug design, cancer genetics, or clinical trial administration, scientists across many areas of biology and medicine are finding Claude can help them do their research in a fraction of the time it would’ve taken just a couple of years ago. I believe sufficiently powerful AI, working in concert with humans, could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade.

I don’t want to get ahead of myself. At this point all we have are early results. Experiments and clinical trials will still take time. And although they involve slow and ponderous processes, I believe those processes can be substantially accelerated by AI. We hope that in the future fewer families miss a cure by just a few years.

Medicine is just a particularly vivid example, but there are many others. Our customers—the world’s most ambitious companies, nonprofits, and individual people—are already applying the intelligence we’ve built to stimulate economic growth; lift people out of poverty; protect democracy and free societies; even make everyday services like the DMV work better. We’re proud to work alongside them. And I’m extremely optimistic about what we can do together in the future.

At the same time, we have always been honest that this technology has very real risks. These range from misuse of the technology by individuals or nation-states, to economic disruption, to losing control of AI systems. We discuss these risks not because we think they are inevitable, but because we think they are avoidable.

Avoiding them depends on the choices made by the people building AI. There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety, versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety. And an obsession with safety and with public benefit has been woven into Anthropic’s DNA from the start. From safeguards against biological and cyber risks, to alignment training and testing, to looking inside our models like an X-ray, Anthropic has pioneered methods for understanding and steering the behavior of AI systems.

There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us. The incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed, even more so than it has already, towards double- and triple-checking that those AI systems are safe and secure.

And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control. We will not bend to either business or political pressure. Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing.

If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top. When the race to the top is working properly, it doesn’t matter which company has the best models—everyone wins because everyone is building safely. The race to the top works best when driven from the front of the pack, and we fully hope and expect to do so, but the goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.

The advent of machine intelligence is one of the seminal moments in human history, and we have a rare opportunity to shape it for the better.

This moment is bigger than any one company, or any one country. It will take all of us, working together, to ensure this technology goes well for us and the many generations to come. Starting today, we hope that you’ll join us on this mission.

text:
A case study of how self-funded devs can make increasingly competitive harnesses, better than many well funded labs or university groups.

As part of growing community of participants in competitions @yukonresearch, we have been increasingly encountering talented folks who aren't working in big ai labs or universities but are extremely good in building harnesses that can make big progress in frontier science problems.

One of our goal with https://t.co/9ZpEsupgtw has been to create an open platform for them to showcase the prowess and competitiveness of their harness in frontier science problems. 

In a bid to make the competition fair and data driven, we took inspiration from @demishassabis's Einstein test. We took our OG competition @yukonresearch, https://t.co/leqhW4oEPP, and any submitted harness is then backtested on how it makes progress in finding resource-efficient quantum circuits for Shor's algorithm (without any internet access). 

After submission of a harness, you can see how effective your harness has been in finding better and better quantum circuit for per unit dollar. One can say this is akin to innovation per unit dollar for that harness.

We encourage more of you to submit your harness to this competition.

text:
分享一些思考，周末写个完整文章：

2021 年的历史背景是这样的： 当时 GPT-3 刚发布不久，硅谷主流 VC 的认知是「一个很酷的文本补全 API」，最火的创业项目是 Jasper、Copy ai 这类任何时代都会出现的营销文案工具，资本的注意力大部分在 Crypto 和 SaaS 上。

Dario Amodei 七人从 OpenAI 出来创立 Anthropic，没有任何公开产品、没有收入、短期不打算商业化的情况下，融完了 B 轮

为什么这么着急 close 了 B 轮，因为他们按照 Scaling Law 做推理，算力、数据都会成为核心，「重剑无锋，大巧不工」，所以需要重仓建设算力和数据，是重资产型创业。

不巧的是，上一时代的共识总会成为下一时代的盲区，VC 们还停留在 08-20 年移动互联网 + 云SaaS时代，所有人都被驯化出一个信仰——「重资产、买硬件是蠢生意，轻资产 SaaS + 流量分发才是王道」。这直接导致 2021 年完全看不懂算力。

21 年前沿的人随着 ‘The Bitter Lesson’ 发现"弱模型时代的大多数「产品」，本质上都是在给智能不足打补丁"，人类手工雕琢的复杂技巧，永远干不过随算力和数据扩展的通用方法。所以做功能是贬值资产，做智能是复利资产。

这里点名评判 CVer，最喜欢做各种小 trick，现在被 LLM 一脚踹成路边不是没道理的

另外是 Anthropic 整套股权架构非常值得学习，哪怕前期引入了巨头的战略投资甚至现在上市后，Founder LLC 的七人组也以近乎平分股权的方式牢牢掌控 50.1% 重大事项投票权，所以可以过滤掉短视资本、不去做乱七八糟的产品

当然也是他们持股、身价如此接近的原因，真的很难见到创业公司 IPO 之后，初创团队每人的持股和身价还几乎持平的事情

不管你再如何讨厌 Dario，不得不承认的是 2021-2026 年一个时代已经结束了，或许这个时代的主要矛盾是：如何把人类历史几千年沉淀的文本知识，压缩成通用推理智能

接下来要考虑新时代了，或许 2026-2035年的主要矛盾是：

当「罐装智能」变得无比廉价便宜、唾手可得之后，为什么现实世界依然没有被彻底改写？到底是什么卡住了它？

在经历了风波以后，sky @SkyEcosystem 开始出招了。

看到出了一个新的治理提案，Core Council 紧急启动了一笔 525 万 USDS 的 $SKY 回购计划。

连续 7 天，每天额外拿出 75 万 USDS 买入 SKY，买回来的代币全部销毁。(sky 跌的有点太惨了)

希望可以缓解市场波动，稳定市场情绪。

前面我提到过，那个被指认与创始人 @RuneKek 关联的钱包，拿 SKY 作为抵押品，借出了约 7700 万 USDS。

现在 SKY 价格持续承压，抵押品也在不断缩水。

所以 Sky 这时候紧急回购 SKY，确实可以给币价提供一定支撑，客观上也能缓解这些大额借款仓位的风险。

但我觉得回购 SKY 并不能直接解决 stUSDS 的流动性问题。

我刚才又看了一眼 Spark 数据：

stUSDS 资金池还有约 1.615 亿美元。

可以立即提取的资金只有约 3.79 万美元。

年化收益率已经从昨天的 19.74%，进一步提升到了 24.74%。

等于说，池子里的钱仍然几乎全部被借出去了。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

现在 Sky 可以迅速启动 525 万美元的紧急回购，7 天内把钱花出去。

但对于 stUSDS 的存款人来说，什么时候能恢复正常提款，目前仍然没有一个明确的解决方案。

同样，回购是不是可以长期稳住 SKY 的价格，还是个未知数。

SKY 继续下跌，大哥约 7700 万 USDS 的债务和抵押品风险还是没解除，这个是最大的雷。

等于说，存款人的流动性还没有解决

所以 Sky 现在应该拿出一套直接针对 stUSDS 的解决方案，不然还是个充满气的大气球
author: blmario669
quoted_text:
最近有人在传，老牌 DeFi 协议 Sky @SkyEcosystem 要暴雷了。

要知道，Sky 的前身就是 MakerDAO，算是 DeFi 领域的老祖宗了。这种级别的协议一旦出了大问题，整个以太坊 DeFi 生态恐怕都要跟着遭殃（参考之前的 LUNA、三箭以及 FTX）大盘还会大跌。

有一种说法，说是创始人 @RuneKek 从 Sky 借出了大量资金，拿去填自己旗下游戏公司 @RawPowerGames 的资金窟窿。

这件事虽然目前没有得到证实，但 Sky 现在就像一个随时可能爆炸的大气球。

我大概捋了一下。

1/ 创始人关联钱包，借走了资金池近一半的钱。

目前，与 Sky 创始人 Rune Christensen 关联的钱包，拿着价值约 1.85 亿美元的 $SKY 作为抵押，从 Sky 借出了约 7700 万 USDS。

相当于这个资金池每借出去 100 美元，其中就有 48 美元借给了这个关联钱包。

而且，这个钱包已经半年左右没有主动还款。

按照目前约 20% 的借款年利率粗略计算，光是这 7700 万美元的债务，每天就会新增约 4.2 万美元的利息，一年下来超过 1500 万美元。

虽然这种抵押借款没有固定的还款日期，但一个大户长期借走资金池近一半的钱，剩下的人就很容易受到影响。

2/ 巧合的是，Rune 旗下游戏公司刚刚破产。

今年 4 月，Rune 关联钱包的债务就已经超过 7200 万美元。

10 月 26 日，这个钱包又从 Sky 借出了 100 万 USDS。

结果仅仅过了 4 天，10 月 30 日，Rune 创办的丹麦游戏公司 Raw Power Games 就宣布破产。

到了 11 月 14 日，Coffee Stain 又宣布，以约 540 万美元收购该公司破产资产中的游戏 IP 及相关资产。

也就是说，这家游戏公司经营到了资金断裂、不得不破产的地步，而 Rune 关联钱包在破产前几天，还从 Sky 借了一笔钱。

于是有人怀疑，Rune 是不是把从 Sky 借出来的钱，拿去填游戏公司的窟窿了。

3/ 现在 stUSDS 资金池几乎被借空了。

截至今天（11 月 19 日），Spark Data Hub 的数据显示：

资金池总规模约 1.6195 亿美元
能够立即提取的钱只剩不到 3 万美元
资金利用率接近 100%
年化收益率已经达到 19.74%

这个 stUSDS 是干什么的？

简单来说，就是有人把 USDS 存进去赚利息，Sky 再把这些钱借给拿 SKY 做抵押的人。

存钱的人赚利息，借钱的人付利息。

原本是一个很常见的 DeFi 借贷生意。

结果现在，1.6 亿多美元的资金池，能够立即拿出来的钱只剩几万美元。

对于存款人来说，账面上虽然有钱，但想把钱提出来，就得等借款人还钱，或者等其他人继续往里面存钱。

而且，这种情况已经持续了一段时间。

Sky 风控团队自己也承认，自 11 月 13 日以来，这个池子的资金利用率就一直高得离谱，24 小时平均利用率持续超过 99.98%。

4/ 清算机制有问题。

正常情况下，我们把币抵押给借贷平台，如果币价跌得太厉害，抵押品不值钱了跌破清算线，平台就会自动卖掉一部分抵押品，把借出去的钱收回来，即清算。

但是 Sky 早在 2025 年，就因为 SKY 市场流动性不足，暂时关闭了相关自动清算功能。

如果几千万美元的 SKY 同时需要卖掉，而市场上又没有足够多的人接盘，价格可能会被砸得很惨。

所以 Sky 当时决定，遇到需要清算的仓位，就通过治理来人工处理。

独立合约审查显示，直到今年 9 月，这个自动清算功能仍然没有恢复。

那么，如果 SKY 价格继续跌，有人抵押的 SKY 已经不够还债了，但这些币又不能及时通过自动清算卖掉，亏损就可能越来越大。

Sky 的规则早就写明，如果最后卖掉抵押品，仍然不够偿还借出去的钱，剩下的窟窿就可能由 stUSDS 存款人分摊。

也就是说，存钱进去赚利息的人，最后还有可能连本金都亏掉一部分。（他这个超过 19% 的利息很高，但是不建议参与）

5/ Sky 已经开始想办法让借款人还钱了。

11 月 18 日，Sky 风控团队连续调整了借款利率。

他们的想法是，既然大家把钱都借走了，那就提高借钱的成本。

原来借 100 美元，一年可能只需要付十几美元的利息。

现在继续借着不还，利息就会越来越贵。

按照 Sky 官方的模拟，如果资金池一直处于借满的状态，借款年利率在几天内就可能升到接近 50%。

这是什么概念？

假设 Rune 关联钱包的债务仍然是 7700 万美元，按照 50% 的年利率计算，每天新增的利息就会超过 10 万美元。

利率这么高，借款人会更有动力尽快还钱。

但是，如果借款人没有足够的现金还款，或者不愿意卖掉手里的 SKY，那就比较麻烦了。（死猪不怕开水烫）

继续借着，债务越来越大。

如果想卖掉大量 SKY 来还钱，又可能把 SKY 的价格砸下去，进一步影响其他人的抵押仓位。

所以 Sky 现在面临的问题很棘手。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

这事如果爆了，后续可能引发可怕的连锁反应。

Sky 是老牌 DeFi 协议，发行的 USDS、sUSDS 已经被很多链上金融平台使用。

目前出问题的是 stUSDS 资金池，USDS 的市场价格还稳定在 1 美元附近。

但是，如果后续 SKY 价格继续暴跌，大额借款还不上，stUSDS 存款人开始出现亏损，事情就可能向外蔓延。

因为有些人还把 stUSDS 抵押到其他 DeFi 平台，借出了更多的钱。

一旦 stUSDS 出现大幅贬值，这些人的抵押品也会跟着缩水，进一步引发其他平台的清算。

如果市场对 Sky 失去信心，连 USDS 都开始被大量抛售，那影响的范围就更大了。

很多 DeFi 协议之间，本来就是你借我的钱、我拿你的币做抵押，资金相互关联。

一家大型协议出了问题，很容易牵连其他协议，传导风险。

2022 年 Luna、Celsius、FTX 接连出事的时候，大家应该都见识过这种连锁反应有多可怕。

现在这个行情，本来市场情绪就很脆弱，流动性也不充裕。

最近接二连三的黑天鹅已经够多了，市场实在经不起再来一次大型 DeFi 协议的系统性危机。

希望 Sky 真的不要暴雷，否则天塌了。

text:
This industry has this interesting trait of respecting whoever ran it up the most rather than whoever ended up keeping the most.

It's the same with people who made their money on the downswings. That arguably takes more skill and keeping money through both kinds of market is the real skill.

A seasoned trader is mostly defined by things you never see. They have the discipline to flip their bias quickly when new information comes in, rather than defending a position because they were loud about it. They also know when they have no edge and they're willing to sit out for weeks while everyone else forces trades.

Running it up takes one good market but keeping it takes all of the above. The number that matters is what you still have at the end of the run and not what you peaked at.
