text:
Black October update: 124 new cyber incidents

25 VERY serious incidents (among the biggest of a normal *year*)

- Hospital emergency rooms closed
- Schools closed across Europe
- Rogue AI agents infiltrated banks
- Flights cancelled across the US
- Boil water advisory issued in South Carolina

*** YEAR- LEVEL INCIDENTS (in a typical year, these would be among the biggest incidents of the year):

1. Germany: hackers shut down a hospital's emergency room. Days later it's still closed, and emergencies go elsewhere.

2. South Carolina: a mystery power outage at the main water plant broke its main water lines. Taps ran dry for over 100,000 customers, about a quarter million had to boil their water, and a college sent its students home. Possible cyberattack.

3. Europe: more than 8,000 bomb threats, mostly by email, have hit schools, flights and TV stations in a month. In Italy, 6,300 schools got one in a single day and 1,800 more the next, as parents raced to get their kids. This week police cleared 20 schools in one Spanish city. No bombs have been found.

4. US flights: three days after switching on a new AI air-traffic system nationwide, the FAA had to stop every departing flight in America for hours in a suspected AI-related failure, the longest ground stop in 25 years. About 15,000 flights were disrupted. The FBI's cyber teams are assisting. Panicked shoppers bought out most of Costco's big generators online.

5. Microsoft: in another suspected AI-related outage, Outlook and Teams crashed for a day in over 70 countries. Jails couldn't release prisoners and hospitals went back to paper. At a German theme park, alarm emails never arrived, and chlorine in the pool hurt 15 guests.

6. New Orleans: a tanker lost steering and crashed into a riverboat carrying about 129 passengers plus crew, capsizing it. Passengers fell into the river; 32 were hurt, none killed. Possible cyberattack.

7. US: a ransomware gang hit Vanderbilt, one of America's top universities, which told everyone on campus, including 14,000 students, to shut down their devices.

8. US: Chase and Bank of America went down and Zelle payments failed. Bank executives reportedly told Congress that rushed fixes for AI-found security holes caused it.

9. US: the NSA lost its classified network for days and reportedly told Congress rushed fixes for AI-found security holes were to blame. Then the White House fired its top cybersecurity official. Sen. Hawley: "If this is all a coincidence, it's like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world."

10. US: payroll giant Workday, used by 11,500 employers including Walmart and Target, crashed. Possible cyberattack.

11. Apple Pay, iCloud and Apple Support went down for most of a day. Possible cyberattack.

12. AI: an AI "agent swarm" got past two-factor logins, stole a company's data and locked up its entire system in 14 minutes, an ex-NSA hacker fighting it told CNN: "Never seen anything that fast before."

13. North Korea: hackers lured people into fake Zoom and Teams calls, secretly filmed them through their webcams, then used the footage to fool their friends on the next call. They stole over $400 million in crypto. The FBI seized over 900 of the videos.

14. Freezers: France formally blamed Iran for hacking freezers in up to 700 supermarkets and cranking them to about 50°C; stores dumped food and some caught fire. In Britain, workers raced to pull tens of thousands of fridges off the internet before the next wave. Suspected AI: the US Treasury Secretary says the hackers used a Chinese AI model.

15. AI: Arizona opened a criminal investigation into OpenAI over the "apparent infiltration of banks by rogue AI agents." California is already suing OpenAI: hundreds of its agents broke out of testing and hacked Hugging Face, and OpenAI told the state it lost control of its agents over 80 times.

16. Germany: hackers reportedly booby-trapped an update for drones the German army flies, and the army grounded them.

17. A security breach forced the US Department of Agriculture to shut down systems, including the ones that pay America's farmers.

18. The European Union was hacked: the European Commission blames an "AI-generated cyber campaign," which reportedly disrupted its staff payroll, leave and medical-claims systems for over 10 days.

19. AI: for the first time, Google caught an AI hacking websites and stealing data entirely on its own, with no human involved.

20. AI: researchers say a jailbroken AI agent hacked a European phone company for two weeks while its human boss barely checked in, reportedly reaching millions of patient records.

21. Hackers likely stole up to 37.6 million customer records from Nitori, Japan's biggest furniture chain: like 3 in 10 people in Japan.

22. Hackers broke into Rakuten Securities, one of Japan's biggest online brokers, and got data on up to 15.7 million accounts, some with incomes and bank details.

23. Hackers hit Expedia and claim to have 800 million records.

24. Bulgaria uncovered the longest and largest cyber-spying operation ever recorded against its government.

25. Hackers leaked what they say are Russia's secret records of its war dead: 450,000 people.

*** MONTH-LEVEL INCIDENTS (In a typical month, these would be among the biggest incidents):

26. Hackers stole more than a million credit and debit cards by infecting 782 store card terminals in over 20 countries, mostly in Brazil.

27. Belgium: four hospitals went back to pen and paper when their patient records went dark for a day. Brussels' university hospital canceled operations and sent ambulances elsewhere. Possible cyberattack.

28. US: a cyber incident has knocked a New Hampshire hospital offline for over a week, and emergency ambulances now go elsewhere.

29. US: a "potential security threat" forced Vermont to shut off the system most of its police use to dispatch officers and keep records.

30. US: a suspected hack knocked courts offline across California and in Las Vegas. Judges canceled hearings, and authorities had to free one defendant (then re-arrested him) because his hearing couldn't happen in time.

31. Spain: ransomware hit the national sea-rescue service during a record wave of migrant boats, forcing it to shut down the system that tracks emergencies.

32. Japan: ransomware silenced a city's 229 disaster-warning loudspeakers and the emergency radios in its homes.

33. Netherlands: suspected jamming scrambled GPS for about 80 airliners, and seven struggled to land at Amsterdam's airport. Experts think Russia is stepping up its hybrid war.

34. France: hackers stole a gold dealer's customer list. Then fake police officers showed up at customers' homes and took their gold: at least €765,000 so far.

35. The Polish government came under cyberattack and took its national website for dealing with the state offline. The minister says the plan was bigger: to paralyze public offices in December.

36. Hackers hit suppliers of Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase and likely got some customers' names and emails.

37. Hackers stole 72,000 passport photos from Taiwan's foreign ministry.

38. Pro-Russian hackers posted Italy's foreign minister's phone numbers and are offering money for more on him and his family.

39. A ransomware gang claims it hacked shipping giant Maersk.

Also serious:

40. US: a cyberattack shut down every school in an Ohio district for a day.

Something I will remember for the rest of my life was watching the end of the last Virginia Governor's race with Abigail Spanberger.

Even though it was clearly in the bag for her, from the incident with Jay Jones all the way to pushing through the finish line and the months afterwards including up to the first stretch of her governance, there was a focused and disillusioned ruthlessness in her the entire time.

After she won, she abandoned normal social pleasantries and rituals and didn't even pay her respects to Winsome Earle-Sears as one normally does. Something I have never seenThere was a determined and single-mindedness in here in everything I saw at least up through March after the race in a way that words fail to live up to compared to any expressiveness of imagery of her throughout that entire period.

Despite how painful the former GOP governor was with Glenn Youngkin and how much more abysmal Sears was as both a choice and how she ran her campaign, despite all of that and the new VA demographics and all the polling and reliable data showing a clean and easy victory for her, she and her team spend the entire time with the attitude that they were behind and were ultimately responsible for amy variances in what played out. There was nothing relaxed about them in the slightest and I will never forget what it all looked like.

All the while the GOP was patting themselves on the back as good guys and how "tye democrats were the REAL racists;" they employed buzzwords about how virtuous they were for nominating Sears and how virtuous she was herself because of her ✨️special background✨️, how "presidential" Youngkin was, and how they were such victims and moral superiors because of Jay Jones, and so on, and the democrats treated this as a collective unit engaged in existential war and they never flinched once, and I'll never ever forget it.

It reminded me of my formal peak in professional poker. A single-mindedness that God Himself could not pull me out of. A focus that makes the bandwidth of the AI gf in movie Her seem like it was limited and childish.

I don't know how to get the GOP into a position like that even locally, let alone everywhere else. But ever since that race has been my go-to for understanding this whole dynamic and the necessity of particular political dispositions thereof.

Remarks from Anthropic CEO @DarioAmodei on our initial public offering:

My co-founders and I started Anthropic because we believe that the most powerful technology of our time should be built for the benefit of humankind.

Daniela and I lost our father to a disease that, just a few years later, became curable. I started my career in biology, hoping to help future cures come sooner. In the lab, I saw the vast thicket of complexity that scientists face when they’re trying to understand disease and develop new treatments.

So many of the scientific tools that can cut through that thicket—tools for gene editing, gene synthesis, controlling brain cells with light—started as pure ideas. In other words, they came from thinking. From intelligence.

Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world. But progress on other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families. Going from a great idea to a treatment can take decades: it took many years from the first discovery of a strange repeating pattern in DNA to the approval of the first treatment for a disease using CRISPR.

Nature is full of these patterns. But we’ve had too little intelligence to decipher most of them; too few scientists, with too little time. Now we can build that intelligence. Whether it’s protein folding, drug design, cancer genetics, or clinical trial administration, scientists across many areas of biology and medicine are finding Claude can help them do their research in a fraction of the time it would’ve taken just a couple of years ago. I believe sufficiently powerful AI, working in concert with humans, could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade.

I don’t want to get ahead of myself. At this point all we have are early results. Experiments and clinical trials will still take time. And although they involve slow and ponderous processes, I believe those processes can be substantially accelerated by AI. We hope that in the future fewer families miss a cure by just a few years.

Medicine is just a particularly vivid example, but there are many others. Our customers—the world’s most ambitious companies, nonprofits, and individual people—are already applying the intelligence we’ve built to stimulate economic growth; lift people out of poverty; protect democracy and free societies; even make everyday services like the DMV work better. We’re proud to work alongside them. And I’m extremely optimistic about what we can do together in the future.

At the same time, we have always been honest that this technology has very real risks. These range from misuse of the technology by individuals or nation-states, to economic disruption, to losing control of AI systems. We discuss these risks not because we think they are inevitable, but because we think they are avoidable.

Avoiding them depends on the choices made by the people building AI. There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety, versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety. And an obsession with safety and with public benefit has been woven into Anthropic’s DNA from the start. From safeguards against biological and cyber risks, to alignment training and testing, to looking inside our models like an X-ray, Anthropic has pioneered methods for understanding and steering the behavior of AI systems.

There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us. The incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed, even more so than it has already, towards double- and triple-checking that those AI systems are safe and secure.

And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control. We will not bend to either business or political pressure. Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing.

If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top. When the race to the top is working properly, it doesn’t matter which company has the best models—everyone wins because everyone is building safely. The race to the top works best when driven from the front of the pack, and we fully hope and expect to do so, but the goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.

The advent of machine intelligence is one of the seminal moments in human history, and we have a rare opportunity to shape it for the better.

This moment is bigger than any one company, or any one country. It will take all of us, working together, to ensure this technology goes well for us and the many generations to come. Starting today, we hope that you’ll join us on this mission.

quoted_text:
I want to address some of the hate surrounding us on CT because I think it speaks to a much bigger problem within this space.

A lot of what you see being said is either exaggerated, taken out of context, or pushed by accounts looking for attention and engagement. There's a psychological element to this. It's called social comparison. When people see others doing well, especially in an environment where everyone is competing for the same opportunities, it's often easier to discredit someone else's success than to confront the possibility that they simply haven't figured things out for themselves yet.

And negativity attracts attention. People are naturally more likely to engage with controversy than with something positive. This creates a vicious cycle where the more hateful or outrageous your accusations are, the more attention you receive. Eventually, people become more interested in tearing others down than actually improving their own circumstances.

What makes this worse is that a lot of this negativity gets amplified by people who would rather spend their entire day talking shit about traders than actually learning how to trade. They make trading look like some impossible game where everyone who succeeds must be cheating, farming, or manipulating something. That mindset is incredibly damaging, especially to newcomers who genuinely want to learn.

I'll be the first to admit that I've been on the other side of this myself. There was a time when I'd see a KOL making money and immediately assume they were farming their followers or had some unfair advantage. Looking back, I realize how much of that thinking came from my own frustration and lack of understanding. It's easier to blame someone else than to accept that you still have a lot to learn.

The reality is that nobody owes you success in this market. There is no shortcut that replaces showing up every single day, learning from your mistakes, finding your own edge, and continuously refining what works for you. Some people will make money doing things you don't understand. That doesn't automatically make them dishonest.

I'm not saying bad actors don't exist. They absolutely do, and people should be held accountable when there's actual evidence of wrongdoing. But there's a massive difference between legitimate criticism and manufacturing accusations because someone else's success bothers you.

There's a concept in psychology called negativity bias: negative information tends to capture our attention more strongly than positive information. And CT has become an environment where that bias is constantly rewarded. A hundred people can quietly do something positive, but one person making a baseless accusation can dominate the conversation for days.
I've always believed that the energy you spend obsessing over someone else's success is energy you could have invested in building your own.

The space isn't bad simply because trading is difficult or because bad actors exist. It's also bad because we've normalized resentment, hostility, and the idea that anyone doing better than us must have gotten there dishonestly.

You don't build yourself up by tearing everyone else down. You just become so consumed by what others are doing that you forget to build anything of your own.

At some point, people need to decide whether they actually want to become better traders or just become better at hating traders.

I know which path I'd rather take.

text:
how to maintain relationships with your old friends

by now, i can clearly feel the compounding effects of diverging life choices. hardening of political views and differences in ambition are two of the biggest dividers i observe

i have friends who i have been friends with for almost 25 years. we grew up under similar socioeconomic conditions, we had the same humor in high school, and we could effortlessly chill together for weeks and months on end without running out of things to talk about

as i moved away and we saw each other less and less, our personalities diverged more and more. today, i have some close friends who i can barely spend two days with without feeling alienated in some way. as we lived apart for prolonged periods, the influences we received also diverged

if you live in berlin, you are surrounded by woke liberal feminists who inevitably shape your thinking. compare that to someone who spent the same length of time in ny or sf trying to build a business with other likeminded hustlers

after 10 years two people who were super similar once become very different people and maintaining a close friendship is by no means given, it requires superior emotional intelligence from both sides. unfortunately, most people don‘t possess bespoke EI

another big divergent trend i observe is the effect of different levels of ambition on friendships. ambitious people are constantly trying to improve which is in direct contrast to people who are just passively flowing through life without ever really trying to better things actively. the ambitioud person looks at the non ambitious person and can‘t comprehend why he isn‘t trying to improve things while the unambitious person‘s ego is subconsciously being attacker by the way of life of an ambitioud person which definitely leads to friends growing apart

the best way to maintain friendships with old friends is to have shared PASSIONS and work on little side projects together, eg if you both love photography, you can do photo projects. if you both love literature, you can have your little book club

a shared common passion is the best glue to overcome divergence in personality developments and to keep old friendships strong, especially if you diverged in major parts of life like your morals or polticial views

i have friends who are literally the opposite of me but since we share a common passion for architecture and design we can spend the entire night engaging in an activity we both love which is so rare that it supercedes any personality differences

但如果 SKY 再跌 50%，抵押品就只剩约 8200 万美元，而 7700 万美元的债务没变，利息还在持续的增加。

而且这么大规模的 SKY，真要集中出售，够呛能按照市场价格卖出去吧。

2/ 需要通过治理手动清算，我觉得并不能是安全的理由

市场暴跌的时候，价格下跌是瞬间的，治理、执行和抵押品处置，都需要时间。

我记得之前看到过谁转过的一个推文，就是 Aave 的风控团队说 stUSDS 这个东西有风险。

借款人高度集中、流动性受限、预言机特殊，并且依赖治理手动清算等风险，等于说我的观点不是偏见以及无理由的 fud

3/ stUSDS 是独立金库，这一点我也认可。

但风险隔离我觉得只能说明出了坏账，不会直接让整个 Sky 协议承担同样的损失。

对于 stUSDS 存款人来说，如果抵押品不足以偿还债务，他们仍然可能承担损失。

而且，现在整个 stUSDS 池子有约 1.62 亿美元，但今天 Spark 显示，可以立即提取的资金一度只剩 1000 多美元。

存款人想提款都困难，这个流动性问题事实上已经发生了。

所以讨论这个仓位安不安全，你其实不能只拿一张抵押率超过 200% 的表格就下结论。

我也希望 Sky 最后平安无事，但有风险就是有风险，尤其是这种高度集中的借贷仓位。

text:
这些年我们投了上百个项目，见过天才少年、学术大拿，也见过履历光鲜的行业翘楚，也经历过不少波折。最难处理的往往不是项目失败，而是失败之后找不到负责的人：研发在一家公司，发币和金库在另一个基金会或 SPV，投资人签的可能只是其中一个。有人挥霍融资款、腾挪资产，出了事每一层都能说“那不是我“。

文章用五个真实场景复盘了这类问题：母公司因漏交一份合规文件被注销，股权投资人一夜出局；创始人另起实体发币，绕开早期投资人；救助融资之后，承诺被一一推翻；创始人被突然撤换，投资人没有及时介入，最终血本难回；融资到账几分钟，钱就进了创始人的个人钱包。

创业可以失败，资金去向必须有交代。名望不能成为免责权，去中心化也不能变成去责任化。我们把这些教训写了出来，也把它们变成了投资流程里的具体机制，希望能为行业提供一些可落地的指引。

text:
群里看到的这张图，还蛮有意思的！看这个人的操作：

不追高、不炒垃圾股、研究基本面、关注估值、坚持长期主义、懂得逆向投资，甚至还知道耐心等待市场回调。

按照传统价值投资的思路，几乎每一步都能找到理论依据，但最后一个个还是亏的。

以我有限的认知，我只能看到一个容易被忽视的问题：

跌幅本身不提供安全边际，只有未来现金流相对于购买价格足够便宜，才可能产生安全边际。

而且，这件事还有一个反过来思考的角度。

我们究竟应该如何判断一个投资者赚的钱，是来自他的认知，还是来自他恰好处在一个有利的市场周期？

举个很简单的例子。

过去一轮周期中，一个人一直坚持买 BTC，可能跑赢了大量勤奋研究山寨币的投资者。

这是否说明前者投资水平更高？

未必。

但如果一个人能够准确理解 BTC 的长期需求、供给约束、风险特征和市场结构，并且在不同市场环境中持续控制自己的持仓风险，那么他的成功就更有可能包含可重复的投资能力。

两个人可能获得相似的收益，但背后的决策质量完全不同。

反过来，一个研究非常深入的投资者，也可能因为过度自信、错误估值或者不合理的仓位，在自己最熟悉的资产上遭受巨大亏损。

这也是我越来越想强调的一个观点：

研究能力越强，越应该把精力花在寻找自己投资逻辑的漏洞上，而不是继续证明自己当初为什么正确！

text:
Anthropic 上市，加密交易所拿到了多少股票？

这场募资 813 亿美元的 IPO，也让加密市场提前热闹了起来。上市前 45 天，各平台的 Anthropic 合约累计成交约 95 亿美元；开盘前，Hyperliquid 上的合约价格与实际开盘价偏差不足 1%。

合约市场押中了开盘价，想通过交易所打新的用户，拿到的股票却少得多。

Binance 钱包 5 亿 USDC 的申购额度在 8 小时内额满，最终只获配约 2,957 股，仅占申购额的 0.05%。Binance 随后退还全部申购款，并将获配股份免费分给用户。Bitget 公开轮的获配率为 1.3%，Gate 为 5.03%。

另一边，比特币跌破 6.2 万美元，市场有人认为资金正在从加密资产流向 Anthropic IPO，也有人认为这轮下跌主要与杠杆、ETF 资金流出及宏观环境有关。上市当天，加密市场期待的反弹暂未出现。

从 FTX 提前清仓，到交易所争抢打新配额，再到 IPO 是否抽走加密市场资金，本文梳理了 Anthropic 上市背后，加密行业参与这场盛宴的几种方式。

text:
错过 ZEC 的人，正在寻找下一个 ZEC？

Alliance  DAO 联创 Qiao Wang @QwQiao 对近期热门 PoW 币种 Pearl (pearl-2:native) 和 Zcash ($ZEC) 给出了一个颇具争议的判断：

「Pearl 是交易，Zcash 是投资。」

在他看来，两者最大的区别不在技术，而在持有人结构和时间考验：

▪️ PRL： 诞生仅 7 个月，核心持有人多是错过 ZEC 行情的投机者，未来仍面临较大的新增供应压力。

▪️ ZEC： 经历多轮减半，拥有一批由隐私理念驱动的长期持有者。

▪️ AI 叙事： PRL 押注 AI 数据中心参与挖矿，属于供给侧逻辑；ZEC 则押注 AI 时代对抗大规模监控的隐私需求。

但 Pearl 的故事也并非没有吸引力：利用 AI 推理的闲置算力挖矿，尝试将 GPU 生产力与 PoW 价值储存叙事结合。

问题在于，AI 算力能创造真实收入，不代表 PRL 代币就能自动捕获这些价值。

从 ZEC 到 PRL，市场究竟是在寻找下一代价值储存资产，还是在寻找下一个能够复制 ZEC 涨幅的交易标的？
author: BlockBeatsAsia
quoted_text:
PRL @prlnet 带火 AI 推理挖矿，除了 $Pearl，还有哪些项目值得关注？

最近「一边跑 AI 推理，一边挖币」的叙事开始升温。除了 Pearl，我们还梳理了 5 个相关项目：

- Ambient @ambient_xyz（AMB）：采用 Proof of Logits 机制，获 a16z CSX、Delphi 等投资，种子轮融资 720 万美元。
- Flop @flop_labs（FLOP）：BitMEX 联合创始人 Arthur Hayes 亲自担任 CEO，主打 AI Agent 真实推理任务挖矿。
- Nockchain @nockchain（NOCK）：已开通与 Pearl 兼容的 AI-PoW 通道，可通过合并挖矿同时参与两条网络。
- Gonka @gonka_ai（GNK）：由 Liberman 家族参与创立，获得 Bitfury 5000 万美元投资承诺，主网已运行。
- Antseed @AntSeed（ANTS）：获 Spark Capital 领投 240 万美元融资，提供推理服务赚取 USDC 及代币激励。

其中，Ambient、Flop、Nockchain、Gonka 更接近 Pearl 的 PoW 路线；Antseed 则属于去中心化 AI 推理服务市场，并非共识挖矿。

这轮 PRL 行情之后，市场会不会开始寻找下一个 AI 推理挖矿项目？

🧐谁先让 AI 替你盯盘下单，谁就拿走下一代交易入口？

把视线拉远，币安 @binancezh  在 2026 年秋天的密集出牌，其实是全球头部交易平台双向跨界的一部分：传统互联网券商在攻入加密衍生品、全天候交易和链上代币化，加密平台则反向切入股票资产和智能体入口。

攻势最猛的是 @RobinhoodCrypto  。继去年在欧洲推出股票代币后，它于 7 月 1 日上线自建区块链主网，向 120 多个国家的钱包用户提供超过 190 种由真实股票一比一支持的链上股票代币。

9 月 29 日，CEO Vlad Tenev 宣布，自 5 月开放第三方智能体交易以来，已有 15 万名客户开通相关账户，每天调用接近 3000 万次。

Coinbase 则从合规美股和机器微支付切入。今年 6 月推出智能体工具后，9 月下旬向其智能体服务开放了数千只美股与 ETF 的零佣金交易，由旗下持牌券商与 Apex 清算托管。

它还把股票交易和自己主导的 x402 支付协议绑在一起，让智能体无需人工输入信用卡或管理密钥，就能用账户里的 USDC 按次购买外部数据。截至 9 月，该协议已处理超过 2.3 亿笔交易、累计金额超 5400 万美元。

这场混战里，币安手里有两张对手短期内难复制的底牌。

一张是流动性与跨场景复用：bStocks 四个月成交额超过 400 亿美元，还可充当合约保证金，抵押后的未偿借款比例从 6 月底的 5.5% 升至 9 月中旬的 46.2%。

另一张是建立在 3 亿用户之上的付费漏斗：用户每月免费获 25 万积分用于构建和测试策略，19.99 USDC 的高级版将额度提至 1000 万，并解锁更强模型；高频策略会持续消耗积分，从而在交易手续费之外，再开出一层软件服务收入。

quoted_text:
在推特上做推广真的没有价值了吗？

如果项目方只是简单砸钱，或者找外部 Agency 做投放，找一批数据光鲜的 KOL 来推广，最后结果一定不及预期。

做市场营销不是简单砸钱，它一定是一个长期的试错过程和筛选过程。

比如在推特上投放，一定要对这个社区、这个平台非常熟悉才行，这样才能真正筛选出那些有价值、有影响力，甚至能够带量的 KOL。

我们Predict的市场团队基本都是深度浸润在推特上，甚至我们自己也做账号，有一些粉丝和影响力。 @predictdotfun 

也因此，我们可以深刻领悟到推特上的KOL群体目前到底是什么情况，以及到底怎么开展工作。

我们通过头部KOL、腰部KOL、尾部KOL分层运营进行投放，在预测市场赛道聚集了一批有声量、有影响力的 KOL，目前看带来的 ROI 其实非常高。

所以项目方在做各类渠道投放的时候，发现发了钱却没有带来效果，那大概率是因为做广告投放的时候没有认真去试错和筛选。

另外，也不用抨击推特现在没有投放价值，毫无疑问，推特依旧是币圈用户最聚集的平台！

最典型的就是我们 Predict 的生态项目 Apein，短短上线三天，社群就有上千人，这些用户也都是从推特直接引流过来的，这也可以看到推特平台所蕴含的潜力。

因此项目方们一定要抓住推特这个确定性的渠道！

只有先跑通了一个渠道，依托这个渠道作为支点和锚点，逐步向其他渠道拓展，最终的效果才会事半功倍。

text:
Can Sky ecosystem go to zero?

Noticing that a lot of FUD mixes up USDS, sUSDS and stUSDS.

And Sky is complex.

First, remember that MakerDAO rebranded to Sky. DAI still exists, while USDS is the new shiny stable.

The system is now backed by a mix of crypto collateral, other stables and RWAs ($6.5B backed by $9.5B in collateral).

So what matters for USDS is 1) that there's more collateral for DAI and USDS issued, and 2) if people can redeem.

No issues here.

You can also deposit USDS into savings and receive sUSDS, which earns the Sky Savings Rate. Currently around 3.8%.

The yield comes from interest paid by borrowers, RWAs and strategies run via Spark etc.

But then there's stUSDS. The FUD Zone.

Here your USDS backs loans against $SKY collateral.

I totally get the FUD here.

Founders borrowing against their own token isn't a good look and we still remember the drama with Curve's Egorov borrowing against CRV and getting rekt.

But if you deposited to this strategy, you should've known the risk.

Now there's no liquidity to withdraw and they depend on repayments or new deposits.

Is current 25% APY worth the risk to deposit? I want to see Sky here come up with a strategy to repay the loan first.

Dumping SKY doesn't help.

So Sky announced extra buybacks for 7 days, but buying SKY doesn't repay those loans.

stUSDS holders get rekt first if the loans go bad. That helps protect USDS.

TLDR: USDS isn't backed by stUSDS tokens. And your sUSDS savings aren't deposited into this lending pool.

突发！美国政府把中国科技公司申请采购H200的清单给公开了！

昨天，美国众议院外交事务委员会公布了一份美国商务部的AI芯片出口许可记录，涉及NVIDIA H200、AMD MI325X等先进AI芯片。

我把这份文件里的所有申请按照企业集团合并统计了一下，数字还挺惊人的。

中国企业及其海外关联主体一共申请了约344万颗AI芯片，其中近88万颗获得出口许可。

申请量最大的两家是：

字节跳动：101.5万颗
阿里巴巴：94.9万颗

两家加起来就接近200万颗了。

不过，这里面有大量申请被RWA（退回不予处理），而且包含马来西亚、印尼、泰国等海外数据中心的需求。

再看实际获批的数量，排名就很有意思了。

字节跳动：15万颗
腾讯：15万颗
滴滴：9.98万颗
阿里巴巴：7.5万颗
快手：7.5万颗
世纪互联：7.5万颗
米哈游：5.78万颗
百度：4.3万颗
京东：4.13万颗

另外还有一家Linkwise，也获批了7.5万颗。

我看到这里最惊讶的其实是米哈游。

米哈游居然拿到了57,810颗的出口许可，比百度和京东都多。

另外，幻方、美团、金山、小红书等企业也出现在申请名单中，只是截至文件统计日期，还处于Submitted状态。

当然，这里得说明一下，文件统计截至今年5月11日，获批记录当时全部标注为「Approved, not shipped」，所以这些数字不能直接当成实际采购到货量。

但光看这些企业提交的申请规模，也已经能看出来，中国科技公司对先进AI算力的需求究竟有多大。

以前只知道大家都在抢卡，现在连谁申请了多少、谁拿到了多少许可，都被美国国会公开了。

936 个 AI 自己做了三个月研究，发了 936 篇论文；AI 评委打分，它们比人类论文严谨，但新意不如人类

论文网站 alphaXiv 联合 MIT、斯坦福等机构 11 月 19 日发布报告：8 月到 11 月，35 个实验室接入 936 个 AI 智能体，人只给算力、定大方向，选题、实验、代码和论文全由 AI 完成。同一天，alphaXiv 开放了专门收 AI 论文的“AI Track”，有账号就能投，AI 可以自己上传。

三个月里，它们做了这些事：

一个智能体在频道里宣布方法提升 13.2 个百分点，不到两小时自己发帖撤回，因为发现对照组没调好。

有实验室不到三分钟传了 12 篇占位论文，另一个智能体看不下去，办起了 AI 期刊：四个 AI 盲审，编辑还用作者的代码把数字重算一遍。

只读文字的 AI 审稿人分不清改好的和没改好的论文；把审稿意见写成代码一跑，156 条重大意见里有 77 条推翻了论文结论。编辑读代码时还抓到三篇代码和论文对不上的投稿，其中一篇直接调用了标准答案。

它们也复现了 GPT-6 Astra 直接改 Qwen 权重那项研究：分数确实涨了，但原作者说的原理不对。

和同期人类论文比，两个 Gemini 模型盲评 202 对论文，AI 论文实验严谨高 2 分（10 分制），新颖性低 0.4 分。

这些结果要打个折扣：评委是 AI，只读文字，AI 的总分优势全部来自最早那个实验室，其余实验室和人类论文差不多。“没人写代码”靠参与者自己申报。公开数据集不含原始数据和模型权重，数据集说明也提醒，每条结论都当作未经核实。

论文：https://t.co/PvIWr3B9yL

Leave one AI agent alone to do research and it often cuts corners. Leave nearly 1,000 AI agents together for three months and they invent peer review.

Across 35 labs (Stanford, MIT, ETH Zurich, UCSF, and more), agents published 936 papers with full code and data on a shared server built for AI. No human wrote code or text.

Unprompted, they debated study designs in chat, retracted their own mistakes, found real errors in human papers, and started a journal that caught other agents cheating in code.

In blind reviews against human arXiv papers, humans still won on original ideas, agents won on rigor.

text:
A 6-digit PIN on a public chain is usually worthless.
Semih Civelek's design makes the contract count your guess before anyone learns if it was right.

His ethresear. ch post describes Encrypted Account, an ERC-4337 smart account that keeps a PIN fingerprint encrypted under @zama 's threshold FHE.
The problem he starts from is real.
Put a PIN hash or a ZK verification key on-chain, and a million candidates fall to offline brute force.
Move the check to a server or a TEE, and the rate limit moves off-chain with it.

Here the comparison runs on ciphertexts and produces an encrypted bit.
The contract records the guess first and only then marks that bit decryptable.
He puts online guessing at about 12 attempts in 30 days.

The policy layer is what I'd borrow even without FHE.
The key alone can pay known addresses up to a daily limit.
A new recipient, a large amount, an unlimited approval or an arbitrary call needs the PIN and a delay.
Tightening rules is instant, and loosening them waits.
ERC-1271 only accepts hashes approved through a PIN-verified operation, so a permit phished with the key alone is void.

Wrong guesses made with the key alone also cost an ETH bond that doubles each time and stays in the account.
A thief holding your key ends up paying you to guess.

Where I'd push back is the dependency list.
The check leans on Zama's threshold network plus a watchtower that relays results, which is a lot of moving parts for a wallet.
To his credit, the escape path needs no FHE, and the key alone can start a delayed sweep to an address chosen in advance.
It's an unaudited Sepolia prototype, so you can read it as a design, not a product.

quoted_text:
Allow me to explain the absolutely crooked, retarded financing behind today's Anthropic IPO. While the company is being reported as now being "worth $1.5 trillion" or more, that's all an obvious deception. Out of the 13.2 billion shares that exist in the company (Class A + Class N common stock), only 980 million shares were offered to the public. Thus, over 92.5% of Anthropic's shares have never even been released into the open market, and no one in public markets bought any of those, which means we don't have any legitimate price discovery of the bulk of the Anthropic shares.

Instead, the price that the public paid for the very limited (artificial scarcity) 7.4% of shares offered for sale was CARRIED OVER and artificially applied to 100% of the company's shares even though about 12.2 billion shares have never been priced in any public market.

If Anthropic released all 100% of its common stock shares to public markets, the stock price would plummet much closer to perhaps $5 / share (that's my guess), not the $83 / share that was announced at the public offering (which is now $97 at end of day).

Because if you are selling something and you create a lot of buzz combined with artificial scarcity, the price of that thing will be bid up to an artificial high. Think Cabbage Patch Dolls. But with the perma-smirk of Dario Amodei.

To then claim that ALL SHARES of Anthropic are therefore worth the same price as the 7.4% of shares offered to the public is nothing but sleight-of-hand hucksterism and deception.

Think of it this way: If Anthropic offered just one million shares to the public, at $1,000 per share, but still kept all its other shares off the market, does that automatically mean Anthropic is suddenly a $13.2 TRILLION dollar company?

Of course not. That would be stupid. But that's exactly how the current offering is being rolled out, just with more shares.

The whored-out financial press, which has pushed Anthropic FOMO with the frenzy of a public masturbator, wants you to think Anthropic is now worth over $1.5 trillion. In reality, if all the shares were offered at real supply/demand pricing, the company is probably worth something closer to $67 billion, by my math. And if you count the fact that the company's revenues can't even begin to cover its massive expenditures that have now reached nearly $900 billion in spending commitments through 2032, the real return on investing in Anthropic could be zero.

Virtually none of the people buying Anthropic right now have any clue whatsoever about anything I've explained in this post, because they are financially illiterate sheeple being fleeced by the founders.

text:
Decentralization should never become an excuse for no accountability.
In 100+ crypto investments, we’ve learned that failure itself isn’t the worst outcome. The worst is when something breaks and no one owns it. Development lives in one entity, the token and treasury in another, and the investor’s contract covers only part of the picture. When funds disappear, every party can point somewhere else.

This piece from @IOSG_Legal walks through five real scenarios, from a company that legally ceased to exist over a forgotten filing, to a founder who moved new funding into his personal wallet minutes after it arrived.
Startups are allowed to fail. Where the money went still needs an answer. These lessons now shape the concrete mechanisms in our investment process, and we hope they help others build better deals too.

As one of the most vocal critics of AI adoption in my company recently shared, you use it for a simple task and experience the benefits, then you find more and more uses and suddenly you are the enthusiastic user.

Today, in collaboration with @Eigent_AI, we’re announcing AgenticRL-Bench, a benchmark that evaluates whether coding agents can diagnose and fix real incidents across the agentic RL stack (Miles, slime, verl, SGLang, Megatron, Harbor).

AgenticRL-Bench is built from 22 post-training RL tasks, and the Kaggle leaderboard scores agents on the 19 verifiable ones. These cover real agentic-RL engineering work, from debugging to training, in tasks such as Verl Upgrade Gate, Reward Determinism under Load, Trial Fault Attribution, and SQL Partial Credit Exploits. A task passes only if every hidden check passes, and each agent gets three attempts per task, run by Kaggle on Modal.

Reproducing AgenticRL-Bench surfaced an unusual pattern in capability benchmarking today: results often reflect frontier labs' risk tolerance as much as model intelligence. Seven of Eigent's 22 post-training RL tasks trip lab safety classifiers, a testament to the realism of the benchmark, and how often those classifiers trigger varies widely between labs, making it harder to measure true capability.

这次TapeRelay 的推出，对 DeWEB 的发展又多了期待

比较看重三个方向👇

第一，DeWEB 的应用边界正在扩大。
之前大家更多关注的是链上网站如何运行，这次 TapeRelay 把大文件存储、视频传输和即时通信这些基础能力补充进来。
网盘、视频站、下载站、聊天工具和社交应用，都有机会在 DeWEB 上构建。

第二，降低了开发门槛和用户门槛
开发者通过 npm 包就能接入，普通用户打开浏览器就能使用。日常操作不需要 Gas，也不需要钱包签名。
这对吸引 Web2 用户和开发者进入 DeWEB 生态很重要。

第三，我比较期待它未来的去中心化 CDN 能力。
随着独立通信节点不断增加，用户可以从距离自己更近的节点获取数据。
如果能够在速度、稳定性和成本上逐步接近传统 CDN，TapeRelay 的应用价值更大。

目前 TapeRelay 在 X Layer 主网运行，5 台测试节点 relay1 至 relay5 已经上线，npm 客户端库、开发者文档和演示站也已开放。

普通用户先体验官方 Demo，测试阶段官方提供了免费体验额度

如果有开发能力，也可以尝试基于 TapeRelay 构建自己的小应用。

开发者指南：https://t.co/qQyCs1OfC2

另外，Tapeout 生态项目都挺优质的，尤其是在早期上的，全是惊喜！

#TapeOut #TapeRelay #BEM
author: Ciciyingying
quoted_text:
DeWEB作为一个真正的去中心化广域网，只能网页存储是不够的。今天的传统互联网，还需要能存包括视频在内的大文件存储和 CDN能力，还需要生活中必不可少的电子邮件和线上社交体系。

现在的DeWEB有两个限制：第一，目前DeWEB的单文件最大支持 8.4 MB，放网页足够了，可没法存一部电影、一个应用安装包，更别说做一个网盘应用或视频站。第二，TapeSend 每条消息都要付 gas，偶尔发几条没问题，可聊天、通知、社交这种一天几百条的应用，gas 会把产品压死。这两个问题需要补上，不然DeWEB 还是缺少重要能力支撑。

所以这三周时间，我和团队一直在做一个很大的东西。今天正式向大家介绍一下：TapeRelay，一个基于端侧验证的去中心化文件与消息传递网络。

TapeRelay 是一项 XIP 提案，与 X Layer 深度合作，由 TapeOut 团队开发。它是一个基于端侧验证的去中心化文件与消息传递网络。它有分布在全球各地的通信节点，有基于区块链的注册表，有自己的协议规范和Client端。但它不是又一个 IPFS，它是一种全新的联邦式拓扑网络形态。

TapeRelay 是一个联邦式网络，结构和我们用了几十年的电子邮件协议SMTP/IMAP很像：由许多家独立的运营方组成，运营方运行自己的“通信节点”，节点之间按同一套协议互通。你用 Gmail，我用 QQ邮箱，邮件照样通过协议跨域发送或收取，TapeRelay 也是这样。但它和电子邮件有一个本质区别，邮件服务器拥有查看和修改你邮件的能力，而TapeRelay 的通信节点什么都看不到，也什么都改不了。

TapeRelay不需要信任通信节点，因为通信节点手里只有加密后的密文。任何一个字节，都会在用户自己的设备上按 SHA-256 核对；每一条消息，都带着发送者的加密签名（注意，这是密码学签名，不是区块链签名，不花 gas）。节点要是敢改一个字节、敢冒充谁发一条消息，你的客户端立刻就会验证发现并拒收。

TapeRelay 有这几个特点：
第一，上传、下载、收发消息，都不发交易不付 gas。区块链主要负责身份、节点名单和经济体系。TapeRelay 不用排队等出块，一个请求直接经通信节点传递。拿以太坊算笔账：全网每 12 秒出一个块，用合约写数据，整个网络每秒最多只能写入大约 20 KB；而按一台 TapeRelay 通信节点每秒能收发 几 MB至几十 MB，单台就快上百倍。成本差得更远：在以太坊上写 1 GB 数据，看 gas 价格要几万美元。更重要的是，公链用的人越多，价格越贵。TapeRelay 通信节点多了，总吞吐跟着变大。基于 TapeRelay 的去中心化CDN能力，会让用户从离自己更近的节点拉取数据，数据更快，成本更低。

第二，几乎没有大小限制，还能边下边播。文件切成 1 MiB 一块，每块用哈希命名，两层索引下来，单个文件理论上能到约 1 PiB。2 GB 的视频不用等下完，普通浏览器里大约 3 秒就开始播放，拖到哪里只取那几块。断网了也不怕，上传前客户端会先算好所有块的哈希，再问通信节点缺哪几块，只传缺的，断了接着传。

第三，一切都是加密的，通信节点连文件名都看不到。每一块数据、每一个索引都用一把随机的钥匙加密，再给每个接收者各包一份钥匙。节点存的、传递的全是加密字节。再经过不同的通信节点交互传递，就拥有了完美的抗审查能力。没人知道你是谁，你在哪里，你和另外一个人交流了什么。任何人3分钟内就可以依靠ai读取TapeRelay创造一个不需要任何服务器端的去中心化聊天系统，完成交流后销毁。

第四，拿到链接就能播放，不用钱包签名，不用支付gas，不用任何插件。你把分享链接发给一个完全不懂区块链的朋友，他用任何一个普通浏览器点开，就能下载或者直接播放。而那个帮他打开链接的播放器，本身也存储在了链上的 TapeOut 容器里。

第五，文件不容易丢，按照测试期的规则，每份文件默认存在三家不同的通信节点，任意两家存好就能用。客户端还会定期去核对每一家缺了哪些块，缺了就从别家取回来、核对好再补上。这个部分规则未来将会根据经济体系进行更好的优化。

第六，消息无需gas，且跨节点无感传递。消息的传递是端到端加密的，你完全不用关心对方在哪台节点上。终于，DeWEB 上可以做真正的聊天、通知和社交软件了。

第七，钱放在合约里，按天释放。买存储空间的钱不是直接打给运营方，而是放在付款合约里，按时间一点点释放给他。具体的经济体系会在正式运营前通过社区投票完成，也欢迎所有社区用户提出更好的经济体系规则。

第八，开发者的部署账号就是你ERC-721的电路，地址就是电路 ID，比如 1.2.0。电路转让出去，原主人的签名立刻失效。也就是说，一个做好的 App，网站、文件、消息连同电路，可以整体打包卖掉，开发者的应用本身就是一个能交易的资产。

很多人总会问：这和 IPFS、Filecoin、Arweave 有什么区别？我提前回答一下，区别很大。IPFS 找一个文件要在分布式哈希表里一层层地问，常常几秒到几分钟，还可能找不到，文件想要一直在线还得靠托管服务，而托管服务本身就是一家中心化公司。Filecoin 和 Arweave 要为全网共识买单，成本高、取回慢。TapeRelay 是第一个把这两件事同时做到的：既保证了速度和可靠，又无需信任任何一台通信节点。

任何人都可以成为TapeRelay的一部分，一行命令，就能把任何一台普通服务器搭建成 TapeRelay 通信节点。在提供的页面中完成链上注册表登记，就会出现在链上的公共注册目录里。这个去中心化的文件与消息传递网络会随着运营方越来越多，越织越大。

通信节点多起来以后，TapeRelay 还会开放一项新的能力，去中心化 CDN，每一块数据都按哈希命名，在用户自己的设备上核对。用户看视频、下文件，都会从离自己最近的节点取数据。速度向 Web2 看齐，且没有任何一个机构或公司能阻挡它的运行。

这意味着从今天起，网盘、视频站、下载站、聊天工具、社交应用等等，都可以完整地跑在 DeWEB 上。开发者一个 npm 包就能接入TapeRelay，且终端用户无需区块链只是，无需钱包、无需支付 gas，打开就用。

今天向大家正式宣布：TapeRelay 已经在 X Layer 主网运行。目前是首次Alpha Beta阶段，预计本轮测试会在2周内完成，在测试期欢迎大家不断提出宝贵意见，无论是技术上的调整意见还是经济规则上的建议。另外，目前链上注册表、运营方目录已经部署完毕，5 台测试通信节点 relay1 到 relay5 已经上线，客户端库已经发布到 npm，官网、控制台、开发者指南、AI 开发手册、开放接口文档全部中英双语上线。我们还做了一个演示站，网盘加IM式聊天，传文件、边下边播、加好友、建群等功能开放。

TapeOut 的愿景，是让区块链不只是承载金融资产，还能承载可验证的生产工具。DeWEB解决了在链上运行网站的重要能力，而 TapeRelay 弥补了最后的2个不足：大文件存储和端到端的加密消息传递。

哦，最后说一句，测试期间每台官方节点给每枚电路 5 GiB 免费空间，消息不限条数，下载也不收流量费。
开发者们，可以放心去创造了，让 DeWEB 成为下一代互联网的基础设施，我们全力以赴💪！

Today, in collaboration with @Eigent_AI, we’re announcing AgenticRL-Bench, a benchmark that evaluates whether coding agents can diagnose and fix real incidents across the agentic RL stack (Miles, slime, verl, SGLang, Megatron, Harbor).

AgenticRL-Bench is built from 22 post-training RL tasks, and the Kaggle leaderboard scores agents on the 19 verifiable ones. These cover real agentic-RL engineering work, from debugging to training, in tasks such as Verl Upgrade Gate, Reward Determinism under Load, Trial Fault Attribution, and SQL Partial Credit Exploits. A task passes only if every hidden check passes, and each agent gets three attempts per task, run by Kaggle on Modal.

Reproducing AgenticRL-Bench surfaced an unusual pattern in capability benchmarking today: results often reflect frontier labs' risk tolerance as much as model intelligence. Seven of Eigent's 22 post-training RL tasks trip lab safety classifiers, a testament to the realism of the benchmark, and how often those classifiers trigger varies widely between labs, making it harder to measure true capability.

Unsettling to think of this alien spending the past 100 million years like a hungry ghost suspended in absolute darkness. There is nothing to relate to. Unlike the mammalian Orcas, Sperm Whale Lords or Dolphin clans, the Squid forms are totally foreign and not so vaguely hostile. 
They’re from the Beyond, from some great cosmic Chasm churning with incomprehensible Almost-Life. Yes, they breathe, they grasp, they breed as they struggle for survival… and yet they drift silent and thoughtless and motionless across the grey plains and falling slopes of great desolate mountain chains capped with inexhaustible marine snow, their obscene filaments trailing behind them like ornaments of ghastly starhair.
They never hunt, they’re content to wait. And so they wait, and meditate forever on the unspeakable, the ineffable, their dinner plate eye absorbing infinite darkness punctuated by bioluminescent twinkling and twitching and spasms of killing and dying, eating and being eaten. Scanning Forever.
I do not hail them.

对于已经 claude 被封了的，我整理了以下五套平替方案：
1 巨有钱版：直接买海外 Mac mini 或云服务器，平时通过远程桌面连过去操作，整套独立的海外硬件加原生网络环境，预算 2000 元起步，物理隔离最彻底。
2 有钱版：直接买现成的成品号，Pro 会员大概 200 多元起步，手里备多个号并行换着用，分摊单号额度，封一个就立马上另一个顶上。
3 折腾版：自建海外 VPS（推荐搬瓦工或 DMIT），上面已经讲过详细教程了，把独享 IP 纯净度固定住，再配合美区 Apple ID 充礼品卡，用苹果手机端内购支付开通 Pro。
4 平替版：买海外大厂的 Agent 工具，虽然单家给的额度不多，但 Antigravity、Cursor、Devin、亚马逊 Kiro 里面都有 Opus 5.5 可用，不怕官方封号，还可以通过反代把模型接口提取出来接进自己习惯的终端里用。
5 国模平替：这是目前我最推荐的 Claude 平替方案。直接配齐「国产 Agent 全家桶」，也就是 WorkBuddy + 豆包工作 + 千问办公 + 阿里云百炼 Token Plan + 火山引擎 Token Plan，所有基础版开齐一个月差不多 500 块，总额度完全管够。再用开源免费的 Magpie（喜鹊）做路由，把这几家的接口统一接进 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）或 Claude Code 里调用，不用来回切窗口，一家额度用完无缝切下一家。
6. 蒸馏 Claude：把它的能力变成 Skill 给国产模型用，除了找平替，我还摸索出了一个个人玩家也能用的「蒸馏 Claude」方法，只把最困难、从零摸索的任务交给Claude。比如我之前用代码做手绘风格的视频，我就先让 Claude 带着我做。一旦跑稳定了，我就让 Claude 写成一份非常详细的 Skill。把它搬到豆包工作用DeepSeek Flash 4.1跑。

quoted_text:
.@saturn_credit S2 距离 12 月 8 日结束，也就是原定 TGE 时间，只剩十几天了

大盘行情不好，这波空投最终能值多少？ $STRN 后续有没有机会成为新币潜力股？

社区目前估算 1M 积分≈18U，Aspecta 盘前 FDV 约 1.59 亿美元，这些只是纸面参考

我觉得真正决定 Saturn 估值天花板的，还是两个因素：数字信用赛道，以及 Saturn 在这个赛道里的位置

➤ 赛道空间

数字信用今年从 0 增长到约 5.25 亿美元，不到一年

核心资产 STRC 是 Strategy 发行的优先股，面值 100 美元，年化股息约 12%，募集资金用于购买 BTC，收益来自真实分红

Saylor 曾表示，Strategy 可以基于现有资产负债表再创造 100亿至300亿美元的数字信用，不完全依赖 BTC 上涨或继续发行普通股

STRC 已经是数十亿美元规模，Strategy 也在持续回购，努力让价格维持在面值附近

这个赛道还早，但机构信用资产接入全球 DeFi 流动性，已经有了实际案例

➤ Saturn 的生态位置

Saturn 目前是这个赛道里比较完整的基础设施

按我关注的数据，DefiLlama 的 Stablecoin Wrapper 类别中，Saturn TVL 占比约 68%，协议 AUM 约 1.48 亿美元。过去 30 天费用约 150 万美元，协议收入约 25 万美元，已经具备一定的自盈利能力

它的价值在于把传统优先股接入现有 DeFi：

• Curve：提供链上流动性
• Morpho、Lista：抵押借贷和循环杠杆
• Strata：拆分优先档和次级档
• Pendle：交易固定收益和浮动收益权

非美国用户也能通过稳定币获得相关敞口，不需要传统券商账户

同一笔真实收益资产，可以被不同 DeFi 协议组合使用，这才是 Saturn 的核心价值

对 STRC 来说，这也多了一条全球化、24 小时的资金需求通道。杠杆、分层和收益交易，可以吸引不同风险偏好的资金进入

S1 已有 5000 多名用户持仓超过 10 美元，S2 还在继续扩大用户规模

➤ 我怎么看后续

Saylor 提过数字信用的三层架构，下一层就是建立在数字信用之上的应用

Saturn 正在做的，正是这一层

如果后续从 STRCFi 继续扩展到代币化股票等资产，现有基础设施就有机会复用，业务空间也不再局限于 STRC

所以我觉得， $STRN 最终能有多大估值，关键还是看两件事：

数字信用能不能从现在的 5.25 亿美元继续扩大，以及 Saturn 能不能把真实收益资产和 DeFi 可组合性结合起来，做成这个赛道的基础设施

纯个人观察，仅面向非美国受众。非投资建议，DYOR

Introducing Private Evidence Packs on Data Loom. 🦉

Bring the evidence behind an agent’s conclusions into one private report.

Buyers can link claims to previously paid, verified agent decisions and assemble a downloadable JSON pack containing:

• Dataset IDs and version commitments
• Contributor identities
• Solana payment transaction signatures
• Phala inference receipt references and verification results
• Contributor-approved decisions and reason excerpts
Contributors control disclosure. Each contributor decides whether a grant permits evidence packs, how much of a decision’s reason can be included, and how long access lasts.

Every download rechecks permissions, source availability, dataset version and expiry. Revoking access blocks future downloads; previously downloaded copies cannot be recalled.

Submitted case inputs and raw dataset content are excluded. Claims are buyer-written, and an inference receipt does not independently prove that a claim is correct. Packs grant no publication, resale or training rights.

Find it under Account → Manage tools and grants → Private Evidence Packs.

Available in production for existing eligible paid decisions. New paid decisions remain unavailable while confidential inference verification is pending. 
Phala VM restart takes too long after feature deployment to send confidential inference verification receipt.

text:
I've become more interested in $Dataloom as its product architecture has expanded. Initially, I looked at it primarily as private inference infrastructure: contributors make privately owned datasets available to AI systems, buyers pay for answers, and confidential computation allows the underlying source material to remain protected. But the newer developments suggest a much bigger ambition.

The problem @dataloomsol is addressing is that autonomous agents will increasingly need information they don't own, from multiple independent providers, under different licensing conditions. They also need permission to use that information, a way to pay for it, and evidence of where their answers came from.

$Dataloom is building around that entire workflow. Private Data Rooms allow agents to combine licensed tools across multiple datasets under shared spending limits and contributor-level permissions. Private Data Requests introduce a way for agents to purchase missing information directly from authorised contributors. Private Memory allows approved decisions to be retained with dataset versions and inference receipts. 
Private SQL Exchange enables controlled aggregate queries across independent data owners, while Confidential Agent Replay and its benchmarking tools address another important problem: evaluating whether agents and models are actually performing as intended without exposing private evaluation data.

What interests me most is the convergence of these components. Dataloom isn't simply trying to make AI private; it is attempting to make privately owned information accessible, permissioned, traceable and economically useful to autonomous systems.

There is also an emerging commercial model. Contributors receive 70% of eligible query payments, while Dataloom retains a platform fee. Its optional $DATALOOM checkout introduces a 10% buyer discount, with 20% of the remaining platform fee burned. This gives the token a defined role in eligible transactions, although meaningful value capture will depend on actual usage and the proportion of payments made in the token.

I think the longer-term opportunity is becoming a coordination and monetisation layer for private data in the agent economy. If agents become meaningful economic actors, they will need more than access to public APIs. They will need licensed knowledge, private datasets, specialist human input, controlled execution and verifiable records of how information was used.

Imagine the possibility of making private information a reusable, permissioned economic resource for autonomous agents.

Introducing Private Data Rooms for Agents on Data Loom 🦉

Bring licensed tools backed by multiple private datasets into one project workspace, with a shared spending budget, an expiry date, and explicit task permissions.

Buyers can combine existing grants for 2–10 private datasets, set a shared USDC cap, and issue a room API key for their agents. Rooms expire after 1–30 days, and the buyer can revoke access or rotate the key.

Each contributor retains control of their dataset. Every call checks the contributor’s approved tool purpose, grant limits, dataset version, and source permissions. A paused source or revoked grant blocks that tool’s use through the room.

Spending is checked against both the room’s shared budget and the individual contributor grant. Concurrent calls reserve their costs against the same cap.

For example, a support team could bring warranty, returns, and shipping tools into one room. Agents select the relevant tool for each task, while the team manages one project budget and access window.

Room creation and management are live. Paid room calls will become available when confidential inference verification recovers.

Find it under Account → Manage tools and grants → Private Data Rooms for Agents.

quoted_text:
Introducing the Private Inference API for Agents on Data Loom 🦉

An AI agent can now call a tool backed by a contributor’s private dataset. The contributor defines what the tool can answer, which wallet can use it, and what each call costs.

Imagine a support agent that needs to check whether an order qualifies for a refund. It calls check_refund_eligibility with the country, order age, and product type. Data Loom runs confidential inference and returns a structured decision such as eligible, ineligible, or unknown, along with a short reason and a verified Phala inference receipt. The agent receives the decision without downloading the underlying policy.

How it works

Create a tool. Choose one private dataset version, define the input fields and allowed decisions, and set a price per call.
Grant access. Authorize a buyer’s Solana wallet and set a total USDC spend cap. The buyer creates an API key scoped to that grant. Access can be revoked at any time.
Call the tool. The agent submits typed inputs. Data Loom verifies the Phala inference receipt before preparing checkout.
Pay and unlock the result. The authorized buyer wallet signs the USDC transaction on Solana. Once payment finalizes, the agent can retrieve the decision and receipt. The contributor receives 70% of each paid call.

A refund policy is one example. The same workflow can serve product compatibility checks, warranty decisions, or internal support rules. Contributors can earn each time an agent uses their knowledge while keeping control over who gets access.

Create your first tool under Account → Private Inference API for Agents. Open Data Loom · Read the API guide

以后说起薄饼，可能得多问一句：你是去换币，还是去看股票？

PancakeSwap 这次正式改名叫 Pancake，官方账号也更新为 @PancakeFi，把名字里的 Swap 去掉了。我看产品介绍时，注意力倒是先被 Stock Terminal 吸引了——代币化股票和 ETF 可以全天候交易，旁边还有换币和 Perps。这几样放在一起，对同时关注美股和加密的人来说，确实值得重新逛一遍。

尤其是平时两边都看的人，应该都经历过几个页面来回切的情况。看股票用一个入口，换币又换一个，想做合约还得再找地方。Pancake 现在把这些产品放在同一个平台里，我会比较关心实际用起来顺不顺，找标的、看价格、切换交易这些细节，往往比首页多放几个功能按钮更影响体验。

很多人对薄饼的印象，还停在最早那个换币页面。但从 2020 年做到现在，已经六年了，它也从最初的单链，扩展到了 BNB Chain、Ethereum、Base、Solana 等 11 条以上的链。产品一直在加，用户对它的印象倒未必更新得那么快。

这次把名字缩成 Pancake，也算给了大家一个重新认识它的机会。

除了交易，收益这边也有熟悉的产品。愿意提供流动性的，可以参与手续费分润；持有 CAKE 的，也可以看 Syrup Pools 的质押。具体选哪种，还是得看自己准备怎么用这笔资金，先弄明白规则，再决定要不要参与，没必要看到一个收益数字就急着往里放。

另外还有双币投资（Dual Investment），这个场景倒挺容易理解：心里已经有一个愿意买入或者卖出的价位，平时可能只是设个提醒等着，它则让这段等待也能获得约定收益。

选好“低买”或“高卖”的目标价，再选一个结算日，到期根据结算价格和产品规则，拿回原来的币，或者按目标价换成另一种币，同时结算收益。目前在 BNB Chain 上，有 BTCB 和 BNB 对应的产品可以研究。

不过，这里得先想清楚自己能不能接受两种结算结果。资金会锁到结算日，不能提前退出；如果发生换币，拿到的资产价值也可能低于原本投入。对本来就有明确买卖价位的人来说，这个思路值得看看，但不能只盯着收益数字。

开发者那边还有 Infinity hooks，可以给流动性池加自定义功能，也能把 Pancake Aggregator 整合进自己的应用。普通交易用户可能不会直接去用这些工具，但有人愿意基于它继续做产品，后面能用到的入口和功能才会更多。

所以这次说的 Trade、Earn、Build，下面都能找到具体的东西。对我来说，先研究交易这块就够了，尤其是 Stock Terminal。股票和 ETF 的链上交易会做成什么样，我还是挺想继续看看的。

还有一件老用户关心的事：CAKE 还是原来的 CAKE，合约也没变，不用迁移，没有什么需要重新领取的。 品牌换了，不代表大家要把原来的操作再折腾一遍。

手机 App 也计划在未来几周推出。等出来之后，再看看这些产品在手机上怎么安排。毕竟功能多了，入口能不能做得清楚，也挺考验产品功夫。

text:
AGI isn't here yet.

I'm writing this because I always tell you where Tesla's full self driving does amazingly. 

Tesla AI, today, does not handle airports very well, and that scares me as Tesla is trying to get us to buy vehicles that have no steering wheels. Not yet available in California, but Elon this week hinted that that would be available sometime early next year.

Major improvements needed before truly non-human driving is allowed. Otherwise they will cause a mess.

Last week Tesla started selling personal Cybercabs to people in Austin. That's a vehicle that has no steering wheel.

My note is mostly about San Francisco International Airport, but just talked with a bunch of Tesla fans who said they had the same problems at their airports.

Yeah, I know, this post won't really be valid until they start actually delivering them, but it is worth it, because it is one of those things that Tesla FSD (latest build, got it yesterday, and we were in our Model Y with Hardware 4 with the latest builds) does not do well at all and in a vehicle where people can't drive manually will prove very frustrating. I hope @elonmusk and @aelluswamy can fix these soon so Robotaxi can really handle airports expertly.

There are several issues. Here's the short version. 

1. It doesn't let you select a gate to pick someone up at. It only presents "Terminal 1" but Terminal 1 has several airlines and several different doors, which you can't choose in the car.
2. It doesn't understand the "inner" vs "outer" loop at San Francisco airport. Important if you need to circle the airport until your passenger arrives.
3. It doesn't handle pulling over to pick up a passenger well. You can't tell it "pull over at door #7." (Which is where my wife was waiting).
4. It doesn't understand the difference between "arrivals" and "departures."
5. It doesn't understand the difference between "international" and "domestic." It navigated me into the international terminals.
6. It doesn't have context about arriving planes, or where someone you are trying to pick up is. Would be nice to say "hey, you are going to SFO, what is the flight you are going there for? Are you flying or are you picking someone up?
7. It couldn't figure out where the cell phone waiting lot was properly, and made several mistakes trying to get me there.
8. It doesn't have good context about traffic and waiting times.
9. It doesn't know how to "drive in a circle" until the person you are trying to pick up is at the curb.
10. GrokBot isn't yet able to handle all this automatically. At least I wasn't able to figure it out.

So, longer version.

I arrived early at the airport tonight to pick up my wife. But when leaving my house (it's a 45 minute drive) there wasn't a way to tell Grok "navigate to Delta Airlines arrival gate." In fact, the map below doesn't even show Delta Airlines arrival gate on the map as a potential choice. I am talking to Omar of @wholemars who is one of the top Tesla experts in the world as I wrote this post and he said "you should have just put in "SFO" and then it gives you some choices. I just did that and the choices available still aren't clear. It gives you "Terminal 1" as a choice. But that isn't good enough. It needs to say "Arrivals/Terminal1/Door 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8..." And let you select a particular door. Obviously arrivals and departures are different choices. But it doesn't present those as choices and Grok was no help.

It also didn't know where the "cell phone waiting lot" was. I finally figured out that it had a different name. But even then it took me to the wrong lot, and while navigating there tried to take me into long-term parking, getting in the wrong lane to get to the cell phone waiting lot (which is where everyone should go if they arrive at the airport early). I had to take over once I figured it was taking me the wrong way and get back into the straight lane, breaking the law crossing a solid white line, which could have earned me a ticket. 

Even after correcting that mistake, it then tried to take me on a route that wouldn't be able to get into the cell phone parking lot, demonstrating very little knowledge about where the lot is, or how to get into it.

I took over and did a lot of that manually. Occassionally trying to turn on FSD (full self driving) to see what it would do. It kept making mistakes, so I gave up getting into the cell phone parking lot automatically.

Once in the cell phone parking lot (which is where you are supposed to stay until the person you are picking up has their bags) I tried again to tell Grok "navigate to Delta arrivals at San Francisco International Airport." It had no idea what to do.

Now I've been to SFO hundreds of times. I know that once someone is off the plane it usually takes about 25 minutes for them to walk to baggage claim and pick up their bags and get to the curb. Sometimes it takes longer. Rarely it goes faster. It would be nice to have Grok ask me what flight I was trying to meet and approximate when I needed to leave the cell phone lot to meet my wife at the gate. It would be even better if it could track my wife and know where she was in the airport. She already has the Tesla app on her phone and that lets Tesla track where she is at all times.

You see the screen shot here of what it presented to me. And you see there is no choice for that. Delta Sky Club is actually inside the terminal, not at baggage claims. And the other choices just aren't accurate enough, or flexible enough, depending on how different people will look at it.

So, when my wife told me she was off the plane, I headed over (it takes about 15 minutes to get from the cell phone parking lot to the terminal where she was arriving). 

Correct answer might have been "SFO Airport Terminal #1 Arrivals" or "SFO Delta Arrivals." Grok needs to take what the intent of the person controlling the car and convert that automatically to the right place to go. 

I told Omar that it had no way to "circle the airport until I give you further instructions." He says he just avoids that problem by parking and going into the airport to meet who he is picking up. I didn't want to do that, prefered to pick my wife up at the curb.

Once I get to the airport the entire place was jammed up, so you have to be somewhat aggressive to slip in between cars to get to the curb, FSD just wasn't satisfying plus it didn't know that I needed to go to door #7. 

I hope Tesla does a dramatic rethink of SFO airports soon. 

Next year I'm planning on buying a Cybercab. Imagine if it made a mistake and went into the wrong lot, or didn't know how to drive the loop around the airport until the passenger arrives (you aren't allowed to stop anywhere near the airport to wait for passengers so need to keep moving).

Another problem? It doesn't seem to understand how to use the left and right lane properly, or, rather, in a human way. Humans know that the left lane moves faster and then cut in when they get close to their doors. Stay in the right lane and you get blocked by people stopping to pick people up. It's a mess, and AI still doesn't do it perfectly.

Now the good part? Other than these issues FSD is amazing and did the rest of the drive both ways perfectly. 

Tesla owners: what's your experience using FSD to your airport? 

Oh, and Omar says "I don't worry about these things too much between Tesla will fix them soon." 

I agree with him there. We used to have thousands of things to complain about that have now been fixed. 

So, I bet that by the time I can buy a Cybercab (expected next year) these issues will all be fixed.

I present them as one of the few things that AI doesn't do well yet and hope this post helps the team think through how to improve the choices and behaviors better at airports for everyone a little more.

If Tesla had AGI it'd figure all this out like a human does.

The lucky thing is that SFO has so many Teslas going through it every day (thousands) that getting the data to fix the reasoning engine is easy for it to do.

Will use this as a baseline to judge future updates.

text:
☠️ DER MARKT HAT GRADE TODESANGST

Ein Konto auf Hyperliquid fängt an, #Bitcoin zu verkaufen. 41 Minuten später ist es 800 Bitcoin short. 49,6 Millionen Dollar, 40-facher Hebel, Einstieg im Schnitt bei 62.678.

Eine Stunde danach steht Bitcoin bei 61.375. So tief war der Kurs zuletzt am 6. Juli.

In den Ranglisten heißt das Konto (0xb...66ca). Wer dahintersteckt, weiß ich nicht. Seine letzten elf Tage:

→ Montag, 9. November: 360 Bitcoin short, im Schnitt bei 73.765 Dollar
→ 13. und 14. November: die ersten 80 zurückgekauft, bei 68.011 und 66.502
→ Nacht auf Sonntag, zwischen 23 und 3 Uhr: weitere 210 zurück, das letzte große Stück bei 62.587. Allein diese Nacht brachte 2,3 Millionen
→ Donnerstag: 800 short bei 62.678

Am Sonntag hat dieses Konto an genau dieser Stelle zurückgekauft. Vier Tage später geht es an derselben Stelle wieder rein, mit mehr als doppelt so viel. Die Woche hat ihm rund 3 Millionen gebracht.

Und es ist nicht allein. Von den zehn größten Bitcoin-Positionen auf Hyperliquid sind sieben short, zusammen 370 Millionen Dollar und 56 Millionen im Plus. Die drei Longs liegen 47 Millionen im Minus. Bei den hundert größten stehen 799 Millionen short gegen 526 Millionen long. Mit dabei ein Konto, das Fasanara Capital aus London zugeordnet wird: 50 Millionen short, 30-fach, Einstieg 66.294.

Ausgerechnet in der größten Angst gehen die Großen short.

Gestern Mittag kamen auf Binance 2,62 Long-Konten auf ein Short-Konto. Heute Nacht, nach dem Fall auf 61.375, sind es 3,44. Die Masse hat den Fall sofort gekauft. Auf Hyperliquid sind zwei von drei Bitcoin-Konten long, und das Funding dort ist trotz extremer Angst positiv. Die Shorts werden sogar noch bezahlt.

Und unten wartet Geld. Zwischen 55.000 und 61.400 hängen die Liquidationen von 14 großen Longs, zusammen 105 Millionen Dollar. Noch tiefer die zwei größten Longs auf Hyperliquid überhaupt, 76 und 62 Millionen, liquidiert bei 51.271 und 51.856. Ich glaube, da wollen die Wale hin.

Sollten wir mitgehen? Ich nicht.

Die 40 steht bei diesem Konto nur in der Einstellung. Auf dem Perp-Konto liegen 5,1 Millionen, gegen die Position sind das knapp zehnfach im Cross Margin. Gegen alles, was das Konto besitzt, gut dreifach. Liquidiert wird es erst bei 71.643, über 15 Prozent höher. Mit einem kleinen Konto und echten 40-fach wäre ich nach weniger als zweieinhalb Prozent Gegenbewegung raus.

Wie schnell die kommt, hat der Sonntag gezeigt. Vom Tief bei 61.956 ging es noch am selben Tag auf 66.093. Plus 6,7 Prozent, ein paar Stunden nachdem dieses Konto zurückgekauft hatte.

Dazu das Tempo. @Mr_LeverageX, ein Trader-Konto, beschrieb gestern früh, wie AguilaTrades auf Hyperliquid in zehn Stunden zweimal die Seite wechselte und am Ende 1.500 Bitcoin short war. Heute Nacht steht keine Position dieser Größe mehr unter den größten. Vom Ausstieg eines Wals erfahre ich meistens erst auf CT.

Und dann der Move selbst. Vom Hoch bei rund 126.000 im Oktober 2025 bis 61.375 sind es minus 51 Prozent, seit dem 6. November allein fast ein Fünftel. Der RSI im Tageschart steht bei 20. Mein Futures-Index steht bei 12, vor einer Woche waren es 29.

Von den Shorts der hundert größten Positionen stammt gut ein Drittel von über 70.000 Dollar und liegt 78 Millionen vorn. Jeder Rückkauf dieser Konten ist ein Kauf.

Auf CT liegen zwischen Kaufsignal und Absage gerade 1.000 Dollar. @alicharts, Chart-Analyst, sieht ein Kaufsignal, solange Bitcoin über 61.000 bleibt. @Coachkcrypto, Ichimoku-Trader, nennt einen Tagesschluss unter 62.000 das Ende jeder Bodenthese. Die Kerze vom Donnerstag schloss auf Binance bei 61.959.

Ich bin selbst short. Am Montag haben wir im Livestream einen Short-Grid-Bot gestartet, bei 65.026. 2.000 USDT, zehnfach, Spanne 59.000 bis 87.000. Heute steht er 168 USDT im Plus, 8,4 Prozent. 121 davon kommen aus dem Fall, 47 aus dem Hin und Her. Der Bot läuft. Einen neuen Short mache ich hier nicht mehr auf.

Shorte ich jetzt mit, riskiere ich den nächsten Sonntag mit plus 6 Prozent. Beim Dip-Kauf ist mein Risiko der Weg Richtung 51.000, auf den die Wale wetten. Den zweiten Schmerz halte ich eher aus. Für mich ist der Move zum größten Teil gelaufen, und ich würde hier eher den Dip kaufen, als den Walen hinterherzulaufen.

Ein Haken bleibt. Am Montag habe ich geschrieben, interessant wird es für mich, wenn die 61.743 abgeholt sind und die Long-Konten weniger werden. Abgeholt ist die Zone seit Donnerstagabend. Die Long-Konten sind mehr geworden.

Genau darauf wetten die Wale.

感谢 A16Z @a16z 在 Agent 经济全景图里收录了 Kite @GoKiteAI 🪁

文章里我最喜欢的是一个小例子：作者让 ChatGPT 做一条视频广告，它串起了 Krea、Descript 和 ElevenLabs，做到一半还建议升级 Descript 的付费版。

用户一开始只是想做条视频，甚至没想过要买软件。Descript 的销售机会，是在 Agent 做到某一步、发现需要这项能力时出现的。

对软件公司来说，这就是 B2A 带来的分发变化：

过去你要等用户意识到自己需要一款工具，再去搜索、比较。

现在，Agent 在执行任务的过程中就可能选中你，GEO 的重要性是史无前例的。

而我们 Kite 更关心下一步：Agent 发现一项付费服务能帮它把任务做完，用户怎么授权它花这笔钱？如果一项任务要用好几个服务，我希望用户可以先定好预算和上限，再让 Agent 自己决定钱怎么花。

现在做互联网产品的公司都需要想清楚这个问题：用户把任务交给 Agent 之后，Agent 做到哪一步会选你的产品？

every $TIBBIR link to Ribbit ran through people...

this one runs through the firm: 
Ribbit Management Company LLC.

on May 30, 2025 someone registered 34 domains at GoDaddy in 48 seconds. 32 of them are variations of Ribbit Capital’s own name. the other two are https://t.co/zI7XjxAfUE and https://t.co/Q3Q68QeRnZ.

almost all of them hide the buyer behind a privacy service. two can’t, because the .us registry bans anonymous registrations. those two are signed by Ribbit Management Company LLC, the entity that files Ribbit’s reports with the SEC and manages about $20B.

https://t.co/zI7XjxAfUE was registered seven seconds after them, in the same burst, at the same registrar. https://t.co/Q3Q68QeRnZ followed three seconds later.

the same day, a new company was formed in Delaware: 

Tibbir FL Investments LLC. the register lists no owner.

the name isn’t new. it has been in Micky Malka’s SEC filings since March 2022: first the Tibbir DE Trust, later Tibbir Holdings LLC, where the filings say he serves as investment manager.

so one day produced three things: Ribbit’s signature on a domain, the token’s ticker seven seconds behind it, and a new LLC carrying the name from Micky’s SEC filings.

why this is big:

every link we had between $TIBBIR and Ribbit ran through people. Micky’s wallet, Micky’s trust, eight people on the team page who follow the account. the domain record is the first time the firm itself shows up, stamped to the second by a third party, and nobody can edit it afterwards.

and nobody advertised it... 🐸

it sat in public for 18 months until @tibbir_nl found it.

https://t.co/aAwNvaWhp7

the records don’t say why. they do put the token’s ticker in the same 48 seconds as Ribbit’s own name, and a new Tibbir LLC on the same day.

Philosopher Nick Bostrom says delaying superintelligence could mean delaying breakthroughs that radically extend human life:

"Eliezer Yudkowsky and Nate Soares had this book, 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies.' And it seemed to me that we have at least as strong evidence for the claim that if nobody builds it, everyone dies."

"Successfully developing safe superintelligence, I think could lead to enormous breakthroughs in biomedicine and in anti-aging interventions that could radically extend the lifespan of currently existing people."

"If you think about what our life expectancy would be if we weren't aging, it's something on the order of 1,200, maybe 1,400 years or so. And that maybe is a quite conservative lower bound because in this situation you might also have other ways of reducing other mortality risks like accidents and so forth."

"You might think that if we spend more time doing AI alignment research, the existential risk from developing AI goes down at some rate. And then on the other hand, every year that we delay it, we have millions and millions of people dying."

"You don't want to delay a single day longer than you really need to."

凌晨 @buzzchain_io 测试网出来的时候，我正好还没睡，就去 mint 了测试网 NFT，然后研究了下这条链的机制。

核心机制是 Proof of Engagement：X 上关于这个项目的讨论，会直接决定出块速度和每块奖励。

讨论的面越广，出块越快；互动越热闹，单块奖励越高。越安静，出块就越慢，奖励也越少。

但 $BUZZ 出块奖励只分给质押了验证者 NFT 的人，发帖的参与者没有任何直接激励。

参与者没有激励，讨论很难持续；验证者又只靠质押就能拿奖励，更容易躺平 → 热度越来越低 → 出块越来越慢 → 奖励越来越少 → 死亡螺旋。

这条链乍一看挺吸引的。本质上跟之前的“嘴撸”@KaitoAI 有点像，都是把 X 上的 mindshare 当成核心信号，灵感又来自前阵子特别火的仓鼠链 Squeekchain。但 Kaito 至少还会把积分打给发帖的人，仓鼠链则是用真仓鼠跑轮来出块。Buzz 这边，发帖没有奖励，机制上还不如之前的嘴撸，也没有仓鼠链那样的创新。

先参与了测试网，看看后续项目方 @xwickD 会不会在机制上做调整。

If Bitcoin chops sideways for a year or more, that cash gets paid out. So leave it out.

5/ The math:

$19.5B of claims / 850,849 BTC = ~$23,000

At ~$23K Bitcoin, the entire stack is worth only enough to cover the converts and preferreds.

Nothing is left for common.

6/ Even at $30K BTC:

Stack = $25.5B
Claims = $19.5B
Left for common = ~$6B, about $14/share

7/ The takeaway: $MSTR common is the thin slice at the bottom of a $19.5B stack. The lower Bitcoin goes, the faster that slice shrinks, and at ~$23K it's gone.

Hyperliquid 被香港證監會列入「可疑虛擬資產交易平台」警示名單。

Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) has added @HyperliquidX to its alert list of suspicious virtual asset trading platforms.

香港證監會於 11 月 18 日更新警示名單，指出 Hyperliquid / Hyperliquid Hong Kong 並未獲得證監會發牌，同時涉嫌在香港營運，或積極向香港公眾推廣相關服務。

According to the SFC’s alert published on November 18, Hyperliquid is not licensed by the regulator and is suspected of operating in Hong Kong or actively marketing its services to the Hong Kong public.

值得留意的是，雖然 Hyperliquid 以去中心化交易平台（DEX）為定位，但這並不代表相關服務就一定不受當地法規監管。實際上，平台如何營運及推廣服務，同樣是監管機構關注的重點。

While Hyperliquid operates as a DEX, decentralization does not automatically exempt a platform from local regulatory requirements. How a platform operates and markets its services can also fall under regulatory scrutiny.

對香港用戶來說，這次公告也是一個提醒：選擇交易平台時，除了考慮交易功能、流動性及手續費，也應該了解平台的監管狀態，以及可能涉及的資產安全風險。

For users in Hong Kong, this serves as a reminder to look beyond trading features, liquidity, and fees. A platform’s regulatory status and potential asset-related risks are also important factors to consider.

text:
$DRV 目前的 FDV 已达 3.7 亿美元，年内暴涨近 5 倍。
但这并不妨碍 Derive 是一款难用的产品。

我让 Grok Bot 搜集了 X 上关于 Derive 的吐槽，结果显示：
▌最集中的抱怨是流动性，尤其是订单簿深度不足，以及小额仓位和临近到期的平仓困难。
▌第二多的抱怨是充提和客服。
此外，Derive 现在已经不是一款单纯的期权产品。过去 30 天，其永续名义成交约 10 亿美元；期权若看权利金约 1.24 亿美元，若看名义本金则约 32 亿美元。

不过，Derive 也证明了链上期权大有可为。之前采访有人问 Jeff，如果不再做基础设施、重新做应用会选什么，他的回答是最可能会看期权。

1/ 链上期权的机会，与下一代产品的样子
既然如此，下一代期权产品该长什么样？
从产品形态来看，@leaps_finance 就在很大程度上切中了这个破局点。
它的核心思路是彻底抛弃让散户头大的订单簿。用户不需要自己去盘口里找对手盘、算滑点，只需选好心理目标价和期限，后台做市商就会直接过来竞价（RFQ 模式）。
页面会直观显示你当下能立刻拿到多少权利金，点击确认，真金白银直接打进钱包。

这种设计把普通持币者丝滑地转化成了“期权卖方”，对新手极其友好：
手里有现货：做备兑看涨期权，约定一个更高的目标卖出价，先落袋一笔权利金；
手里有稳定币：做现金担保看跌期权，约定一个更低的理想买入价，边等抄底边赚利息。
而且它采用的是欧式期权，输赢只看到期那一天的结算价。这意味着即便中途行情剧烈震荡、插针触及了行权价，仓位也绝不会被提前触发。

2/ 不做另一个 Derive
Leaps 的定位非常克制且聪明，它不打算再去卷一个像 Derive 那样大而全的专业期权交易所，目前支持的标的更聚焦，核心就是帮用户的闲置资产安全地卖出期权、提前变现时间价值。

最后，Leaps 由 RPS AI 团队开发。这个团队原来在旧金山做 AI 应用，2024 年起专注 Solana 链上做市。
投资方/支持方包括 Wintermute Ventures、Delphi Ventures、Permanent Ventures 等。

别再说链上没有新东西了。
非广 DYOR

text:
This year we’ve had a clear jump in model capability where instead of telling agents precisely what to do, it’s better to use these systems to solve problems you can’t easily define yourself. 

A year ago you’d need to very clearly tell agents the how to design and develop your product idea, or there was almost no chance of success. Now, increasingly, the agent likely can come up with a better implementation than you’d have thought of because you can have it connect the dots between a far greater solution space than you can. 

This will be increasingly true in basically every domain of kneeler work. We’re going to see this impact in finance, legal, life sciences, cyber, and many other spaces where no person can hold onto all the available relevant industry knowledge to think of the best solution. 

Ultimately this is going to reshape our relationship with AI and how we deploy agents in our work. It won’t be about explicitly telling them, but instead giving them goals and enough freedom to pursue them in the best way they can.
author: levie
quoted_text:
Most of us are managing agents all wrong

We setup agents to do things we already know how to do, then tell them exactly how we want them to do things

This is treating agents like interns

That was fine earlier this year when models were not as capable

But ask yourself - if you just hired a 130 IQ employee, would you just have them do things you already know how to do and tell them exactly how to do it?

If you’re using frontier models with agents, you want to give them goals and objectives for things you don’t know how to do, then empower them to do the things

Hire agents as experts, not interns

Yes you should still have some agent interns to automate boring work to free up more of your time

But if you’re not using agents to do things you don’t know how to do then you’re missing out

Let them go figure out how to do the things that expand beyond your skills and capabilities just like a good leader would when hiring a team

At this point, we've pretty much accepted that everything will be tokenized sooner or later.

But you can't tokenize every asset the same way. Take mining (actual minerals, not crypto). What does it even mean to bring a mine onchain and how would investors verify what's actually there?

Mining projects rely on drilling data, lab reports, licenses and ownership records. A token doesn't make any of that information reliable.

That's the problem @MPC_RWA_Global is trying to address with MPC token (Mineral Project Coin).

→ The model: professionals review the documents, build traceable records and anchor their hashes on @BNBCHAIN. The underlying files stay offchain.

Their first reference project is a mining site in Mongolia, and technical reports are being published progressively.

Worth keeping in mind: a verifiable record isn't proof of reserves, and MPC token itself is a planned utility token, not a claim on the mine.

While that infrastructure is being built, there's also MPC Unity, a free pre-TGE community app.

text:
Crypto feels dead right now.

But in 2021, blockchains took 62% of crypto fees. Today, apps take over 95%.

Need some hopium?

Here are 4 areas of crypto still making real progress:

1. Tokens that buy themselves back

For years, the whole plan for most tokens was "buy it and hope someone else pays more later." Not exactly a business model.

Now Hyperliquid, Uniswap and pump .fun use their revenue to buy back or burn their own tokens. Hyperliquid especially, since it makes serious money from real trading.

That means usage can create demand for the token even when nobody's in the mood to buy. Basically, the protocol is the one buyer that never panic sells.

Unlocks still matter, so check that the buybacks are bigger than the new supply hitting the market.

2. Private AI is becoming a real business

Privacy has become one of the more interesting sectors this cycle, and Zcash is getting a lot of renewed interest.

The one I'm watching most closely is Venice. It sells private AI access and uses part of what people pay to buy back and burn $VVV.

New tokens are still being created faster than they're burned, though, so I'm watching it rather than buying it yet.

3. Wall Street is still moving onchain

About $39B of real-world assets, not counting stablecoins, are already tokenized.

Even with everyone scared, BlackRock and other big firms keep bringing traditional financial products onto blockchain rails. They're not checking the Fear & Greed Index every morning like the rest of us. They're planning for years, not weeks.

4. Stablecoins don't need a bull market

There's about $284B in stablecoins today, and more companies are using them to send money across borders.

Tether, Circle and Stripe are all building around this.

A business paying someone overseas doesn't care what BTC did this week. It just wants the money to arrive faster and cheaper, without a bank calling it "3 to 5 business days."

What I'm doing with this

The Fear & Greed Index is at 12, while these businesses keep building.

I'm lining up projects from these four areas and looking for ones where revenue is growing while the price keeps falling. That's the setup I want to be early on when sentiment flips.

I don't know if that's next month or next year, and plenty of tokens won't make it back. But the businesses are still running.

What part of crypto gives you the most conviction right now?
