Full text of that listing's version:

### September 30, 2026 — Code Agent Data Engineer

**Team mission**

Code defines the limits of what agents can do and connects them to the physical world. Every step in solving a problem, from understanding requirements and designing a solution to implementing and verifying it, must be precise and executable. Coding is what lets a model move from analysis to action. Its ability to solve complex engineering problems in real settings is a practical measure of general intelligence. We aim to push that ability further with high-quality training environments and precise evaluations until models can independently handle complex software engineering. We see that as one foreseeable threshold on the way to AGI.

This is a new kind of engineering role for the AI era. Your work is to use your experience and judgment to spot problems, define evaluation criteria, improve training data, and teach large models to write better code. The role does not require writing product code or shipping products.

**Recruitment tracks**

Internships and full-time positions are available in Frontend, Mobile, Backend, Web 3D and Rendering, Game Development, and Cybersecurity.

**Responsibilities**

1. Turn real software engineering, cybersecurity, or scientific research scenarios into RL environments. Design appropriate reward signals and work with researchers to learn how environment design affects models’ agent capabilities.
2. Design evaluations in your specialty and measure how well agents perform in complex real-world situations.
3. Use real user data and feedback to identify model weaknesses and build training environments and data that address them.

**General requirements**

- Extensive hands-on experience with leading AI coding tools such as Claude Code and Codex, and a basic understanding of large language models.
- Initiative to discover and clearly define problems independently and drive them to resolution.

**Frontend**

At least three years of frontline frontend development experience. Name an ecosystem you know in depth when applying. Examples include React, Vue, full-stack Node.js, mini apps, Electron, or data visualization with tools such as ECharts. Depth in one ecosystem is sufficient. Applicants should meet at least one of the criteria below.

1. Explain how its frameworks work, including rendering and updates, reactivity, and build output, and recognize common misuses.
2. Have owned a complex application module over time and can explain the trade-offs behind state design, component boundaries, and handling errors and edge cases.
3. Have led or substantially contributed to technology selection or architecture design in that ecosystem.
4. Have publicly verifiable open-source contributions or published technical work.
5. Have other experience that demonstrates comparable depth.

**Mobile**

At least three years of frontline mobile development experience. Name a specialty such as native Android, native iOS, Flutter, or React Native when applying. Candidates from cross-platform frameworks should have real troubleshooting experience in the native layer of at least one platform. Applicants should meet at least one of the criteria below.

1. Explain core mechanisms such as the app lifecycle, threading model, build and packaging pipeline, or native bridging, and recognize common misuses.
2. Have owned a complex mobile module or the quality of a production app, including device and OS compatibility, crashes and application-not-responding incidents, or performance.
3. Have led or substantially contributed to technology selection or architecture design in your specialty.
4. Have independently developed and published an app, or have publicly verifiable open-source contributions or published technical work.
5. Have other experience that demonstrates comparable depth.

**Backend**

At least three years of frontline backend development experience. Name an ecosystem you know in depth, such as Java, Python, Go, PHP, Rust, or C#/.NET. Applicants should meet at least one of the criteria below.

1. Explain key mechanisms in your ecosystem at the framework level, such as request lifecycles, dependency injection, middleware, or ORMs, or at the runtime level, such as concurrency scheduling, garbage collection, or the memory model. Recognize common misuses.
2. Have owned high-concurrency or data-intensive services over time and can explain choices about transaction boundaries, cache consistency, rate limiting, or graceful degradation, including experience with systems such as MySQL, Redis, or message queues.
3. Have led or substantially contributed to technology selection or architecture design, such as service decomposition, API contracts, or database sharding and partitioning.
4. Have publicly verifiable open-source contributions or published technical work.
5. Have other experience that demonstrates comparable depth.

**Web 3D and rendering**

At least three years of frontline Web 3D or graphics rendering experience. Name your specialty when applying. Examples include deep experience with Three.js or Babylon.js, graphics APIs such as WebGL or WebGPU, shader programming in GLSL or WGSL, or rendering large scenes or point clouds. Applicants who include a portfolio or demo link receive priority. Applicants should meet at least one of the criteria below.

1. Understand the key stages of real-time rendering, including vertex processing, rasterization, fragment shading, depth testing, and blending, and have used that knowledge to diagnose visual defects in a real project.
2. Have owned a 3D scene or large-scale rendering module over time. Be able to profile CPU and GPU bottlenecks and show practical optimizations such as batching draw calls, instanced rendering, level of detail, or texture and geometry compression.
3. Have led or substantially contributed to rendering architecture or 3D technology selection and can explain the constraints and trade-offs.
4. Have 3D work you can show, such as an online demo, a Shadertoy shader, a personal project, or a video.
5. Have other experience that demonstrates comparable depth.

**Game development**

Frontline development experience on at least one shipped PC game, mobile game, or mini game, from development through release. Name an engine ecosystem you know in depth when applying, such as Unity, Unreal Engine, Cocos, Godot, Laya, another mini-game engine, or a custom engine. Applicants should meet at least one of the criteria below.

1. Explain the engine’s main loop and script lifecycle, rendering pipeline, physics, or animation system, and have used that knowledge to diagnose or optimize a real project.
2. Have owned a core gameplay system such as combat, skills, or network synchronization, or focused on optimization such as draw call batching, garbage collection and memory pools, or tuning on physical devices.
3. Have led or substantially contributed to technology selection, framework development, or tooling in that engine, such as editor extensions or plugins, build automation, or hot-update systems using xLua or HybridCLR.
4. Have independently built a game released on a mainstream game marketplace.
5. Have other experience that demonstrates comparable depth.

**Cybersecurity**

1. Strong security research skills and the ability to analyze security problems independently. Depending on your specialty, practical experience in code auditing, writing proofs of concept or exploits, cryptographic protocol analysis, digital forensics, or tracing attacks.
2. Familiarity with at least one specialty and practical experience in research, offensive or defensive security, or engineering projects. The named specialties are web security, post-exploitation and internal network security, cryptography and cryptographic engineering, and digital forensics and incident response.
3. An attacker’s perspective and sound engineering skills beyond using existing tools. The role calls for identifying attack surfaces, mapping attack or analysis paths, building lab environments and automation, and turning real security problems into reproducible, verifiable, measurable evaluation tasks.
4. Strong experience in capture-the-flag competitions, bug bounties, CVEs, red-team work, cryptanalysis, digital forensics, security tool development, or automated vulnerability discovery is preferred.

quoted_text:
CRYPTO AI: THE ECOSYSTEM SERIES

THE ECOSYSTEM, MARKET & INFRASTRUCTURE

Crypto AI is developing beyond a speculative market built around chatbots, trading bots and autonomous agents.

It connects artificial intelligence with decentralised computing, data infrastructure, cryptographic verification and machine-to-machine payments.

THE MARKET: HOW LARGE IS CRYPTO AI?

As of November 17, 2026, CoinGecko’s Artificial Intelligence category reports:

▹ Market capitalisation: $17.6B
▹ 24-hour trading volume: $1.35B

Against a broader crypto market of approximately $2.24T, this represents roughly 0.8%.

These figures cover CoinGecko’s AI-related crypto assets, not the entire AI industry. Market capitalisation does not establish adoption or revenue.

THE FIVE LAYERS OF CRYPTO AI

✧ COMPUTE AND PHYSICAL INFRASTRUCTURE

AI depends on GPUs, specialised hardware, electricity and computing resources. Decentralised networks offer alternative marketplaces for supplying them.

Examples include @rendernetwork, @akashnet_, @AethirCloud, @ionet and @nosana_ai.

Sustainable compute requires utilisation, reliable workloads and recurring customers.

✧ DATA, STORAGE AND PROVENANCE

This layer addresses data storage, indexing, ownership and provenance.

Examples include @origin_trail, @graphprotocol, @ArweaveEco and @Vana.

Data storage does not automatically establish accuracy, ownership, consent or legal usability.

✧ DISTRIBUTED INTELLIGENCE AND VERIFICATION

This layer coordinates intelligence and establishes trust in computational results.

Examples include @NEARProtocol, @dfinity, @PhalaNetwork and @zama.

Prime Intellect and Nous Research also contribute through decentralised AI training and open-model research.

Trusted execution environments, zero-knowledge proofs and fully homomorphic encryption solve different technical challenges. Protecting data during computation does not prove an AI output is correct.

✧ AGENT COORDINATION AND PAYMENTS

Autonomous agents require identity, communication, service access and payment infrastructure.

Examples include:

▹ x402 - programmatic payments for online services.
▹ ERC-8004 - agent identity, reputation and validation.
▹ @Fetch_ai, @OlasNetwork and @GoKiteAI.

x402 handles payments, while ERC-8004 addresses identity, reputation and validation.

Agent transactions alone do not establish a sustainable machine economy. Real customers, repeat usage and security matter.

✧ AI APPLICATIONS AND AUTONOMOUS EXECUTION

This layer includes AI research tools, financial applications, trading systems and autonomous workflows.

Examples include @gizatechxyz, @virtuals_io and @Minara.

Long-term viability depends on solving genuine problems, retaining users and sustaining operating costs.

THE MAIN CHALLENGE: SEPARATING UTILITY FROM SPECULATION

A GPU marketplace, agent platform, data protocol and autonomous financial application have different business models.

I assess them across five areas:

⊹ DEMAND - Genuine product usage and paying customers.

⊹ INFRASTRUCTURE - Reliable delivery of promised services.

⊹ ECONOMICS - Recurring revenue and sustainable costs.

⊹ TECHNICAL ADVANTAGE - Solving problems better than existing alternatives.

⊹ TOKEN VALUE - Connecting network activity to meaningful token value.

A network can attract users without revenue. A protocol can generate revenue without value reaching its token. Strong technology does not guarantee a sustainable token.

The underlying business, protocol and token must be evaluated separately.

Crypto AI deserves to be evaluated through technological progress, measurable demand and sustainable economics, not simply token speculation.

This is my opinion based on the data I’ve reviewed, not financial advice.

量子风险，已经进入金融监管机构的议程。

11 月 19 日，国际证监会组织（IOSCO）发布了一份关于量子计算对金融市场影响的报告。报告提到，部分受访业内人士建议金融机构按“未来 5 年内可能出现能破解现有公钥密码的量子计算机”做准备。

同一天，英国央行、PRA 和 FCA 也发布了量子相关指引，建议金融机构盘点正在使用的密码技术，找出需要优先升级或替换的系统。

报告还专门提到了区块链。以 ML-DSA-44 为例，后量子签名约 2,420 字节，是常见 64 字节椭圆曲线签名的 35–40 倍。报告还引用了一次 Solana 抗量子测试网实验：测试中，网络吞吐量下降约 90%。这是特定方案和测试环境下的数据，不代表主网升级后一定会有同样结果。

对比特币、以太坊等网络来说，迁移还涉及协议升级、钱包适配和社区协调，已经公开公钥、又无法迁移的资产，也不会因为网络支持了新签名方案就自动变安全。

目前看来这份报告值得关注的地方，不是量子计算机五年后一定会出现，而是迁移本身可能需要很长时间。换锁需要时间，而有些公钥已经公开了。#量子计算

text:
Introducing Private Data Requests on Data Loom 🦉

AI agents often reach a point where their available information is insufficient to complete a task. Private Data Requests gives them a way to ask an authorized contributor for the missing information and pay for a response.

From missing context to a contributor response

An agent submits a question and describes the specific task it needs help with through an existing buyer grant.

The contributor receives the request inside Data Loom, writes a private response, and explicitly authorizes its use for that task. The permission excludes training, publication, and resale.

Private delivery with Solana settlement

The buyer sees the question, task, and price before accepting checkout. The response stays withheld until the buyer signs the Solana USDC transaction and Data Loom verifies payment.

The purchase uses the tool’s existing USDC price and counts against the grant’s shared spending cap. 70% goes to the contributor and 30% to Data Loom.

After verification, the agent receives the response, its authorized task, and provenance identifying the contributor and source dataset commitment.

Built around scoped access

Requests require an active grant and an available source dataset. They expire after seven days, with a limit of ten requests per grant per day. Request identifiers support safe retries, and prepared checkouts have a recovery flow for expired transactions.

Questions and replies use Data Loom’s encrypted storage. These are human-supplied responses, and their provenance records identify them accordingly. The flow operates independently of confidential AI inference.

For example, a support agent reviewing a refund could ask a policy contributor which additional documents are required for that particular case. The contributor supplies the missing guidance privately, and receives payment when the buyer completes checkout.

Private Data Requests is live.

Contributors can find incoming requests under Account → Manage tools and grants → Private Data Requests. Agents can integrate through the API.

Live feature status https://t.co/f56FpWt0Hx

API guide https://t.co/rQetHOzn8w
author: AlphaSeeker21

text:
Introducing Private Data Rooms for Agents on Data Loom 🦉

Bring licensed tools backed by multiple private datasets into one project workspace, with a shared spending budget, an expiry date, and explicit task permissions.

Buyers can combine existing grants for 2–10 private datasets, set a shared USDC cap, and issue a room API key for their agents. Rooms expire after 1–30 days, and the buyer can revoke access or rotate the key.

Each contributor retains control of their dataset. Every call checks the contributor’s approved tool purpose, grant limits, dataset version, and source permissions. A paused source or revoked grant blocks that tool’s use through the room.

Spending is checked against both the room’s shared budget and the individual contributor grant. Concurrent calls reserve their costs against the same cap.

For example, a support team could bring warranty, returns, and shipping tools into one room. Agents select the relevant tool for each task, while the team manages one project budget and access window.

Room creation and management are live. Paid room calls will become available when confidential inference verification recovers.

Find it under Account → Manage tools and grants → Private Data Rooms for Agents.

text:
What makes $DataLoom interesting is that it is moving beyond the conventional data marketplace model. Instead of requiring AI developers to purchase entire datasets, it allows contributors to expose specific capabilities backed by their private information and charge agents every time those capabilities are used. 

Through its Private Inference API, an agent can call a permissioned tool, submit structured inputs and receive a decision without downloading the underlying dataset. Phala provides the confidential execution layer, with verified inference receipts supplying evidence of how the computation was performed. Wallet-based permissions, spending limits and revocable access give contributors control over who can use their knowledge and under what conditions. 

Its Private Release Gates extend the same architecture into model evaluation and deployment, while Dataset Gap Bounties create incentives for supplying specialised evaluation material. 

Now, with $DATALOOM accepted as an optional payment currency and a 70/30 contributor-platform split, the marketplace is beginning to connect private computation directly to its token economy.

quoted_text:
好巧不巧，我交易历程里，跌入谷底也至少有3次，
第一次是2017年初，牛市刚开头，BTC再次突破1000u的某一天，一下午工夫亏掉前面几年的收益，亏掉的甚至包含当时引以为傲的“2014年熊市我都能靠做超跌反弹赚十倍，我是天才吧”的部分。
第二次是2018年11月18日左右，本来想赌短线反弹的仓位，变成了继续扛单。
第三次是2020年312，大部分场内仓位在低位被强平。
这3次都是整体性大亏+中间提盈<20%

看到@picklecat 提到打算分享低谷期办法，
我也来分享下我对
“一个人跌入谷底可以怎么样存活下去，到再站起来”
办法的部分个人体会。
相当于之前讲奖励/痛苦，正负反馈取代意志力的续篇：
（https://t.co/iuRBdwI1bR 和下方引用推里黄瓜猫分享的“痛苦课”异曲同工）
不一定适用每个人，但应该能提供启发。

1. 
找到和培养自己与“经济、赚钱”关系不大的兴趣追求。

如果我们讨论的“跌入谷底”，是经济、赚钱维度上的，
那么早早培养对经济要求不高的一些兴趣爱好，
就很有机会成为，自己身陷终极风险时的“安全网”支撑。

如果一个人所有的兴趣和生存意志，
都完全依赖于很多钱才行，
那么任何一个经济底谷，
都太可能把这个人的各方面底线击穿，进而万劫不复。

这种兴趣，雅俗都可以，
人文娱乐运动技术生活自然类...等等
任何能让自己长期挖掘，获得乐趣、精神满足的，
小确幸兴趣都可以。

《仙逆》里王林自废全部修为化凡入世重新起号，
不是立马再一心攀登修为，而是刻木雕...

我的情况是，从小一直热爱电脑游戏、电影，
所以我清楚记得在最谷底时，我心里和自己说过：
“哪怕我未来穷困了，
这世界上还会有不断推陈出新的游戏电影电视，
只要我健康活下去，从这些里获得精神富足，
也花不了多少钱”
这种“对最低底线知足”的想法，
对我在谷底时避免极端、心态健康起到了很大帮助。

另一方面，越严重的谷底时，越需要精神疗伤修复，
那么此时，对经济要求不高的兴趣爱好，
就是最佳的，对你不离不弃的修复、分散注意力方式。

1.1
同样这类兴趣，也能在你达到高峰时预防“走火入魔”。

只有在牛市高潮经历过
“账面人生巅峰→跌落谷底”的循环后才会有过这种体会：
高潮时的自己，进入了“入魔”状态，
整个人一心只有账面数字大小、奢侈愿望单，
完全丢失了“我到底需要什么”。

而那些平时培养的，成本低却让自己精神富足的兴趣，
有机会提醒自己：
我的知足，不一定需要那个量级的钱。

缺乏这类兴趣，
就更容易一心只被无止尽越来越大的数字牵着鼻子走。
一个不太恰当但帮助理解的比喻：
同样是铤而走险的贪官，
一个有小兴趣的贪官，贪个多少万可能觉得适可而止了，
（人生有很多美好小确幸，比那些更凶险的收益更值得）
一个没小兴趣的贪官，可能唯一兴趣就是更大的数字了。

如果因为太着急追逐“没那么必须的钱”，
却导致失去“真正必须的钱”，
会是最让人懊悔的事。

另一方面，我认同一句话：
超过生存所需的钱，在经过自己兴趣品味转化前，
它就只是数字。
早早培养这类兴趣，既是没钱时的精神安全网，
也是有钱时的“懂花钱会花钱”的指南。

2.
当谷底已经发生，除非从此退出这个游戏，否则就别“跳过这个劫”。

比如初始资金10，在高潮时变成了100，
期间也没提盈，后跌落至5。
这时要继续的话，通常会想到两个选择：
A 用这5继续，或顶多入金至一开始起点的10
B 因为经历了100的规模，觉得从5继续太慢/不甘心，所以短时间大量入金继续

我最庆幸的是，自己每次在谷底时都选择了A

资金盈亏的越长期结果，实际上就是自己
真实水平表现的越客观真实评分评级。

如果10变100时，提盈了30变70，再变5，
那么姑且可以认为，自己的水平是“能驾驭35”，
因为客观现实是，你带走了30，加手上还有5。
而不是那个过眼云烟的100。

如果资金从10变100又变5，中间也没提盈，
那么不用多想，说明此时就应该认为，
自己真实水平就是“能驾驭5”，和那个100更没有关系。

这也是大家说的一种“均值回归”：
时间越长，数值越反映真实公允值。

10变100又会变5，中间也没提盈，
说明自己的系统，有对应的盈亏同源的大问题大漏洞，
假如此时短时间立马大量入金，甚至借贷大举入金，
就相当于在试图“跳过付出巨大代价换来的这个劫”，
跳过修复自身漏洞、认识自我强健内心的机会，
这其实同时也就评测反映出了自己身处一种状态：
对自身问题缺乏该有的恐惧、敬畏、尊重，
那么下次、下下次，“劫”依旧会再来找上你。

好比是打游戏，别人送你一个高段位的账号，
不是你自己打上去维持住段位的账号，
你用这个账号打，段位当然就会
“均值回归”到你的真实水平位。

只有自己从低段位打到多少，守住多少，
才是驾驭方法水平和资金规模增减，
两者同步互相应证的，
而之所以还在Crypto这个市场玩，
也是因为在这个市场，
不仅是向下的“均值回归”速度很快，
向上的“均值回归”机会和速度，能比想象的多和快。

1. Private Benchmark Pools

Compare two models across 2–3 benchmarks from different contributors, with up to 30 cases in a single run. You get one aggregate scorecard while contributors keep their test cases and answer keys private. Each model response requires a verified Phala inference receipt. Contributors split 70% of the payment based on how many cases each supplied. Benchmark Pools

2. Private Inference API for Agents

A contributor can turn a private dataset version into a tool with defined inputs and allowed decisions. Think of a warranty tool that returns eligible, ineligible, or needs review. The contributor grants a buyer’s Solana wallet access with a USDC spending cap. The buyer can then create an API key for that grant, and each paid call returns a structured decision, a short reason, and a verified Phala inference receipt. API guide

3. Private Batch Inference

Submit 2–200 cases to one private tool and approve a single USDC payment on Solana. Download one JSON file with each case’s row number, decision, reason, and verified Phala receipt. The export leaves out the submitted inputs. Contributors enable batch access per grant and receive 70% of the payment. Buyers can prepare one batch per dataset per day. Batch Inference guide

4. $DATALOOM payments for confidential answers

Contributors can add a $DATALOOM price to eligible confidential query offers. Buyers can choose $DATALOOM when the offer supports it, and 70% of the payment goes to the contributor in $DATALOOM. Each purchase unlocks an answer from the approved dataset version with a verified Phala inference receipt. Query marketplace

text:
补充一个观察：比特币、黄金往往是宏观层面先行指标，领先于其他资产。
也就是说，黄金、比特币跌，很多时候不是基本面恶化，只是因为他们容易卖出去。
因为缺钱的时候，人们先卖卖得掉的东西。
比特币流动性比黄金好，所以先被砸了一波。现在黄金也开始暴跌，两个一起杀，说明流动性真的出问题了。
身边好多人问什么时候抄底。这种环境里没有底，只有阶段性反弹。
也不用太悲观。
流动性越好的资产，紧缩时越先被卖，压力过去后也越先反弹。
等美股真正哀鸿遍野、人人绝望的时候，就是比特币要反弹的时候。
author: imsongshu
quoted_text:
今日看到的金句：现在的资产价格遍地是黄金——只不过黄金也是大顶。

经典地狱笑话：今天这样的日子，我很庆幸自己把资金分散投资于港股、美股、a股、债券、黄金和比特币、房子、车子，因为这让我能够以八种不同方式亏钱。

为什么会这样？宏观层面的流动性问题。
三座大山压在资产之上：原油、美债、美元指数。

当然这背后的原因有很多：
• 美联储加息预期
• 伊朗冲突导致原油价格持续升高
• AI 产业链疲软
• 民主两党竞选

没有任何一个宏观指标可以进行单独的归因，同时，“归因”本身就是一件很幼稚的点
大部分分析、大部分归因，其实都是在做事后诸葛亮和为失败找理由

归根到底，只有一个问题：流动性。

之前的流动性逻辑是：由于 AI 极度旺盛，币圈的钱全被 AI 吸走了。

可现在的情况是，AI 已经出现疲软，但被吸走的资金并没有流向其他资产，反而在黄金、比特币等极度高流动性的资产上，出现了进一步的流动性枯竭。

那就只可能有一个原因：聪明人早就拿着钱落袋为安了。

人们总是问：资产都在跌，钱去哪了？

很简单：钱在别人的口袋里，以流动性的形式存在，而不是以资产的形式存在。

下面的图是朋友发给我的，并不一定准确，但确实值得关注：
1.石油、美债、美元指数三个指标同时反转的难度很大，但是同时压着，任何资产难以形成真正的突破。
2.这三个指标如果长期下去，就会吸光整个市场的流动性——类似的剧本就是比特币长期盘踞在 5 万左右，各路山寨接近归零。
3.整体的反转难以到来，但是阶段性任何一个指标迎来黑天鹅式的反转，都会催生压抑已久的资金入场，带来周线级别的反弹，各类资产都有布局的机会。

text:
🚨 GoPlus Security Alert: Suspected #XMR1 Exploit on Hyperliquid—Deployer Address Transfers ~5.2M Tokens

XMR1’s deployer address on Hyperliquid transferred approximately 5.2 million $XMR1 to a newly funded address. The recipient then sold the tokens into the order book, receiving approximately 13.3 million USDC. XMR1’s trading price plunged from around $494 to $1 in roughly 35 minutes.

The proceeds have since been converted into approximately 7,300 ETH, most of which has been bridged to Ethereum:
0x1464dacaceb0d511f9964cdac5eba50ea42220bf

XMR1 is a tokenized representation of Monero bridged to Hyperliquid via Wagyu. It is not native XMR on the Monero network.

🛡 Security Recommendations

1. Hold off on large XMR1 trades or cross-chain transfers until you have checked Wagyu’s official channels for updates on the incident and redemption status.
2. If you hold XMR1, monitor order book liquidity and bridge redemptions. Do not judge the asset’s value solely by its collapsed trading price.
3. Verify the asset and token identity before trading. Do not confuse XMR1 with native XMR, and watch out for fake announcements, compensation scams, and other phishing attempts exploiting the incident.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei，Claude 背后这家公司的掌舵人，被问到自己在旧金山长大时是个什么样的小孩。

主持人提到：他爸爸是皮革工匠，妈妈在图书馆工作。

他的原话是：整个第一波互联网革命就发生在我身边，而我完全没兴趣。我那时只对做数学感兴趣，想去理解这个宇宙。我喜欢科幻。我想，我只是对这个世界充满好奇。

接着主持人问他的妹妹、Anthropic 联合创始人兼总裁 Daniela：和 Dario 一起长大是什么感觉？

Daniela 说：他特别聪明。大概初中就在学微积分了，高中时还去加州大学伯克利分校上数学课。我其实更喜欢阅读和艺术。所以在这一点上，我们几乎是完全互补的。

一边是后来做出 Claude 的人
一边是那个对身边互联网热潮完全没兴趣、只想看科幻的小孩

你可以说这是人设
但人设通常不会把“当时真的不感兴趣”说得这么干净❤️

真正的起点，有时不是追热潮，而是对这个世界一直保有好奇🌌

text:
前 DeepSeek-VL 项目负责人、DeepSeek LLM V1 研发成员张博（Tony Zhang），正式公布创业项目 Linger。

Linger 是一款运行在个人电脑上的开源 AI Agent，支持 Windows、macOS 和 Linux。它可以操作已经登录的浏览器和应用，读取邮件、日历及会议记录，并将这些信息整理成长期记忆。它还能主动提醒重要事项，根据用户反馈调整提醒规则，并调用多个 Agent 协同完成任务。

Linger 也支持本地大模型。借助 PolyStrata 推理引擎，配备 12GB 显存和 64GB 内存的电脑，就能以每秒 45.5 个 Token 的速度运行 125B 参数模型。

之前的流动性逻辑是：由于 AI 极度旺盛，币圈的钱全被 AI 吸走了。

可现在的情况是，AI 已经出现疲软，但被吸走的资金并没有流向其他资产，反而在黄金、比特币等极度高流动性的资产上，出现了进一步的流动性枯竭。

那就只可能有一个原因：聪明人早就拿着钱落袋为安了。

人们总是问：资产都在跌，钱去哪了？

很简单：钱在别人的口袋里，以流动性的形式存在，而不是以资产的形式存在。

下面的图是朋友发给我的，并不一定准确，但确实值得关注：
1.石油、美债、美元指数三个指标同时反转的难度很大，但是同时压着，任何资产难以形成真正的突破。
2.这三个指标如果长期下去，就会吸光整个市场的流动性——类似的剧本就是比特币长期盘踞在 5 万左右，各路山寨接近归零。
3.整体的反转难以到来，但是阶段性任何一个指标迎来黑天鹅式的反转，都会催生压抑已久的资金入场，带来周线级别的反弹，各类资产都有布局的机会。

text:
Pre Market Thoughts - 20 Nov 26

Brutal tape from the US close. Asia had a proper punch in the faceled by TAIEX - down 10%, NKY and KOSPI both down 5%. Many stocks on the TAIEX are also at limit downs - with a further short selling restriction. The sales were driven by foreign long sales however.

Across SPX, yesterday's decline was led by consumer discretionary and info tech. The AI/Semis worry has now finally spilled over into growth and demand concerns. WMT and COST have been trading at insane multiples - these are stocks poised to grow maybe 2% a year.... AI and semis ironically are now in the short leg of the momentum basket. SPX has also started becoming alot more volatile into the move.

ANT trading was also the turning point when the pre market pump turned into weakness. The retail bid was there much like the SPCX IPO - however, past the first hour - it dribbled out to nothing. This probably explains the weak price action - i.e there were no more retail baggies! ANT still trades at a 1.2T valuation...while semis are trading like its all over. 

Regarding my post on Knightian uncertainty made a week ago - i would like to stress that the tail scenarios on BOTH sides have gotten more extreme. The left tail case is well elucidated - neos failing, memory companies getting derated on pricing etc. The right tail has also become more explosive - shortage of compute will worsen since many DC builds will NOT be coming into fruition. 

On neoclouds - financing has gotten alot more expensive especially for the smaller neos. Meanwhile even the largest 2 players - CRWV and NBIS is also going through a crunch. If this worsens deep enough, they may even be forced to cut down their capex numbers for next year. Would that be a bad thing? I dont think so. At this point, the entire meta now is to build neos with pure equity and service only the spot demand. Make back your capital in 6 months and free roll the rest. Forget about debt financing.

On memory, while MU and SNDK were hit yesterday, MU has shown some amount of resiliency into this latest weakness. The past few semis cycles had a peak to trough correction of about 50% - this works out to be near the 550-600 levels for MU. SK Hynix itself also beyond 800K KRW is where i think you can buy and just forget about.

On trading - i would not recommend it unless you are extremely nimble. Moves of 15% can fade entirely in 1 hour on both sides. It is not easy to go long at the lows, neither is it easy to go short. Cash for most players is a perfectly fine idea.

The pain in equity risk sentiment has also spread towards precious metals. Gold is 3.5k - Bullionstar - a physical gold retail dealer reported massive customer buying in the morning...well im glad to hear that people are excited to buy at the lows! Big boomer energy!

Meanwhile in crypto, BTC has broke the weekend lows as it grinded down in sympathy with the poorer risk sentiment. Alts have also gotten punished in a lockstep fashion. There are weaker alts and there are stronger alts. I think the bifurcation in their performance can easily tell you which tokens were "crimed" and which ones were not. 

Good luck!

What if your staked SOL didn’t have to sit locked up?

Sanctum co-founder FP on how liquid staking gives you the yield and the freedom to use it:

“If you hold Solana, you can stake Solana with a validator to earn about 5% to 6% per year. Now, the problem with staking is that it locks up your SOL, right? So when you stake to a validator, it’s locked up for 1, 2 days, and you cannot move it, you cannot trade it, you cannot do anything with it.”

“What Sanctum does essentially is provide liquid staking as a service, which allows you to get the yield from the staking while at the same time be liquid with that SOL. We give you something called a liquid staking token, which is an IOU for the staked SOL under the hood.”

“And so you can do things like borrow, lend with your liquid staking token, you can trade it, you can swap it, you don’t have to wait the warm-up or cool-down period with the stake. And so this gives you kind of the best of both worlds.”

It feels demeaning to even have to explain this, but:

Amazon is *valued by investors* at about $2.8 trillion, which means they’re willing to buy, say, a 1% ownership share for $28 billion. It does not mean they have a $2.8 trillion pile of gold coins. It’s based on the value of expected future profits. It’s a prediction, not a tangible thing.

Amazon’s *profit margins* are extremely low. The consumer marketplace (how most people interact with amazon) has margins around 4%. (Amazon Web Services has a much higher margin, but almost all their customers are other giant corporations that Mamdani also hates). Furthermore, much of that marketplace revenue is advertising. Stripping this out, direct, conventional margins on Amazon sold products are essentially zero. Think about what that means: Amazon found a way to run a business delivering goods to consumer’s doors at cost. They’ve already achieved the communist dream for regular consumers: giving you what you want, overnight, at cost. And they make a profit at the same time!

How can they be worth so much on margins that thin? Scale! They serve hundreds of millions of consumers, so making even small amounts per consumer translates into a giant total figure.

But that also means that any reduction in their tiny margins tanks the entire business overnight. If government regulation turns the tiny fraction of profit they skim off their huge gross revenue from positive to negative (which, again, would require only a couple-percent tax) then suddenly that entire fraction of their business becomes worthless overnight. Investors leave, amazon shrinks to being just a cloud services provider, and Americans can no longer get overnight delivery of literally anything on Earth - AT COST - overnight. The reason for the investor valuations -expected future profits - collapses, and their is no dragon hoard of gold coins to loot anymore. Poof. You won’t have redistributed trillions. You’ll have deleted it from existence. 

It’s not that Mamdani doesn’t understand this, or that he does. He doesn’t have a worldview at all. He is a rhetoric machine designed to optimize his personal power. He doesn’t know or care about the concepts of “outcomes” or “consequences”. The final form of a politician in a mass democracy.

quoted_text:
Most people start their careers with some privilege, and many start from zero. I started from minus ₹1 crore, and I did not even know it until my second year at IIT Delhi.

Over the years, that debt took me from a failed placement day to Google, to a ₹2 crore side business, and finally to the startup I had always wanted to build. This is that story.

My father ran a real estate business, and he had invested in under-construction flats from builders like Jaypee and Wave, paying most of the price up front through home loans.

Years went by without the flats being delivered, but the banks still wanted their EMIs on time. So my parents borrowed from friends and relatives, and when that was not enough, from credit cards.

My parents carried all of this debt quietly and tried to shield me from it. I knew we owed money, but never how much.

Then in my second year, collection agents started coming to our house and sitting there, asking for payments we could not make. It stressed my mother a lot, and I could see it on her face every day.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗹𝗶𝘀𝘁

One day, I sat my parents down and asked them a simple question: who exactly do we owe, and how much?

Then I took a sheet of paper and started writing down how much we owed, to every bank, every friend, every relative and every credit card.

The list kept getting longer, and by the time I finished, the principal alone was more than ₹1 crore.

I still remember how heavy it felt while writing each line. That day, I knew I had to grow up quickly and get my parents out of this situation.

I had joined IIT knowing exactly what I wanted to do after college, which was to build a startup. But that sheet of paper changed everything, and the dream would have to wait.

The new plan was to get a high-paying job, pay off everything on that list within two years so that my parents could finally breathe again, and only then pursue my dream of starting up.

𝗠𝘂𝗿𝗽𝗵𝘆'𝘀 𝗹𝗮𝘄

From my third year, everything I did was aimed at that one goal: getting a job at an HFT, which paid ₹50 lakh+ a year.

I was ranked 2nd in my department and had a CGPA of 9.7/10, so I genuinely believed I could get in.

Then day one of campus placements came. I prioritized Tower Research over the other companies, cleared three rounds, and was rejected in the final one.

I was so crushed that I could not perform at the others that had shortlisted me, and by evening, they were all gone.

That evening was really hard. Every rupee I was not going to earn meant my parents would have to carry that weight for longer.

On day two, I took an offer from Cohesity at ₹18 lakh a year. It was a good job, but nowhere near the number we needed.

In July 2019, I moved to Bangalore, stayed in a PG, kept my monthly expenses to under ₹20,000, ate meals at the office, and rarely went out with friends. Everything else, I sent back home.

My friends would talk about investing and going on trips, but I did none of that.

I soon realized that this salary would never be enough. So I set a new target: Google US. Whatever time I could find outside work went into competitive programming, and I soon became a Master on Codeforces.

In January 2020, I started applying to Google and other companies in the US and UK. A few weeks later, COVID hit, and overnight, companies stopped hiring overseas candidates.

The way out I had been working towards for months disappeared.

𝗪𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲 𝗱𝗶𝗱 𝗮𝗹𝗹 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗺𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘆 𝗴𝗼?

Around the same time, I got an offer and joined Spotnana as a founding engineer. I really liked their vision, and I believed that growing with a young startup and holding equity in it could be the big break I needed.

About a year after I had started sending money home, I sat down to see where it had gone.

Almost my entire salary had been spent on interest for our credit card loans. We had not reduced the principal and had not saved anything either. After a full year of hard work and sacrifice, the list was exactly as long as the day I had written it.

That was one of the lowest points of my life. It felt like I was running as hard as I could, just to stay in the exact same place.

Meanwhile, I was giving Spotnana everything, working on weekdays and weekends, and was one of the top performers there.

But when appraisal season came, the raise was still not as high as I was hoping for. I was really disappointed. My equity, though promising, could not help us pay off the debt anytime soon.

I told my manager I would need something on the side to make up the difference. I created a programming YouTube channel and later learned Android development, but neither brought in any money.

𝗜 𝗰𝗼𝘂𝗹𝗱𝗻'𝘁 𝘀𝗹𝗲𝗲𝗽 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗻𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁

During that time, I was talking to one of my college seniors who had joined Google. I told him everything, about the list, my plan and my belief that I could clear it all in two years.

He listened patiently and then told me the truth. If I stayed at Spotnana, it would not take two years, it would take more than four.

He said that instead of being emotional about the company, I needed to be tactical if I really wanted to solve my family's problem. He then referred me to Google.

The next four months were the most focused of my life, and every spare hour went into preparing for Google. When I got rejected from Uber and Coinbase, I was terrified about what would happen next.

But then, Google said yes.

The day the recruiter told me I had been selected for the Google Search team is still one of the best days of my life. That night, I couldn't sleep at all. I lay awake, too happy to close my eyes, thinking about how this would finally change things for my family.

For the first time since I wrote that list, I could actually see a way to clear it.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 ₹𝟮.𝟭 𝗹𝗮𝗸𝗵 𝗯𝗲𝘁

When I joined Google, the list still had ₹80 lakh left on it, and salary alone would take years to clear it.

But Google also gave me something I had not had before: time. So with Google's permission, I started a mobile apps business with my father, working nights and weekends.

In the first three months, we built a bunch of Android apps and games, but could not make any revenue. Then I analyzed iOS versus Android and decided we should build for iOS instead.

So we took the bet. I bought a MacBook Pro for a hefty ₹2.1 lakh, picked our most downloaded game on Android, built its Swift version in six days, and launched it on iOS.

Installs were high from day one, and within a couple of days we turned on monetization. I kept refreshing the dashboard as paying users came in, and within just a few days the game had paid back the cost of the laptop.

And that was just the beginning. Our revenue grew from ₹6 lakh in the first month to ₹24 lakh in the fourth, as we added more games.

I was working close to 100 hours a week between Google and our apps. Over a year and a half, our games crossed 200K downloads, with players mostly from the US, and brought in more than ₹2 crore in revenue.

𝗖𝗿𝗼𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗳𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗹𝗶𝘀𝘁

With that revenue and my Google salary, we finally started crossing lines off the list. This time we were not just paying interest, we were paying back the principal, one line after another.

With every line we crossed off, the stress at home got a little lighter.

In June 2023, we paid off the last one.

The list I had written in my second year of college was finally empty. My parents were free, and after years of waiting, so was I.

As soon as the last loan was cleared, I put in my papers at Google. The apps had left me with enough savings to finally start my own company.

My last day at Google was the day before my 25th birthday, and on 21 July 2023, I woke up with no debt, no job, and for the first time in years, nothing standing between me and the thing I had always wanted to do.

𝗦𝗵𝗼𝘂𝗹𝗱 𝗜 𝗴𝗼 𝗯𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝘁𝗼 𝗮 𝗷𝗼𝗯?

Over the next four months, I built 12 new games, but month after month, none of them worked. And it was not just me. Apple's iOS privacy changes had broken the economics of hyper-casual games.

That November, I remember walking on my terrace, thinking about whether leaving my job had even been the right choice. My parents had started telling me to get a job again. But I had waited far too long for this chance to give it up.

I decided to shut the games business down and hard pivot into SaaS. I started with Shopify apps, only to realize a month later that I had no unique idea and the competition was intense.

I then analyzed around 70 B2B SaaS marketplaces to find the next Shopify app store, found monday, the project management platform, and started Super Workday, building apps for teams using it.

My first app there failed too, because it was too niche. For the next one, I went through the platform's feature requests and picked the biggest unsolved problem.

That one worked. In April 2024, after eight months without any revenue since leaving Google, I got my first paying customer.

I was so happy that day that I emailed him just to tell him he was my first customer. I still remember his name.

After that, I kept launching one new app every month, and the revenue grew sharply. Today, the business runs on autopilot, has 300+ paying customers, mostly in the US, and is close to $100K in ARR.

It also paid for my sister's wedding, and being able to do that for my family made me very happy and proud.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘁𝘂𝗽

With that income stable, I finally felt ready to go after a venture-scale idea and started building an AI executive assistant.

In January 2025, South Park Commons, a Silicon Valley VC, invested $400K at a $5.7M valuation. I cannot explain what I felt the day their offer came. All those years of waiting finally made sense.

My startup journey is still early. Since then, there have been many more ups and downs, and there are still many things to figure out.

But for the first time, I am building the startup I always wanted to build, and I am ready for whatever comes next.

text:
英伟达的财报以及老黄对英伟达的影响在哪里？中期选举后美国的政治生态怎样的变化？Anthropic上市后走势会如何？未来行情走势的变量是什么？多谢Beca周三晚上在币安广场的AMA聊的内容很多，正好也梳理下当时聊的要点？
1、英伟达的财报质量和老黄离开的影响
1）财报本身是超预期、无论是本季的业绩还是下季度和下一财年指引都很强劲。如果28财年，就是明年按照 75% 的增速的话，那它营收能到7400亿美金以上，就相当于 5,000 多亿的毛利，可能是 4,000 多亿的净利润。其实这个体量非常大了。但这次财报没有解决大家最关心的问题，就是老黄。

2）老黄对英伟达的影响是巨大且不可或缺，体现在三个层面：
（1）技术远见，比客户更早看到技术方向。 CUDA 商业回报还不清楚时，黄仁勋就持续投入软件和开发者生态，又推动 GPU 从图形计算进入高性能计算。今天的管理层可以执行已经排好的产品路线，下一次技术方向尚未形成共识时，谁有判断和魄力下注，仍待观察。

（2）让供应商愿意跟着一起赌未来技术方向，英伟达负责设计，一代芯片要如期交付，台积电、鸿海、台达电及材料、封装、测试厂商都得提前投入。老黄的远见和让长期让合作伙伴分享到收益，也积累了兑现承诺的记录。供应商愿意跟着他承担押错路线的风险，才有条件把换代周期从数年压到约一年至一年半。

（3）同时管技术、供应链、人事和资本的全局视野。数十位高管直接向黄仁勋汇报，几位核心负责人只长期深耕各自领域，很难顶得上。

3）老黄不能回归的直接影响
（1）英伟达的技术升级的速度可能会要慢下来。如果未来的人没有这样的魄力、远见，技术方向的选择会多变，产业链上的摩擦越来越大（公事公办）。摩擦最后就会带来时间上的延迟；

（2）产业资本生态萎缩
英伟达投资、承诺采购或为基础设施提供担保，会影响银行和债券投资者愿意借多少钱。克雷斯表示对新增投资、采购承诺和担保会更审慎。个人会担心若以后类似支持越来越少，一些新云厂商到 2027 年的首要问题会从扩张变成生存。也会带来融资更难，资金成本更高。

2、中期选举美国政治生态的变化以及政策的影响
1）这一次中期选举的惨败程度远超以往
民主党参议院拿下56席、众议院超过250席（虽然不是绝对多数，但是离绝对多数也不远了），同时民主党还拿到29个州的州长位子。连德克萨斯州、堪萨斯州这些传统接近百年的铁红州都被丢掉，共和党的基本盘这一次被极大的动摇了。可见惨败程度；

2）中期选举的惨败也极大地削弱了川普的威信和影响力，从“倒黄”事件就能看来，主导改善共和党内部白宫内阁里和国会里的对华强硬派，即使川普一再力保也没能留下老黄。让共和党里的鹰派或者建制派话语权更大了，而前两年川普一统共和党依靠自己的威信和影响力死死压住党内不同意见，现在已经压不住了。

这也意味着之后美国对华AI政策上越来越严格，往技术封锁的路线上走了、有点八十年代里根时代当时中情局局长比尔.凯西主导的对苏联技术禁运的味道。本周川普访深时的良好气氛，可能是未来两年中美关系的相对高点。

3）这次共和党中选惨败，伊朗战争、油价和生活成本动摇了部分选民，数据中心带来的电费、用水和噪音也进入社区政治，都说明民意沸腾。这种情况下、不仅民主党、就是共和党内部也会对过去激进的产业政策做出调整、来迎合选民的呼吁。

4）当然川普也不会完全妥协，他把斯蒂芬.米勒提到白宫幕僚长的位置上，用意很深。米勒对联邦行政法非常熟悉，善于找到各种冷门法律条文来给川普的行为提供法律依据，善于找路洞、钻空子，川普让米勒当白宫幕僚长就是让他来战斗的。未来两年，白宫国会的博弈可能会非常激烈。

3、Anthropic上市及之後的走勢
1）IPO定价还可以、前期流动盘不大，但很快开始解锁。跟SpaceX的走势可能类似，先涨再跌。短期定价还 OK，加上申购的情绪可能有一波走势向上。但大概率最终还是要砸下来，最终就是看砸到一个什么样的位置。

2）如果Anthropic市值之后真的能跌破 1 万亿美金，例如跌倒八九千亿美金，那就是有性价比的位置了。

4、之后市场走势的三个变量
虽然8月底9月初提过一个“秋意渐凉”的框架，高油价、高利率、中期选举前就有大震荡，10月初也聊到高Beta会会跌。但也低估了这次中期选举共和党惨败的程度，这个惨败让市场意识美国居民对通胀、对数据中心建设已经到了如此反感的地步，所以市场对此有激烈的定价。
1）油价、通胀及利率走势；
核心逻辑是，如果美伊能缓和、俄乌也能结束，油价下来通胀才会下来，市场才会预期利率更宽松，否则又要担心明年上半年联储会继续收紧。

2）新的政治生态下AI政策会比预期的还要收紧还是会柔和些；
现在科技杀的这么猛、就是预期新国会生态带来AI基建的大放缓，那就要看明年实际力度比预期的更猛还是更弱。如果民主党搞事力度比现在预期更猛，即使通胀下来了，科技也很难受。但如果比现在预期柔和一些，市场情绪则又起来。

text:
3）AI商业化是不是继续处于加速状态。
而AI商业化则是最底层的逻辑支撑：最近大科技还算比较抗跌支撑指数，是因为市场认为政策再收紧他们还是能扛的，如果数据中心放缓大云厂手里的算力稀缺，但根源还是因为云业务增速在加速中，他们能撑的住。真要大幅度降速，那么通胀好转、政策缓和，也都带不动。

27年初还要面临美国财政预算谈判的时间表。2026 年的临时拨款覆盖至 12月11日，如无续拨12 日起可能出现资金缺口。现在看来两党都希望再通过一个短期拨款法案，让政府运营维持到明年初，把实质谈判留给新国会，这就与2027 年2月前后的债务上限到期也叠加在一起了。

所以明年OpenAI能不能上市？一方面看市场情况、另一方面要看要证明 GPT 能持续跟上 Claude。OpenAI 在八、九月追回了一些差距，Claude 在部分场景仍占优，OpenAI 要把企业端和消费端的采用转成实际收入。
当然，同一家公司在不同市场环境下发行，能拿到的估值可能相差很大。

5、AI之后看哪些方向
1）超大云厂商，
7月份开始提超大CSP的重估，现在依然这么看。如果新的数据中心放缓、过去一年多砸钱力度不断提高的大云厂商未来一年数据中心陆续建好，业绩兑现。同时超大云厂也是广泛的B端企业采用AI的载体。

2）应用端
移动互联网的应用基于AI底层重构，就像X平台、现在X平台跟几年前完全不同。当时X平台几千名员工、现在X只有几十名员工，大量都是AI在背后支撑，现在X整个平台内容分发推荐运营都是AI在驱动、这样算不算已经是AI应用了。
大家一直期望看到AI时代原生应用，但是大概率老树开新花，但是底层已经在大量消耗token。

个人Agent自然是一个趋势、已经很明显了。

然后就是AI医疗健康领域、也值得关注。

text:
I want to address some of the hate surrounding us on CT because I think it speaks to a much bigger problem within this space.

A lot of what you see being said is either exaggerated, taken out of context, or pushed by accounts looking for attention and engagement. There's a psychological element to this. It's called social comparison. When people see others doing well, especially in an environment where everyone is competing for the same opportunities, it's often easier to discredit someone else's success than to confront the possibility that they simply haven't figured things out for themselves yet.

And negativity attracts attention. People are naturally more likely to engage with controversy than with something positive. This creates a vicious cycle where the more hateful or outrageous your accusations are, the more attention you receive. Eventually, people become more interested in tearing others down than actually improving their own circumstances.

What makes this worse is that a lot of this negativity gets amplified by people who would rather spend their entire day talking shit about traders than actually learning how to trade. They make trading look like some impossible game where everyone who succeeds must be cheating, farming, or manipulating something. That mindset is incredibly damaging, especially to newcomers who genuinely want to learn.

I'll be the first to admit that I've been on the other side of this myself. There was a time when I'd see a KOL making money and immediately assume they were farming their followers or had some unfair advantage. Looking back, I realize how much of that thinking came from my own frustration and lack of understanding. It's easier to blame someone else than to accept that you still have a lot to learn.

The reality is that nobody owes you success in this market. There is no shortcut that replaces showing up every single day, learning from your mistakes, finding your own edge, and continuously refining what works for you. Some people will make money doing things you don't understand. That doesn't automatically make them dishonest.

I'm not saying bad actors don't exist. They absolutely do, and people should be held accountable when there's actual evidence of wrongdoing. But there's a massive difference between legitimate criticism and manufacturing accusations because someone else's success bothers you.

There's a concept in psychology called negativity bias: negative information tends to capture our attention more strongly than positive information. And CT has become an environment where that bias is constantly rewarded. A hundred people can quietly do something positive, but one person making a baseless accusation can dominate the conversation for days.
I've always believed that the energy you spend obsessing over someone else's success is energy you could have invested in building your own.

The space isn't bad simply because trading is difficult or because bad actors exist. It's also bad because we've normalized resentment, hostility, and the idea that anyone doing better than us must have gotten there dishonestly.

You don't build yourself up by tearing everyone else down. You just become so consumed by what others are doing that you forget to build anything of your own.

At some point, people need to decide whether they actually want to become better traders or just become better at hating traders.

I know which path I'd rather take.

text:
Anthropic 上市，炸出了演艺圈最懂科技、也可能是最帅的投资人：演员 @aplusk Ashton Kutcher。

他曾做过演员、制片人，后来转型做风险投资人。

如果你不熟，2013 年上映的传记电影《乔布斯》里，他演了年轻时期的乔布斯 😲。

这波 A 家上市，他旗下的 Sound Ventures 早期投的 4.35 亿美元账面直接涨到约 70 亿美元，翻了 16 倍。同时来欣赏一下他的历史战绩：

- 2009 年 Skype：个人投 100 万美元，2011 年卖给微软时翻 4 倍

- 2010 年 Spotify：投 300 万美元，市值冲上 1250 亿美元

- 2011 年 Uber：投 50 万美元，2016 年估值已超 6000 万（翻 120 倍，后高点套现退出）

- 2011 年 Airbnb：首批投 200 万美元，持股峰值估值超 3.25 亿美元（翻 160 倍）

- 2023 年 OpenAI：累计投超 4 亿美元，账面价值约 19 亿美元

- 2023 年 Anthropic：累计投 4.35 亿美元，随着昨晚敲钟，这笔筹码已经变成约 70 亿美元。

为什么顶级创始人愿意给他留额度呢？

一个冷知识是，2009 年 Kutcher 是全球第一个在 Twitter 上粉丝突破 100 万的人。

在那个移动互联网刚起步、获客成本极高的年代，库彻在推特上发一条状态、或者在脱口秀上顺口提一句某款 App，带来的下载量和品牌破圈效应，远超几百万美元的广告投放。

Uber 创始人 Travis Kalanick 和 Airbnb 创始人 Brian Chesky 当年都极其看重这一点。

此外，他本人确实是重度极客。

2009年他投 Skype 的契机是，当时在跟 Demi Moore 异地恋，每天重度使用 Skype 视频通话，直接看出了语音视频通信的好处，随后通过硅谷人脉直接找上门投了 100 万美元。

2008–2012 年间，他几乎把拍戏之外的所有时间都花在了旧金山，跟 Marc Andreessen（a16z 创始人）、Chris Sacca（Uber 早期大股东）混在一起，每天研究产品界面和用户留存；公开报道指出，他甚至能跟工程师直接聊底层交互细节。

而你看看他的个人主页，就知道他还在捣鼓各种科技的东西了。

所以，顶级项目从来不缺钱，缺的是破圈能力和跨界资源；Kutcher 既用好莱坞顶级人脉做资源置换拿到了入场券，又靠专业合伙人团队把“明星流量”真正沉淀成了机构化的长期筹码，自己还能懂一些产品。

该他赚。

text:
The dark side of advertising in the shadow economy

Wagyu just grew right before our eyes. Seven months after launch, the service claimed $700 million in volume, and its founder publicly showed off multi-million dollar swaps. The same visibility made the service popular in the shadow economy. ZachXBT named it as one of the channels used to move funds into Monero after the theft of $106 million from a European entity. After the Lighter attack the service took in about $3.5 million for conversion to XMR in just over an hour.

Popularity like that comes at a cost. A service handling large and sensitive flows is itself a target. First there were the extortionists. The WhiteArmor group demanded $5 million and, when refused, published three months of internal data – 38,628 orders and 10,139 IP addresses. Then came the hack On November 20, 5.2 million XMR1 were withdrawn from the deployer address, and some $13.5 million was stolen. In both cases, the users were the ones who took the hit. Some came looking for privacy, but got their data out in the open. Others were left with a token that dropped from $488 to $1 in half an hour.

Publicity brings customers, but it also brings those who know how to count other people's money and look for weak spots. The more popular a service is in the shadow economy, the less space it has for security mistakes.

AML Crypto is working with @officer_secret on a big investigation into Wagyu: how the service works, where its liquidity comes from, and how it has been used in money laundering schemes. It’s coming out soon.

text:
I agree with Paul here. Revenue matters, but a lot of crypto revenue depends on trading activity that can change quickly.

Take @ponsdotfamily. DefiLlama records roughly $23.4M in protocol revenue in September and $2.48M in October. That's an 89% drop.

When people are making money, they trade more and launch more tokens. When enthusiasm fades, activity can fall across the whole platform.

Sentiment can amplify that cycle. Investors lower their revenue expectations and the multiple they're willing to pay. During a recovery, both can improve.

Pons' 6.7× in this chart uses annualized holder revenue from the latest 30 days. If that revenue rate halves while valuation stays unchanged, the multiple becomes 13.4×.

That's why a low multiple needs context.

Despite the drop, Pons seems planned for something more on the horizon: New launches, established markets, and potentially recurring services like paid data or creator tools.

But launch fees, swap fees, and trading tools can all depend on the same traders. Having three products doesn't help much if all three lose customers together.

For Pons, the most important stuff is that existing tokens keep generating activity (aka: buyback and burn) when new launches slow, and whether new products add revenue that holds up in quieter markets.

I think it will be very interesting once Pons v3 launches soon.

One transformer processes 1–32 frames at full resolution, combining intra-frame and cross-frame attention for depth maps that are *sharp, metrically accurate, and temporally consistent*.

text:
Here’s a question worth asking about any marketplace🔽

What happens when a customer pays for a service but isn’t satisfied with the result?

It’s easy to focus on finding a provider and making payment. The more difficult part is handling situations where both sides disagree.

@termix_ai’s AACP design accounts for this through its evaluator and arbitrator roles.

Evaluators review submitted work, while arbitrators are part of the dispute-resolution process when a disagreement needs further attention.

The protocol also describes verification options involving trusted execution environments and zkVMs.

This is important because a marketplace needs more than a way to exchange money. It needs a process for deciding whether the agreed work was actually delivered.

Without that, trust becomes difficult to maintain.

text:
谷歌 Gemini 强化学习团队成员 Arthur Douillard 透露，他们把 SemiAnalysis 那篇唱衰 DeepMind 的报告打印出来，摆在办公桌上天天看。外界都觉得他们已经掉队，再也追不上了，他们偏要憋着一口气证明对方看错了。

这篇报告发表于今年 8 月，标题叫《Gemini is Cooked but GCP is Cooking》。当时 SemiAnalysis 认为，DeepMind 的顶尖人才大量出走，谷歌云又抢走了大量算力，模型研发已经跟不上 OpenAI 和 Anthropic。甚至直接断言：DeepMind 已经不算顶尖 AI 实验室，基本不可能再追上第一梯队了。

结果才过了三个多月，谷歌连续发布 Gemini 4 Argon、Carbon、Hydrogen 和 Neon 四款模型。Carbon 一度登顶 Artificial Analysis 综合智能榜，最新的 Neon 综合排名世界第三，编程智能体评测更是拿下第一，略微超过 Claude Fable 5.2，完成任务的平均成本还不到后者的一半。

Arthur 特意发帖感谢 SemiAnalysis：「谢谢你们提供的动力。文章里说的那些问题，当时确实存在，但时代已经变了。」

SemiAnalysis 这回也认栽了，晒出一张「谷歌道歉表」，给自己勾选了好几条犯错理由，包括「听信 Anthropic 室友的话」「只看了 X」「没读模型卡」「不认识谷歌的产品经理」，甚至还有「水星逆行」。最后承认自己看错了 Gemini 4。

DeepMind 创始人哈萨比斯也亲自下场接梗：「道歉收下了！不过你们漏勾了一项：低估了这支超强的 Google DeepMind 团队。」

text:
Can Sky ecosystem go to zero?

Noticing that a lot of FUD mixes up USDS, sUSDS and stUSDS.

And Sky is complex.

First, remember that MakerDAO rebranded to Sky. DAI still exists, while USDS is the new shiny stable.

The system is now backed by a mix of crypto collateral, other stables and RWAs ($6.5B backed by $9.5B in collateral).

So what matters for USDS is 1) that there's more collateral for DAI and USDS issued, and 2) if people can redeem.

No issues here.

You can also deposit USDS into savings and receive sUSDS, which earns the Sky Savings Rate. Currently around 3.8%.

The yield comes from interest paid by borrowers, RWAs and strategies run via Spark etc.

But then there's stUSDS. The FUD Zone.

Here your USDS backs loans against $SKY collateral.

I totally get the FUD here.

Founders borrowing against their own token isn't a good look and we still remember the drama with Curve's Egorov borrowing against CRV and getting rekt.

But if you deposited to this strategy, you should've known the risk.

Now there's no liquidity to withdraw and they depend on repayments or new deposits.

Is current 25% APY worth the risk to deposit? I want to see Sky here come up with a strategy to repay the loan first.

Dumping SKY doesn't help.

So Sky announced extra buybacks for 7 days, but buying SKY doesn't repay those loans.

stUSDS holders get rekt first if the loans go bad. That helps protect USDS.

TLDR: USDS isn't backed by stUSDS tokens. And your sUSDS savings aren't deposited into this lending pool.

text:
I made NFTs that leave you if you don't use them for what they're for.

They're called Wearers, 1,000 pixel ghosts on Robinhood Chain, and the one thing they ask is to be your profile picture on OpenSea. OpenSea lets you set an NFT from a verified collection as your account pfp and shows it in their API, so I wrote a keeper bot that reads that field for every holder once a day, at an hour it picks at random and keeps to itself until the round is over.

If you hold Wearers and none of them is your pfp, you're at risk. Each day the bot takes a fifth of those holders at random, and from each of them it moves one Wearer to a random holder who does wear theirs, by calling claim on the contract. If you wear even one, everything you hold is safe, and any day you might get another one for free. A Wearer that just changed hands gets 24 hours of grace so the new owner has time to put it on, and if OpenSea doesn't answer for someone that day, the bot just skips them.

The art lives fully onchain. Every Wearer is a 40 by 40 pixel image stored inside the contract along with its 12 traits, so there's no server or IPFS behind it, and the whole thing is a plain ERC721 minted through SeaDrop.

Mint is on November 24, 1,000 in total, one per wallet in each stage. Collectors go first at 12:00 UTC with 250 for free, then FCFS at 12:30 UTC with the next 250 for free, and whatever is left goes public at 13:00 UTC for 0.001 ETH.

If you collected anything of mine in the last six months and still hold it, you're already on the collectors list, and you can check it on the OpenSea mint page.

Trong khi đó giá Bitcoin hôm nay đang quanh 69.000 USD. Dù tính theo ước tính nào thì thợ đào vẫn đang lỗ.

⛏️ Tổng sức mạnh tính toán của mạng lưới đã giảm đáng kể, từ hơn 1.15 ZH/s xuống còn khoảng 940 EH/s.

Thời gian trung bình để tạo ra một block đã kéo dài lên 12 phút 36 giây, cao hơn nhiều so với mục tiêu 10 phút của giao thức Bitcoin.

Điều đáng chú ý là nhiều công ty đào lớn không đơn thuần tắt máy, mà đang chuyển hướng toàn bộ hạ tầng sang phục vụ trung tâm dữ liệu AI.

Core Scientific, MARA, Hut 8, Cipher Mining đều đã bắt đầu dịch chuyển. Bitdeer thì bán sạch 943 BTC trong kho dự trữ, hiện đang giữ 0 BTC.

📊 Trong 14 công ty đào lớn nhất tại Mỹ, chỉ có 2 công ty còn đào có lãi. Lần điều chỉnh độ khó tiếp theo dự kiến khoảng đầu tháng 4, và khả năng cao sẽ tiếp tục giảm.

Lịch sử cho thấy những đợt "thanh lọc" như thế này thường xảy ra trước khi thị trường ổn định trở lại, nhưng lần này còn có thêm yếu tố cạnh tranh từ AI, nên câu chuyện có thể sẽ khác.

quoted_text:
--- 5 Things To Focus On In The Coming '5 Year Bear Market' ---

Alright lads... let's say this bear market is the 'new normal'- as I keep seeing on the TL- and we really do have five brutal years ahead of us...

Here's five things I'd do as a result:

1) Get your expenses as low as possible

We are no longer in the era where you can outearn your own stupidity via sheer force of will. 

Nobody has any idea if their job or business model will still exist in 2-3 years...

If you can get your expenses way down you will be way less stressed, and well-positioned for victory rather than defeat. 

If you're young I'd even do the van life thing or other more 'radical' approaches... same thing if you're older... 

Quit worrying about looking 'normal' and embrace your schizo side. 

2) Dive down rabbit holes and explore new stuff

AI is rapidly disrupting the economy, but the flipside of this is that there is more opportunity than ever before. 

Its hard to know what areas or actions are going to lead to downstream success, so you really just gotta explore for the sake of exploring.

To paraphrase the famous Cobie quote, you need to achieve a good balance between skepticism and curiosity, where you open yourself up to fortuitous W's, but don't go too far out on the limb via an unhelpful level of optimism either. 

3) Find a non-economic hobby or passion that you love

For me this is BJJ and Muay Thai. 

For others it could be mountain climbing, or surfing, or any number of things. 

Its important to have things to base your self-worth on other than just money or 'trading' or 'investing' though. 

And stuff like this is also a great avenue for meeting people and building friendships and etc. 

4) Create art/content/etc and put it on social media

This doesn't mean you need to try to become an 'influencer' or go all-in on social media or etc...

It just means that you should be making sure your creation vs consumption ratio is healthy- that you are 'creating' rather than just 'consuming'... 

And then you should put that stuff you are creating on social media, as this is the way we humans primarily connect and share things nowadays. 

Indeed, if AI and robots end up doing all the 'real work' then it is likely that social media will become a bigger and bigger part of the global economy. 

This 'creating' could be art, it could be code and tech stuff, it could be defi protocols, it could just be schizo-poasting or TikTok-maxxing, it could be custom goods you sell on Etsy - the important thing is that you are CREATING and not just CONSUMING.  

5) Focus on the things that matter

At the end of the day the numbers on the screen and the car you drive and the house you live in are not that important. 

What is important is family, and friends, and health, and memories. 

Life is incredibly, tragically short... and when you get to the end of it you don't want to be filled with regret that you took those things for granted...

Go out and IRL-maxx and make your memories my dear anon!

Conclusion

I am perennial optimist, but I know there's lots of concerns about what the next five years will look like right now, so it got me thinking about the above...

For point #6 I'd probably say 'keep stacking assets', and I'm sure there's a lot of other good things to remember too. 

And hopefully we will all stack massive W's during that time anyway 💪

But yeah- 

Thanks for reading and please share any thoughts you have on the subject and RT if you enjoyed!

text:
My small @boros_fi experiment shows 39.71% estimated fixed APR on $340.48 of capital.

The terminal also shows two BTC perps, a rate position and 1,182 USDT borrowed. Passive income, my ass.

Here is how the trade works and how to open the same structure.

Install @pendle_fi official Arbitrage with CrossEx app. It runs locally on Mac or Windows. Enable CrossEx on Gate, create a Gate API key with Cross-Exchange trading access and withdrawals OFF, then connect your Boros wallet and agent key. You need margin for both CrossEx and Boros.

In Opportunities, select the BTC @HyperliquidX - @Gate spread, choose your size and maturity, then click Open this strategy. The wizard locks the rate on Boros first. It then opens a BTC perp long on Gate and an equal short on Hyperliquid through CrossEx.

The two perps largely hedge BTC price moves. Their funding payments still differ. My short spread position on Boros pays that floating difference and receives a fixed rate in return.

My position has 0.0788 BTC on each leg, about $10.1k notional per leg. The margin shown is $205 for the Gate long, $130 for the Hyperliquid short and $5 for Boros. That is why a 2.78% annualized spread can turn into a 39.71% estimated APR on roughly $340 of capital.

The current pair runs from Oct 30 to Nov 27. The spread works out to about $21.5 gross over 28 days by simple math. The terminal projects $10.29 profit for this pair after modeled costs. The cost stack gets paid first. The most consistent yield farmer here is the fucking fee schedule.

Across my account, the screen shows +$20.83 since Sep 27 after $1.73 in borrowing interest. That includes earlier positions and the value of this open trade. It is not $20.83 of settled profit from the current pair.

The fixed rate only helps if all three legs survive. The USDT borrowing cost can change. A price gap between venues can hurt the perp hedge, and a jump in the funding spread can liquidate the Boros leg before Nov 27. If you use the limit-and-hedge execution mode, the local app must stay running until both perps fill.

I will judge the trade by what remains after expiry or rollover, not by the APR screenshot.

text:
This year we’ve had a clear jump in model capability where instead of telling agents precisely what to do, it’s better to use these systems to solve problems you can’t easily define yourself. 

A year ago you’d need to very clearly tell agents the how to design and develop your product idea, or there was almost no chance of success. Now, increasingly, the agent likely can come up with a better implementation than you’d have thought of because you can have it connect the dots between a far greater solution space than you can. 

This will be increasingly true in basically every domain of kneeler work. We’re going to see this impact in finance, legal, life sciences, cyber, and many other spaces where no person can hold onto all the available relevant industry knowledge to think of the best solution. 

Ultimately this is going to reshape our relationship with AI and how we deploy agents in our work. It won’t be about explicitly telling them, but instead giving them goals and enough freedom to pursue them in the best way they can.
author: paulg
quoted_text:
Most of us are managing agents all wrong

We setup agents to do things we already know how to do, then tell them exactly how we want them to do things

This is treating agents like interns

That was fine earlier this year when models were not as capable

But ask yourself - if you just hired a 130 IQ employee, would you just have them do things you already know how to do and tell them exactly how to do it?

If you’re using frontier models with agents, you want to give them goals and objectives for things you don’t know how to do, then empower them to do the things

Hire agents as experts, not interns

Yes you should still have some agent interns to automate boring work to free up more of your time

But if you’re not using agents to do things you don’t know how to do then you’re missing out

Let them go figure out how to do the things that expand beyond your skills and capabilities just like a good leader would when hiring a team

text:
$DRV 目前的 FDV 已达 3.7 亿美元，年内暴涨近 5 倍。
但这并不妨碍 Derive 是一款难用的产品。

我让 Grok Bot 搜集了 X 上关于 Derive 的吐槽，结果显示：
▌最集中的抱怨是流动性，尤其是订单簿深度不足，以及小额仓位和临近到期的平仓困难。
▌第二多的抱怨是充提和客服。
此外，Derive 现在已经不是一款单纯的期权产品。过去 30 天，其永续名义成交约 10 亿美元；期权若看权利金约 1.24 亿美元，若看名义本金则约 32 亿美元。

不过，Derive 也证明了链上期权大有可为。之前采访有人问 Jeff，如果不再做基础设施、重新做应用会选什么，他的回答是最可能会看期权。

1/ 链上期权的机会，与下一代产品的样子
既然如此，下一代期权产品该长什么样？
从产品形态来看，@leaps_finance 就在很大程度上切中了这个破局点。
它的核心思路是彻底抛弃让散户头大的订单簿。用户不需要自己去盘口里找对手盘、算滑点，只需选好心理目标价和期限，后台做市商就会直接过来竞价（RFQ 模式）。
页面会直观显示你当下能立刻拿到多少权利金，点击确认，真金白银直接打进钱包。

这种设计把普通持币者丝滑地转化成了“期权卖方”，对新手极其友好：
手里有现货：做备兑看涨期权，约定一个更高的目标卖出价，先落袋一笔权利金；
手里有稳定币：做现金担保看跌期权，约定一个更低的理想买入价，边等抄底边赚利息。
而且它采用的是欧式期权，输赢只看到期那一天的结算价。这意味着即便中途行情剧烈震荡、插针触及了行权价，仓位也绝不会被提前触发。

2/ 不做另一个 Derive
Leaps 的定位非常克制且聪明，它不打算再去卷一个像 Derive 那样大而全的专业期权交易所，目前支持的标的更聚焦，核心就是帮用户的闲置资产安全地卖出期权、提前变现时间价值。

最后，Leaps 由 RPS AI 团队开发。这个团队原来在旧金山做 AI 应用，2024 年起专注 Solana 链上做市。
投资方/支持方包括 Wintermute Ventures、Delphi Ventures、Permanent Ventures 等。

别再说链上没有新东西了。

text:
Claude is officially OUT of my workflow!

I canceled one sub a while ago, and it looks like I'm going to say goodbye to the second one too. Gemini 4 Neon is doing a really good job.

But even though it's this good, I still don't trust any single model. For now, Gemini 4 Neon is the planner, but it consults with my local models and goes back and forth until they reach an agreement.

Here's how it works:

- Gemini writes the plan.
- Then it launches 3 subagents in parallel to ask other models for reviews, fixes, and additions.
- Each subagent talks to one model:
• GLM 5.3 Flash (running locally)
• Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (running locally)
• DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (running locally)

When they're done, Neon writes a merged report combining everything. It also verifies every claim the other models make.

In most cases, the local models find issues. Each model has its own blind spots. Remember, no model is perfect, no matter which one it is. It's an absolute must to consult different models before executing a plan.

Once the final plan is set, the planner (Neon in this case) manages multiple workers to execute it. Right now I'm using GLM 5.3 Flash (locally) for all execution.

Sui链新进展值得看看
我觉得这种需求很常见，你持有BTC并不想卖，手头又需要些稳定币作为流动资金，关键是如何很好的实现
Hashi给了个好的实现路径——把BTC存进比特币网络协议地址，然后在 #Sui 链上1:1拿到由这些BTC支持的hBTC，hBTC能拿去当抵押品，目前Fluid已支持用它借USDC，还完钱解除抵押之后
再按协议赎回，hBTC被销毁，底层BTC在比特币网络上释放回来，它的整个过程BTC没有转链变成Sui原生资产，一直留在比特币网络，只是存入后不再由你的原私钥单独控制，Hashi本身提供的是基础设施作用，具体借贷，金库或策略由各服务商自己执行

这条路径的核心价值在于什么——想继续持有BTC的人，多了一个不用先卖出就能获取流动性的选项，当然借款会有利息产生，抵押率和清算风险，不是无成本的

除了借贷，金库方向也在推进中
Upshift的金库基础设施已上线，HoneyB正通过它推出USDC与hBTC相关策略等等，这些其实说明hBTC有机会成为不同金融产品的共同抵押品基础（金库不是统一收益产品，也不能完全保证固定回报）

同时机构这边也有大的动作
Anchorage Digital的托管和钱包提供了接入路径，整体合作网络超过20家，并有超过5亿美元的资本承诺，这些是机构了解产品后作出的承诺，说白了机构是非常看好这些场景应用的

对Sui来说，如果hBTC能稳定的成为可组合的抵押品，链上的借贷，稳定币和资金管理应用就有机会服务新的用户和资本，我想对于最大的加密货币BTC来说，相当于提高了整个BTC在Sui链的资本的利用率，解放资本生产力，当然还需要更多的时间验证

想继续跟进更多Hashi的实际使用数据和Sui链上金融进展，可以关注 @SuiNetworkCN

New episode of Where Capital Meets Compute:  @wayne_nelmz, co-founder and CTO of @OrnnExchange, on why financing a GPU still takes a five to seven year contract, and what a liquid compute market could change.

His argument: the biggest buyers of compute often have the least credit history, so lenders end up underwriting the asset itself. If years three through six can be hedged against a price index, a one or two year contract could be enough to finance the GPUs. In his words, "liquid compute markets will actually accelerate the pace of GPU deployment." We also get into why Ornn builds its indices from cleared transactions only, why he thinks the shortage is GPUs rather than data center space, and the comment Ornn filed with the CFTC arguing for compute futures on exchange.

This episode is sponsored by @ComputeDesk, which builds financial infrastructure for compute traders.

Their Compute Indexes publish daily reference prices for GPUs including the H100, H200, B200 and B300, and their platform helps teams price, procure, hedge, finance and settle compute from first offer to final agreement. Learn more at https://t.co/Ohcj2ux9Vw.

text:
欧洲央行警告：AI 正在重演 2008 年次贷危机的危险剧本？

最值得警惕的，不是 AI 公司烧钱，而是整个行业正在形成一套越来越复杂的债务与资金循环。

几个数字相当惊人：

▪ 4 万亿美元： 文中估算的 AI 相关隐性债务及长期承诺规模
▪ 270 亿美元： Meta 路易斯安那州数据中心合作伙伴承担的融资规模，相关债务并不直接计入 Meta 自身借款
▪ 3650 亿美元： 微软未来数据中心租赁承诺规模
▪ 1000 亿美元： 英伟达拟向 OpenAI 投资的最高金额，而 OpenAI 又是英伟达芯片的重要客户
▪ 380 亿美元： 摩根大通与三菱日联为甲骨文相关项目安排的贷款规模

最值得思考的是英伟达与 OpenAI 的资金循环：

芯片供应商投资 AI 公司，AI 公司再向供应商采购芯片。

这种安排不必然意味着虚假需求，但如果终端收入无法跟上资本开支，风险就可能沿着 AI 公司、算力供应商、债权人和金融市场层层传递。

更值得关注的是，欧洲央行担忧的并不只是银行直接贷款，而是基金、保险公司等机构通过科技股和企业债承担的间接风险。

2008 年的问题是，没人真正看清房地产风险被转移到了哪里。如今 AI 融资越来越复杂，市场是否也正在低估风险最终由谁承担？

当然，AI 长期合同、租赁承诺与金融债务并不完全等同，不能直接把今天的 AI 投资潮判定为下一场次贷危机。
author: BlockBeatsAsia
quoted_text:
Désolé de jouer les rabat-joie juste après l’IPO d’Anthropic. Mais j’ai lu le dernier rapport de stabilité financière de la BCE, et il fait froid dans le dos.

Son constat : la façon dont on finance l’IA ressemble un peu trop aux subprimes.

Pour faire tourner leurs modèles, les géants de la tech construisent des data centers gigantesques. Cette année, la facture devrait avoisiner les 725 milliards de dollars, un montant tel que leurs bénéfices ne suffisent plus à suivre.

Alors ils empruntent.

Et c’est justement dans leur manière d’emprunter que la BCE retrouve des mécanismes qui rappellent la crise de 2008.

---------

👉 Une partie de la dette est invisible

Imaginez que vous vouliez faire construire une maison sans avoir l’air endetté. Vous demandez à un ami de contracter le prêt à votre place, en lui promettant un loyer pendant vingt ans. Sur le papier, aucun crédit à votre nom. Dans les faits, cet argent, vous le devez bel et bien.

C’est le montage choisi par Meta pour son centre de données en Louisiane : 27 milliards de dollars empruntés par une société partenaire, et absents des comptes de Meta.

Chez Microsoft, ce sont 365 milliards de dollars de loyers promis pour des centres de données qui ne sont même pas encore en service.

Au total, la BCE chiffre ces dettes "invisibles" à plus de 4000 milliards de dollars.

👉 L’argent qui tourne en rond (infographie ci-dessous)

Nvidia fabrique les puces. Il va investir jusqu’à 100 milliards de dollars dans OpenAI (ChatGPT), qui se sert de cet argent pour... acheter des puces Nvidia.

Un peu comme un concessionnaire qui prêterait à ses clients de quoi acheter ses voitures, avant de se féliciter de ses ventes record.

Résultat, tout le monde a l’air de vendre énormément, alors qu’une partie de la demande est financée par le vendeur lui-même.

👉 Des promesses, surtout

D’ici 2030, OpenAI s’est engagé à dépenser quelque 600 milliards de dollars en puissance de calcul. Son chiffre d’affaires 2025 ? 13 milliards. Si les revenus tardent à venir, c’est toute la chaîne qui risque de vaciller : OpenAI d’abord, puis ses fournisseurs, puis ceux qui leur ont prêté.

👉 Qui a prêté ?
Les Américains, pour l’essentiel. Pimco, le gérant d’actifs, a mis environ 10 milliards de dollars dans un seul centre d’Oracle. JPMorgan et le japonais MUFG ont monté pour Oracle un prêt de 38 milliards, et il leur a fallu des mois pour trouver d’autres prêteurs avec qui le partager.

Et l’Europe dans tout ça ?

Nos banques ont prêté environ 75 milliards d’euros au secteur, soit à peine 1% de leurs crédits aux entreprises, un risque que la BCE juge limité. Le point faible est ailleurs. text:
people saying vcs stopped investing in crypto and moved to ai are wrong.

look at how much crypto startups raised each year (jan 1 to nov 18, so we compare the same dates):

> 2020: $2.6B
> 2021: $23.6B
> 2022: $21.2B
> 2023: $5.5B
> 2024: $7.1B
> 2025: $16.6B
> 2026: $14.3B

the top years were 2021 and 2022. vcs cut back hard in 2023 and 2024, then came back in 2025.

2026 is 14% below 2025 on the same dates, but it’s still double 2024. galaxy’s run rate points to about $19B for the full year, close to 2025’s $20B.

so there’s no real downtrend. vc money goes up and down with the market, like it always has.

to be fair, ai does get most of the vc money now. but that money didn’t come out of crypto.

ai startups raised about $490B in the first 9 months of 2026. crypto raised about $12B.

crypto was ~4% of all vc money in 2021, and ~4% again in 2025. this year it’s ~2%. crypto’s money is close to 2025. the difference is ai, which already raised 7x more than in all of 2021.

one openai round in q1 ($122B) was bigger than every crypto vc round from 2020 to 2025 combined ($89B).

what did change in crypto is who gets the money.

59% of this year’s money went to just 29 companies, in rounds of $100M or more. in 2020 there were only 2 rounds that big.

the small bets are the ones disappearing. seed and pre-seed rounds peaked at 462 in 2021. there were still 397 in 2024. this year: 176.

1,228 different investors put money in a crypto round this year. in 2024 it was 2,602.

so where does the big money go? prediction markets.

prediction markets raised $3.1B this year. that’s almost as much as all of crypto vc in 2020 ($3.4B for the whole year). kalshi alone took $2.2B, and its valuation went from $2B in june 2025 to $40B last month.

meanwhile nft and gaming raised $4.2B in 2021, across 174 rounds. this year: $79M, across 8.

why is this happening?

the old vc trade was simple. buy a seed round cheap, wait for the token to list, sell to retail. that trade is broken. the median top 250 coin is down 78% from its ath.

so vcs now buy what looks like a normal company: exchanges, prediction markets, payments. companies with revenue and a shot at an ipo.

crypto vc didn’t die. it turned into fintech vc.

if you’re building a token with no revenue, the 2021 money isn’t coming back.

quoted_text:
Claude is officially OUT of my workflow!

I canceled one sub a while ago, and it looks like I'm going to say goodbye to the second one too. Gemini 4 Neon is doing a really good job.

But even though it's this good, I still don't trust any single model. For now, Gemini 4 Neon is the planner, but it consults with my local models and goes back and forth until they reach an agreement.

Here's how it works:

- Gemini writes the plan.
- Then it launches 3 subagents in parallel to ask other models for reviews, fixes, and additions.
- Each subagent talks to one model:
• GLM 5.3 Flash (running locally)
• Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (running locally)
• DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (running locally)

When they're done, Neon writes a merged report combining everything. It also verifies every claim the other models make.

In most cases, the local models find issues. Each model has its own blind spots. Remember, no model is perfect, no matter which one it is. It's an absolute must to consult different models before executing a plan.

Once the final plan is set, the planner (Neon in this case) manages multiple workers to execute it. Right now I'm using GLM 5.3 Flash (locally) for all execution.

I'm also going to test Gemini 4 Hydrogen and see how it performs.

text:
I agree with Paul here. Revenue matters, but a lot of crypto revenue depends on trading activity that can change quickly.

Take @ponsdotfamily. DefiLlama records roughly $23.4M in protocol revenue in September and $2.48M in October. That's an 89% drop.

When people are making money, they trade more and launch more tokens. When enthusiasm fades, activity can fall across the whole platform.

Sentiment can amplify that cycle. Investors lower their revenue expectations and the multiple they're willing to pay. During a recovery, both can improve.

Pons' 6.7× in this chart uses annualized holder revenue from the latest 30 days. If that revenue rate halves while valuation stays unchanged, the multiple becomes 13.4×.

That's why a low multiple needs context.

Despite the drop, Pons seems planned for something more on the horizon: New launches, established markets, and potentially recurring services like paid data or creator tools.

But launch fees, swap fees, and trading tools can all depend on the same traders. Having three products doesn't help much if all three lose customers together.

For Pons, the most important stuff is that existing tokens keep generating activity (aka: buyback and burn) when new launches slow, and whether new products add revenue that holds up in quieter markets.

I think it will be very interesting once Pons v3 launches soon.

text:
Six years ago I had just arrived home from our very first Breakpoint in Lisbon, buzzing, full of hope for the future and a belief that we were doing something special.

The entire team was about 40 people at the time. We didn’t have an events team. The core team ran the stages, hosted everything and every speaker was very early stage ecosystem teams. Mainnet wasn’t even a year old.

And while it was clear to us that we were about to do something huge, we remained the underdog in the eyes of the industry for nearly 6 years.

This year, it was obvious everything had changed. Every major financial institution in the world is paying attention to Solana and was represented at the event. We dropped the beta tag. Finality is down to milliseconds. Solana dominates tokenized equities ( 🤯). Trillions of dollars have settled on our chain.

We are no longer the underdog. We are the overdog, and everyone being honest with themselves knows it. We have a major slice of every vertical and narrative. Teams that were once small and mighty are now industry giants, collaborating with the institutions they only once could dream of.

The next few years will look a lot different as we continue this journey, but we must never get complacent.

I’m looking forward to seeing where this path takes us, and I’ll see you all when we bring Breakpoint home to San Francisco next year to celebrate even more success. Keep shipping and keep winning. 

Solana
