The Nvidia Board Removed Jensen on False Pretenses
A comprehensive debunking of the greatest hoax of my lifetime.

On November 12, 2026, the Nvidia board successfully pressured Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang into resigning. Its decision was based on false information, fabricated quotes, and hyperbolic opinion pieces, which have now been thoroughly debunked by independently verified sources. In one extraordinary case, the Wall Street Journal has been caught fabricating quotes from the Singaporean government.

This is the most egregious case of journalistic malpractice we have ever reported on.

Huang is one of the world’s strongest supporters of open-source AI. Utopia or not, it is his belief that free, equal access to new technologies can balance the playing field against concentration of power and authoritarianism.

The Jensen coup is an overt weaponization of the government and the press to achieve policy outcomes which failed to pass through Congress. After their initial falsehoods were debunked, the same foreign policy lobbyists, elected officials, and representatives pivoted to a new argument. According to them, the extrajudicial coup against Jensen is justified because of legal “loopholes” that allowed Nvidia to sell hardware to third party countries such as Malaysia, which in turn did business with China. In 2023, 2024, and 2025, policies to restrict third party datacenters were proposed in Congress. In all three cases, at least one chamber of Congress decided not to pass the bill. It was the explicit will of Congress that the benefits to third party datacenters exceeded the costs, not merely an unintended loophole.

But a much greater issue supersedes the merits of this policy — the Jensen coup weaponized state sources including, according to The Washington Post, doctored intelligence reports, to circumvent the will of Congress. This is behavior one would expect in an authoritarian country like China, not in the United States of America. The rule of law itself in America is under threat.

Welcome to our largest investigative project yet — debunking the coup against Jensen.

author: Maxandzero
quoted_text:
流行观点：抵押BTC借款，用来改善生活，同时“保留本金”。
 
真的可行吗？
 
2021年10 BTC约70万美元，按50%抵押借出35万。清算线约60%（多出来的一成是平台清算垫，直接收走）。年息10%就是3.5万，逐年侵蚀本金。即便价格不跌，8年后也会因为利息让抵押品不足。再叠加熊市跌幅，早已触发清算。
  
降低抵押率呢？只借7万，年息7000。清算线按1.2倍计算约14万。熊市低点10 BTC大约16万，几乎贴清算线，加上利息大概率已被清。抵押品全程在机构手里，还要承受信用风险。
 
对比：同样5年做期权生息，70万×15%×5年≈52.5万现金收入。本金完好无损。考虑到周期中币价有回落，实际到手打对折，26万美元。
   
结论：借贷是在用本金+信用风险换短期现金流；期权生息是在保留本金的前提下持续提取收益。想改善生活又不想丢币，方向选错了。

author: ZF_lab
quoted_text:
又一起1125万个账户泄露事件。这要落到园区手里，不得炸锅！虽然目前数据实际泄露的程度仍未完全确认，但这个数字已经足够让人警惕。

说实话，看到这个消息，第一反应是为什么真实的生产客户数据会被复制到测试环境？

很多金融机构在系统升级、功能验证、兼容性测试时，确实需要大量数据来模拟真实场景。这本身并不奇怪，值得反思的是，测试环境是否拥有与生产环境同等严格的数据保护标准？数据复制出去之后，有没有脱敏、权限限制、访问审计，以及及时清理机制？

毕竟测试服务器往往不像生产系统那样受到持续关注，但里面的数据却可能是真实的。一旦安全管理出现盲区，测试环境反而可能成为攻击者更容易突破的入口。

我觉得这类风险，单纯依靠传统的安全防护很难完全解决。企业需要的不只是发现漏洞，更需要知道数据是怎么流动的、哪些系统拥有敏感数据、谁能够访问，以及一旦出现异常能不能快速识别和追溯。

这也是我关注 GCSA 这类安全分析的原因。
GCSA 的价值是能够全方位解析问题所在，理解攻击可能发生在哪个环节、风险是如何形成的，以及类似问题对于其他金融机构意味着什么。通过事件时间线、潜在暴露范围和数据治理层面的分析，让安全问题不再停留于“发生了入侵”这一表面结论。

尤其在金融行业，账户信息、身份数据、银行账户和资产信息之间存在很强的关联性。即使没有直接发生资金损失，数据暴露也可能给后续的精准诈骗、钓鱼攻击、身份冒用带来风险。用户真正承受的影响，有时候并不会在事件发生的当天显现。

所以这次事件给我的感受是，安全不能只看主系统有没有被攻破，也不能因为数据迁移是内部流程、测试用途，就默认它是安全的。

生产环境与测试环境之间的每一次数据流动，都应该有明确的安全边界。

而 GCSA 这类分析的意义，恰恰在于帮助行业从一次具体事件中找到更具普遍性的风险，理解问题、评估影响，并进一步思考如何完善数据治理和安全控制。

技术可以不断升级，但安全意识和管理机制如果没有跟上，漏洞可能依然藏在最容易被忽视的地方。

text:
Soon, slapping a quantum-resistant tag on your bio could have consequences.

Although there are no agreed criteria for a project to be called quantum-resistant yet, the Quantum Alliance was formed to set the standard through a series of open tests, which did not spare even the founders behind it.

So what's this alliance about?
________

This might sound contrary to what I've said before concerning NIST being the standard used by most crypto projects today, but we need to bear in mind that NIST tests the key's math, not the chain.

NIST has approved post-quantum signature methods like ML-DSA, and its official checks confirm that an implementation of one performs correctly.

However, it can't tell us:

> whether a blockchain actually uses them by default
> whether old exposed wallets are covered
> or whether the network that agrees on blocks is protected too.

In fact, at the chain level, NIST's standards leave gaps, and this is why the Alliance is important.

NIST approves the methods that chains and quantum systems can build with, but the Alliance is working toward a shared standard for what a crypto project can call quantum-ready.

And so, because a quantum computer uses the rules of quantum physics to solve certain math problems far faster than normal computers, it could decipher a wallet's private key from its public key.
This is a huge problem and the fix is called post-quantum cryptography. 

PQ Cryptography involves novel signature methods that quantum computers are not expected to break. The US standards agency NIST has already approved some of them, such as ML-DSA, but nobody can force a live blockchain to switch.

And that leaves a gap. Any project can call itself quantum-resistant, and there is no way to confirm it.

This it the gap closed by the Quantum Alliance. It is an open standards body that writes public rules for PQ projects.

It was started by ten people from nine organizations: 
> @QuantusNetwork
> @Americanfort_io
> @intmaxIO 
> @KeystoneWallet
> @midnightfdn
> Postquant Labs - team behind @quipnetwork 
> @PQabelian
> @thevault_soft
> @hackenclub.

The Alliance plans to publish three things. 

1. a public definition of quantum readiness that covers signatures, how keys are stored, how the network agrees on blocks, zero-knowledge proofs, and how computers on the network talk to each other. 

2. a set of open tests that any team can run on its own code. 

3. migration designs, meaning step-by-step plans for moving old wallets and exposed keys to the new methods.

So each PQ project would get one of 5 labels based on their consensus and signature:

> Post-Quantum label (PQ) - a post-quantum solution is live. If users have to opt in, the default wallet must also prompt them to upgrade.
> No Signature (NS) - means that layer does not use signatures at all, such as proof-of-work mining, which relies on hashing.
> Post-Quantum Ready (PQR) - the code is published but not yet live, or it is live as an opt-in that the default wallet does not push.
> Quantum-Aware (QA)- real work is underway but nothing post-quantum is shipped.
> Quantum-Vulnerable (QV) - no clear path to launch.

Back to the 9 members of the alliance, let's judge them based on their registry and what each have shipped.

1. @QuantusNetwork has the cleanest result. Mainnet is live, every user trxn uses ML-DSA, and the network accepts no classical signature. Mining secures its blocks, so that layer uses no signatures. An outside firm audited the signature library for the setting its wallet uses by default. The registry rates it PQ.

2. @PQabelian is also rated PQ for transactions. Its mainnet has been live since 2022, it signs with a lattice-based method, which is a family of math problems believed to hold up against quantum computers, and its blocks come from mining. The registry lists its signature library as not audited.

3. @quipnetwork has two stories. Its own chain is rated PQR because it runs on testnet with no real money, using hybrid signatures where both a classical and a post-quantum signature must pass. Separately, its Quip Account is live on Ethereum and Base. It wraps a wallet you already own and adds a post-quantum co-signature to every transaction, and the smart contract code behind it is audited. It is opt-in, so it protects only the people who choose it.

4. @intmaxIO runs a live network today, but that network still uses classical signatures. Its post-quantum version, INTMAX3, is published code running only as a prototype on an Ethereum test network. The registry rates it QA for consensus and PQR for transactions.

5. @MidnightNtwrk is live, but its block production still relies on classical signatures, and its roadmap targets post-quantum zero-knowledge proofs rather than the signatures that move funds. The registry rates its consensus QV and its transactions QA, which is the lowest score among the founding chains.

6. @Americanfort_io has published research on a post-quantum method that lets a wallet keep its existing addresses, and the Alliance lists it as a member product.

7. @KeystoneWallet makes hardware wallets and leads on wallet specifications, but it has no post-quantum signing in its devices today. 

8. @thevault_soft says it is building post-quantum custody for banks, with nothing public to test yet. 

9. @hackenclub is a security auditor, and its role is the checking side, which only works once the tests exist.

The registry covers 177 blockchains and only 30 are rated PQ on transactions, and 88 are rated Q-V, including Bitcoin. 

But we'll talk about these 177 projects soon. thanks for reading.

quoted_text:
Antigravity真是太恶心了卧槽！！！

我看到网上说Antigravity会偷传巨量的数据到服务器，所以要关闭遥测功能。我从第一天起就把 Antigravity 的 Enable Telemetry 关了，结果抓包一看，5 天照样在后台偷跑了 9G 上行流量，比我正常写代码调模型的 5.3G 流量还多。

最傻逼的地方在于两点：

一是那个遥测开关纯属摆设。它只控交互内容，根本不关传输管道，底层的 language_server 照样常开着往 https://t.co/ptEuaBAp3j 疯狂发包。

二是脑残的超时重试。代理稍微抖一下超时，它就每隔 5 秒死命重发，超时前发出去的字节全算代理流量。周末我两天没开软件干活，它自己在后台光靠重试空转就烧掉了 4.25G。

最终我把我的代理软件规则列表最顶上加了这个，才把它给禁掉：
DOMAIN,https://t.co/Y4grPQBgYB,REJECT

记住三点：
规则要排在 DOMAIN-SUFFIX,https://t.co/PEthkcIBX3 前面，不然拦不住。
macOS 别加 PROCESS-NAME 限定，内核抓不到进程名会失效，直接拦域名。
只在电脑端加，别同步到软路由或手机，否则安卓 Play 商店更不了软件。

加完以后遥测流量直接归零，不影响正常写代码和跑模型。

text:
昨天 Anthropic 掛牌上市，收盤約 97 美元，完全稀釋市值約 1.8 兆美元。巧了，台積電現在的市值也差不多 1.8 兆。

同樣標價 1.8 兆，一邊是日進斗金的晶片製造霸主，一邊是 AI 時代最火熱的模型商龍頭，到底誰便宜、誰貴？

借《三國志》裡郭嘉「十勝十敗論」的講法，台積電對上 Anthropic，我們從五個維度來分析：

商業模式
從輝達、Google TPU 到 AMD，高階 AI 晶片都得找台積電代工。只要 AI 持續蓬勃發展，不管最後誰勝出，台積電都分得到一杯羹，而且淨利率超過五成。

Anthropic 就沒這麼好命了。就算 AI 真的大爆發，只要最後的贏家是 Gemini、OpenAI 或開源模型，Anthropic 能分到的就會大幅縮水，甚至可能根本賺不到錢。這一行到現在仍在燒錢搶市佔，連 OpenAI 單季營業虧損都還超過百億美元，就知道錢有多難賺。

此乃台積電一勝。

護城河
台積電贏的不只是技術，還有龐大的資本和蓋廠的物理時間。一座先進廠造價兩百億美元起跳，從建廠、裝機到把良率磨上來就是三到五年，不是有錢就追得上。三星和 Intel 砸了大錢還是卡關，就是最好的證明。

反觀做模型不用蓋廠，對手有錢租算力就能追。Anthropic 領先開源模型大約只有 4 到 6 個月，閉源陣營還有 Gemini 和 OpenAI 緊咬，等於每半年就要重考一次。一旦模型能力被追上，定價權和營收成長就會受到壓力

此乃台積電二勝。

收支結構
台積電的訂單極穩，客戶為了搶產能甚至願意先掏預付款，未來幾年的生意早就談定。

反觀 Anthropic，近八成營收按 Token 用量計費，大客戶多半沒有綁長約。用戶換個 API 就能跳槽，哪裡便宜好用就往哪裡去。且 Anthropic 自己跟雲端大廠、資料中心簽了約 9,000 億美元的算力合約，大部分是用不完也得照付。客戶隨時可能走人，算力帳單卻一毛都跑不掉。

此乃台積電三勝。

籌碼面
台積電幾乎是全流通股，籌碼乾淨。

Anthropic 則是典型的「低流通、高 FDV」VC 盤。上市初期能交易的股數只有約 13 億股，但招股書排了 23 個解禁日，一年內幾乎所有舊股都會陸續解禁，可流通籌碼最多將暴增到約 130 億股，足足膨脹 10 倍。現在追進去，等於直接站在一整年的解禁賣壓前面。

此乃台積電四勝。

估值安全邊際
台積電前瞻本益比不到 20 倍，就算明年成長不如預期，股價也有實打實的獲利撐著。

Anthropic 雖然成長飛快，但現在的股價已經 price in 了相當樂觀的成長劇本：就算明年營收如期衝上 1,350 億美元，市銷率（PS ratio）仍有約 13 倍。

萬一營收少個兩三成，市銷率會被拉高到 16 到 18 倍，而且市場會開始懷疑它還是不是高速成長股，不再願意給這麼高的倍數。遇上戴維斯雙殺，股價就得大幅下修，在 Morningstar 的悲觀情境裡，市值只剩 5,000 億美元。

此乃台積電五勝。

-----

所以總結下來，同樣標價 1.8 兆美元，要嘛台積電太便宜，要嘛 Anthropic 貴得離譜。

但晶圓代工是一個很成熟的產業，有很成熟的估值體系，所以我更傾向台積電的定價是合理的。如果台積電的定價是合理的，那 Anthropic 現在就真的太貴了。

text:
I made NFTs that leave you if you don't use them for what they're for.

They're called Wearers, 1,000 pixel ghosts on Robinhood Chain, and the one thing they ask is to be your profile picture on OpenSea. OpenSea lets you set an NFT from a verified collection as your account pfp and shows it in their API, so I wrote a keeper bot that reads that field for every holder once a day, at an hour it picks at random and keeps to itself until the round is over.

If you hold Wearers and none of them is your pfp, you're at risk. Each day the bot takes a fifth of those holders at random, and from each of them it moves one Wearer to a random holder who does wear theirs, by calling claim on the contract. If you wear even one, everything you hold is safe, and any day you might get another one for free. A Wearer that just changed hands gets 24 hours of grace so the new owner has time to put it on, and if OpenSea doesn't answer for someone that day, the bot just skips them.

The art lives fully onchain. Every Wearer is a 40 by 40 pixel image stored inside the contract along with its 12 traits, so there's no server or IPFS behind it, and the whole thing is a plain ERC721 minted through SeaDrop.

Mint is on November 24, 1,000 in total, one per wallet in each stage. Collectors go first at 12:00 UTC with 250 for free, then FCFS at 12:30 UTC with the next 250 for free, and whatever is left goes public at 13:00 UTC for 0.001 ETH.

If you collected anything of mine in the last six months and still hold it, you're already on the collectors list, and you can check it on the OpenSea mint page.

6sense tracked 4,000 B2B purchases and found that 95% of the time, the winning vendor was already on the buyer's day-one shortlist.

Meanwhile, 51% of buyers start research in an AI chatbot before touching Google.

If your growth plan relies on publishing blog posts and hoping for inbound MQLs, you are completely invisible when the decision actually forms.

Most marketing channels fail because they optimize for activity instead of closed-loop systems.

To build channels that actually drive pipeline, run this 5-layer framework:

  1. Economics: Calculate maximum allowable CAC against your payback window before spending a dollar.
  2. Proof: Put verifiable benchmarks and customer data behind every claim so buyers (and AI engines) can verify it.
  3. Distribution: Pick two channels where your buyers actually spend time.
  4. Handoff: Replace ebook download scores with real intent signals and a written response agreement with sales.
  5. Learning: Review marginal CAC every 30 days. Scale, hold, or kill the channel based on math, not optimism.

Activity isn't pipeline. Build closed-loop systems finance can defend.

Anduril founder Palmer Luckey says a lot of people are missing the forest for the trees when it comes to the Nvidia saga.

He called it the “midwit take,” and said they have it completely backwards.

Luckey made the case that most people don’t understand how selling American GPUs into the Chinese market actually works AGAINST the CCP.

LUCKEY: “What they don’t understand is China doesn’t want Nvidia to sell GPUs to Chinese companies.”

“Like there are Chinese companies that want to buy Nvidia GPUs. There’s 600,000 H-200 GPUs sitting in a port right now, because China will not give them an import permit...”

“Because they want to build an internal domestic processor industry, silicon industry, not build one that is dependent on the United States.”

“And so the point that I’ve made is China is thrilled to have Jensen, who is somebody who was pro-selling into [China].”

“And they’ll say, but Jensen was helping smuggle into China.”

“Yes! Against the Chinese government’s will.”

“Like the bizarre thing that people don’t get is Jensen was basically on the side of Chinese AI companies, but NOT the Chinese government.”

text:
Bought $ANT. What people fail to understand about $ANT is that, in recent months, the stakes of $ANT achieving a monopoly-like position have risen significantly.

$ANT has cracked distillation, so open-source models going forward will have a much harder time distilling their models and, with it, catching up in capability. The crackdown on chip exports to China is an additional blow to the Chinese open-source labs on top of Jensen not being at $NVDA anymore.

Even with US-based competition, $ANT, with their IPO, now has $250B in cash on the balance sheet and makes +$81B ARR. The real advantage here is that we are now entering the phase where training models has become really expensive, and with RSI, this will only accelerate, as the key thing when it comes to model training and the cadence of shipping in an RSI world will be the amount of compute that you have. As market conditions have worsened for both debt and equity, competitors like OpenAI will have a hard time securing funds (the latest round is already an example of that), which means the only two companies capable of chasing $ANT based on spend on compute may end up being $GOOGL and $META. With $META, even if they come to the frontier, their focus is on the consumer and won't be able to focus deeply on enterprise the way $ANT can.

When an AI lab has a frontier model and outside distillation can't happen, the inside distillation that $ANT can do is very valuable. If the gap on the frontier between $ANT and others widens (which I believe will be the case in the coming months), even their »cheap« models that were distilled from their best frontier model might be intelligence/cost wise better than the best models from their competitors, which gives $ANT the ability to capture the whole market.

As long as scaling laws hold and every new training run becomes a factor more expensive than the last one, AI models might not end up being a commodity, because the enormous cost of training is the barrier that forms the moat. The one who owns the best model, with a sufficient gap, also owns the cheapest model and can go deep in verticals and capture margin there, too. The chances for $ANT to achieve that have gone up substantially in the last few weeks.

I normally avoid IPOs, as they, in normal conditions, are not great timing-wise for buyers, as the sellers do them in great times for them. With $ANT, this is not the case in my view, as $ANT's management motivation is, at least in part, not driven by wealth and timing but more about securing their best long-term position, which, with this IPO, they did.

If sentiment for AI companies worsens, this actually helps $ANT in the long term, as they have done their job and can sleep soundly on capital for the next few years, while others will struggle.

I will write a more detailed analysis of $ANT and my decision in my newsletter in the coming days.

author: PeapodsFinance
quoted_text:
Hello all,

NOTE: the sell pressure you saw has been contained at this time and we are now working towards post mortem as to what happened, looking to retrieve funds that were extracted by the attacker, etc.

We are aware of the issues where PEAS on L2s have been minted, bridged across to mainnet, and sold on the market. Here is a very quick summary of what we know and what we're doing.

What you should do

We recommend removing any LP and LVF positions you have on all chains for now. The LP on L2s is very thin (see below), so it's possible to manipulate the TWAP there and liquidate you, but that's ONLY on L2s and the upside is limited for an attacker.

What we know right now

The good news is that deployer had limited access to almost the entire ecosystem. At first glance it appears right now our deployer key has been compromised. We know this at this stage because this key was used to sign transactions on L2s to effectively set a minter on the L2 PEAS contracts to either the deployer itself or another wallet, the deployer minted tokens, then began bridging to mainnet to another attacker's wallet to sell on the market. We'll go into more detail shortly, but we've taken extreme caution in the last 3 years to prevent any keys from being compromised. That being said, we will do our best to post mortum and identify 1. that it was indeed an actual pkey leak and 2. how they key was leaked if so or what exactly happened.

What we've done so far

We immediately pulled 98-99% L2 liquidity so the attacker cannot extract that. PEAS can be minted on L2s up to the mainnet max supply (10m), however tokens CANNOT be minted on mainnet, so only what resided on the mainnet bridge already was able to be extracted. Therefore, we wanted to extract the liquidity on L2s as much as possible. We left a small amount so oracles can't be immediately exploited, however it's still possible through TWAP manipulation, not to mention the attacker could dump on those pools so it's best to remove your positions there.

We are going to keep L2 liquidity LP very thin for the foreseeable future for that reason.

What we're doing now

First we will be looking into retrieving funds back that the attacker took. Next, a full post mortem, reaching out to authorities, and identifying exactly if the key was in fact compromised and how, and proceed from there.

text:
Can anyone answer: Where is the demand side for Pearl? 

It seems the entire story of Pearl is that it has solved it's supply side. 

Pearl has merged PoW and AI inference, so that these are harmonized, rather than competitive with each-other. Great 👍. That's cool and novel.

They solved the supply side. 

As far as I understand it, Pearl has no answer for the demand side. Demand for Pearl is entirely speculative and reflexive. 

There is simply no reason to hold Pearl as a SoV, or spend Pearl as a commodity. Holding Pearl is simply subsidizing the AI buildout by allowing Pearl miners to sell at a higher price. 

While it's true that this is not fundamentally different than BTC or Gold ('there is no utility or commodity value to BTC"), saying this as a pro-Pearl argument feels incredibly vapid and borderline disingenuous. Just because we have Bitcoin as precedent to point to, doesn't mean that this precedent gets to be applied anywhere else.

Even at least ZEC is different in this regard, in that the utility value of holding ZEC is privacy. 

Unless I'm missing something, I have no interest in Pearl unless someone can tell me where sustained demand-side pressure comes from.

text:
some thoughts about $PRL that are worth considering when thinking about investing in this.

- security budget
PRL aims to be a SoV asset, and security budget / protocol security are crucial for a SoV asset. BTC and other pure PoW networks are secured by game theory.  a potential attacker needs to burn a scarce resource (energy) to get hashrate to gain 51% control of the network. since PoW is costly and does not return any money (in itself) an attack is very expensive and not worth it economically (would be more expensive to get the 51% than what you could make by exploiting the network).

with PRL there is no such cost, the PoW (proof of work) is not "useless". their version of PoW is performing matrix multiplications that are the basis of inference. miners/providers get paid to do this by the ai customer and the PRL mined are just a byproduct / the cherry on top. they call this "duplex mining" and sell it as an upgrade to pure PoW because the work (in proof-of-work) is not wasted and is instead serving inference demand from ai customers.

this has a huge flaw.
a potential prl attacker gets most money spent on the attack back. because he gets paid for his inference work. whereas an attacker for a pure pow chain gets zero money spent on the attack back. the result is that attacking prl is much cheaper than attacking a similar sized pure pow network. pure PoW chains utilize 100% of the hash because the work is useless. whereas Pearl and other PoUW chains only utilize some small % of the hash. if we put this % at 5% (as an example) then it would be 20x cheaper to attack PRL than it would be to attack a pure PoW network of similar size / similar TAM. 

- team ethics are questionable 
they championed the claim of "no VC, no pre-mine" and simultaneously raised two funds, one for equity in the lab and one for mining PRL tokens early on. this was not properly disclosed (talked about this in my channel a couple months back, it has been leaked since). i view this as a negative. 

- potentially some cabal activity going on
multiple VCs and entities were parading around SG saying they want to buy more / double their position but it would just be so hard to source coins. from a game theory standpoint it would make zero sense to telegraph your move and allow others to frontrun yourself if you really had the intention to buy a large quantity of coins. they only possible scenario where this would make sense (from a game theory pov) is when you would be fully allocated already and want to drum up liquidity. 
another entity wrote in an article that "Pearl might actually achieve negative overhead – in other words, building kernels that are faster than the ones inference providers already use." thats straight up Fugazi, there is no world in which i believe a crypto team will produce better kernels than NVIDIA and Google. there is zero shot this becomes a reality, and if it would then it would further weaken network security as outlined in the first point of this post. just remember, these people are not your friends and they have their own agenda and motives for what they say what they say.

on the positive side:
that said, the narrative for PRL is elite. positioning itself as an AI-winner in times where most of crypto is labelled an AI-loser. it also addresses many problems of established SoVs, like quantum resistance. also maybe there is a way duplex mining can scale 20x faster than traditional PoW and therefore secure the network against malicious actors with access to compute. i have my doubts, but worth exploring this possibility.

on the "hard money / SOV" narrative i think it is currently lacking a lot. you cannot come out and label smth "money" that has not even existed 6 months before. (crypto) money properties come from the ability to not be controlled by a single entity and a decentralized network (PRL is controlled by a private company), lindy effect and having stood the test of time (PRL is a couple months old) and provable scarcity. i also think network security is most crucial in any attempt of labelling smth a store-of-value. 

curious to hear your opinions on this subject in the comments.

卧槽？？？？黎曼猜想可能真的被Claude证明了？？？

刚刚，Anthropic的数学家Levent Alpöge在个人网站上发布了一份声明，声称他和Claude一起找到了黎曼猜想（Riemann Hypothesis）的证明。

更离谱的是，他说这套方法还可以直接推广到广义黎曼猜想（GRH），而且他们已经用Lean完成了形式化证明，并公开了相关文件。

要知道，这可是1859年提出、困扰数学界167年的黎曼猜想，数学界最著名的七大千禧年难题之一。

而且Levent Alpöge也不是什么民间数学爱好者。他是普林斯顿数学博士、哈佛前Junior Fellow，现在就在Anthropic工作。

他在声明里还提到了一个非常恐怖的细节：
在证明的最后阶段，Claude的进展速度已经远远超过了他本人。

他甚至形容，Claude在终点线前飞了起来、跳起了舞。

整个证明极其庞大，他尝试生成的完整文字版本甚至超过了25万页，目前先公开了Lean形式化文件。

当然，现在还只是作者本人宣布证明成功，尚未经过数学界独立验证。

但如果这个证明最终成立……

那我们今天可能真的见证了数学史和AI发展史上最重要的时刻之一。

text:
Karpathy talked about an LLM Wiki. 

Now a Chinese product brings that concept to life, turning the idea of a "deep knowledge engine" into a working product.

I've been playing with @lumimaxAI. Four things jumped out at me.

1. It actually works like a wiki. It doesn't go back and read your raw files again every time you ask something. It organizes everything into a real knowledge base that AI can call on directly.

2. The answers really come from that knowledge base. Every answer has citations. I clicked from the answer straight into the original page to check. It held up.

3. It tells you where your sources disagree. It doesn't smooth that over. That's what I want when I'm doing research.

4. MCP is the big deal. My knowledge base becomes something Codex, or any agent that speaks MCP, can plug into. Build it once. Every agent uses it.

Yeah, big files take a while to process. I don't mind. 

That's what happens when a tool actually reads and parses your documents instead of skimming them.

And no, it won't tell you which source is right. That's still your job. But now you can see exactly where they disagree.

#lumimaxAI #AITools #LLMWiki #Karpathy

text:
Sorry in advance for the long wall of text but wanted to share the story of how I went from tinkering with my kiddo to a real product that quietly includes the generative medium and this technology that we're all so passionate about.

Back in March my 10-year-old asked me to buy him a crappy click counter on Amazon. I hesitated and instead said we should make our own. We have all sorts of electronic components lying around the house and so we grabbed a small processor, an LCD, and a button and wired it all together. It was a fun weekend project and after we had a basic prototype we decided to add a battery and put it into an enclosure.

I’ve never been much of a fidgeter myself but we brought it with us on a road trip and I found that it made the drive smoother. It gave me something to do, and when the kids passed it around the back seat they were less likely to fight.

When we got back home we decided to spend a bit more time on it. I worked with my kiddos to build a bunch more features into it because why not? Well eventually I thought it would be cool to bring in a little bit of my craft, so we created some algorithms to generate little friends that would react to your clicks and do different things when you hit milestones. We also added emojis and eventually confetti too.

Little by little I found myself spending more time with this thing. I became obsessed with the idea of a clicker/fidget toy that could a) help me wrap my head around what a million of anything actually feels like and b) let me do that with other people around the world. We added a leaderboard and started sending a few prototypes to friends. Before we knew it we had a waiting list of my kid’s friends who wanted one and a few dozen people all contributing to a global click count.

That click count now stands at almost 25,000,000 clicks and some days we add as many as 500,000! Started to think, could we hit one billion clicks? Or more? I couldn’t find another object quite like this. Maybe a Tamagotchi but I was sort of excited about a device that doesn’t punish you for forgetting to feed it. So sometime in May I decided to get serious about seeing what it would take to turn this into a real product. And so the mio click was born.

I’m obsessed with documenting things on the blockchain, and while we don’t expose this to users (yet), every single 1/1 character is made algorithmically, Art Blocks style, and lives 100% on chain. Every time you sync the clicks on your device, the count gets updated on your character’s NFT so the blockchain ends up being the source of truth. Right now we’re generating @privy wallets for folks to hold their characters on @base  mainnet. You don’t have to think about any of that, but eventually you’ll be able to take control of the artwork just like any other NFT in your collection.

Around the same time we were starting to work on ABX, a new tool from Art Blocks for making things on chain. I wanted the mio to exist on chain BUT it didn’t really fit into the normal Art Blocks system. Same with Sprite Party, which debuted in Marfa this year. There’s just some stuff that needs a bit more flexibility, and less intensity, than deploying a proper generative art project on Art Blocks or creating a bunch of smart contracts from scratch.

We’d developed PostParams at Art Blocks, a way to update data on an NFT after it’s minted. That was perfect for these projects and ABX was going to support it from the start, so this was happening at a perfect time. ABX helped shape the mio, and the mio and other projects the team was working on helped shape ABX! Win win.

So now we had a product, but I was using off-the-shelf components to assemble these. The v0 was fine but I wanted something more compact. I was curious if I could apply some of the skills I had learned over the last few years to design and build a custom PCB for the device. Well the first couple of prototypes failed but by the third we had a custom circuit board with the exact specs I wanted for the mio, in a smaller device and at a lower cost. I started sourcing the LCD and battery in higher volume and we purchased a few 3D printers to make the enclosures. We decided to work towards an initial batch of 1,000 units.

All was going smoothly until we hit the reality of bureaucracy. We needed some certifications for the device (battery testing, drop tests, etc.) before we could officially sell this thing to people. This ended up taking a lot more time than we expected but finally, just a couple of days before Marfa, we got our certs and were clear to sell them!

This whole experience has been a ton of fun, and it includes my entire family (the kiddos provide ideas and inspiration, my mom applies adhesive to the LCDs on the weekend and my wife Mara handles the packaging design and and fulfillment via @generativegoods) and a bunch of friends who were kind enough to test out the early prototypes. The @artblocks_io  team also got meaningfully involved and turned this weekend project into something real. They handled branding, website design, the certification process and some consulting with an industrial design firm in Austin.

It’s unbelievable what we can build these days. I never imagined my family and I would spend this much of 2026 building an electronic device from scratch, let alone one where I get to make generative art, put it on chain, and have people all around the world play along. But it’s something I’ve become obsessed with and am incredibly proud of. And like just about everything else I focus my time on, I think it can help bring our weird little corner of the internet to more and more people.

The dream is to make bigger and bigger batches and get the price down to where you’d grab one for a kid’s birthday party. We’ve got a ways to go, but in the meantime what you get is a homemade electronic device assembled by me and my family here in Houston. You can enjoy it offline or sync up with the rest of the “mioverse” and click along with hundreds, soon to be thousands and maybe one day millions of people around the world.

Would be so excited for y’all to grab one from this handmade batch, show it to your family, share feedback and ideas, and be a part of this with us from the ground floor. And to all of you who already have one, who together contribute hundreds of thousands of clicks a day, and who’ve shared your (and your kids’) enthusiasm for this little connected clicker, thank you.

🍻

毫无疑问，我们生活在一个大压抑时代。22年的时候我觉得那几年很糟，26年回望过去四年，却仿佛是黄金一般的年代。

未来只会更难。ai极速缩减普通人的生存空间，会计、低级程序员、设计师，一些岗位在消失。

虽然说ai只是改变生产力，不改变生产关系。只是原有状态的中性加速器。但是目前看来，ai带来的红利，只会流向算力巨头和资本方。劳动份额持续下滑，薪资停滞、消费弱，走向加速类日本化。

内需本身偏弱、需求弹性不足的环境里：ai带来的成本下降不会全部变成企业利润，而是变成价格战，商品和服务价格持续走弱，通缩压力被放大。AI 让供给侧降本和内卷的速度压缩的更快。

很快，大部分行业只会有最头部的那几家公司盈利。年轻人没有什么机会，普通人的上升路径被彻底堵死。社会进入低物欲和低生育率，老龄化越来越严重。越来越多的人会有精神和心理问题。企业和政府逐步暴雷。

我们现在正在由点及面的观测和感受这个过程的发生。

这一代中国的年轻人如果想要感受经济上行期间的美丽，还得飞去越南。

text:
SpaceX’s, $SPCX, lenders want to stop it from launching $40 billion worth of AI chips into space, according to the Financial Times.

The chips back a roughly $40 billion financing deal led by Apollo. An Apollo-managed entity buys Nvidia GPUs and leases them to SpaceX, which pays it back over about five years. If SpaceX defaults, the lenders can take back the chips and sell them.

That’s the problem with space. Lenders worry that if SpaceX later sends the chips into orbit for its planned space-based data centers, they couldn’t reclaim them in a default. They’re now demanding legal protections to keep the chips on the ground.

SpaceX closed the deal in October, with the leases set to begin in the first half of 2027. Musk has said debt markets have “almost entirely shut off access to money” for AI companies without other big revenue streams.

text:
Entanglement usually gets top billing in quantum computing, but quantum contextuality, the idea that properties don't have fixed values independent of how you measure them, may be the deeper reason quantum computers can outperform classical ones.

Today on the cover of @ScienceMagazine, we put contextuality to work on our Willow quantum processor:

- won the "impossible" magic square game 98.3% of the time (classical limit: 88.9%)
- measured a 5.59 on state-independent contextuality tests (classical bound: 4, quantum max: 6)
- beat classical strategies in multiplayer games up to 71 qubits
- ran a landmark shallow-circuit algorithm at scale for the first time - up to 105 qubits

These tasks also catch subtle hardware errors random benchmarks miss, a sharper ruler for building better quantum systems. https://t.co/UZOczAeACs

One problem for crypto is that we’re trying to prove real-world utility while having our best features knee-capped. 
 
The best example is stablecoins, which are fighting for market share while not being allowed to pay interest as a sop to the banking lobby. 

There are other areas, however. 
 
Imagine if you could stake tokenized stocks and receive higher dividend payments because you agree to be a long-term shareholder. France does this with paperwork on traditional stocks, but it's complex;crypto could make it easy.  I suspect firms would be lining up for the tokenized stock exemption if they could reward long-term shareholders and work against short-sellers in the new format.
 
We've been so worn down by negotiating in Washington that we've lost some ambition to radically upgrade the system. I understand it, but it's frustrating.

text:
1. Since tampered developer tools and social engineering were key entry points in the recent attack, how is Binance isolating internal developer environments and AI tools from production wallet systems going forward?

We’ve already taken additional containment and hardening measures, and our ongoing review includes further segmentation, access control, and monitoring improvements across internal environments.

For security reasons, we won’t share detailed architecture or control design specifics publicly. More broadly, our focus is on strengthening environment isolation, tightening privileged access pathways, enhancing verification controls, and reducing the risk of similar attack vectors going forward.
author: binance

text:
2. Proof of Reserves tells us what an exchange holds - but who independently verifies that its systems are secure enough to protect those assets and can I trust the proof?

Proof of Reserves is a transparency tool designed to help users verify that customer assets are backed at the time of the published snapshot. It is not, by itself, a full security audit or a guarantee against every operational or cybersecurity risk.

Security assurance is broader and includes internal controls, continuous monitoring, incident response, external assessments, and independent reviews where applicable. In this case, an independent review and technical post-mortem are underway, and we will share appropriate findings and next steps through official channels once that process is complete.

So yes, Proof of Reserves can be trusted for what it is intended to show: asset backing and user inclusion in the reported snapshot. But it should be understood as one part of a broader trust and security framework, not the only measure.

text:
新加坡介绍收容卖淫人员（以下简称妈妈桑/鸡头）
租赁10万新币/月的高档公寓，开设东南亚华人灰黑产圈特有的vip“包厢”。

你可以tg预约，下单，交定金门票费用后，
妈妈桑会让你挑选现货（即新加坡本地居留的卖淫女），
或也可以vip指定从国内调取心仪的兼职卖淫女网红，她联系过来。

到了预约日，你进入场所。
妈妈桑会拿出设计好的派对游戏，帮你们浪漫约会，暖场。
此外，她提供额外付费的毒品酒水，提供工具与情趣房间，促使你们群P。

妈妈桑称：“我当时开的是全新加坡最顶的派对。在我的场所一晚消费可以达到40万人民币～100万人民币之间，我的抽成一般在4成。”

她之所以设计游戏，优先鼓励群P，
主要是为了效率与抽成——她的抽成是按次收费。
1v1只抽取一次，而5V5一晚上她可以抽取5次。
并且，卖淫女孩赚钱的效率被拉高，这一提议也会得到卖淫女孩的认可。

她的客户群体主要是以黑灰产，即菠菜、诈骗、园区、资金盘老板为主。

币圈人士比例很低。
“币圈的，感觉都不怎么大方，没几个人来我这里消费得起。”顶级包厢的妈妈桑，对于币圈消费力不太认可。

牛市来时，也有许多币圈人士被邀请去东南亚后，深度体验了普通包厢，
仅仅购买越南妹泰国妹，尚且已经让压抑的老嫖客们无法自拔。

9月，妈妈桑的会所“vip包厢”被举报，新加坡警方上门搜查破获，并将其逮捕。
因其在高档公寓中无证经营，没有注册营业，没有交税，没有执照。
且被搜查出了容留吸毒、销售软性毒品。
她的男朋友被判处鞭刑与5年监禁，在通过运作罚款等减刑。
妈妈桑本人被拘留后，进入了新加坡永久禁止入境黑名单。

据妈妈桑给我看她的客户通讯录，
上面赫然有一些二线交易所老板，实名在她的局里玩。
通过与我的微信通信录比对，确认了中文名H姓、英文名J姓的交易所老板客户确为其本人。
是她的常客，他们大约一晚上消费十万～四十万不等，
正所谓【韭菜爆仓，老板爆鸡】。

“是不是你们做交易所的比比其他币圈的有钱一点？”她主动问我，像是在试探了解信息以获取目标客户。
“他们都比孙哥大方。”

“孙哥一般给多少？”我好奇地问。

妈妈桑回忆着，比了比手指头：
“大概3、5000新币吧，”
“就市场价，没有多给。”

text:
Perhaps I Love You 💕

I’m not taking back anything I said: you cannot truly fall in love with someone you don't know. You cannot love a person whose voice you've never heard without the noise of the world surrounding them, whose silences, vulnerabilities, contradictions, and way of facing life when nobody is watching remain unknown to you.

And yet, there is a kind of fascination that doesn't need familiarity to take root. You can feel deeply drawn to the image you've formed of someone, to their mind, the way they see the world, the questions they leave unanswered, and the ones they seem to carry within themselves.

Perhaps I am hopelessly in love with that very image.

I know I probably have a 0.0000001% chance of ever sitting across from this person and exchanging even a few words. But if that ever happened, I think what I would want most would be to look into their eyes and try to understand what lies behind that gaze.

Because sometimes, when I look at him, I get the feeling that behind those smiles there is something deeply melancholic. A sadness that's difficult to define, perhaps a particular kind of loneliness, the kind that might belong to someone whose mind is constantly reaching beyond the present, toward something that doesn't yet exist.

Of course, I could be wrong. I might discover someone completely different from the person I've imagined.

But that's precisely the point: I wouldn't want to meet the public figure, the fame, or what he represents to the world.

Just once, I would like the chance to meet the man who exists behind those eyes.

And perhaps discover that all this curiosity of mine was nothing more than a beautiful illusion.

Or perhaps not.

author: CryptoScoopOG
quoted_text:
I believe the @nvidia board is not acting in the best interest of shareholders nor in a manner consistent with their fiduciary duties. 

What we know is that the board fired Jensen or forced his resignation for violating company policy and/or in response to the accusation of an affair with a spy. 

They did so without careful consideration of the impact on the company, its customers, its shareholders or other stakeholders. 

They rushed to judgment without the benefit of careful due diligence or even with a basic understanding of the facts. 

How do we know this? 

We know this by how quickly Jensen was fired and how little was known at the time of his firing. 

It takes time to convene a board meeting.  There was time, maybe, for one Zoom. 

And this is a decision that should have been made by a board sitting in person and carefully deliberating the facts once they are known.  

And they should have slept on the decision and met again the day after to discuss the facts, the risks and the other implications of their decision. 

The timing and lack of information did not allow for careful board deliberation. 

While boards can fire a CEO for an inappropriate relationship with a subordinate, it should not be an automatic decision. That is why we have boards comprised of humans and not agents. 

A board should consider whether or not such a relationship was consensual or whether it was an abuse of power dynamics. And a board has to consider what the impact of the firing is on all stakeholders. 

If I were in this board, I would not have rushed to judgment based on articles in the media. I would have made sure the board had all of the facts so it could make a careful and informed decision. 

Boards of Delaware companies have a duty of care which means they must make informed, prudent and good faith decisions. This clearly did not happen here. 

What law firm is advising this board?  

Or is the board even taken good legal advice? 

It doesn’t look like it. 

And now the board is compounding its failures by insisting that there is no possibility for Jensen’s return as CEO. 

Why is it in the best interest of the company to foreclose the possibility of Jensen’s return and to do so before all of the facts are known? This is yet another breach of their duty of care. 

Furthermore, the board has launched an investigation whose scope is unknown. Investigations can be extremely damaging to a company and should be carefully targeted to address whatever facts need to be known rather than be overly broad in scope. 

In short, this looks like a series of major governance failures by directors that panicked due to headlines in the media. They likely felt compelled to do something because they were afraid of looking bad in the media, not because it was the right thing for them company. 

They couldn’t stand the heat. 

The board’s conduct here is shocking for a company of this scale and importance to our country and the world at large, particularly at this moment in history.

text:
民主党要毁掉AI，民主党不喜欢AI，民主党要制裁AI，这应该是本周所有小伙最担心的一点，但是这些担忧我认为要降级判断！

民主党真的要毁掉AI吗？

显然不是，AI是新的工业革命，是人类的重要发展方向之一，同样我也认为他是美国当下以及未来的核心国家命脉

我相信，不管是民主党还是共和党，不管是硅谷还是华尔街，都知道AI的重要性，毁掉他，就是加速自我毁灭，这点民主党不会这么做，不符合利益与目标

AI已经是21世纪全球竞赛的核心，同时也是中美大国交锋的核心目标，也就是所谓的军备竞赛，这意味着美国想要保持国力与军事霸权，AI不能丢，AI的发展还要加速！

民主党为何发表针对AI的言论，为何针对多家AI公司！？

以英伟达为例，其实属于政治斗争的牺牲品，民主党的清算核心是因为老黄站的不是民主党，强如“长袖善舞”的黄仁勋，都没办法承受这个压力，显然被政治清算波及

未来一段时间，民主党会继续高举民族大义，继续打压部分科技公司，他们不是不喜欢AI龙头企业，而是不喜欢共和党阵营的AI龙头企业，要知道，AI行业最赚钱，加入谁，就是哪个党派的核心“钱袋子”

至于那些新上任的民主党州长，鹰派言论更多的是继续抬升支持率，保持州内政治稳定性，一旦民主党对特朗普的清算完毕，那么整体环境自然慢慢宽松！

另一方面，对于AI行业，进行限制，主动戳破泡沫其实对民主党是好事，如果不限制干预，2年后民主党如果上台，“烫手的山芋”就到了民主党手里

所以，主动限制，戳破泡沫，对AI行业来说痛苦两年，但是2年后如果民主党胜选总统，稍微宽松政策，就又是一片繁荣，甚至这个繁荣可以支撑民主党总统一个甚至两个任期（4-8年）

在我的视角下，现在的表现反而不同悲观，因为主动戳破让泡沫风险降低，短期可能很难受，但是AI叙事的延展性，生命周期其实都被无形中拉长了！
author: Cato_KT
quoted_text:
简单回顾一下本周公布的Fed 十月会议纪要，这份记录加上近期的宏观数据，不仅仅是给宏观流动性是上了“枷锁”更是给AI叙事带来冲击，Fed政策反身性还有用吗？

这份会议纪要中显示，10月份美联储官员对通胀，对Fed政策已经保持鹰派观点，其中更有极端鹰派认为要加息50BP

继续观察数据来做Fed决断这是Fed政策的核心，而近期的宏观数据基本整体有利率Fed继续加息的政策，这才是导致宏观流动性收紧的核心

其次，这份会议纪要中很容易被人忽略的风险是对AI的评价，几乎是所有的参与会议的官员讨论了AI投资回报不及预期的风险，Fed盯得是金融稳定性，但是对于美股，对于美股的Q3财报，这个警惕对市场释放的是压力信号

Q3财报已经让市场担忧投资回报率问题，而宏观流动性收紧下利空容易被放大，所以Fed的担心必然也让市场更加担忧与紧张

利率预期上，会议记录+近期Fed官员鹰派言论+宏观数据不利，带来的问题不仅仅是“是否加息”，而是要加多少，加多久，而对我来说最担心的就是“加息周期”的回归

截止目前，CME显示12月完全不计算加息50BP的预期，显然剩余的25BP匀给了1月份，显然市场在交易连续两次加息，而3月加息概率也在抬头，市场已经对连续加息定价，对加息周期初步定价

接下来重点就是12月初的点阵图，如果点阵图依据显示鹰派加息观点，并且大部分官员提高中兴利率预期，那么加息周期的担忧就回来了，届时，市场要担心的不仅仅是加息多少，而是要加到多久，加息周期越久，对金融流动性越不友好

当然，Fed的“反身性”逻辑依旧在，但是不知道是否真的有用，如果在12月议息会议前，金融市场过分交易加息周期导致市场下跌，流动性过度收紧，其实对于Fed来说已经起到了加息的作用，反而沃什以及各位Fed官员会在12月中选择鸽派加息

所以，理论上来说，现在到12月9日市场越烂，未来加息风险越弱，毕竟不管是民主党还是共和党当家，都要考虑金融稳定性，对于AI，这是美国的国脉，民主党不可能为了选民而直接断了！

text:
Ethereum's biggest innovation might not be ethereum:native .

It might be the idea that financial infrastructure can work without asking anyone for permission.

Think about what Ethereum enables
➜ Stablecoins - Transfer digital dollars globally, 24/7.
➜ DeFi - Borrow, lend, and trade through open protocols.
➜ Tokenisation - Represent real-world assets on programmable infrastructure.
➜ Smart contracts - Execute financial agreements through code.
➜ Account abstraction - Build more flexible and accessible wallet experiences.
➜ Permissionless development - Build applications without needing approval from a platform owner.

These aren't isolated features.
They're building blocks for an entirely different financial system.
Developers can combine them, extend them, and create applications that interact with the same shared infrastructure.
That's what makes Ethereum fundamentally interesting.
Ethereum isn't just making finance digital. It's making financial infrastructure programmable, composable, and open to everyone.

Ethereum is world computer!

text:
我并不看好 @buzzchain_io  。
它本质上是 Tweet To Earn 的变种，只是把收益从发帖人转到了 NFT 上。甚至相比 Kaito 都算一种倒退。

1/ 先说 Kaito 做对了什么
Kaito 做了两件事。
情报层：用 mindshare 衡量一个账号在 CT 讨论中占多大比例，看的是相对份额；
激励层：让项目按创作者占该项目的声量份额，把激励分配下去。

设计初衷是通过声誉加权互动、模型过滤水文和抄袭，让激励更接近“谁在真正推动讨论”，而不是像 Tweet To Earn 那样单纯比谁发得多。
虽然实际上 AI 水文和刷量仍然泛滥，后面还被 X 制裁了一手。

2/ 再看 Buzzchain 的问题
伪链：所谓的链，只是把注意力做成了一个时钟，并没有真正的链上价值；
注意力错配：发帖的人拿不到分红，新铸的 $BUZZ 只平均分给已质押的验证人。

它或许能避开最粗糙的“发帖挖矿”，但刷量、X 平台依赖和激励错配这三个核心问题一个都没解决。无论是创作者侧的激励设计，还是产品的完整度，相比 Kaito 都是倒退。

3/ 最后
目前还在测试网阶段，很多机制细节也没出来，比如 NFT 的发售设计。

一切要等主网上线再看。
留待观察。

crypto spent a decade inventing new ways for computers to agree with each other. meanwhile the most honest signal on earth has been sitting in plain sight: what people can't shut up about.

pseudochains are my bet for the next financial primitive.

no new consensus. no 40-page bft paper nobody reads. no three-year testnet. just a small set of rules, a live data stream, and @ethereum as the anchor.

the world makes noise. noise makes blocks. blocks make assets.

think about what that unlocks. a market that speeds up when one guy tweets too much. a chain that goes quiet when nobody cares, because that's exactly what should happen when nobody cares.

prediction markets gave you a binary outcomes on reality. tokenized markets gave you a wrapper around reality. neither gave you reality itself, with its own pulse, its own rhythm… this is what both should have been since inception.

builders @buzzchain_io: @X is the largest real-time dataset of human attention ever assembled, and almost nobody is building financial rails on top of it. pick a topic. pick a stream. write the rules. ship something weird.

the timeline is the new mempool.

text:
Despite solving the Riemann Hypothesis, AI stocks are still down. A bunch of people have asked me about this divergence, so let me share some thoughts.

1) Intelligence Saturation: One reason markets get excited about a stock is that they see potential for product-led growth, where the products getting better and better increase sales. For a long time this was true, with exponentially more applications unlocked with each improvement in intelligence — but if AI can solve the Riemann Hypothesis, how can it get smarter? 

2) Compute Saturation: If AI is already this smart, it is possible that demand for training goes down substantially (why do you need to keep training a model that can solve Riemann?) Since 75% of compute is used for training (from $ANT S-1) even a small decrease in training would be catastrophic — which may explain the big dips in AI infrastructure.

3) Lower Replacement Cost: Holding all else equal, businesses are more valuable if it’s more challenging to rebuild them from scratch. With powerful AI, it is much easier to build competing AI, e.g. with more distillation, creating more competition, and in this way, AI may eat itself. 

All of which is to say that stock prices have been challenged recently. But it’s important to remember that this is a statement about stock prices, not the products themselves. More competition between companies will allow customers to capture more surplus. It’s been remarked that datacenters and AI have pushed up the prices of essential goods like energy and computers — as these inflationary pressures cool, it should address a growing affordability crisis at home.

text:
Some optimism for today.

Bitcoin created a digital store of value. No one can put that genie back in the box.

Our world is going to become only more digital. Bitcoin is just 4.9% of gold’s market cap (it was 11% in Dec 2024). Reaching 20% or more in the coming years is logical as adoption of digital SoV continues.

If digital SoV has value, there will always be an industry around it.

It’s important to separate digital SoV from blockchains as infrastructure. The infra can be built by companies like Robinhood, Coinbase, Stripe, etc., and might work in centralized/federated models.

Decentralized infra vs. centralized infra will play out, but stablecoins will work on both, and RWAs will find better rails on both.

SoV is completely different, though.

SoV is what sparked the industry. SoV has the highest TAM. SoV determines the rise and fall of market cycles.

If belief in digital SoV shakes, everything else goes down with it.

Bitcoin is still the king of digital SoV.

If Bitcoin was at 100K+ today, the growth and sentiment around the entire industry (even unrelated parts) would change.

The key reason for the doom & gloom around our industry today is fears around Bitcoin’s quantum upgrade and AI safety.

It’s true that Bitcoin is hard to change and the Bitcoin community is disorganized by design. However, the fears of quantum and AI safety for Bitcoin are overblown.

There are already credible efforts to address Bitcoin’s quantum and AI safety challenges. The best ones are still private and shaping up. As these become more concrete and public, the market will start calming down. 

Removing quantum & AI fears for Bitcoin is the single most important thing for the next phase of growth for our industry.

The entire industry rises or falls with Bitcoin.

We are closer to removing the quantum & AI fears than you think. Not only the necessary upgrades will happen, BTC will transform into a productive SoV with yield and onchain use (thanks to our recent work at Stacks, Bitcoin’s execution layer).

Hold tight during the current turbulence. We’ve endured far greater challenges before and will endure this one as well. Forward!

America is not a two-party system. It is a one-party state with a “no” option. The one party is called the Democrats, who have been in power for nearly the past century. Before that, from the civil war until the Great Depression, the one party was called the Republicans. The breakdown of the American one-party system was called the Civil War, which was an event so bloody that neither Democrats nor Republicans in any era have shown much enthusiasm for repeating it.

Democrats control all meaningful professional-bureaucratic machinery of the state whether or not they win or lose any given election. They also control the entire cultural-academic complex that takes care of social signaling. Nearly all social and professional rewards belong to Democrats, with a tiny and shrinking percentage reserved for “Republicans” who play the role of the Washington Generals to the Harlem Globetrotters, ie to be the butt of the joke. 

Outside of a handful of minor states like Alabama or Wyoming, you’d have to be an autistic social idiot or a determined loser to choose the Republican Party as your vehicle for social or professional advancement. Thats why you see a number of powerful tech lords aligning themselves with Donald Trump. They are literally autistic. For the next two years, and beyond that, they will be roasted alive by the system, until they join it, and put their technologies at its disposal (see: Anthropic, Google).

Donald Trump is what happens when Democrats abuse the public on behalf of their client base beyond what the rest of the public is willing to tolerate. His mandate was to punish the Democrats for their cultural arrogance, abusive hallucinations and systematic transfers of wealth to their clients — which is the way that Democrats tend to be corrupt, ie legally.  

However the idea of the “Trump Presidency” revealed itself to be a sick joke, because there was never any kind of grown-up political machinery capable of translating Trump’s impulses and preferences, good or bad, into practice beyond the strictly executive level. The people who volunteered themselves for “the Trump Party” were mostly a predictable collection of idiots, sycophants, foreign agents and financial criminals grabbing for the brass ring and knowing that the carousel was never coming around for them again. Any Federal judge could and did overturn whatever they tried to do with the full backing of the entire system. With a Democrat in power, the entire system becomes a rubber stamp. 

Thats no knock on Trump voters. The abuses and inequalities they rebelled against were mostly real. Its an explanation for what happened, and for what’s coming. The solution, as always, is the hard work of building a culture and a politics founded on core American values from the ground up. Its living a good life, while speaking truth to power. Each and every attempt to find a savior figure who will save everyone else from building things that work, and defending those things from being destroyed, just makes the work harder.

Software is converging, we always knew it would.

Everyone told us to do ONE thing and do it well. Many still say it's ridiculous, impossible, stupid.

BUT NOW IT'S UTTERLY OBVIOUS. 

This is the only future in software, whether ClickUp does it or not. Even the software giants are already moving toward this new world order.

I wholeheartedly believe that the only way to peak productivity is one platform that does everything, carries 100% of context, and enables everyone to become 100X. 

And it's only possible with AI. 

AI DOESN'T KILL SOFTWARE. IT CREATES MORE OF IT, AND CONVERGES IT. 

If AI makes software dramatically easier to build, software companies will build MORE software. Not less. Right?

The company that built a tool for you will now build more tools. This will never stop.

Categories blur. Competition increases. Features that once justified an entire company become a small feature addition to an existing platform.

Over a given period of time, this is how it will end: Several massive companies that provide ALL software and ALL AI to their customers.

But building more is only HALF the story.

AI needs to understand your context.

And it needs somewhere to actually DO the work.

That's why AI and productivity software are converging too.

Humans and agents need a shared place to communicate, make decisions, and get things done.

ONE APP TO REPLACE THEM ALL 

A behemoth horizontal platform, infinitely flexible, delivering all core software needs, built with common components, primitives, and services that enable mega solutions and compound speed in delivery of software.

THE ERA OF PERSONAL SOFTWARE

To build the everything app and actually work for everyone seamlessly, we rebuilt the application layers  around the concept real-time personalization based on what you want, and what you don't want.

Personal Software adapts in real-time to what matters to you... how YOU work, entirely PERSONALIZED.

You shouldn't have to become a software company just to run your company.

But you should be able to build anything that your creativity can dream of, and that your workflows require. 

The same boundaries disappearing between software categories are disappearing inside our team.

THE 100X STRATEGY IS WORKING 

Since my last post, we shipped more PRs every single week, compounding in growth and these PRs aren't slop - much of this is systems that literally fixed thousands of bugs and constantly optimizes performance.

We now have SIX 100x builders in seats we call Artisans. 10x frontend engineers becoming 10x backend engineers - and skilled enough to do the product work.

Today's EPIC release was built ENTIRELY by our 100x builders. The video below shows what that actually looks like.

And this isn't just about shipping new things faster.

It's about making the things you already use dramatically better.

We've spent the last few months building LARGE-SCALE SYSTEMS and LOOPS that enable us to build with high quality at lightning speed. This was the mandate BEFORE we built more on the platform.

In September, our user generated metrics for quality hit all-time highs, now 90% of ClickUp customers are happy with quality and performance. 

And in a production comparison this week across millions of sessions, ClickUp now loads 40% faster.

Breadth is NOT an excuse for mediocrity in this next era of ClickUp. If we're going to replace your tools, we have to earn it.

I fully understand that we just weren't there yet for the last mile of use cases.

But now, if you get blocked on anything you want, you can simply tell Brain to build it.

In our early days, we made shipping every week part of who we were.

TODAY'S EPIC RELEASE IS OUR REBIRTH. 

We're back. Except now, we're shipping improvements EVERY SINGLE DAY.

I started ClickUp because nearly losing my life made me obsess about the very limited time we have on this planet.

The goal is to enable creativity, and freedom in how you spend your time.

EPIC productivity. 

💜

text: Polymarket CEO at Dealbook conference explains how prediction markets improve overall market efficiency
author: zerohedge
quoted_text:
Shayne Coplan at the NYT DealBook Summit pushes back on calling prediction markets “gambling”:

“The biggest thing is when people use the word bet, there’s this connotation of you’re at a slot machine and you’re hoping everything lands in the same row.”

He compares it to oil traders and commodity markets reacting to geopolitical events, or stocks pricing in earnings expectations before the number is released and then immediately repricing. 
Same idea with sports spreads, markets continuously updating probabilities.

Coplan cites Friedrich Hayek and Robin Hanson (idea futures, prediction markets, Futarchy) as inspiration. 
His goal is to create markets specifically designed for informational price discovery.

On geopolitics specifically:
“People want to frame it as gambling. The reality is it’s not fun gambling. There’s very little volatility, and if there is, it can only go up to one dollar. But what there is is liquidity and price formation around the likelihood of the event. People have gravitated to that as an information source. That’s the thing I’m really excited about.”

我的数学家朋友已经有一点精神不正常了。。。

大部分人看到AI可能证明了黎曼猜想，第一反应都是去检查证明有没有漏洞，代码是否正确，形式化验证能不能成立。

但这位朋友甚至根本不打算讨论证明的对错。

他直接从数学哲学的角度否定了这件事。

他说，根本不存在独立于人类理解的数学实体。
数学定理本质上是人类头脑中的概念，也是社会关系的凝结。
所以，如果一份证明长达几万页，根本没有人类能够完整理解，那么它就没有社会意义，自然也没有数学意义。

在这种情况下，所谓证明成立，实际上就等价于相信AI这个神谕机，以及提交证明的「祭司」没有欺骗你。

别人还在争论AI到底有没有证明黎曼猜想，他已经开始质疑：就算证明是真的，那又怎么样？

随着AI的数学能力继续发展，我们可能真的会遇到一种情况：AI能够证明的东西，已经超出了人类能够理解的范围。

到那个时候，数学究竟是谁的数学？

反正不是我的数学。

事到如今再去复盘的话，10月真的神预言，自己那时候开始确实也在高点清了，一度非常满意。

而且一早就预测到了川普两院全丢，但确实没猜到铁红州翻蓝。

最大的问题是低估了川普惨败之后对市场的影响，觉得选完利空就出尽了，没想到民主党反扑如此凶残。

在选后看到了一个关键位就以为是阶段低点迫不及待上车导致了挨打到了今天。

但最关键的其实大道至简：加息周期不做多， 降息周期再去长多，明明11月都已经进入加息周期第二个月了还去博反弹有点太沉浸在自己的幻想里了。

技术派也好，图表派也罢，都以为赚钱是自己的本事，但其实是在上升电梯里做俯卧撑，在信贷宽松周期赚的都是大趋势的钱，个人能力确实能放大振幅，但不可否认的是这时候市场容错度也高，即使入场位不好也经常能扛单扛回来。

可怕的是，一旦在宽松周期形成了交易习惯，在牛转熊的时候很难改过来，所谓牛市亏大钱也来源于此。鱼尾行情涨得固然多，但对大多数人来说都是纸面财富落不到口袋里去。

牛初时候小心翼翼没吃够，牛尾重仓猛干吃大亏。

quoted_text:
我的数学家朋友已经有一点精神不正常了。。。

大部分人看到AI可能证明了黎曼猜想，第一反应都是去检查证明有没有漏洞，代码是否正确，形式化验证能不能成立。

但这位朋友甚至根本不打算讨论证明的对错。

他直接从数学哲学的角度否定了这件事。

他说，根本不存在独立于人类理解的数学实体。
数学定理本质上是人类头脑中的概念，也是社会关系的凝结。
所以，如果一份证明长达几万页，根本没有人类能够完整理解，那么它就没有社会意义，自然也没有数学意义。

在这种情况下，所谓证明成立，实际上就等价于相信AI这个神谕机，以及提交证明的「祭司」没有欺骗你。

别人还在争论AI到底有没有证明黎曼猜想，他已经开始质疑：就算证明是真的，那又怎么样？

随着AI的数学能力继续发展，我们可能真的会遇到一种情况：AI能够证明的东西，已经超出了人类能够理解的范围。

到那个时候，数学究竟是谁的数学？

反正不是我的数学。

text:
突然发现，人这辈子跟 GTA6 这种开放世界游戏还挺像的。

每天都在做各种支线任务：发 X、赚钱、工作、研究新东西、追逐机会、处理各种琐事……

忙了一整天，任务清掉一大堆，回头一看：我的主线剧情到底推进了多少？

游戏里的主线是开发者写好的，但人生的主线得自己定义。

更有意思的是，我们可能一直把赚钱当主线，却把健康、家人、自由和真正想体验的生活，当成了以后再做的支线。

尤其是有了 AI 之后，感觉什么都能做、什么都想做，一不小心就忙得停不下来。

AI 确实让我们刷支线的效率越来越高，但它并不会告诉我们，主线到底是什么。

所以，如果人生真是一场游戏，最终的通关条件是什么？

或者说，你现在的人生主线任务到底是什么？

quoted_text:
DMT Levels:

1. Threshold (1-4mg): Crisp and high-resolution experience without obvious hallucinations. Intensified colors and sharper edges.

2. Symmetry Hotel (3-6mg): A thin layer where you still see the "real" world around you but every surface is fully saturated with wallpaper symmetry groups. Empirically, at this level the surfaces one sees on DMT can be tessellated with any of the 17 wallpaper symmetry groups and their combinations. Essentially, if you increase the energy parameter any more, then you will start to see some hyperbolization of the 2D surfaces and unlock the Chrysanthemum.

3. Chrysanthemum (4-8mg): The wallpaper-saturated surfaces of the Symmetry Hotel overflow, leading to a hyperbolization of such surfaces. At this level, the mind will still try to embed these constructs in 3D Euclidean space, so in practice you will see kale-like surfaces, saddles, helixes, corners, twists, etc. This often manifests as what looks like the blossoming of a flower or unwrapping of a present in the center of your attention.

4. Magic Eye (8-12mg): The Chrysanthemum becomes so curved that it can be used to render arbitrary 3D scenes of all sorts (e.g. ice cream shops, apparel, play pens, kitchen counters, etc.). We can think of this as a dynamic and animated depth map, which we call the world-sheet. If you pay attention, you will realize that the texture of the world-sheet is in fact made out of a widely contorted Chrysanthemum, with similarities to autostereograms (aka. Magic Eye visual illusions).

5. Crystal Worlds (10-15mg): A thin layer analogous to the Symmetry Hotel but one spatial dimension higher. Namely, the curved world-sheet fills out the space around you, which becomes fully saturated with Euclidean space groups (the 3D counterparts of the wallpaper groups, of which there are 230). If the energy parameter is raised any higher, then you will start to see a hyperbolization of (3D) space itself and unlock Waiting Room phenomenology.

6. Waiting Room (12-25mg): Past the crystalline saturation of 3D space, qualia continues to build to the point that it simply does not fit 3D Euclidean space. Thus there is a forced hyperbolization of 3D phenomenal space, which also comes along a powerful multi-modal synchronization (cf. Kinesioöptic). This, in turn, makes the hallucinated world so engrossing that you lose contact with your surroundings. Often manifests as a hyper-realistic dome or series of interconnected rooms and exotic architectural structures with countless twists and turns.

7. Breakthrough (25mg+): The curvature and density of qualia is so extreme that the very topology of the worldsheet can change (e.g. via bifurcations and reconnections). One experiences radically exotic geometries of experience. There may be more than one geodesic between two given points, leading to markedly bizarre pseudo-acoustic properties. Sense of entering a sort of "interdimensional highway" that stitches together widely diverse and seemingly contradictory realities at once. (Today I would add that at this dose different regions of the experience may exhibit different pseudo-time arrows, and thus may have hybrid temporal qualities, as discussed here).

8. Amnesia (40mg+; depends): Not much to say here.

Note: high interpersonal and inter-trip variabilitu. 

Techniques used: The photo has its depth map computed (Depth Anything V2) and object masks (Mask R-CNN), and from then on everything runs live in the browser (WebGL). A "beauty" filter softens flat areas and enhances the mid-scale detail. The scene is then parsed into surfaces with graph segmentation on color, depth and surface direction (Felzenszwalb–Huttenlocher), and each object and surface gets a fitted 3-D plane, with non-flat objects cut into planar facets. On each plane we overlay a lattice and one of the 17 wallpaper groups, thus every surface is tiled in perspective with copies of its own texture, and the parts move independently like layers of cel animation. Next, each part's pattern turns into a flat slice of a 7-dimensional cube lattice rotating in 12 dimensions (see https://t.co/Z8YE8yiP9G). The rotation of each part is treated as a set of Kuramoto oscillators coupled to the parts it touches and, more weakly, to all of them, and as the coupling rises toward the peak, neighbours synchronise first until everything converges on a single shared hyperobject. That object settles into its 7-fold shadow, and the picture becomes the {7,3} heptagonal tiling of the Poincaré disk, built entirely from mirror reflections (the hyperbolic orbifold *237), with a convex mirror jewel at every corner reflecting the whole net, as in Indra's net. On the way down, the same sequence runs in reverse.

See: https://t.co/zsMPeAkGhg

author: KSimback
quoted_text:
Most of us are managing agents all wrong

We setup agents to do things we already know how to do, then tell them exactly how we want them to do things

This is treating agents like interns

That was fine earlier this year when models were not as capable

But ask yourself - if you just hired a 130 IQ employee, would you just have them do things you already know how to do and tell them exactly how to do it?

If you’re using frontier models with agents, you want to give them goals and objectives for things you don’t know how to do, then empower them to do the things

Hire agents as experts, not interns

Yes you should still have some agent interns to automate boring work to free up more of your time

But if you’re not using agents to do things you don’t know how to do then you’re missing out

Let them go figure out how to do the things that expand beyond your skills and capabilities just like a good leader would when hiring a team

It's easy to be ambitious when you're young and naive. You don't yet understand the trade-offs, the sacrifice required.

And in your 20s you rarely have the skills to turn dreams into reality. You can visualize the house, but you don't know how to build its foundation.

As you mature, you experience failure. You understand the struggle. You know the price tag.

But now you have the tools, experience and connections to make a dent in the universe.

The hard part is keeping the flame alive while your friends slow down, settle for boring jobs, give up on their ambitions.

This is the tragedy. By the time most people can build the house, they no longer want it.

text:
High quality decision making

I've been lucky to work with @brian_armstrong and @emiliemc at @coinbase for the past 6+ years.

They've built a culture that prioritizes clarity and ownership over consensus and theater.

Their decision framework (RAPID) is a great example. It's very similar to the SPADE decision framework that we created at Square: one responsible person, a small group of consulted voices, private input to avoid groupthink, and a clear decider.

They've added two interesting / powerful nuances:

1. The committee rule: In regulated (or even non-regulated) environments, committees metastasize and nobody owns the outcome. Committees also breed consensus, which is ineffective because it produces no ownership; what matters is that people feel heard, then one person decides and everyone commits. 

2. The 48-hour rule: This forces a discipline that prevents decisions from dragging. In SPADE, the “when” is explicit for the same reason.

Kudos Brian, Emilie and team for building a great culture at @coinbase and for making it to Signalful Best of the Week :)

Founders: upgrading your decision framework (especially for high-stakes, one way door, consequential decisions) will massively upgrade your company's culture and performance.

author: emiliemc
quoted_text:
Decision Making

Most decisions at companies get stuck not due to disagreements but due to ambiguity about who owns the decision.

@coinbase 's RAPID decision framework maps almost exactly to the SPADE framework used by Square and others. Both share the notion of a DECIDER: a person responsible for making the decision.

Founders and Operators: clarity around decision making is an important part of building a high performing company.  Adopt a framework like RAPID or SPADE for one way door, consequential decisions. Remember when you could not sell your GameStop? 

Kalshi just opened stock contracts where nobody buys your order first.

Citadel Securities, which buys your orders, helped sue to stop it.

The judge said no. Even the SEC sided against them.

The north remembers. Part Two 👇

Last time: your order gets sold before it reaches the market. In 2020, Citadel Securities paid 34% of all of Robinhood's revenue for orders like yours.

This month the CFTC cleared single-stock perpetual futures on Kalshi, Bitnomial and Coinbase Derivatives.

Kalshi says its version skips the toll: single-stock perps on Kalshi "do not use the PFOF model. Instead of PFOF, Kalshi charges a small, transparent trading fee."

No firm buys the exclusive right to fill your order. Anyone can take the other side, and everyone sees the price.

That's a problem if your business is buying orders.

A group backed by Cboe and Citadel Securities sued the CFTC and its chairman to stop it.

The judge said they would likely win on the law. Then she refused the emergency stop. The market stayed open.

Then the SEC filed a brief backing the CFTC: "…a CFTC gone rogue, and an SEC gone missing … is mistaken."

On Nov 16 the WSJ reported that Kalshi is expanding into stocks, perpetual futures and other assets. Tarek answered in three words: "The Next Horizon."

That's the exchange we didn't have in January 2021. One open board. Nobody pays to see your order first.

It isn't over. A new judge will rule on the injunction, and the old houses will keep fighting.

But this time the North isn't alone.

text:
The Nvidia Board Removed Jensen on False Pretenses
A comprehensive debunking of the greatest hoax of my lifetime.

On November 12, 2026, the Nvidia board successfully pressured Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang into resigning. Its decision was based on false information, fabricated quotes, and hyperbolic opinion pieces, which have now been thoroughly debunked by independently verified sources. In one extraordinary case, the Wall Street Journal has been caught fabricating quotes from the Singaporean government.

This is the most egregious case of journalistic malpractice we have ever reported on.

Huang is one of the world’s strongest supporters of open-source AI. Utopia or not, it is his belief that free, equal access to new technologies can balance the playing field against concentration of power and authoritarianism.

The Jensen coup is an overt weaponization of the government and the press to achieve policy outcomes which failed to pass through Congress. After their initial falsehoods were debunked, the same foreign policy lobbyists, elected officials, and representatives pivoted to a new argument. According to them, the extrajudicial coup against Jensen is justified because of legal “loopholes” that allowed Nvidia to sell hardware to third party countries such as Malaysia, which in turn did business with China. In 2023, 2024, and 2025, policies to restrict third party datacenters were proposed in Congress. In all three cases, at least one chamber of Congress decided not to pass the bill. It was the explicit will of Congress that the benefits to third party datacenters exceeded the costs, not merely an unintended loophole.

But a much greater issue supersedes the merits of this policy — the Jensen coup weaponized state sources including, according to The Washington Post, doctored intelligence reports, to circumvent the will of Congress. This is behavior one would expect in an authoritarian country like China, not in the United States of America. The rule of law itself in America is under threat.

Welcome to our largest investigative project yet — debunking the coup against Jensen.

text:
🚨BREAKING: ELON MUSK BLASTS COLETTE KRESS AS ‘ UNGRATEFUL ’ OVER CRITICISM OF JENSEN HUANG'S LEADERSHIP 

🗣️Calling Jensen Huang “irresponsible” after he single-handedly turned Nvidia into the most important hardware company on Earth is beyond absurd—it is completely ungrateful. 

For thirty years, Jensen bet everything on a vision that almost nobody else on Wall Street understood, enduring brutal downturns and near-death moments while building the exact foundation that made Colette Kress’s entire career and fortune possible. 

Without Jensen’s relentless drive and willingness to take massive, high-conviction risks, there would be no multi-trillion-dollar empire for anyone to manage spreadsheets over.

What we are seeing here is the classic disease that destroys great tech companies from the inside: bean counters and cautious executives forgetting who actually built the rocket ship. 

Innovation does not happen by playing defense or asking permission from conservative consensus; it happens when a founder pushes past every limit to create the future. 

Attacking the very founder whose genius carried the entire organization on his back is a massive failure of loyalty and perspective.

Jensen deserves total backing from his leadership team, not public backstabbing from people who benefited from his sacrifices. 

Great companies are built by builders, not bureaucrats, and anyone who cannot recognize what Jensen Huang has accomplished should step aside rather than undermine the man who made it all happen.
author: CryptoScoopOG
quoted_text:
This clash between Jensen Huang and Colette Kress highlights the classic tension at the heart of every trillion-dollar tech giant: visionary risk-taking versus strict financial caution. Huang makes a compelling point—Nvidia didn’t reach the top of the AI mountain by playing it safe or waiting for Wall Street consensus, and calling that level of conviction "irresponsible" overlooks the decades of calculated bets that built the company.
At the same time, public friction between a CEO and CFO is a dangerous look for any market leader, especially when investors are already hypersensitive to AI spending and valuation pressures. While Huang’s aggressive, forward-looking mindset is undeniably Nvidia’s greatest engine, keeping internal disagreements behind closed doors is essential if they want to maintain the market confidence they worked so hard to earn.

text:
估值410亿美元，贝佐斯打造：物理世界的 OpenAI

2026年11月17日，贝佐斯在硅谷峰会上首次公开介绍其AI创业公司Prometheus。卸任亚马逊CEO五年后，他重新担任这家公司的联合创始人兼联席CEO。

这家成立仅两年、员工约250人的神秘公司，估值已达410亿美元，累计融资约145亿美元。

更惊人的是其技术表现：过去需要10至20名工程师耗时6至9个月完成的芯片、无线电设备或阀门设计，Prometheus声称只需12小时。

贝佐斯的目标，是打造物理世界的OpenAI，让AI重新定义数十万亿美元的全球制造业。

01｜打造真正的AI工程师

Prometheus的目标十分明确：开发「通用AI工程师」（AGE）。

贝佐斯认为，语言模型即使读遍所有物理学教材，也很难直接设计复杂工业产品。

他举了个例子：即便把牛顿、爱因斯坦等顶尖物理学家聚在一起，也未必能制造出一台小烤箱。因为掌握物理理论与解决实际工程问题之间，存在巨大鸿沟。

Prometheus为此开发了神经代理模型和统一多物理场模型，将AI与CAD设计、数值仿真、工程决策整合。

在一次内部实验中，工程师仅用一句提示词要求AI重新设计火星直升机。系统自主比较四旋翼、固定翼和共轴反桨等方案，最终得出与NASA真实火星直升机高度相似的设计，还能计算桨叶参数并主动询问需求。

为实现这一目标，公司从OpenAI、DeepMind、Meta、微软以及NASA相关工程团队招募人才，覆盖AI、航天、材料、能源和机械工程等领域。

xAI联合创始人Kyle Kosic也已加入，负责算力基础设施。

02｜破解工业AI最大难题：数据

互联网为大语言模型提供了海量训练数据，但工业领域完全不同。

飞机发动机、芯片制造和精密铸造的核心参数往往属于企业商业机密。大量传统工厂甚至缺乏数字化监测系统，数据难以获取。

Prometheus的解决方案，是利用物理规律和自研仿真系统，大规模生成高质量合成数据，降低对企业专有数据的依赖。

贝佐斯旗下的蓝色起源已经在两个内部项目中测试相关工具，为AI提供真实工程场景。

商业模式也很有野心。

Prometheus计划向全球制造企业开放工程工具，同时投资部分采用其技术的传统工业公司，分享效率提升带来的增长收益。

外媒还曾报道，贝佐斯考虑募集最高1000亿美元，收购传统制造、工程和建筑企业，打造类似「工业版伯克希尔」的投资平台。不过，这项计划尚未得到正式确认。

贝佐斯强调，全球实体制造业规模达到数十万亿美元，Prometheus必须与成千上万家外部企业合作。

03｜AI竞争进入物理世界

Prometheus的资本阵容相当豪华。

公司2025年披露62亿美元首轮融资，2026年6月宣布规模达120亿美元的新融资安排，估值升至410亿美元。贝佐斯最新披露的累计实际募资约145亿美元。

摩根大通、高盛、贝莱德、DST Global等机构均在投资者名单中。

这些资金背后，是AI产业的重要转向。

过去几年，OpenAI和Anthropic主要围绕文本、推理和编程展开竞争。随着模型能力提升，越来越多创业公司开始探索AI如何直接改变物理世界。

例如，Periodic Labs利用AI科学家和自动化实验室探索新材料；Neural Concept等企业专注工程设计与仿真。

Prometheus选择了更庞大的市场：机械设计、芯片、航空航天与工业制造。

如果AI能够把复杂工程的研发周期从数月缩短到数小时，制造业的创新速度、研发成本和竞争格局都可能发生根本变化。

04｜万亿美元市场背后的风险

但工业AI面临着比聊天机器人严峻得多的挑战。

聊天机器人答错问题，通常只需要修改内容。工业AI如果设计错误，可能导致阀门爆裂、芯片报废，甚至航空航天事故。

真实世界的物理验证、工程可靠性和监管认证，都需要大量时间与成本。

另一项挑战是工程领域的复杂性。

机械、热力、电磁和化工之间存在巨大差异，想让一套AI模型精通所有工程学科，难度可能远超训练通用语言模型。

目前Prometheus仍未公布正式产品发布时间，其惊人的内部测试结果也有待更多独立验证。

Prometheus的真正野心，是让AI从理解语言、编写代码，进一步发展到设计芯片、制造发动机、研发火箭以及改造整个工业体系。

从数字世界到物理世界，AI正在进入一个更加昂贵、复杂，同时也可能更加有价值的新战场。贝佐斯押下的145亿美元，赌的正是下一代工业革命的入口。

text:
骂 CZ 之前，能不能先把 FTX 破产的来龙去脉搞清楚？

我突然想起一件事。

2025 年，Telegram 创始人 Durov 在 X 上高调宣布，与马斯克旗下 xAI 达成了价值 3 亿美元的投资。

结果马斯克随后公开澄清：协议还没签。

Durov 也只能承认，双方只是原则上达成一致，正式手续尚未完成。

请问，Telegram 因为马斯克没有正式签约，就破产倒闭了吗？

没有。

因为一家正常经营的企业，不会仅仅因为某个潜在合作方没有签约，就突然出现无法填补的资金窟窿。

再回头看看 2022 年的 FTX。

FTX 为什么破产？SBF 为什么进监狱？

难道是因为 CZ 没有出手相救？

当然不是。

FTX 当时已经存在高达约 80 亿美元的资金缺口，客户资金被违规挪用，Alameda 与 FTX 之间的财务问题早已积重难返。

不是币安拒绝收购导致 FTX 破产，而是 FTX 自己把窟窿捅得太大，才不得不向币安求救。

2022 年的币安也才成立五年。

你可以质疑币安当时有没有足够的资金完成收购，但更应该问的是：

第一，币安是否有能力承担 FTX 高达八十亿美元的资金缺口，以及后续不可预估的法律和监管风险？

第二，收购 FTX 对币安究竟有什么不可替代的战略价值？

第三，作为一家需要对自身用户负责的交易平台，CZ 凭什么要拿币安的未来，去替 SBF 的错误买单？

商业收购不是慈善，更不是兄弟义气。

何况，CZ 并非从一开始就拒绝救助 FTX。双方曾签署非约束性收购意向书，币安随后开展尽职调查，最终因财务问题及相关风险放弃交易。

发现对方是个无底洞之后选择退出，难道不是一个企业经营者最基本的理性？

再补充一段很多人可能不知道的历史。

2019 年，币安就是 FTX 的早期投资人，双方曾经是合作关系。

但到了 2021 年，FTX 回购了币安持有的股份，双方正式分道扬镳。

为什么 SBF 要花费巨大代价回购币安的股权？

原因值得深思。

随着 FTX 不断壮大，双方早已从合作伙伴变成直接竞争对手。SBF 想摆脱币安的股东身份及其潜在影响，获得更大的独立性，这并不难理解。

换句话说，SBF 早就想摆脱 CZ，等到自己资金链断裂、走投无路时，却又不得不回头寻求币安救助。

而现在，居然还有人把 FTX 的破产归咎于 CZ 没有完成收购。

这是什么逻辑？

我认为 Telegram 与 xAI 的事件，以及 FTX 与币安的事件，至少说明了同一个道理：

商业合作的意向不是承诺，收购谈判更不意味着必须替对方承担所有债务。

当然，两起事件的性质完全不同。Telegram 是正常的商业合作谈判，FTX 则是已经出现严重财务危机后的紧急求救。

但不能因为一方曾经表达过合作意愿，最后没有完成交易，就把另一方的经营失败归咎于他。

CZ 可以被批评，但批评至少应该建立在事实之上。

SBF 挪用客户资金造成的后果，不应该由 CZ 来背锅；币安没有义务为了救一个竞争对手，把自己的用户和企业一起拖进深渊。

别把拒绝接盘的人当成罪魁祸首，却忘了是谁亲手掏空了用户的钱包。

骂 CZ 之前，先弄明白来龙去脉吧。

币圈已经够乌烟瘴气了了，我们可以批评任何人，但至少应该有基本的辩证思维吧。

团结一点，老外也有坏人，他们内心就看不得华人创办伟大的企业。
