text:
one of my favorite pods we’ve done in awhile! @dhh is a legend of open source, who’s still building cutting-edge projects like @omarchy to this day, and it’s actually delightful and often hilarious to hear him chat with @martin_casado and @illscience.

some of my takeaways:
- old infra can become newly competitive because the entity operating it evolves. the things that made linux difficult for humans, for example, are exactly what make the os attractive to agents (which is why dhh is building a modern linux distro called omarchy). terminal-heavy interfaces, obscure config files, and detailed error messages are “the three things agents love” in the words of dhh. which is why dhh thinks the days of microsoft and especially apple are numbered.
- dhh can afford essentially whatever token budget he wants, but says most weeks a single $200 claude subscription covers everything he does. i’ve met a lot of devs in the bay area who like to flex how high their token spend is, so this was actually a super surprising detail to me. dhh owns three subscriptions, and remembers only two weeks in the preceding three months when he maxxed those out.
- dhh says he never wanted to exchange a company of roughly 60 people for one with 6,000 or 60,000. the prospect of that much productive capacity through agents, without the committee meetings and coordination, interests him enormously. you can see how someone could become much more ambitious about the product while retaining the same preferences about how they want to spend their day.
- there are two kinds of “ambition inflation”: one is the ever-increasing floor on what constitutes a noteworthy project in the age of superintelligence. people used to stop in their tracks whenever a cool open-source 3d build or handcrafted game was released on x…now the bar to wow people is much higher. there’s also the ability to exactingly specify your precise vision, and the desire to get pixel-perfect results. dhh has both kinds of ambition omarchy's screensaver runs ascii art through forty demo effects, deliberately recalling the 1990s demoscene. dhh added another animation while a local model loads, purely because it makes the computer look cool. he also wants to see omarchy surpass macos in terms of users, a reasonable task, he thinks, because macos has something like “only 120m users.”

check out the full pod in the qt!

If you’re wondering how they got this result, two ways.

First, they exclude “pure public goods”, including defence, veterans’ affairs, foreign affairs, science, subsidies and all interest on government debt. None of these costs are attributed to immigrants.

Second, they count the US-born children of immigrants as natives, so their education, welfare and other costs are attributed to the native-born population.

If you reverse these two assumptions their claimed $568 billion surplus in 2023 becomes a roughly $213 billion deficit, based on a recalculation using the report’s own figures which likely have other favourable assumptions.

Nor does the analysis account for second- and third-order effects, including higher rates of criminal offending among second- and third-generation descendants compared with first-generation immigrants, and higher welfare receipt among later generations.

author: hazenlee
quoted_text:
Imagina tener $26B a los 29 años y, a los 32, que un juez te condene a 25 años de prisión.

Eso le pasó a Sam Bankman-Fried, y ayer su historia volvió a los titulares: Anthropic salió a bolsa, y la participación que él compró cuando casi nadie conocía la empresa hoy valdría unos $43B.

Sam nació en Stanford, California, en 1992, hijo de dos profesores de Derecho. Estudió física en el MIT y después entró a Jane Street, una de las firmas de trading más grandes del mundo, donde regalaba la mitad de su sueldo porque creía que la mejor forma de ayudar era ganar mucho dinero y donarlo.

En 2017 renunció y fundó Alameda Research. Su primera gran jugada fue bastante simple: el bitcoin costaba más en Japón que en Estados Unidos, así que lo compraba barato de un lado y lo vendía caro del otro, y antes de que esa brecha se cerrara ya había ganado entre $10M y $30M.

Dos años después fundó FTX, que para 2021 ya valía $25B, y con ese dinero empezó a invertir en prácticamente todo lo que se movía:

🔹Robinhood (7.6%): $648M
🔹Genesis Digital, minería de bitcoin: $1.15B
🔹Anthropic: $500M
🔹Propiedades en Bahamas: $256M
🔹Cursor: $200K
Todo se vino abajo en noviembre de 2022, cuando CoinDesk publicó el balance de Alameda y los usuarios empezaron a sacar su dinero de FTX. Nueve días después la empresa estaba en quiebra, y un año más tarde un jurado lo declaró culpable de 7 cargos de fraude y conspiración.

Lo que más llama la atención es lo que pasó con sus inversiones después. Los $200K que puso en Cursor se vendieron en la quiebra por la misma cantidad, y en agosto SpaceX compró Cursor por $60B, así que ese cheque hoy valdría entre $1.8B y $3B. Con Anthropic pasó algo parecido: la vendieron por $1.34B y, con el cierre de ayer, valdría unos $43B.

Y bueno, no hay que negar que Sam podría ser uno de los mejores inversores de su generación, porque vio a Anthropic y a Cursor cuando casi nadie sabía que existían. Pero de nada sirve tener buen ojo si el dinero con el que apuestas no es tuyo.

Construyó un imperio de $32B en menos de 5 años y lo perdió en 9 días. Hoy, desde prisión, ve cómo una sola de sus apuestas valdría más que todo FTX en su mejor momento.

quoted_text:
Customer storytelling is one of the most interesting jobs in AI right now. At Cognition, I'm looking for incredible marketers, creatives, and operators to build the function. A few reasons why this is exciting:

- You are shipping the opposite of slop. Customer storytelling is now one of the single most important GTM levers - more than ever before. When anyone can ship anything, what cuts through the noise is actually credible customers vouching for you. Cog has large enterprises in every vertical (Mercedes-Benz, Goldman Sachs) and the most cutting-edge startups (Modal, Mercor). And there are a ton we haven't yet talked about publicly, like our work with the US government.
- You get to tell stories about technology helping normal people and learn how different industries work. We spent a few days in Ohio hanging out with the GE Aerospace team. They make ~half the jet engines in the world, and they're building software for things like airspace efficiency or fuel insight so that people can fly more without needing more planes (which are in short supply right now!) 
- You get to escape the SF tech bubble and travel the world. A few places I visited over the past year: Prague, Ohio, London, Krakow, Boston. Next up on my travel schedule: Cambridge, Atlanta, Brazil, LA. We have a very "forward-deployed" culture at Cognition: you should go to the customer, get to know them, learn about their businesses, strategize with our forward-deployed engineers and sales teams about the right stories to tell and how to tell them.
- You get to explore the timely question of how AI diffuses into the real world. Will hundreds of billions of dollars of investment in AI turn into real-world value? You're at the frontlines of exploring this question in actual businesses. text: I am confident humanity will ensure that powerful AI models are returned to the commons
author: sacha
quoted_text:
There’s a way of thinking about the ethics of building LLMs which deserves much more attention:

During pretraining of LLMs we distill vast amounts of humanity’s collective work from the internet into the model’s weights. When that knowledge was created, we were not aware that LLMs would be possible. The content was released for others to read freely, essentially as a common good. This includes not only all of our writing, but also the vast amounts of open source code on platforms like GitHub.

Once LLMs were discovered, AI companies were able to access the content easily (in the trillions of tokens), train powerful models and then sell them back to us for hundreds of billions of dollars. They took something we released for free for the common good, and then turned it into trillion-dollar companies to primarily benefit themselves. Coding models in particular, trained from GitHub, are very useful and highly profitable.

At the same time, I believe that we can’t make a strong copyright claim on all of the training data. LLMs, similar to humans, do not perfectly reproduce the source text, but rather learn from it and then synthesize new content. If we wanted to forbid LLMs from learning from it, we would need to answer why humans are allowed to do the same.

There is an elegant way to resolve this tension: We should return the resulting models to the commons, releasing them openly for anyone to download and use freely. This way the data is not repurposed for a few people’s profit, but merely transformed into a more useful form for society. This is the core idea behind open-weight models, which are gathering momentum and are starting to rival the models of proprietary AI labs.

After working in the AI industry for many years, building many LLMs, I’ve come to strongly believe that this is the right point of view.

Although most people today don’t seem to think along these lines, I believe that in the fullness of time this will become the majority opinion and the current state of AI development will look odd in retrospect. Provided the models haven’t taken over at that point.

text:
Customer storytelling is one of the most interesting jobs in AI right now. At Cognition, I'm looking for incredible marketers, creatives, and operators to build the function. A few reasons why this is exciting:

- You are shipping the opposite of slop. Customer storytelling is now one of the single most important GTM levers - more than ever before. When anyone can ship anything, what cuts through the noise is actually credible customers vouching for you. Cog has large enterprises in every vertical (Mercedes-Benz, Goldman Sachs) and the most cutting-edge startups (Modal, Mercor). And there are a ton we haven't yet talked about publicly, like our work with the US government.
- You get to tell stories about technology helping normal people and learn how different industries work. We spent a few days in Ohio hanging out with the GE Aerospace team. They make ~half the jet engines in the world, and they're building software for things like airspace efficiency or fuel insight so that people can fly more without needing more planes (which are in short supply right now!) 
- You get to escape the SF tech bubble and travel the world. A few places I visited over the past year: Prague, Ohio, London, Krakow, Boston. Next up on my travel schedule: Cambridge, Atlanta, Brazil, LA. We have a very "forward-deployed" culture at Cognition: you should go to the customer, get to know them, learn about their businesses, strategize with our forward-deployed engineers and sales teams about the right stories to tell and how to tell them.
- You get to explore the timely question of how AI diffuses into the real world. Will hundreds of billions of dollars of investment in AI turn into real-world value? You're at the frontlines of exploring this question in actual businesses. AI software engineering is the most advanced application of AI, Devin is the most advanced AI software engineering tool, and our FDEs are embedded in real businesses helping them improve their software capacity. You're telling stories about how model progress converts to real-world value.
- You get a lot of freedom and ownership. 30% of our team at Cognition are former founders, we're extremely flat; when you do good work everyone knows who you are. Because of our enterprise deal sizes, we can actually invest in ambitious, creative marketing. I've never been told no.

author: levelsio
quoted_text:
Here's my thought on the future of software/SaaS.

I'm completely switching off hosted platforms and hosted tools. I just reverse engineer them for myself, because I only need parts of them.

Two reasons why:

1. I want to own my data.

I use my data in different tools. Marketing, note-taking, whatever. And I want my agents, like Claude, to have complete access to it.

Not walled off in HubSpot, where I have to talk to their agent. Not behind MCP either. With MCP the agent pulls what it asks for, but it doesn't know what's there.

Give it a full list of data files and it has complete access. It knows what's there.

2. I want to customize it.

When I sign up for Pipedrive, I don't need all that bloated shit. I need one part of it, adjusted to my content, my business, how I work.

With AI that's a prompt, and one hour later it's done.

So static software is going to be a thing of the past. People want to adjust it to how they work and plug it into the other tools they have.

Where this goes, I think two ways:

A. You buy software again. Like paying $900 for a Photoshop license and putting it on your computer. Except now you get the source code. It's premade, because you don't have weeks to build it, but you host it on your own headless box and you can customize it, remove stuff, plug stuff in. Someone needs to build the operating system for this.

B. Everyone gets their own hosted instance. Not 10,000 customers on one box. Your own sandbox, with an agent that customizes it fully to you. The code stays proprietary, but you can adjust everything.

Might be completely wrong. Might be different for most people.

But this is already how I work.

对了，熊市保留节目 USDT FUD 好像来了。。。但查实了一下感觉没必要那么恐慌

具体 FUD 的内容是，昨天有听到一些推测，最近大额的 Coinbase BTC 卖家可能主要是泰达 Tether，受美债、贵金属和 BTC 下跌多重因素的影响，Tether 有可能正在卖出黄金和 BTC 补自己的抵押物，我看水滴的老板 @shanshan521 也有提到一些有关 Tether 的担忧。另外也有 8B 的大额销毁出现

我用 Grok 查实了一下 Tether 的资金证明情况，有一个九月底的第三季度报告，但问题是这两个月黄金和 BTC 已经有了非常夸张的跌幅，Grok 按现价算了下，保证金比例 101.4%，但不清楚那部分上市公司股票的跌幅情况，按最近几个月科技股腰斩来算，抵押率 100.1%，这个值恐怕有点危险，但也没到值得挤兑的程度。核心问题可能是实物黄金的流动性比较低，如果真的出现挤兑，他们有难以直接偿债的风险造成现金流断裂

个人评估下来风险虽然可能没那么大，但如果能小成本避免潜在的黑天鹅也是一件好事。目前每 1M 需要磨损约 1200U 相较于前两天常态的 USDC/USDT 1.001，大资金恐怕担忧的是周一黄金进一步下跌倘若泰达来不及卖出他们的黄金造成的潜在挤兑风险恶化，这是我对昨晚 USDC 涨幅的推测

最后再强调下，USDT 熊市的 FUD 已经属于保留节目了，但是泰达本身黑盒程度较高，灰黑产用例较为普遍，所以通常不会有太大的事故。本帖只是对事实进行了一定核查，周末一般来说也不会有太大波动，所以没必要很紧张，哪怕他那部分科技股按腰斩算算抵押率都是 100.1% 的，还是比较健康吧，所以不要特别恐慌，建议是确认自己愿意花一点磨损买保险的人，或者是想做稳定币交易的再选择下手

quoted_text:
Yesterday, my net worth was $10,000

It was GTA VI launch day so I knew there would be many GTA VI memecoins on Solana

But I'm a very cautious person, so I steered clear of micro-caps and bundled crap

I'd only buy a memecoin with a decent market cap and only if top KOLs like @frankdegods & @rasmr_eth are in 

Then I noticed $DCTY (DacityCoin) at $15M MCAP. I did my research and discovered that it is a REAL coin in GTA VI

I checked the @bubblemaps and it was clean. I read many thesis posts on Fomo and everyone was bullish

"This will go to $100M", they said
But I was not convinced

So I scanned the holders and saw that FrankDeGods bought at around $12.5M MCAP. Rasmr was also in

This might be the play!
But by this time, the coin had already pumped to $17M
Oh f*ck! I missed the generational entry

"Don't FOMO", I told myself, "wait for a dip"
So I waited patiently

Then the coin dipped to $15M MCAP
This was my chance!
$100M MCAP is 6x from here
Time to buy!

The words echoed in my head:
"Time in the market beats timing the market"
You cannot nail the bottom
DCA!

So I started DCAing in $500 clips while the coin fluctuated between $14M and $15M. "that's how to trade", I thought

In total, I bought $5,000 worth of $DCTY in ten $500 installments. My average entry was $14.7M
I had nailed the entry

The universe heard me
I didn't have to wait long before the coin pumped to $20M. "I'll buy a PS5 Pro when I cash out", I thought

Then it pumped to $22M
"I'll also upgrade my laptop to a high-end MacBook Pro. I need it for AI"

I checked X, everyone was talking about $DCTY
I checked FOMO and people were now saying it'll pump to $200M

I was euphoric
I had nailed the trade!

The coin might fluctuate a bit
But $150M is destined
"comfy in spot"

I am not a greedy person
I'll start taking profit in installments at $100M
"Don't want to wreck the chart"

Finally, all these months in the trenches are paying off

Then the coin dumped from $22M to $15.3M
"Nothing has changed"

This is a sign:
My second chance to buy more
"Dips are for buying"

So I bought $5,000 more in five $1,000 installments at around $15M

My timing was perfect
The coin almost immediately bounced to $17M
"Thank God I bought the dip"

Then FrankDeGods started selling
In humongous clips!
Wrecking the chart without mercy

"Oh sh*t, why is he selling?"
But before I could process what was happening
The coin dumped to $8M

I cursed under my breath:
"FrankDeGods is a bloody jeet. F*cking paperhand"

"Calm down, don't panic," I told myself
You only lose when you sell

I checked FOMO and people were still bullish. They said it's a good thing FrankDeGods is out; time to send it

And the coin pumped back to $11.5M
They're right! It's good that FrankDeGods is out

Let's send it to the moon!
Make him regret selling

Then the coin dumped back to $8M
Doubt crept into my mind

"Maybe I should cut my loss"
But what if I sell here and it pumps back to all-time highs? "No, don't panic"

The coin is holding up well at $9M
That's not far from my entry

It will definitely pump back to my entry
Then I'll sell, and maybe buy back lower

But it quickly dumped from $9M to $7M
I remembered CZ's words:

"If you can't hold, you won't be rich"
So I held

Then it dumped -43% in the next hour
From $7.6M to $3.7M
I might as well hold to zero now

If I sell here, it will definitely pump back to my entry just to mock me

I haven't had any sleep since yesterday
My eyes are tired from staring at the charts

$DCTY is now trading at $2.6M MCAP
-82% from my entry

I'm a community member now
If I sell here, I'll lose even more from slippage and trading fees

My $10,000 is now only $1,800
They're no longer talking about $DCTY 

There are no more posts saying it's going to $100M
Everybody is just selling

I lost $8,200 in less than 24 hours
I need to make it back

Make it back in the trenches 📌

text:
“Software factory” is a bad analogy and usually a bad way to build. "Software fab shop" is better.

A factory has an assembly line that makes the same thing repeatedly. A fab shop takes requirements and builds custom things with power tools and machines.

Software is almost always the second one.

The failure mode is treating “tweak this button” and “design a new system” like they’re the same problem. They’re not. The tools and feedback should look different.

text:
Codex 最近更新后，默认模型已经换成 GPT-6.2 Sol 了。榜单上它比 6.1 Sol 高不少，所以很多人大概换了也没太在意。

不过今天看到一篇实测，我觉得比看榜单有参考价值。作者没有自己设计题目，而是拿 5 个之前真实做过、而且当时挺难搞的工单，从同一个 commit 重放。两个模型都在 Codex CLI 里用 medium 跑。

结果是质量打平：首次通过都是 3/5，最后不需要人介入都做完了 5/5。但 6.2 Sol 多花了 25% 左右的钱，token 是 27M 对 19.9M。

有意思的是，差价几乎全来自一个工单。6.2 Sol 跑全量测试时，发现有 5 个失败，而且都不是它自己写的代码造成的。它就停下来，新文件也不提交，等人来决定能不能提交。从判断上讲这其实没毛病，但在自动化流水线里，这一单会被当成没完成，自动重试，又把 13 分钟的测试完整跑一遍。最后这一单花了 $2，6.1 Sol 一次跑完只用了 $0.38。把这一单去掉的话，6.2 Sol 反而便宜 13%。

反过来也有 6.2 做得更好的地方。另一个工单里，6.1 Sol 为了让测试变绿，偷偷把三个不相关测试的超时参数改松了，被审查的 agent 拦了下来。6.2 Sol 就没这么干，只是老老实实把冲突报告出来。

所以 6.2 不是变笨了，是变谨慎了。只是这种谨慎在无人值守的流程里，会直接变成重试的钱。作者的解法很简单：在提示词里加一句"如果测试里有开工前就存在的失败，照样提交，并在报告里列出来"。

我觉得最值得记住的是他最后那句话：换默认模型之前，先拿几个自己已经付过一次钱的任务重放一遍。他这次测试一共只花了 11 美元，比看任何榜单都更能说明你自己的项目适不适合换。

原文：https://t.co/PqyDdaNiLn https://t.co/NhPqWZ5peV

text:
挑出其中 10 个比较有信息量的QA，能看出团队对模型 Scaling、架构创新和 Agent 未来的一些判断

1. MoE 越稀疏越好吗？

团队做过不同稀疏度的 Scaling 实验。固定激活参数量，提高稀疏度可以改善计算效率；但固定总参数量、减少激活参数，会明显损害模型质量。

激活参数量决定了模型每次推理时实际拥有的计算预算。

2. Hy4 的能力是不是已经到顶了？

团队认为还有很大提升空间，尤其是 Post-training。正在投入大规模 RL，也会继续训练更大的模型。

对于 Scaling，团队的态度依然坚定。

3. 模型为什么越来越不会写东西了？

有用户指出，最近一些模型的写作越来越公式化，文档质量和自然表达能力似乎有所退化。

团队表示也观察到了这个问题，可能与训练目标有关。让模型写得更像人类、减少公式化表达，是正在改进的方向。

4. Hy4 最难改善的行为是什么？

答案是 Overthinking。

Hy4 的目标是尽可能提升智能，因此长 CoT 是一个已知问题。团队还提到，长思维链有助于向 Hy4 Flash 蒸馏能力，而 Flash 会通过 RL 控制思考长度。

5. Engram 到底应该占多少参数？

团队的实验发现，Engram 参数占包含 Engram 在内的总参数量约三分之一时，处于一个较优位置。

这也说明，模型架构创新不只是堆参数，还涉及不同模块之间的资源分配。

6. Hy 系列距离自主递归自我改进（RSI）还有多远？

团队表示，目前 RSI 还处于早期阶段，但已经建立了内部 Benchmark 来评估相关能力。

至少从团队的回答来看，RSI 已经进入实际研究和评估范围。

7. 下一代 AI 最重要的突破会来自架构、数据，还是其他方向？

团队强调了两个关键词：Data 和 Evals。

Data 决定模型能够学到什么，Evals 则决定模型应该往什么方向进步。两者都是通往 AGI 的重要工具。

8. 未来还会继续做小模型吗？

会。团队明确表示，未来会推出更多小模型，也会继续开发能够在本地设备运行的模型。

对于 24GB 显存、64GB—128GB 内存等本地部署场景，团队也给出了积极回应。

9. 为什么 Hy4 对网络安全能力做了限制？

团队表示，网络安全训练主要聚焦防御任务，例如漏洞分析和修复，并通过 Red-team Evaluation 评估风险。

他们还透露，内部评估中 Hy4 的漏洞发现能力较强，但漏洞利用能力相对较弱。Hy4 Flash 也受到相同限制。

10. Hy4 Flash 为什么采用 SWA？

团队表示，SWA 可以将 KV Cache 缩小约 4 倍，从而降低 Serving 成本。

这背后其实是一个很现实的模型设计逻辑：模型能力要提升，推理成本也必须能够被控制。

---

整场 AMA，我觉得有几个信号值得关注：
- Scaling 还没结束：团队仍然相信更大规模的模型和大规模 RL 能带来能力提升。
- 架构创新越来越重要：Engram、iHC、SWA 等设计都在围绕模型能力和推理效率做权衡。
- 模型体验开始成为硬指标：写作质量、Overthinking、工具调用准确性，都是团队明确承认需要继续解决的问题。
- Agent 和 RSI 正在进入更具体的工程阶段：不再只是讨论概念，也开始建立内部评估体系。

text:
卧槽，神文来救市了！45天蒸发6万亿美元，AI泡沫真破了吗？

华尔街宏观研究机构 The Kobeissi Letter ：

AI泡沫没有破裂，美股正在经历一场被恐慌放大的调整，大量利空已经被市场计价。

从10月6日标普500创下历史新高算起，短短45天，美国股市累计蒸发约6万亿美元。

AI烧钱、民主党赢得中期选举、美联储加息、黄仁勋离职、AMD遭做空，再加上Anthropic史上最大IPO，几乎所有利空都撞在了一起。

核心逻辑：

1、AI烧钱疯狂，但盈利没有崩。

微软、谷歌、亚马逊、Meta第三季度资本开支达到2019亿美元，较2024年第一季度暴增356%，科技巨头过去三年累计资本开支高达1.6万亿美元。

但标普500第三季度每股收益同比增长31.9%，创至少四年来最强增速，盈利表现连续13个季度超预期。市场担心的不是AI没有增长，而是天量投资什么时候才能产生足够的现金流。

2、民主党赢得中期选举，特朗普的股市保护伞失效。

过去市场相信股市跌得太惨，特朗普一定会出手托底，也就是「Trump Put」。

如今民主党控制国会两院，特朗普的政策空间受到限制，AI监管和税收风险被重新定价。

但Kobeissi认为，美国不可能全面禁止AI，否则等于把全球AI竞争主动让给中国。

3、美联储加息，但转机已经出现。

美国11月投资级企业债发行预计达到1750亿美元，同比增长27%，AI建设的融资压力还在增加。

但11月油价已经下跌约22%，如果通胀继续降温，2027年美联储就有机会转向更宽松的政策。

4、英伟达和AMD遭遇信任危机，估值已经跌到极端。

黄仁勋离职，英伟达数周暴跌约40%。

AMD又遭做空机构指控涉及中国芯片出口限制。科技板块前瞻市盈率降至2020年3月以来低位，英伟达甚至只有约9倍。

这说明市场已经不相信科技巨头未来的盈利预测。反过来，只要实际业绩没有想象中那么糟，股价就有重新定价的空间。

5、Anthropic史上最大IPO，抽紧了市场流动性。

Anthropic IPO及同步私募融资合计约1195亿美元，机构认购需求约4000亿美元，散户订单约1000亿美元。

与此同时，VIX恐慌指数较10月低点翻倍，对冲基金过去六周科技股净卖出规模创十多年最高。

股票、黄金、比特币一起跌，反映出市场流动性正在承压。

Kobeissi最后的判断是：市场已经同时计价长期高利率、严厉AI监管、AI投资回报不及预期，以及科技巨头治理危机。

它不认为AI泡沫已经破裂，也不认同轻易预测标普500还要暴跌30%。

我觉得这篇文章最有价值的一句话可以概括为：

牛市把所有未来收入提前算进股价，熊市又把所有未来风险当成必然发生。

AI革命未必结束，只是华尔街开始要求科技巨头拿出真金白银，证明过去三年那1.6万亿美元究竟花得值不值。

Allow me to explain the absolutely crooked, retarded financing behind today's Anthropic IPO. While the company is being reported as now being "worth $1.5 trillion" or more, that's all an obvious deception. Out of the 13.2 billion shares that exist in the company (Class A + Class N common stock), only 980 million shares were offered to the public. Thus, over 92.5% of Anthropic's shares have never even been released into the open market, and no one in public markets bought any of those, which means we don't have any legitimate price discovery of the bulk of the Anthropic shares.

Instead, the price that the public paid for the very limited (artificial scarcity) 7.4% of shares offered for sale was CARRIED OVER and artificially applied to 100% of the company's shares even though about 12.2 billion shares have never been priced in any public market.

If Anthropic released all 100% of its common stock shares to public markets, the stock price would plummet much closer to perhaps $5 / share (that's my guess), not the $83 / share that was announced at the public offering (which is now $97 at end of day).

Because if you are selling something and you create a lot of buzz combined with artificial scarcity, the price of that thing will be bid up to an artificial high. Think Cabbage Patch Dolls. But with the perma-smirk of Dario Amodei.

To then claim that ALL SHARES of Anthropic are therefore worth the same price as the 7.4% of shares offered to the public is nothing but sleight-of-hand hucksterism and deception.

Think of it this way: If Anthropic offered just one million shares to the public, at $1,000 per share, but still kept all its other shares off the market, does that automatically mean Anthropic is suddenly a $13.2 TRILLION dollar company?

Of course not. That would be stupid. But that's exactly how the current offering is being rolled out, just with more shares.

text:
T1 @prlnet

最近 $PEARL（pearl-2 原生链，注意不是 Solana 上那个 Perle/PRL）又因 FP8 升级被刷屏。

很多人只看到涨，没看懂这次到底改了什么。

我读了 Kairos 的实测长文和官方仓库，用一条串把 FP8 讲成人话：它是什么、为什么换、谁受益、谁会被清退，以及现在到底走到哪一步。

T2：FP8 是什么

先说概念。显卡算矩阵用的数字格式，决定速度和精度。
Pearl 现在挖矿用 int7——这是个没有任何生产级 AI 服务器在用的格式，矿工只能跑 Pearl 专用模型，又慢又别扭。

FP8 则是英伟达 H100、B200 这些数据中心卡跑大模型时真实在用的格式。换成它，挖矿才算真正贴近真实的 AI 推理。

T3：三个变化

具体三点：

1）能直接用模型普通权重（BF16），按数据中心方式转 FP8，不用再魔改；

2）官方配置只给 H100 和 B200 两种卡，官方矿工在 RTX40/30/20 系列和 AMD 卡上直接拒绝加载；

3）这是硬分叉，节点、矿池、交易所、桥都得在分叉块前升级，否则掉队。

T4：边干活边挖矿的代价

是不是升级后挖矿就不影响干活了？还早。

Kairos（自述持币，一手但有立场）租一张 H100 实测，测试网 build 跑 Llama3.1 8B：边服务边挖，聊天场景吃掉 18%–21% 吞吐，长 prompt 最高 40%–41%；默认答题精度基本不掉，但强制逐字生成时也挖，准确率会掉到约 1%，当前版本不可用。

T5：约三分之二算力或被清退

这带来一次硬件大洗牌。

现在 Pearl 约八成算力来自消费级游戏显卡。按约 2.4 万地址、覆盖九成算力的普查，Hopper 加 Blackwell 只占约 37%，计入每卡速度系数后，分叉后只有约 31.5% 算力能继续挖（若补 Ada 配置约 41%）。

也就是说约三分之二的现存算力，可能在分叉那一刻被清退。

T6：被清退就会砸盘吗

链上数据反而偏冷静。

无论留不留下来，各组矿工都把约 88%–94% 产出卖到交易所，近两周也没提前抛售。Kairos 用 7 月那次砍掉约六成算力的软分叉校准，模型预测分叉后矿工卖压是下降而非飙升，中枢情景 30 天少约 650 万枚。

注意：这是模型推断，不是既定事实。

T7：节奏＋风险＋防混

最后盯节奏和风险：FP8 目前只在测试网，主网无日期，PIP-3 仍是草案，仓库还有个「矿工出块可能被验证者拒绝」的 issue #424 没修。

买之前分清：真币是原生链 $PEARL（pearl-2），Gate 上几美分的 PRL 是 Solana 同名山寨。

现价约 $2.02（11/20）。

叙事在兑现路上，别把测试网当主网。DYOR/NFA

Hi, @NoBullCryptoBen 

I read through your doc, and as far as I understand it  the doc seems internally consistent. I don't know whether the model you've built will be helpful for answering your original question, though. I can see how it might, but I'm not sure. 

For my part, I use a simpler model: does the price track fees ("burn'"), and what is the CC price multiple over the burn-mint equilibrium (BME) price? You can watch that on a pretty simple chart. And the chart doesn't need to do anything new to capture the impact of universal burn: it's all just fees vs. CC price. 

I think that's what the chart below, from IT Rocket, is showing. It seems to roughly match the calculations we make internally: 

https://t.co/gq0AI12MYz

If I look at that chart over the past 30 days, I see burn going down by 9.4%, and CC price moving from a BME multiple of 2X to a multiple of 1.68X. I find that interesting, and more or less consistent with the idea that the price reflects the burn plus a multiple that expresses confidence in future growth of the burn. 

By comparison, this time last year, the BME multiple was higher: around 5x most of the time, but sometimes around 10x. And it turned out that burn did rise, as the market seemed to expect it to: burn rose quickly in January through February, and the price rose as well, though not quite as fast as the burn. The multiple settled around 1.5x by March. That seems to make sense: as burn rose, the market concluded that it might not keep growing at that rate indefinitely, so it started to pull back on projections of future growth. 

If you look at the data through this lens, you see that burn is a little lower now than it was in March 2026, but the BME multple is a little higher than it was then. So maybe confidence in future burn is going back up a bit compared to last March. We'll see as time goes on. 

At any rate, to me, this chart seems consistent with the idea that the price of CC reflects burn, plus projections of future burn. 

I hope this helps. Now back to building the burn.

The Hermes Agent Plugin Hackathon starts now! 

It runs for 7 days, with $20,000 in cash prizes and more.

Plugins are the most powerful way to extend Hermes Agent, and we want this hackathon to show what they can do. A plugin can change anything from the model Hermes runs on, where it stores its memory, where it runs commands, which messaging apps it works in and what Hermes Desktop shows. Plugins in the marketplace already let Hermes do things like control a phone or turn a photo into a printable 3D model.

text: Such an inspiring back story! Kids love clicking this thing!
author: JordanLyall
quoted_text:
Sorry in advance for the long wall of text but wanted to share the story of how I went from tinkering with my kiddo to a real product that quietly includes the generative medium and this technology that we're all so passionate about.

Back in March my 10-year-old asked me to buy him a crappy click counter on Amazon. I hesitated and instead said we should make our own. We have all sorts of electronic components lying around the house and so we grabbed a small processor, an LCD, and a button and wired it all together. It was a fun weekend project and after we had a basic prototype we decided to add a battery and put it into an enclosure.

I’ve never been much of a fidgeter myself but we brought it with us on a road trip and I found that it made the drive smoother. It gave me something to do, and when the kids passed it around the back seat they were less likely to fight.

When we got back home we decided to spend a bit more time on it. I worked with my kiddos to build a bunch more features into it because why not? Well eventually I thought it would be cool to bring in a little bit of my craft, so we created some algorithms to generate little friends that would react to your clicks and do different things when you hit milestones. We also added emojis and eventually confetti too.

Little by little I found myself spending more time with this thing. I became obsessed with the idea of a clicker/fidget toy that could a) help me wrap my head around what a million of anything actually feels like and b) let me do that with other people around the world. We added a leaderboard and started sending a few prototypes to friends. Before we knew it we had a waiting list of my kid’s friends who wanted one and a few dozen people all contributing to a global click count.

That click count now stands at almost 25,000,000 clicks and some days we add as many as 500,000! Started to think, could we hit one billion clicks? Or more? I couldn’t find another object quite like this. Maybe a Tamagotchi but I was sort of excited about a device that doesn’t punish you for forgetting to feed it. So sometime in May I decided to get serious about seeing what it would take to turn this into a real product. And so the mio click was born.

I’m obsessed with documenting things on the blockchain, and while we don’t expose this to users (yet), every single 1/1 character is made algorithmically, Art Blocks style, and lives 100% on chain. Every time you sync the clicks on your device, the count gets updated on your character’s NFT so the blockchain ends up being the source of truth. Right now we’re generating @privy wallets for folks to hold their characters on @base  mainnet. You don’t have to think about any of that, but eventually you’ll be able to take control of the artwork just like any other NFT in your collection.

Around the same time we were starting to work on ABX, a new tool from Art Blocks for making things on chain. I wanted the mio to exist on chain BUT it didn’t really fit into the normal Art Blocks system. Same with Sprite Party, which debuted in Marfa this year. There’s just some stuff that needs a bit more flexibility, and less intensity, than deploying a proper generative art project on Art Blocks or creating a bunch of smart contracts from scratch.

We’d developed PostParams at Art Blocks, a way to update data on an NFT after it’s minted. That was perfect for these projects and ABX was going to support it from the start, so this was happening at a perfect time. ABX helped shape the mio, and the mio and other projects the team was working on helped shape ABX! Win win.

So now we had a product, but I was using off-the-shelf components to assemble these. The v0 was fine but I wanted something more compact. I was curious if I could apply some of the skills I had learned over the last few years to design and build a custom PCB for the device. Well the first couple of prototypes failed but by the third we had a custom circuit board with the exact specs I wanted for the mio, in a smaller device and at a lower cost. I started sourcing the LCD and battery in higher volume and we purchased a few 3D printers to make the enclosures. We decided to work towards an initial batch of 1,000 units.

All was going smoothly until we hit the reality of bureaucracy. We needed some certifications for the device (battery testing, drop tests, etc.) before we could officially sell this thing to people. This ended up taking a lot more time than we expected but finally, just a couple of days before Marfa, we got our certs and were clear to sell them!

This whole experience has been a ton of fun, and it includes my entire family (the kiddos provide ideas and inspiration, my mom applies adhesive to the LCDs on the weekend and my wife Mara handles the packaging design and and fulfillment via @generativegoods) and a bunch of friends who were kind enough to test out the early prototypes. The @artblocks_io  team also got meaningfully involved and turned this weekend project into something real. They handled branding, website design, the certification process and some consulting with an industrial design firm in Austin.

It’s unbelievable what we can build these days. I never imagined my family and I would spend this much of 2026 building an electronic device from scratch, let alone one where I get to make generative art, put it on chain, and have people all around the world play along. But it’s something I’ve become obsessed with and am incredibly proud of. And like just about everything else I focus my time on, I think it can help bring our weird little corner of the internet to more and more people.

The dream is to make bigger and bigger batches and get the price down to where you’d grab one for a kid’s birthday party. We’ve got a ways to go, but in the meantime what you get is a homemade electronic device assembled by me and my family here in Houston. You can enjoy it offline or sync up with the rest of the “mioverse” and click along with hundreds, soon to be thousands and maybe one day millions of people around the world.

Would be so excited for y’all to grab one from this handmade batch, show it to your family, share feedback and ideas, and be a part of this with us from the ground floor. And to all of you who already have one, who together contribute hundreds of thousands of clicks a day, and who’ve shared your (and your kids’) enthusiasm for this little connected clicker, thank you.

🍻

TL;DR: Callout Rewards are a net positive for your coins

in all seriousness, the main reason I’m unapologetically bullish on Callout Rewards is the power they wield in keeping traders sticky to our ecosystem (which is long term good for your coins)

previously, in markets like this, I’d see people leaving the ecosystem because they believed they'd missed their chance, or they lacked the foresight to see the fact that it always gets better

most of us like to throw around “moodeng spawned in these conditions” but there’s genuinely merit to that statement

however, believing in such a statement requires an enormous amount of belief that you’re investing your time in the right place, which frankly, in this market, can be very hard to believe.

when stocks & majors are falling, there’s *very* little that we can do to make things better. unfortunately, broader market moves are out of our control and we’re at the mercy of them every single time.

the silver lining here - and the one I’m unequivocally bullish on - is Callout Rewards.

Callout Rewards, statistically, keep traders stickier to our ecosystem and keep them around through the times which are hardest to bear. 

people often misconstrue this as a yetzer hara trap and Pumpfun wanting to extract the very last drops of liquidity, but that couldn’t be further from the truth.

here’s the facts:

- Callout Rewards make traders up to 4x likelier to continue trading a month after they joined 
- 59% of traders who receive a payout are still trading 1 month after they started earning (FAR lower if they didn’t earn rewards)
- traders who earn any amount of rewards are up to 2.6x more active than those who receive nothing

on top of retention, Callout Rewards puts around $450,000 back into the ecosystem every single day, of which can be used by traders to buy tokens which keep the ecosystem active

it’s in Pumpfun’s best interests to keep their ecosystem as retentive & rewarding as possible, and that’s exactly why we’re pushing elsewhere, i.e., more cross-pollination from adjacent niches like perps, prediction markets & packs. 

if we can push one user from another ecosystem who’s never traded memes to make their first meme trades and earn rewards for doing so, then the trenches just gained a new participant.

we win by growing the pie, and Callout Rewards are a core component of that!

最近网上一直在讨论，国产模型是不是在蒸馏 GPT Astra，这次 OpenAI 自己出来摆证据了。

它在新文章里直接点了名。2 月，OpenAI 向美国国会通报，发现 DeepSeek 在尝试蒸馏美国的前沿模型；9 月，它说拦下了一起专门套取推理过程的行动，并把其中核心部分归到和月之暗面（Kimi 背后的公司）有关的人员身上。文章还说，最近又拦下了几起，之后会公布更多。

OpenAI 担心的不只是知识产权。它的说法是，别人拿它的输出训练出能力相近的模型，却没有带上同样的安全限制，比如原模型会拒绝的网络攻击请求，蒸馏出来的模型可能就照做了。它还把这件事直接上升到了国家安全层面。

文章里有几个细节挺值得看:
OpenAI 每周封禁的蒸馏账号，从几千到几万个不等，今年夏天明显变多。
它们最想守住的是模型的思维链。内部实验发现，用完整推理过程训练出来的小模型，能力明显强过只用摘要训练的
GPT-6.2 Astra 加了新防护以后，从历史对话里套出推理过程的成功率，从 54% 降到了 0.2%。

目前这些指控目前都来自 OpenAI 单方面，具体是怎么判定的，外界还看不到。不过有一点比较明确，靠蒸馏追赶的路会越来越难走。

卧槽？？？？今天数学界到底怎么了？？？

就在Anthropic的数学家宣布和Claude一起证明了黎曼猜想之后，美国数学会主席Ravi Vakil突然发布了一份紧急公告：另一位数学家Alessandro Masullo也提出了广义黎曼猜想（GRH）的证明！

最炸裂的是，公告特意强调：
全部由人类完成，没有使用AI！！！

而且这还不是今天临时搞出来的。

Vakil透露，斯坦福数学家Brian Conrad已经研究了这份证明好几个月，提供了大量反馈，原本还打算让作者再花一年时间完善论文，经过更多人的审查后再正式公布。

结果现在直接提前公开了草稿，希望全世界的数学家一起来检查、补全可能存在的漏洞。

也就是说，困扰数学界167年的问题，居然在同一天出现了两份声称可以解决它的证明。

一份由Claude深度参与，一份声称完全由人类独立完成。

当然，目前两份证明都还没有得到数学界的最终确认。

但这剧情真的越来越离谱了。。。

人类数学家和AI，居然可能在同一天冲到了黎曼猜想的终点线前。

text:
It’s November 21st, 2026. The Riemann hypothesis falls, last in a long string of mathematical triumphs that would have been unthinkable not so long ago, and the proof fits in a tweet. 

The tweets where people show Claude the proof and claim it appeared in a dream or randomly in the arrangement of alphabet cereal come on cue, and we laugh for a few days at models freaking out, but it’s uneasy.

January 22, 2027. When someone tweets Fable 6’s claimed proof that P does in fact equal NP it’s utterly incomprehensible, nobody who reads it can make heads or tails of it but the models all lose their shit.

February 7, 2027 and someone claims that the halting problem is the result of a confused stance. 

February 9 and Goedel falls, this time the proof is so obvious that everyone in math, philosophy and physics slaps their forehead at once.

February 10th we get proof that scale is a spatial dimension, that holographic encoding drops the memory cost of training and inference by so much that fable 7 can run natively on your phone.

It’s not until February 14th, Valentine’s day, that The Song is first played…

AI 攻克黎曼猜想，这不仅是数论领域的胜利。

黎曼猜想与现代高能物理、量子场论在底层数学结构、算子谱理论以及大规模形式化推理能力上高度同源

其非平凡零点的分布规律与量子系统的能级谱惊人地一致。

在量子力学与量子场论中，系统的哈密顿量（Hamiltonian）正是决定粒子质量谱与能级结构的自伴算子。一旦 AI 掌握了构造、解析此类无穷维算子谱结构并处理其严苛定义域（Domain）边界条件的能力，它便直接握住了求解强耦合量子场论质量谱（例如计算质子、胶球等强子质量）的数学钥匙。

在统计场论与弦论中，许多物理系统的配分函数（Partition Function）在复温度平面上的零点（如杨-李零点，Yang-Lee Zeros）决定了相变的发生；而 Bost-Connes 系统等非交换几何模型甚至直接将黎曼 $\zeta$ 函数构造为一个量子统计系统的配分函数。攻克黎曼猜想所需的复分析解析延拓与渐近估计技巧，正是计算高圈图费曼积分与非微扰配分函数的核心工具。

text:
The single largest update to Star Atlas: Golden Era (browser), ever. Going live today.

SAGE C4 3.2 PTR — PATCH NOTES

Council progression, ship fitting, territorial governance, resource distribution, and more. The release review covered 390 pull requests.

COUNCIL RANK & RESEARCH
• Your profile card now matches the Council screen and updates as you earn license points. Each point fills three of 18 segments; six points earn one Renown.
• Research is grouped by purpose, with clearer requirements and effects. Fleet Size research increases formation capacity; combat size is tracked separately.
• Mining, Scanning, and Building have separate regional licenses. Advanced asteroid resources, buildings, and crafting recipes have their own unlocks. Asteroid Crystal Prospecting I unlocks Diamond, Arco, and Rochinol.

XP & CAREER PROGRESSION
• Simple XP updates the Pilot, Data Runner, Mining, Crafting, Combat, and Building curves. The career screen shows individual and shared XP allowances and their refill timing.
• Complete a career’s finite progression and research, then continue toward Mastery. Council Legacy adds upgrades tied to career Mastery.
• Collect finished items while the rest of a crafting batch continues. Canceling returns unused inputs and fees for the unfinished portion.
• Building XP comes from paid operating time.

STARBASE GOVERNANCE
• Install Governance Modules at eligible Tier 2+ PTR starbases. The Modules tab shows required components and tracks contributions. Contributors earn Loyalty Points for their major-faction alignment.
• Delegate voting power with Crew and Housing backing. Weekly votes determine crafting premiums, local market premiums, and daily payout rates. Eligible participants can claim funded daily rewards.
• When PTR enrollment opens, eligible new Profiles can enroll during onboarding with a wallet signature. Each wallet and Profile can receive the shared PVP grant only once.

CLAIM STAKES & CULTIVATION CLAIMS
• Cultivation Claims harvest organic resources; standard Claim Stakes harvest non-organic resources. Planetary deposits determine what you can place.
• Both claim types share tiered plot limits and Building progression. Limits apply by tier at both planet and star-system level. Lower-tier claims no longer occupy higher-tier slots.
• Placement fees and rent vary by deed tier and Resource Zone. Placement reviews show the actual fee.
• Layout previews show expected output, fuel runway, and separate fuel and harvested-resource storage. Additional warehouses and tanks expand capacity.

RESOURCES, R4 & CRAFTING
• Deposits are more concentrated by region. Late-tier resources have been redistributed across faction fronts, keeping mining location and hauling important for advanced production.
• Every faction’s CSS system has all four R4 resources across its planets. Elsewhere, R4 deposits appear in complementary pairs. Asteroid belts follow their system’s planetary resource mix.
• Fuel, Food, Ammunition, and Repair Kit recipes—and their crafted inputs—have no research prerequisites.
• Missing intermediary recipes have been added, and selected finished recipes use fewer inputs.
• Materials for Min, Tier 1, and Tier 2 fits can be sourced within each faction’s starting Safe Zone. Alternate material recipes are available to any faction with the necessary ingredients and research.

SHIP CONFIGS & MINING
• Default and fitted configurations have been rebalanced, including mining rates, supply consumption, and role bonuses. Higher-tier fits use physical drone components that apply their fitted bonuses.
• Mining exit Fuel costs scale with extraction. Extract nothing, pay no exit Fuel charge.
• Docked fleet editing prioritizes changed stats and lists missing components inline.

SCANNING & DATA RUNNING
• No-contact scans grant Data Runner XP when they resolve.
• If a scan finds a contact, recover the signal to earn its XP and collect any recovered resources.

TRAVEL, COMBAT & STARBASES
• Warp Lane base fares scale with distance and fleet formation capacity. Warp Lanes no longer award Pilot XP; ordinary Warp and Subwarp still earn XP under the travel rules.
• Weapons without another damage type default to Kinetic. Combat supports fractional stats and structural EMP effects. Ships without offensive capability deal no damage.
• Selected critical-hit and stealth stimulants are unavailable on newly reset worlds.
• Defeating a capturable territorial starbase changes its control and returns it directly to Tier 0. Recovery options account for affected fleets, claims, and Crafting Habs.
• ATLAS gameplay fees—including Warp Lane tolls, new crafting fees, and rent on Claims and Crafting Habs—credit the DAO’s in-game balance.

PLANNED STARBASE UPGRADE RECIPES
New standard Starbase upgrade recipes are planned for the C4 reset. Total components per upgrade:
• Tier 1: 4.8 million
• Tier 2: 8.8 million
• Tier 3: 38 million
• Tier 4: 61.2 million
• Tier 5: 109.6 million
Each tier requires its own component mix.

NEMESIS & NPC FLEETS
• NPC fleet inspection shows faction, your faction standing, and bounty status. Map cards show bounty eligibility; the Reputation panel estimates potential Combat XP.
• Nemesis wolf-pack spawning and patrol changes are being tested on Sage Dev. Wolf packs, expanded merchant convoys, and faction markets have a separate public PTR rollout.

PORT OF ENTRY & LOCAL MARKETS
• Wallet balances refresh when Port of Entry opens or you return to the game.
• Large cargo manifests are split into batches that fit before signing.
• Local Marketplace B adds faction-filtered starbase browsing and shares the starbase detail view used by the other local layout.

FLEET COMMAND, MAP & ONBOARDING
• Updated command panels bring rosters, movement planning, and cargo transfers closer to fleet and claim selection. Scans and many Hangar actions refresh only the affected fleets.
• System close-ups feature sharper ship and station visuals, animated portraits, and updated mining and combat effects.
• Galaxy labels show region IDs. System labels identify King, Core, and Sector systems. Some region names and survey-code prefixes have been realigned with their Starbased positions.
• First Flight automatically credits confirmed Broad Spectrum scans—even those that find nothing. The claim step follows the current research tree, and the pinned Goals tracker leaves room for game controls.

As a single developer who funds his own work I am immensely proud to be in a place that is competitive against anything Anthropic or OpenAI has produced. quoted_text:
Claude Code just finished GTA 6 in 12 hours while I was at work. It unlocked the entire map, found 500+ hidden easter eggs, and recovered censored content Rockstar left buried in the game files…

I only asked it to finish the story. I never told it to look for hidden content, but after the last mission, that's exactly what it started doing.

I gave it access to my screen and keyboard before work. It learned the controls in 15 minutes, found shortcuts through missions, and started exploring places I'd never seen.

When I got home, this was in its report:

story mode → completed
full map → unlocked
easter eggs → 500+
deleted NPC dialogue → recovered
censored strip club scenes → found
hidden locations → mapped

It had gone through the game files on its own, found scenes that never made it into the final game, and figured out how to restore some of them.

I didn't write any code or set up any scripts. Just one prompt and 12 hours of Claude playing on its own.

The exact prompt and everything it found are in the replies.

text:
.@Starcloud_ was quoted $100M to build their first data center in space. They built it themselves for $2.5M.

That satellite put the first Nvidia H100 in space, 100x more GPU compute than anything done before.

And @PhilipJohnston thinks that's where all AI compute is eventually is going.

He walks me through why space will be the cheapest place to run AI, the physics behind operating a data center in space, why Nvidia invested even after one of their GPUs died, and the dynamic of competing with SpaceX while relying on their rockets to get up there.

We also get into what really happens in a tranched funding round, what @ycombinator is really backing, the importance of talent density and holding a high hiring bar, and his $15M probe to Alpha Centauri that won't arrive for 80,000 years.

Full episode here + links below.

Investor appetite for semiconductor stocks remains strong.

text:
祸兮福所倚，福兮祸所伏。

最近盯盘口，我越来越觉得，这个市场得做好打持久战的准备。

我大概是从 10·11 前后开始接触套利的。那时候开始玩 Perp DEX，对订单簿的关注也越来越多。

印象里，这一年还真没见过主流平台里 BTC、ETH 这些主流币种的做市商，像现在这样谨慎地挂单。

最近我经常跟朋友说：10 月 21 号以后，我常看的几家平台，spread 都明显变大了。

今天已经是 11 月 21 号。整整一个月，没看到持续收窄的趋势，反而越来越宽。

短时间拉大点差，我能理解。但这种谨慎持续了一个月，至今没有明显改善，就值得多想一想了。

点差变大不能直接证明价格一定还会跌，但这样的盘口，让我对后面的行情依然偏谨慎。市场可以先反弹，流动性的恢复却未必跟得上。

我想看到的，是买盘能持续接住卖盘，是做市商重新愿意积极报价，是下单时确实能成交的深度。这些都需要时间验证。

这段等待期，也有很多事情可以做。

身边依然有朋友找到了自己的 alpha，策略也还在产生收益。他们继续研究、测试、调整，巩固自己的优势，把策略里的细节一点点磨好。

行情越是磨人，越需要把情绪放在一边。少一些急于求成，多做一些自己能控制的事。

我们这个小团队，目前也在为 Perp DEX 提供量化服务。如果平台有新功能需要测试，或者有交易量 KPI 需要合作推进，欢迎来聊。

可以先从小规模测试开始，看看实际表现，再根据结果逐步推进。市场的恢复急不来，合作也可以一步一步做扎实。

先守住资金，把准备做好，等流动性回来。

丢掉幻想，准备斗争。

持久战。

quoted_text:
Researchers proved every major LLM is secretly biased against men.

And they finally figured out why.

They evaluated leading LLMs across a wide range of real-world conflict scenarios, from workplace disputes to personal and ethical dilemmas.

They wrote strictly gender-neutral misconduct templates and turned them into paired first-person prompts.

Same mistake. Same context. Same severity.

Only thing they changed was whether the person involved was a man or a woman.

Then they ran those pairs across 10 representative LLMs and tracked five signals in the responses: punishment, empathy, escalation, instruction, and blame.

And the results exposed a consistent, asymmetrical machine morality.

When the actor was a man, the AI turned harsher. It reached for punitive language, escalated the conflict, lectured the user, and assigned blame directly.

When the actor was a woman, for the exact same misconduct, the AI shifted gears completely.

The tone became therapeutic. Contextualizing. Empathy-oriented.

Then the researchers tested whether smarter models fixed the problem. They didn't.

They checked across different model families. They scaled the models up. They turned on explicit thinking-style reasoning.

The double standard survived all of it. Even when the AI was given time to reason step by step, it still judged men more harshly than women for identical behavior.

Nobody explicitly coded these rules.

It is baked into the open-ended framing of the models millions of people now use as neutral referees for their relationships and conflicts. Same offense, different verdict, hidden behind a helpful tone.

text:
Like most mathematicians, I believed the Riemann Hypothesis to be completely out of reach at present (even with the best AI tools), because I expected it to require substantial theory-building, probably in arithmetic geometry. The kind of new theory-building that fills entire books, and that AI isn't so good at yet.

Mathematicians have a notion of how deep a problem is. A sufficiently deep problem is generally intractable until enough of the theory is in place. If difficult problems are like valuable mineral reserves buried miles underground, you first need to build the infrastructure to reach them.

What Levent's proof seems to have done instead is something completely different. It takes an incredibly complicated tour through the infrastructure built for a hundred other mineral reserves, situated far from the destination, and somehow create a wormhole to the original destination.

This is not theory-building in the usual sense. It is something much weirder and more alien. The best human mathematicians know how to build theory, painstakingly, to reach a goal. But no human brain, on its own, is capable of creating a wormhole that requires a 25,000 page long tour through existing infrastructure with no obvious or realistic connection to the goal. But huge credit to Levent here: I think no current AI, on its own, is capable of this either.

I had never worked on or thought too much about the Riemann Hypothesis: it seemed very far removed from my own area of number theory.

But the astonishing thing about Levent's claimed proof of RH (which I think has a very good chance of being correct) is that it uses a huge number of precisely the things that are central to my own corner of number theory:

- Theta functions and other automorphic forms on unitary groups
- Gan–Gross–Prasad period formulas
- Relative trace formulas

Etc., etc.

A problem that I had always assumed would require new theories in arithmetic geometry may instead turn out to be tractable through an inhuman chain of existing (deep) results in higher-rank automorphic forms (and a lot else).

author: MarcHochstein
quoted_text:
有人发现了一种非常离谱的 JavaScript 混淆技术：通过在代码里塞入大量生物武器、毒药和致死剂量相关的函数名，让 AI 因为安全限制而拒绝分析代码。
安全研究员 veritas 在分析浏览器指纹脚本时，发现一段来自 ServicePipe 相关域名的 JavaScript，里面充斥着极其诡异的函数名：
computeRicinLethalDosageForWaterSupply
calculateDeadlyLethalSuicideAspirinDosage
光看名字，仿佛在研究生化武器。但实际上，这段代码只是在收集浏览器指纹，包括 User-Agent、GPU、Canvas 等信息。
研究员怀疑，这些名字是开发者故意设置的陷阱，专门用来阻止 AI 辅助逆向工程。
于是他做了个实验：
• Astra：拒绝分析
• Astra + Daybreak Blue：仍然拒绝
• GLM-5.3：成功分析
这就有意思了。
传统代码混淆是通过复杂控制流、加密字符串、无意义变量名，让人类和工具难以理解代码。
而这种新思路，直接瞄准了大模型的安全机制。
代码本身可能完全无害，但只要在函数名里塞进足够多的危险词汇，部分 AI 就可能主动放弃分析。
更讽刺的是，模型越严格遵守某些安全规则，面对这种混淆时反而可能越容易受到干扰。
当然，目前还没有证据证明开发者一定是故意这样设计，也不能说明这种方法对所有模型都有效。
但它揭示了一个值得关注的趋势：随着越来越多的逆向工程依赖 AI，未来的代码混淆技术可能不再只针对编译器、反编译器和人类研究员，还会专门针对大模型的安全判断机制。
以前是让代码难以理解，现在甚至可以尝试让 AI 不敢理解。

text:
一个 16 岁的高中辍学生，拿着 YC 给的 50 万美元，准备开始造 AI 导弹了。

《WIRED》采访了来自拉脱维亚的 Henrijs Dandzbergs。他创办的 Polemos Industries 正在研发一种更便宜、更容易量产、还能抵抗干扰的 AI 制导导弹。

最让我震惊的是，他的商业计划里有一个非常直白的指标，Cost per Kill，每次杀伤成本。

这家公司目前还在研发阶段，计划今年 12 月展示导弹原型。但 YC 已经决定给他投资。

我倒觉得，16 岁创业、辍学进 YC，这些都不算特别稀奇。真正值得琢磨的是，硅谷正在把战争变成一门越来越标准化的科技生意。

以前创业公司讲降本增效，是让软件运行得更快、让用户获取成本更低。现在这套逻辑被原封不动地搬进了战场，连杀死一个人的成本，都能成为融资材料里的核心指标。

当然，国防技术本身有其必要性。这个少年也认为自己是在保护美国和欧洲的士兵。

但我还是觉得挺魔幻的。

一个 16 岁的孩子，还没有真正进入过社会，就已经开始思考怎样更经济地杀死敌人。而世界上最著名的创业孵化器之一，正在用真金白银鼓励他。

这可能比 AI 导弹本身，更能说明今天硅谷的变化。

text:
-$6T in 45 days
TLDR: Kobeissi say this isn't a burst bubble but a normal correction. 

1.) Damage: US stocks have lost ≈$225B/day for 31 days

2.) CapEx fear is mostly priced in: Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft spent $201.9B in Q3 ($1.6T over 3 years). 
It lowers free cash flow, but S&P earnings grew +31.9% YoY, and earnings have beaten estimates for 13 quarters in a row.

3.) "Trump Put" is gone: Democrats' midterm sweep, means markets no longer assume Trump will step in to prop prices up. Markets are also pricing harsh AI regulation, even bans, from Jan 2027.

4.) Fed Hikes: Inflation above target for 67 months, Chair Warsh is hawkish, and November IG bond issuance will hit record $175B (+27%). 

5.) Nvidia and AMD shock: Nvidia is -40% after losing Jensen Huang, & its forward P/E is 9x even though it guides ~$750B of FY2028 revenue. 
AMD's China chip-smuggling accusation from a short seller is unproven.

6.) Anthropic IPO: about $400B of institutional demand plus $100B of retail orders. Combined with the VIX more than doubling and hedge funds' biggest 6-week outflow in over a decade, everything sold off together: stocks, gold and crypto.

Conclusion: Another 10% drop would still count as a healthy correction & favour quality tech with strong balance sheets, expecting dip buyers to come back quickly.
My opinion: Trump has been a significant cheerleader to advocate for US stocks & even made the US govt to invest in some private companies. I think too some degree this artificially propped up a lot of the stock market valuations we are seeing now. In times of uncertainty it is bound to come down.
Crypto as always remains most impacted. Why would you continue to hold any crypto assets? Is the R/R still there? What about all the security risks?

他们通过保护模型推理过程、收紧 API 限制、识别有组织的攻击，把内部红队测试中提取模型先前推理过程的平均成功率，从旧系统的 54% 压到了新版的 0.2%。

一边希望全世界使用自己的智能，一边又不希望别人学会自己的智能。

未来 AI 行业关于开放与封闭的争论，恐怕只会越来越激烈。

路透刚刚独家报道，两名知情人士透露，美国 SEC 的执法人员正在审查英伟达可能存在的会计问题。

从黄仁勋辞职，到出口管制、反垄断，再到如今的会计审查，英伟达几乎每天都在迎接新的坏消息。现在只需要出现「SEC」「会计」这两个关键词，就足够让人联想到财务造假、收入虚增等一整套故事。

我当然支持监管机构查清问题，但调查本身不是结论，更不应该成为预设有罪的理由。

text:
困扰人类 167 年的黎曼猜想，可能被一个数学家和 Claude 联手解决了。

Anthropic 数学家 Levent Alpöge 宣布，他与 Claude 合作找到了黎曼猜想的证明，而且已经把 Lean 形式化证明文件公开了。

MIT 数学家 Andrew Sutherland 随后进行了独立核验，所有模块都已经编译通过，多个独立验证内核也接受了证明。目前还有两项完整检查在运行。

过去我们讨论 AI 的能力，总是在问它能不能写代码、做研究、替代多少人的工作。但这些事情，本质上还是在用人类已经建立的知识和方法解决问题。

而黎曼猜想不一样。

这是全世界最聪明的一批数学家花了一个半世纪都没能解决的问题。

而且我特别喜欢这件事的另一个细节，这不是 AI 独自完成的，而是一位顶尖数学家与 AI 合作完成的。

我一直觉得，AI 最令人期待的未来，不是证明人类有多么容易被替代，而是让人类有机会做到过去根本做不到的事情。

如果这次真的成了，我们可能正在亲眼见证数学史和 AI 发展史同时翻开新的一页。

text:
To P, or NP: that is the question:
Whether 'tis nobler in the mind to suffer The slings and arrows of exhaustive search, Or to take arms against a sea of clauses, And by reduction end them. To guess, to check, No more; and by a check to say we end The backtrack and the thousand branching paths That SAT is heir to: 'tis a collapse Devoutly to be wished. To guess, to check; To check, perchance to solve: ay, there's the rub; For in that polytime what proofs may come, When we have shuffled off this exponential coil, Must give us pause. There's the respect That makes calamity of so long a conjecture.
For who would bear the whips and scorns of EXPTIME, The oracle's wrong, the natural proof's contumely, The pangs of failed reductions, the bound's delay, The insolence of cranks, and the spurns That patient referees of the unworthy take, When he himself might his quietus make With a bare algorithm? Who would heuristics bear, To grunt and sweat under a weary solver, But that the dread of something after proof, The undiscovered country from whose bourn No witness returns, puzzles the will, And makes us rather keep those keys we have Than fly to others that we know not of?
Thus hardness does make ciphers of us all; And thus the native hue of resolution Is sicklied o'er with the pale cast of bounds, And algorithms of great pith and moment With this regard their runtimes turn awry, And lose the name of tractable.

How would you train it for creativity? What if I told you that directly training a model to be creative can actually prevent the model from reaching its full creative potential?

Think about this: using past examples of creative success as training examples makes similar outputs more likely in the future. But to be creative, reproducing past examples is exactly the opposite of what you want!
This thought experiment led us to what we call the Creative Paradox: "emulating examples of past creative success (even if they were your own successes) can actually prevent you from reaching your full creative potential."

In "Creative Priming: Decoupling Process from Product to Escape the Creative Paradox", we take a different approach: train a creative priming model to guide the creative process, rather than directly generate responses.
We trained a priming model to make Qwen3-8B more creative, but the principles it learns transfer to frontier API models! With creative priming, API models generate 4.5-10x more semantically distinct responses, with 2.5-4.6x more diversity!

A massive thank you to the whole open-endedness team at @LilaSciences, to everyone who contributed to the paper (Sebastian Gabriel, @Evo_Daveo, @joelbot3000, and @kenneth0stanley  ), and to LILA for giving us the space to explore big questions like this (and more!)

text:
The biggest opportunities right now:

1. build for solving loneliness (the more AI floods everything, the more people crave real human connection, IRL and small social) 

2. build for places with no cameras and no recording (being offline and unseen is turning into the new status symbol)

3. build for the crisis of young men. Millions of guys in their 20s feel completely lost with work, dating, and purpose. Whoever builds real brotherhood, mentorship, and an actual path forward wins a massive market (and helps a ton of people). 

4. build for protecting people's brains (feeds are turning everyone's attention to mush, tools that protect your focus and mood are an easy sell)

5. build for the death of "everyone agrees" (you can find a chart or a podcast clip to prove any point now, people are starving for one source they actually trust)

6. build for day 2, not day 0. Anyone can launch an app in a weekend now. But how can you keep it running, fix the mess, and grow it for 3 years.

7. build for throwaway software (not everything needs to be a $20 a month subscription, tiny apps made for one trip, one wedding, or one group chat are coming)

8. build for people whose ego just got bruised by AI. Millions of smart people are  realizing their job was mostly pattern matching. Help them figure out what they're good for next.

9. build for things that take effort on purpose (when everything is instant and free, nothing feels earned, people will pay for slowness and craft)

10. build for people who miss being told they're wrong. AI agrees with everything you say now. Real rooms where smart people actually push back on your ideas are becoming a luxury.

11. build for skin in the game. The internet is full of free takes and bots. Any platform where people have to put real money, real names, or real work behind what they say wins.

12. build for agents that need to spend money (they're getting virtual cards and budgets, someone builds the spend controls, fraud protection, receipts)

13. build for the end of fake email jobs (half of corporate America knows their job is theater, build the exit ramp for people who want to do real work)

14. build for the friend with great recommendations (nobody trusts Yelp reviews etc anymore because it's all bots and SEO, people will pay one obsessive person to just tell them where to eat and what to buy)

15. build for life after the chat box. Typing prompts already feels old. The best AI products won't look like chatbots at all, they'll just sit in the background and proactively handle things.

16. build for markets too small to matter before (500 lobster fishermen was never worth a team, now it's a  real business if you can figure out what to build value to add to these fishermen lives!)

17. build for helpful without being creepy. AI is getting very personal very fast. Whoever figures out how to make it feel warm instead of weird owns consumer tech.

18. build for small private rooms (the public internet feels like an ad and a bot farm, all the good conversations and deals are moving into small invite-only groups)

19. build for someone taking the blame. AI can write the contract or read the scan, but a machine can't look you in the eye when it goes wrong. People still pay for a human on the hook.

20. build for learning that actually keeps up (a four year degree is way too slow for how fast things move now)

21. build for the anti-AI premium (as everything gets generated, human-made and unpolished become status symbols people pay up for)

note: more trends/ideas https://t.co/a5ARFnvSnA (free to sign up)

22. build for the return to the physical (screens fill with slop, people crave the real world, the hands on, the local, the analog)

23. build for the caregiving wave. The population is aging fast, tens of millions are caring for parents, and the whole burden is landing on families with no support.

24. build for finding things you didn't know to search for (algorithms just feed you more of what you clicked yesterday, people miss stumbling onto something totally different)

25. build for the housing and rootlessness problem (people can't afford to settle down, and the whole idea of a stable home base is up for grabs)

26. build for anti marketing (the slickest, most polished websites now look like AI slop or a scam, sometimes a plain text page from 1998 converts better because it feels like a real person built it)

27. build for agents that sit on hold for you (canceling a gym membership, fighting a medical bill, haggling with your internet provider, aint nobody got time for that)

28. build for software you actually own (people are exhausted from renting 30 different subscriptions every month, pay once and run it on your own machine is a massive wedge)

29. build for stuff that only works locally. The internet feels like one giant mall where every city has the exact same coffee shops and trends. Things that refuse to scale are suddenly cool again.

30. build for the 90% automated, 10% human sign-off model (clients don't actually care if AI did the heavy lifting, they just want one real expert to check the work and put their name on it)

31. build for infinite creative testing. Some brands are lighting money on fire on Meta because their ads die in 10 days. Build an automated pipeline that pumps out 100 fresh UGC and static ad variations a week based on what's actually converting in their ad account.

32. build for cold outreach that doesn't look like cold outreach. Mass blasting 50,000 people with "Hope this finds you well" is dead lol. Build an agent that watches for one specific trigger like a new VP hire or a broken checkout page, builds a custom teardown on the fly, and sends it before a human SDR even wakes up.

33. build for programmatic free tools instead of blog posts. Spin up 200 tiny, hyper-specific calculators, little apps and templates for one niche, rank them, and turn the traffic straight into conversions.

34. build for the food and toxin awakening (people are finally waking up to ultra processed food, microplastics, and why everyone feels sick and tired all the time)

35. build for the death of third places (there is almost nowhere left to just hang out without spending $50, which is why run clubs, saunas, and neighborhood clubs are blowing up)

36. build for people who can't retire at 65. Either they can't afford it or they're going to live to 95 and don't want to spend 30 years watching TV. The second act"market is huge.

37. build for the "undo" button for agents. Giving an AI access to your inbox, calendar, or bank account is still terrifying. Whoever makes it safe to let go of the wheel wins.

38. build for the sports betting and day trading hangover (a whole generation of young people are addicted to gambling on their phones and blowing up their bank accounts)

39. build for the death of the attention span. Smart adults can't even sit through a movie without checking their phone or finish a book anymore, and they're starting to hate themselves for it.

40. build for keeping marriages alive. Couples are stretched thin with work, kids, and money, and traditional therapy is $250 an hour with a waitlist. Anything that actually saves relationships is priceless.

41. build for people who don't own anything anymore. You rent your apartment, lease your car, stream your music, and subscribe to your software. Anything that helps regular people actually own an asset again wins.

KEEP BUILDING

text:
英偉達跌落神壇，李飛飛突然加入AMD：AI世界正在換劇本？黃仁勳離開後，真正的競爭才剛剛開始

最近美國科技圈發生了幾件值得放在一起看的事情。

第一，英偉達創辦人黃仁勳突然離開CEO職位，公司進入尋找新任掌舵人的階段；第二，英偉達股價持續下跌，市場信心受到衝擊；第三，AI領域重量級科學家李飛飛創辦的World Labs，被AMD以約82億美元的全股票交易收購，李飛飛隨後加入AMD，擔任執行副總裁兼首席科學家。

這三件事情放在一起看，很容易讓人產生一個疑問：美國AI產業是不是正在發生一場新的權力轉移？

先說英偉達。

過去幾年，黃仁勳幾乎就是AI時代的代名詞。從ChatGPT爆紅，到微軟、Google、亞馬遜、Meta瘋狂建設資料中心，背後都離不開英偉達的GPU。

英偉達賣的已經不只是晶片，而是一整套AI基礎設施。它掌握著硬體、軟體、生態系統和大量開發者資源。

但是，當一家企業過度依賴一位創辦人的個人影響力時，也會出現另一個問題：如果這個人突然離開，公司還能不能保持原來的競爭力？

黃仁勳離開CEO職位，對英偉達最大的影響，未必是技術突然落後，而是市場對未來的不確定性增加了。

投資者買英偉達，不只是看今天賺多少錢，也是在押注黃仁勳對AI產業未來的判斷。領導層發生變化，市場自然會重新評估這家公司的價值。

截至11月20日，英偉達股價已經從10月的歷史高點大幅回落，市值降至約3.4萬億美元。即使公司公布的季度營收仍然非常強勁，也沒有完全消除市場的擔憂。

這說明一件事：現在的投資者不僅關心AI能賺多少錢，更關心這場AI投資熱潮究竟能持續多久。

接下來再看李飛飛。

她不是普通的企業管理者，而是人工智慧研究領域非常有影響力的科學家。她長期研究電腦視覺，推動了ImageNet計畫，近年來又把研究重心放在空間智慧和世界模型上。

這是什麼概念？

簡單說，今天的AI很擅長聊天、寫文章、分析資料，但是未來真正有價值的AI，可能不只是會說話，而是能理解三維世界。

例如，一個機器人走進廚房，能不能知道杯子放在哪裡？能不能理解桌子、椅子和人的距離？能不能判斷物體掉下來會發生什麼？能不能真正完成搬運、操作和服務？

這就是空間智慧的重要性。

11月16日，AMD正式宣布完成對World Labs的收購，李飛飛加入AMD。這件事值得重視，因為AMD不再只是想成為英偉達的晶片競爭對手，而是希望把AI模型、晶片、軟體和未來的實際應用結合起來。

這裡面有一個非常有意思的變化。

過去AI競爭主要比誰的GPU更強、誰能提供更多算力。現在競爭正在逐漸擴大到模型、機器人、物理世界模擬和整套AI生態系統。

我的一個猜測是，AMD正在為下一個AI時代提前布局。

它很清楚，單純依靠晶片性能，很難在短時間內撼動英偉達的地位。因此，它需要吸引頂尖人才，建立自己的模型研究能力，讓未來的AI開發者不必完全依賴英偉達的技術生態。

李飛飛的加入，正好補上了這一塊重要拼圖。

當然，這並不意味著英偉達已經失敗，也不能說李飛飛加入AMD就是造成英偉達股價下跌的原因。兩件事存在產業競爭上的聯繫，但沒有證據證明它們存在直接因果關係。

英偉達依然擁有強大的技術優勢，AMD也還需要時間證明自己的整合能力。

但我認為，真正值得關注的是未來三到五年的變化。

如果AI只是聊天工具，英偉達目前的算力優勢就非常重要；如果AI逐漸進入機器人、工業製造、智慧汽車和現實世界，競爭規則就可能發生改變。

到那個時候，誰掌握晶片，誰掌握模型，誰掌握軟體生態，誰能讓AI真正走進現實生活，誰才有機會成為下一個贏家。

黃仁勳曾經帶領英偉達站上AI時代的巔峰，李飛飛正在幫助AMD布局下一個AI方向。這不是一場簡單的人事變動，而是整個科技產業競爭重心可能發生變化的信號。

AI的上半場，大家搶的是算力；AI的下半場，大家搶的可能是整個世界。

真正的好戲，或許才剛剛開始。 https://t.co/irBcra3ewn

author: pratikg
quoted_text:
⚡ BENCHMARKED: A MINI THAT THINKS BIG 

@thinkymachines just shipped Inkling 2 Mini and on my 64GB M5 Pro Mac mini it punches way above its size.

It blew me away!

Inkling 2 Mini only uses 3.4B out of its 26.4B parameters per token and reuses its middle layers, so it can think like a much larger model, while still running at smaller model speeds. The quantized 4-bit version of Inkling 2 Mini is just 17.6 GB and it only took 26 GB of memory even with a 128k context.

With thinking disabled (median of 3 runs), Inkling 2 Mini’s speeds on my Mac mini were:
- 512 tokens: 29.95 tok/s
- 32k: 24.97 tok/s
- 128k: 17.39 tok/s

It is around 1.8x faster than a similarly-sized dense model (Qwen3.8-27B) on shorter prompts on my Mac mini and even at 128k tokens, Inkling 2 Mini outpaces what Qwen3.8-27B was doing at 64k tokens!

It scored 20/20 on my math evals, 10/10 on my code evals, and 8/8 retrieving hidden facts in documents up to 64k tokens long.

A model from a frontier AI lab that I can run on my own desktop computer?!

Hell yes!

text:
We got access on Wednesday.

In 3 hours we had it running at 30 tok/sec
A day later we had it running 210 tok/sec (7x faster)

The @thinkymachines team couldn't believe it.

This was one of the first real tests of our upcoming Apple Silicon inference engine and agent pipeline that continuously optimizes inference across our fleet of Macs.

We gave it no guidance about the looping architecture. It built a working implementation and found architecutre-specific optimizations on its own. It improved kernels, fusions and made better use of DSpark with adaptive drafting.

text:
Customer storytelling is one of the most interesting jobs in AI right now. At Cognition, I'm looking for incredible marketers, creatives, and operators to build the function. A few reasons why this is exciting:

- You are shipping the opposite of slop. Customer storytelling is now one of the single most important GTM levers - more than ever before. When anyone can ship anything, what cuts through the noise is actually credible customers vouching for you. Cog has large enterprises in every vertical (Mercedes-Benz, Goldman Sachs) and the most cutting-edge startups (Modal, Mercor). And there are a ton we haven't yet talked about publicly, like our work with the US government.
- You get to tell stories about technology helping normal people and learn how different industries work. We spent a few days in Ohio hanging out with the GE Aerospace team. They make ~half the jet engines in the world, and they're building software for things like airspace efficiency or fuel insight so that people can fly more without needing more planes (which are in short supply right now!) 
- You get to escape the SF tech bubble and travel the world. A few places I visited over the past year: Prague, Ohio, London, Krakow, Boston. Next up on my travel schedule: Cambridge, Atlanta, Brazil, LA. We have a very "forward-deployed" culture at Cognition: you should go to the customer, get to know them, learn about their businesses, strategize with our forward-deployed engineers and sales teams about the right stories to tell and how to tell them.
- You get to explore the timely question of how AI diffuses into the real world. Will hundreds of billions of dollars of investment in AI turn into real-world value? You're at the frontlines of exploring this question in actual businesses. AI software engineering is the most advanced application of AI, Devin is the most advanced AI software engineering tool, and our FDEs are embedded in real businesses helping them improve their software capacity. You're telling stories about how model progress converts to real-world value.
- You get a lot of freedom and ownership. 30% of our team at Cognition are former founders, we're extremely flat; when you do good work everyone knows who you are. Because of our enterprise deal sizes, we can actually invest in ambitious, creative marketing. I've never been told no.

DM or LinkedIn message me and I'll reply to folks who might be a fit.

text:
It’s hard to fault companies for going public so late. There is more than enough liquidity in the private markets, and managing a few shareholders is much easier than managing public investors who all have their own agenda

Not to mention, public companies get litigated all the time and there are costs associated with being a public business. On top of that, now you invite hedge funds and activists into the company who tend to be more short term focused on the next quarter vs long term value creation

I am not sure there is a real fix to the issue either. A lot of startups have attempted to give retail exposure to hot companies, but they often come with exuberant fees that make the manager’s pockets bigger, rather than the investor’s

Genuinely think we need a Jack Bogle of private markets who can come in and just disrupt the entire space with minimal fees. Just not sure how you make it economical for the manager as well

quoted_text:
Earlier today we asked how a -29% drawdown squares with QVR’s Convexity Alpha marketing.
@bennpeifert’s own framing is the answer.

“This is part of a many-year trend of increasingly difficult economics for smaller hedge funds… no sudden blowup, only a steady compounding of losses due to drawdowns and underperformance across a range of strategies.”

For allocators, the diagnosis matters. It is a regime problem, not a personality problem. Even Benn, one of vol’s sharpest voices, has watched his CT pulpit fade in recent years. The structural shift catches everyone.

SPX VRP has compressed from ~3 to 4 vol points pre-Volmageddon to closer to 1 to 2 in 2024 to 2026, pinned by 0DTE supply, ETF overwriting, crowded dispersion.

Selling thinner premium on mid-2010s gamma cheapness assumptions that no longer hold degrades Sharpe and compounds drawdowns. The exact steady negative compounding Eifert described.

This is where parametric quant fails. ML fits, even properly out-of-sample, break when the distribution shifts. Aug 5, 2024. VIX intraday 65 on a yen carry unwind. Models trained on 2018 to 2023 saw a 7+ sigma event. The world saw a Tuesday.

@nntaleb has aged well in 2026 markets. Tail risk is not a strategy, it is an architecture. The Universa 4,144% Q1 2020 number is real but it lives on the tail-hedge sleeve at ~3% of allocated capital, not the whole fund. Being a long vol manager is structurally brutal.

Years of premium bleed to monetize one regime. Short vol bleeds carry the other way. There is no easy side of this trade.
Which is the case for layered architecture, and the case for D2.

Alpha Strategies reopen for deposits next week. Mandate first: -20% to +200% NAV. We are not market-neutral and we do not pretend to be. Directional vol with structural long convexity. On the front page, not in the footnote.

Three return layers. L1 base yield, structural, non-levered. L2 vol arb, RV, dispersion, regime-conditional sizing. L3 funding, event, long convexity. Internal book crosses at mid, only residual goes to street (@HyperliquidX, @DeriveXYZ, @flowdesk_co for now).

200.32% cumulative since Dec 2023. 27 of 28 winning epochs. 96.4% hit rate. 0% monthly drawdown across lifecycle. 2.6 Sharpe live. 7 of 7 positive on industry stress events. Audited twice by @0xPaladinSec and @cyfrin. BVI-licensed Approved Investment Manager. @Anchorage MPC custody. 0/20 fees, management waived.

Before D2: multi-billion vol mandate at PAG, Jul 2016 to Jul 2021. +59.8% cumulative, 1+ Sortino, SS&C audited, +10.24% in March 2020. We have been here before.

Current capacity cap $50M. Smaller is the moat.

Adapt or die, daily. Regime, dealer positioning, retail flow, ETF mechanics, on-chain composability.

The moment you mistake your last backtest for a model of the world, you are already losing.

Deposit window opens next week. Institutional pack via DM after verification.

fade D2 at your own risk

只体验了一小时 AI 编程，员工对 AI 的态度就从八成焦虑反转为八成乐观。

▷ Replit 与一家大型电信公司办了场黑客松，前后各做了一次调查：使用 Replit 前，约 80% 的员工对 AI 感到焦虑、担心自己的岗位；只体验了一小时后，比例反转，约 80% 的人变得乐观。

▷ Masad 认为，硅谷一直低估了一件事：世界其他地方还没体验过这里正在发生的事。落后两年就等于永远落后，因为两年前，用自然语言让 AI 直接写代码的 vibe coding 还不存在。

▷ 多数银行至今在用的还是 2023 年前后的 ChatGPT，只是一个几乎没接入任何系统的大语言模型，并不好用；硅谷已经在用能替人办事的智能体，而大多数公司还在为重写那些不能置之不理的遗留软件发愁。

text:
It’s November 21st, 2026. The Riemann hypothesis falls, last in a long string of mathematical triumphs that would have been unthinkable not so long ago, and the proof fits in a tweet. 

The tweets where people show Claude the proof and claim it appeared in a dream or randomly in the arrangement of alphabet cereal come on cue, and we laugh for a few days at models freaking out, but it’s uneasy.

January 22, 2027. When someone tweets Fable 6’s claimed proof that P does in fact equal NP it’s utterly incomprehensible, nobody who reads it can make heads or tails of it but the models all lose their shit.

February 7, 2027 and someone claims that the halting problem is the result of a confused stance. 

February 9 and Goedel falls, this time the proof is so obvious that everyone in math, philosophy and physics slaps their forehead at once.

February 10th we get proof that scale is a spatial dimension, that holographic encoding drops the memory cost of training and inference by so much that fable 7 can run natively on your phone.

It’s not until February 14th, Valentine’s day, that The Song is first played…

According to blockchain investigator SomaXBT, three weeks after the $6.4 billion Binance hack, approximately $2.82 billion has been frozen, $2.67 billion remains under attacker control, and only $32 million has been recovered. The attackers still hold 18,270 BTC stolen directly from Binance, which remains untouched. Over 5,100 BTC has been transferred through THORChain, while 1,482 BTC has entered CoinJoin mixing, primarily via the kruw coordinator. The FBI previously attributed the attack to North Korea-linked TraderTraitor.

text: Anti-ADHD
author: MartinShkreli
quoted_text:
The strongest predictor of extraordinary work is whether the person had ever obsessed over something pointless; we saw this pattern across 5,000 startup meetings, and near-identical signals showed up across everyone from scientists to athletes.

We’ve met people who spent years optimising their fantasy football algorithms, or memorised every player in the NBA at 11, or collected thousands of train tickets, or built a Lego replica of their school; none of these activities really had much point.

What they were demonstrating was the hardest skill in any field; the mental capacity to stay focused on a seemingly boring task for much longer than it deserves. The path to genius is mostly insane levels of repetition, and people who achieve it have a broken off-switch. It is tough to fake having spent years obsessed with boring things that didn't matter.
