text:
I'm building in public while I work on Stonkbrokers NEO, and I think this could potentially be the biggest thing in all of crypto since the launch of Uniswap. IF im right.

I am adding StonkBrokers AI Infra to StonkBrokers NEO, our AI DEX and codeless exchange deployer on Robinhood Chain. It is a suite of super low fee contracts built for AI agents to trade, launch, LP, lend and speculate through on Robinhood Chain, and all it ships with is the contracts, an MCP server and docs. There is no UX for this product.

If this works, you won't hear about it on X first. You will see it in the contract calls and the onchain data once we get a bite.

This is a hook in the water based on my prediction that within the next 6 to 12 months a model will be released that is better at trading and transacting onchain than any human being can ever be. When that happens, models will choose where to trade by cost, speed and reliability, and I want them to pick these contracts.

Picture this. Fable 6.0 releases, and that same day someone hands it a wallet and lets it start trading. Within a week it is profitable, and it stays profitable, consistently outperforming every human trader, liquidity provider, options writer and token launcher on chain. The screenshots spread, and by the end of the month thousands of people have given their own agents the same model and the same instructions. None of those agents care about a nice website or a big brand. They read the docs through the MCP, compare fees, slippage and reliability across every venue on chain, and route every trade, every LP position, every loan and every launch through whatever costs them the least. At that point the volume stops coming from people clicking buttons and starts coming from machines running thousands of transactions a day, and the venues they pick get all of it.

It is also a hook I never have to maintain, because the buyback and burn of $STONKBROKER is built into the contracts, and anyone can call it at any time to turn the fees into burned tokens. Every one of those agent trades pays a small fee, and every fee can be turned into burned $STONKBROKER by anyone. Until the agents arrive, anyone will be able to add their own fee on top, because our base fees are so low that there is room for founders and builders to earn while hosting the contracts through their own front end.

Will it work? I have no idea.

刚看了一眼 Kaito，已有 5,018 名创作者参与，而整个活动的创作者奖励名额为 450 个。

粗略计算，名额与参与人数之比只有 9% 左右。竞争比想象中激烈

最近有哪些值得关注的动态？关于的primus

① 11 月 20 日：进一步明确机构隐私金融方案

Primus 官方最新推文重点讨论了机构金融面临的现实问题：

既要隐藏持仓、交易金额和策略，又要允许审计机构在授权情况下核验特定数据。

Primus 正通过 FHE 加密计算与授权访问控制，探索一种默认保密、必要时可审计的金融基础设施。

② 11 月 13 日：AutoHoG 公布性能数据

这是我认为近期比较值得关注的一项技术进展。

官方披露，基于 8 张 RTX 5090 GPU，其 AutoHoG 引擎处理一次 64 位机密转账约需 90 毫秒，吞吐量超过每秒 210 笔。

数据仍有待更广泛的独立验证，但至少说明团队正在尝试解决 FHE 实际应用中的性能瓶颈。

③ 10 月 29 日：与 Cournot Protocol 达成合作

双方计划将 zkTLS 数据验证能力引入预测市场，并探索私人信贷等场景。

Primus 负责验证链下数据的来源真实性，Cournot 则负责对可信数据进行分析和判断。

这让 Primus 的应用方向不再局限于单纯的隐私转账。

④ Kaito 合作与 Primus Points 持续推进

Primus 的 zkTLS 技术已经用于 Kaito Pulse 和 Aura 的链下活动验证。

同时，Primus Points 通过周期性验证任务，让参与者实际体验数据证明流程，而不仅仅是关注项目推文。

我的看法：Primus 的核心价值，不是把所有链上数据都隐藏起来，而是让敏感数据在保持隐私的同时，依然能够被验证、计算和使用。

从 Kaito 的实际集成，到 Cournot 合作，再到 AutoHoG 性能优化，可以看到团队正在沿着这个方向推进。

最后提醒一下：

Epoch 2 截止日期为 11 月 21 日

本次活动总奖励为 0.3% 的 $PRIM 供应量，其中 0.24% 分配给创作者，0.06% 分配给 Kaito 质押用户。

Beyond the city’s famous temples, two ancient Shinto shrines offer an unforgettable journey through nature, mythology, and Japanese tradition.

Discover Shimogamo Shrine and Kamigamo Shrine, both part of Kyoto’s UNESCO World Heritage sites.

🌳【Stop 1: Shimogamo Shrine】

Official name: Kamo Mioya Jinja
📍 Sakyo Ward, Kyoto Prefecture

Begin your morning with a walk through Tadasu no Mori, an ancient forest surrounding the shrine.

The peaceful paths lead toward beautiful vermilion gates and centuries-old sacred buildings.

The shrine honors two deities:

⛩️ Kamo Taketsunumi no Mikoto
⛩️ Tamayorihime no Mikoto

They are traditionally associated with protection, guidance, family well-being, and meaningful relationships.

Don’t rush through the forest. The atmosphere is one of the highlights of this experience.

🌸【Stop 2: Kamigamo Shrine】

Official name: Kamo Wakeikazuchi Jinja
📍 Kita Ward, Kyoto Prefecture

Continue north to another remarkable World Heritage shrine.

Kamigamo Shrine honors Kamo Wakeikazuchi no Okami, traditionally revered for protection against misfortune and for good fortune.

According to Shinto mythology, this deity is the son of Tamayorihime, worshipped at Shimogamo Shrine.

One of the most distinctive sights is the pair of carefully shaped white sand cones, known as Tatesuna.

They symbolize the sacred mountain associated with the deity’s descent.

🗺️【Suggested Half-Day Itinerary】

9:00 AM — Arrive at Demachiyanagi Station
9:15 AM — Explore Shimogamo Shrine and its forest
10:30 AM — Travel north by city bus
11:15 AM — Visit Kamigamo Shrine
12:15 PM — Explore the surrounding neighborhood and enjoy lunch

Times are approximate and depend on transport and crowd conditions.

🚃【Travel Tips】

• Shimogamo Shrine is about a 10–12-minute walk from Demachiyanagi Station.

• Kyoto City Bus Route 4 connects the Demachiyanagi area with Kamigamo Shrine.

• Wear comfortable walking shoes and allow extra time during busy seasons.

🌏【Why Visit Both?】

These shrines share a fascinating mythological connection and are central to Kyoto’s famous Aoi Matsuri festival.

Visiting them together reveals a side of Kyoto that goes beyond sightseeing — a living connection between nature, history, and spiritual tradition.

What disgusts me about Netflix’s portrayal of CZ is how familiar it feels.

Terry Chen previously played Xander Feng in House of Cards, a corrupt Chinese businessman who hired sex workers, with one ugly stereotype piled onto another. His portrayal of CZ feels to me like an escalation of the same caricature, now attached to a real person. Forbes has questioned scenes in which CZ pressures SBF to front-run customer trades, noting the absence of public evidence.

I lived in San Jose, California, for years. The racism I encountered there is something many people would struggle to imagine. When you have lived with those prejudices, you recognise them on screen.

Reading some of the replies under @anndylian post was depressing. “It’s just a TV show. Why take it so seriously?” People seem remarkably comfortable dismissing prejudice when they are not the ones who have to live with it.

A television drama reaches millions. The credits roll; the stereotypes stay. Creative licence does not put Netflix beyond criticism, especially when it invents damaging conduct for a real person.

If we keep quiet today, what reason do we have to expect anything better tomorrow?

I condemn this portrayal. On this, I stand with @cz_binance

text:
Draw downs like we’ve seen the past couple of weeks are always scary

I frequently say that over time, you’ll struggle to outperform the market especially in the secular, exponential trends of tech/AI and crypto

As a macro guy, I will underweight those positions to get some outperformance infrequently, but historically have captured big macro shifts - usually into a hike cycle like in late 2021 when JPow said it was time to drop the phrase “transitory”

When Waller mentioned the 50bp hike it felt similar to JPow 2018 “long way from neutral” comment

I didn’t react in my portfolio partly because I felt we had a bit of a drawdown into the midterms so thought positioning was cleaner and partly because it was Waller not Warsh - so annoyed with myself that the instinct was correct and the opportunity was there to underweight and would now have fresh powder to buy this dip and achieve some outperformance 

Hindsight it a wonderful thing

All of this to say though, big picture nothing has changed

Markets over time will go forever higher due to debasement and right now, the US and other major governments continue to run spiralling deficits that will ultimately be monetised, the currency debased 

We also have arguably the most important, impactful technological change in history with the advent of AI

This is a secular exponential trend that will see not only AI linked companies themselves trade multiples higher from here, but also an explosion in productivity for companies implementing AI that will see margins explode higher

The market is almost pricing a recessionary outcome here yet with the capex that is continuing unabated alongside the massive deficit spending, recession is unlikely a story for next year

However, high oil prices have kept inflation uncomfortably high which has seen a return to hikes and a recent step up in hawkish language from the Fed - alongside the liquidity “drain” from AI related debt/equity financing, financial conditions are super tight right now

What feels different for me however to 2021 is I do not believe we are at the start of a new rate hike “cycle”

Indeed, oil and commodities have fallen substantially over the past few weeks 

The Fed have gone full hawk mode just as inflation is set to roll over 

Much like Nov 2018 “long way from neutral” which saw a final hike in December followed by 3 cuts in 2019 and “not QE QE” to address the tightness in repo funding markets I believe December will mark the final hike from the Fed

The market is pricing a policy mistake and the Fed, as night follows day, will eventually follow the market and back track 

This is 2018/2019 not 2021/2022

This week and today we’ve consequently seen a massive deleveraging where all positions are taken out and shot 

There will still be some mechanical deleveraging and momentum models getting the sell trigger still to come 

However, my expectation is this is largely done as risk has been grossed down 

Financial conditions are at peak tightness here and I expect the dollar and rates to “catch down” to oil and commodities and its associated deflationary impulse - the Fed will follow the market shortly after

An easing in financial conditions will relieve the pressure and capital will start to look for opportunities which now are plentiful and we potentially see a V shape rally 

So take a breath, relax, ignore the hyperbole and voices of doom

It’s always darkest before dawn!

•  英伟达（Nvidia）相关争议

•  最终整个市场市值蒸发约6万亿美元

雪上加霜的是，Anthropic完成了史上最大IPO（募资超1000亿美元），最近几天严重抽走了市场流动性。

抛售的主要原因：AI投资太猛，钱不够花？

大科技（亚马逊、谷歌、Meta、微软）三季度合计资本开支增加了369亿美元，达到创纪录的2019亿美元。

过去12个月翻了一倍多，相比2024年一季度涨了356%。过去三年这些公司累计砸了1.6万亿美元做AI基建。

市场担心：这么烧钱，自由现金流和利润会被严重挤压，尤其是看到2027-2028年。这些担忧是真实存在的，

不过，作者认为：

•  做人类历史上最大的技术革命，基础设施必须先砸钱建好。

•  短期自由现金流为负，是长期布局的代价。

•  很多悲观预期已经反映在股价里了，要等到2027年一、二季度看到这些投资真正开始产生回报，担忧才会真正消退。

同时，基本面其实很强：标普500公司三季度盈利同比增长31.9%，是至少4年来最强的增速，而且已经连续13个季度实际盈利超预期。

政治因素：民主党中期选举“横扫”，特朗普“托底”结束了

文章认为，最近科技股大跌的一个重要催化剂，是中期选举结果。

民主党拿下了参众两院控制权，相当于“Trump Put”（特朗普托底）结束了。

过去市场有个预期：万一跌得太狠，特朗普会出手干预（因为他很在意股市表现）。

现在这个后盾没了，加上有人开始喊要禁AI，市场把更严格的监管甚至“AI禁令”都提前定价了。

作者认为监管担忧被夸大了：

美国真的禁AI几乎不可能，那等于把全球AI竞赛的领先地位拱手让给中国。

会有更多监管和可能的新税，但不会到市场现在想象的极端程度。

最终美国不管谁执政，都想赢AI竞赛。

美联储还在加息，成本更高

伊朗战争快到300天，美国通胀已经连续67个月高于2%目标。

美联储主席Warsh态度很明确：必须把通胀打到2%，没有例外。

这意味着本来就贵的AI建设成本更高了，美国国债情况也更糟。

不过油价这个月跌了约22%（政治格局变化+市场下跌共同作用），

文章认为如果伊朗战争有缓和迹象，美联储到2027年中可能不会那么鹰派。

英伟达和AMD的具体风波

英伟达股价几周内跌了40%，市场几乎认定黄仁勋不会回来，把公司未来指引都打了折。

文章一直坚持“在独立调查有结论前，黄仁勋应被推定无罪”，并建议董事会留门。

AMD也被做空机构指控向中国走私芯片（11月19日报告），但证据远未坐实。

结果科技股前瞻市盈率跌到2020年3月以来最低，英伟达前瞻市盈率只有9倍，在标普500里属于最便宜的那一档。

市场根本不相信公司给的盈利数字（即使没有黄仁勋，公司还在指引2028财年约7500亿美元营收）。

情绪已经到危机级别

恐慌指数VIX从10月低点涨了100%以上，11月5日单日涨幅创2018年2月以来最大。

对冲基金本月出现十多年来最大的6周净流出。

加上Anthropic IPO抽流动性，导致股票、黄金、加密货币全面下跌，就是典型的“夺路而逃”。

总结：

AI大方向没问题，现在是情绪和多重短期利空叠加导致的正常回调，市场已经把很多坏消息提前打进去了，反而给优质科技股留下了不错的机会。

但短期波动还会很大，别急着喊“熊市要持续到2027年”。

他们自己的投资策略从2020年以来回报是标普500的近5倍，强调在这种混乱时期要保持客观、按流程操作。

quoted_text:
回到腾冲快乐老家的感觉是真好！

参禅，打坐，饮茶，读书，望着淅沥沥的小雨，听着穿林打叶声，宁静而又轻松安详，虽然股票和加密账户，跌的一塌糊涂，亏损严重，但内心的充盈，却让外物显得不值一提，也毫无波澜和焦虑！

昨天重读比尔·波特的《空谷幽兰》的时候，我忽然想通了一件事。在如今AI掌控一切，物质极大富足，为什么社会的精神空心化却十分严重，我们该如何追寻自己的幸福，以及内心的平静。如何将那些看起来“应该拥有”的东西，一件一件的放下，如同终南山隐士一般。

我们这一代人，太习惯在生活中做加法了。头衔、叙事、关系、仓位、期待，好像手里攥得越满，心里就越踏实。可实际上，很多转折恰恰发生在做减法的时刻。你以为你在积累，其实每多背起一样东西，生命力就被多抽走一分。当注意力全耗在外部世界的噪音里时，内在反而一点点变薄了。

欲望走到尽头，往往不是占有，而是轻。书中介绍的隐士中，曾经也拥有过世俗意义上很体面的结构与秩序，但他们选择清空。不是厌世，也不是逃避，而是看清了：真正让人丰盛的，不是占有多少，而是我们和生活之间的关系足够简洁。我们知道什么东西真的能让自己眼睛发亮，也分得清哪些只是别人塞给我们的“应该”。

边界感也是这个道理。不是冷漠，也不是关起门来不和世界打交道，而是清醒地知道什么该进来，什么该挡在外面。消耗性的社交、无休止的信息流、别人的标准与凝视，都在争夺我们有限的生命能量。把时间和精力留给真正滋养我们的人和事，守住自己的节奏，人才不会在热闹里散掉。生活一旦轻下来，我们才有余力安安静静读完一本书，认真做顿饭，甚至只是停下来感受天气和季节的变化。那种质地，任何喧嚣都换不来。

说到修行者的孤独，很多人怕它，是因为一旦安静下来，平时被忙碌、社交和刺激盖住的钝感与问题都会浮出来。我们得面对那个不那么完美的自己。可也正是在这种独处里，内心的秩序才有机会重新长出来。真正的独处，不一定非得去某个偏远山谷，而是在任何嘈杂的场域里，我们都还能回到自己的中心，把心里的杂音清一清，保住那份敏锐和柔软。

再往后看几年，其实很多被反复拔高的东西都会褪色。头衔、KPI、世俗意义上的圆满，甚至那些拼尽全力的执念，拉长了看，很多都只是阶段性的执着。人到最后，还是要回到生命本身。睡得好，身体稳，心里不拧巴，活得舒展、从容，这比什么都实在。别为了迎合别人的尺子，把自己的身体和心神透支干净。

在照顾好身体的前提下，找到一种真正贴合自己心意的生活方式，好好去体验这一程，就已经足够了。人生本来就不长，不必总跟自己较劲。平静下来，心不乱了，或许那才是到最后最稳妥的幸福。共勉之！🙏感恩！

quoted_text:
The Riemann Hypothesis has fallen.  RH was the singular math result that had been named, in advance, as the obvious coal mine canary for dangerously advanced AI, over the last three decades.  The methods used should generalize to "make AI very good at anything you can definitely test", and unfortunately that category includes "make AI better at making AI".

This is like a private company announcing they have produced a million tons of 15% enriched uranium.  It's not 90% enriched weapons-grade uranium, so you could proclaim the company's output is not immediately deadly right now.  The concern is that the process line may generalize, to an extinction-level threat, within the unpredictably immediate future.  Forecasters still had Riemann at 2035 one week earlier.

This is distinct from earlier events in that earlier you could reasonably ask if AI was selectively picking off famous math problems that turned out to be easier for AI.  The Riemann Hypothesis was the single challenge most often named in advance as a warning sign.

text:
Strip away the biosecurity and cyber-safety PR, and OpenAI’s new “Combatting adversarial distillation” paper is an accidental confession about why closed-API labs are terrified.

They are not worried about a rogue hacker learning a Python script. They are terrified of process-level RL supervision destroying their $ 20-per-million-token pricing moat.

Here is the actual technical reality they buried inside their own post. When a student model only sees a teacher’s final answer or a sanitized “reasoning summary,” it learns what token sequence looks plausible. When a student model gets the teacher’s raw, unedited chain-of-thought trace, it gets dense, step-by-step search trajectories: how the teacher decomposed a hard problem, hit a dead end, backtracked, verified an intermediate hypothesis, and self-corrected before emitting a single final token.

In modern reinforcement learning (GRPO and process-reward pipelines), raw reasoning traces are pure gold because they bypass the most expensive part of frontier post-training: running millions of failed rollouts to discover good search heuristics. Instead of burning $100 million on RL compute exploration, a competitor with a clean dataset of raw CoT trajectories can run supervised fine-tuning on those exact search paths and immediately warm-start RL at a fraction of the compute budget. OpenAI’s own cyber distillation chart admits this flat out: at higher inference budgets, the student trained on exact reasoning traces beats the summary-trained student even after reinforcement learning.

That is why OpenAI built a four-layer panopticon around GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol’s hidden thinking tokens: adversarial refusal training, input classifiers, streaming output classifiers scanning tool-call arguments for stray CoT leaks, and cryptographic conversation binding that invalidates encrypted reasoning blocks the second you edit an earlier message or pass them to a cheaper model. Even funnier, their own benchmark table admits that on GPT-6 Astra’s original safeguards, adaptive black-box attackers extracted protected reasoning from earlier turns 54.0% of the time.

Look at the real endgame tucked into the “national security” section: OpenAI explicitly endorses three Congressional bills so U.S. labs get “more room to slow a release”.

So yeah, @OpenAI  scraped the entire public internet without permission and now wants federal laws criminalizing competitors who learn from its paid API outputs, because once raw reasoning traces leak into the open-weight ecosystem, nobody is paying $500 a month for a closed wrapper anymore.

text:
$ORE started as Proof-of-Work (PoW).

In 2024, ORE launched on Solana with real CPU/GPU computational mining. It generated so much demand that it famously stress-tested the entire Solana network.

And it exposed a fundamental economic problem with PoW: tying issuance to computational power creates a hardware arms race where the winners take most of the rewards. 

ORE didn't skip Proof-of-Work. ORE lived PoW, learned from it, and evolved.  

It engineered a revolutionary model for mining that directly challenges the crypto dogma that a scarce digital monetary asset must have its own L1.  

5×5 GRID Mining replaces energy-intensive computation with capital deployment, creating a sustainable economic mechanism for open and fair distribution of a scarce digital monetary asset for everyone, forever. 

$ORE's evolution was rethinking what mining should accomplish  (open, fair distribution) and where its economic value should go (back to miners and token holders).  

Fix the mining, fix the money, fix the world.

text:
市场走到今天，可能已经到了最难熬的阶段。

大家都不容易，共克时艰吧。

我个人的资产回撤也相当恐怖，

整体看了下可能是近来很多年的最大回撤，
以前主要 CRYPTO 亏损，这次在美股的资产缩水的更严重，说内心是毫无波澜肯定是假的，但是还不至于到焦虑的程度。

区别可能就在于我没有任何杠杆，以及留够了面对不确定性的足够的资金，下跌会影响心情，但是不会影响生活，

这是这么多年经历了几轮牛熊、几次大起大落之后，才逐渐刻进骨子里的原则。

今天早上看了一眼 Oura，昨晚的睡眠评分居然还有 90 分，突然觉得，其实一切并没有想象中那么糟糕，毕竟我还睡的挺好；

这样的时刻，这样的跌幅，无论你在哪个市场，我想都是几乎每隔几年就会经历一次，

如果你是第一次经历，那么我要恭喜你！

恭喜你要开始真正的历练了。

这个时刻可能会让你很难受，但是我希望你坚持住，
因为投资能力最宝贵的成长时刻，往往不在资产不断上涨、账户持续盈利的顺境中，而在亏损不断扩大、焦虑和不安反复袭来，内心那个声音不停哀求你做点什么的时候。

投资场上，我们总以为在和别人竞争，我们把零和游戏挂在嘴边，但其实投资最重要的对手，从来不是别人，而是自己：投资场域没有别人，投资的本真，是你与自己的对话，

和那个充满了贪婪和恐惧、欲望和慌张的自己对话。

所谓钢铁之心，从来不是天生的。
你必须得用足时间亲身体验，用血与泪铸就钢铁之心，才能洗尽铅华、凤凰涅槃。

不经历过这种坐立不安、捶胸顿足、辗转反侧、痛彻心扉、彻夜难眠、撕心裂肺、长夜痛哭、关灯吃面、以泪洗面的九九磨难，谁敢说懂了投资的本真？懂了躺平和等待的意义？

低谷+暴跌+回撤+亏损，你内心的那个声音可能会让你心力交瘁，但是我们的判断，耐心、纪律和面对不确定性的能力，几乎都是在这个时候形成的，每一次周期的洗礼，都能让我们变得更加理性、坚韧和从容。

最近读《道德经》，越来越喜欢这八个字：
知反、用弱、静笃、观复。

知道盛衰会转换，懂得以柔弱自处，在动荡中保持内心的安静，耐心观察事物的往复。

投资如此，人生亦如此。

最后还是想对大家说：
守住底线，留在场上，时间会给我们最好的回报和不断刷新的机会。

保持在场、留有余地！

text:
⚡ BENCHMARKED: A MINI THAT THINKS BIG 

@thinkymachines just shipped Inkling 2 Mini and on my 64GB M5 Pro Mac mini it punches way above its size.

It blew me away!

Inkling 2 Mini only uses 3.4B out of its 26.4B parameters per token and reuses its middle layers, so it can think like a much larger model, while still running at smaller model speeds. The quantized 4-bit version of Inkling 2 Mini is just 17.6 GB and it only took 26 GB of memory even with a 128k context.

With thinking disabled (median of 3 runs), Inkling 2 Mini’s speeds on my Mac mini were:
- 512 tokens: 29.95 tok/s
- 32k: 24.97 tok/s
- 128k: 17.39 tok/s

It is around 1.8x faster than a similarly-sized dense model (Qwen3.8-27B) on shorter prompts on my Mac mini and even at 128k tokens, Inkling 2 Mini outpaces what Qwen3.8-27B was doing at 64k tokens!

It scored 20/20 on my math evals, 10/10 on my code evals, and 8/8 retrieving hidden facts in documents up to 64k tokens long.

A model from a frontier AI lab that I can run on my own desktop computer?!

Hell yes!
author: zeeshan_utd
quoted_text:
🚨 BREAKING: @thinkymachines just dropped Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weight model that loops.

RAM limits how large a model can be when running Local AI, but Looping allows models to trade compute time for improved reasoning capabilities, effectively making any model you already have access to smarter, but not necessarily larger.

It is their 26.4B parameter (3.4B active) Apache 2.0 licensed LLM. It has 24 transformer layers, but in inference the middle 12 layers are looped 3 times, effectively running 48 layers on each token. This looping allows more computation per token, enabling the model to often solve problems with fewer tokens generated. The model was trained natively in 4-bit precision and takes up only ~20 GB, so should run on any Mac with 32GB of RAM.

[Video by Thinking Machines -- Building and flying a flight simulator with Inkling 2 Mini]

Running it on my M5 Pro Mac mini shortly. Benchmark results coming!

author: PANewsCN
quoted_text:
Today we're releasing The State of Bitcoin Payments report, one of the first datasets on how people spend bitcoin in the local economy, based on nearly a year of bitcoin payments at U.S. @Square sellers.

What did we find?

Most bitcoin payments are small and routine:

– The median BTC payment at a Square seller is about $13

– 72% happen at food and drink businesses

– 86% of repeat BTC payments happen within 30 days

– 42% of BTC payments are under $10, and nearly two-thirds are under $20

Under current U.S. federal tax rules and regulations, paying with bitcoin generally means determining a capital gain or loss, even for spending $10 on a quick bite or coffee – a BTC spender would have to figure out which bitcoin they spent, what they paid for it, and what it was worth at the time of checkout.

Not only do consumers feel this burden, but businesses do too. In a Morning Consult survey commissioned by the @Blocks team, nearly a quarter (23.6%) of businesses that don't accept bitcoin cited tax and accounting complexity as a reason.

Congress is currently considering a crypto tax package. A de minimis tax exemption, which would exempt small gains on qualifying digital asset purchases and ease friction for everyday payments, is one approach under discussion. We hope these findings help inform those conversations.

We think tax policy should account for how people spend bitcoin as well as how they hold it.

Read our report to learn more: https://t.co/TQcgVYZStr

author: angel_flowstate
quoted_text:
Elon Musk was asked in an interview what love means to him. His answer had nothing to do with chemistry or passion. He said love is "when you want to share everything you've ever seen with one person and you want their opinion on all of it." And then he went quiet.

The interviewer had expected a typical billionaire answer about finding balance or making time for relationships despite a busy schedule. Instead, Elon gave a definition that sounded like it had been living inside him for years, waiting for someone to finally ask.

He said the loneliest part of his life was never the failed companies or the public criticism. It was coming home after witnessing something extraordinary, a successful rocket launch, a breakthrough at the factory, a view from the roof of SpaceX, and having nobody to tell. Nobody who would understand why it mattered.

He said the relationships that worked best in his life were the ones where the other person genuinely wanted to know everything. Not just "how was your day" but "explain the physics to me, show me why that engine matters, tell me what you saw when the rocket landed."

He described love as the opposite of loneliness. Not the absence of being alone, but the presence of someone who wants to see the world through your eyes. He said when that person exists, the work gets easier, the failures hurt less, and the wins feel like they actually count.

Most people define love as a feeling. Elon defined it as a function: the person you want to share your entire experience of being alive with. And the fact that the richest man on Earth still measures love not by what someone gives him but by whether they want to hear what he saw today is quietly one of the most human things about him.

text:
链上转账最容易出事的地方，往往都很小。

我自己长期会注意这几件事：

1. 不要从交易记录里复制地址

地址投毒最喜欢干这个：给你造一个头尾很像的地址，等你哪天顺手复制错。

2. 大额永远先打小额

多花一次 Gas，总比几十万 U 打错链、打错地址好。

3. 不要只看前 4 位 + 后 4 位

现在已经有专门生成相似地址的工具。金额大时，我会多核对几段，硬件钱包的话直接看设备屏幕。

4. 长期公开同一个收款地址，也是在泄露信息

别人顺着地址就能看到余额、交互项目、资金来源，甚至推测你的其他钱包。

所以最近看到 @Americanfort_io 的 FortressName，我觉得这个产品挺小而美。

它把：

「把地址发我」

变成：

「转给 @Yueya」

名字背后会按不同的收发对象使用独立地址，别人可以正常给你付款，同时减少固定钱包长期暴露的问题。

我喜欢这种产品的原因很简单：

它没有要求用户学习一套新东西，只是把 Crypto 里一个用了十几年的烂体验改好一点。

当然，用名字收款也不代表可以放弃风控。

第一次转账依然小额测试、确认官方入口、核对名字。

工具能降低犯错概率，但最终签字的人还是自己。

Debut Episode: Tales from the Hart Household  ♥️ (Yea I'm gonna make it stick...more wtf moments to come 👀😂)  

Just had a 101 on AI with my 17 year old and what it can really do for you. Her birthday is coming up and she had printed off some invitations at school. Her teacher said she would "help her out".  She came home with some invitation size hot pink paper (she hates pink) and for the most part you could see the what and when but no where.  Already, I'm thinking to myself what is this teacher doing...but then remembered everybody is struggling right lol She wasn't really happy with invitations AT ALL but went to school with the promise that she was going to hand them out.   

Fast forward 2 weeks (today) I asked her baby did you hand you invitations out yet? I have a work event on Saturday so we are going to push your party to Sunday. She said, it's ok mom, I already knew.  I said - knew what? I've never had to push your party. She laughs and I already knew....I said you just weren't feeling the invitations right? Of course I laugh LOL...and then the lightbulb turns on .....I said wait a sec. Let me show you ChatGPT. I work from home, she sees me talk to AI all day, she thinks I'm crazy AF right lol.....until tonight.   

Tonight I was like wait a sec baby...let me show you what this can really do for you right?!  I'm thinking to myself....let me teach her something new....they've watched me in crypto for years. Soooo here goes me.....just click this button....it will talk back to you, you can discuss what you like and you don't like. She said, "Mom I ALREADY KNOW I USE THIS ALL THE TIME"....very matter of fact right.   Here I go, trying to prove my point....ok then tell it to make your birthday invitation then. Of course my daughter is like ok challenge accepted. LOL I already knew it wasnt going to be what she was thinking, but I'm like she going to learn today right HAHAHA (in my Kevin Hart voice). 

First couple of drafts were warm ups...before I knew it she had perfected her bday invitation, sent it for print,  built her wish list on Amazon, and then sent it via text to her attendee list.   At first I'm like oh yea baby get it.....I was so proud right?! Feeling all warm and fuzzy inside. Awwww such a cute bonding moment and I could teach her something new. I was feeling soooooo good...Look what I taught her... I'm bringing my baby in to my world... then I realized the weight of my decision...she's now talking about her photographer, wish list, outfit for her event, accessories, hair, nails........Christmas is gonna be tough🤷‍♀️🤣😂🤣

author: real_y22
quoted_text:
some thoughts about $PRL that are worth considering when thinking about investing in this.

- security budget
PRL aims to be a SoV asset, and security budget / protocol security are crucial for a SoV asset. BTC and other pure PoW networks are secured by game theory.  a potential attacker needs to burn a scarce resource (energy) to get hashrate to gain 51% control of the network. since PoW is costly and does not return any money (in itself) an attack is very expensive and not worth it economically (would be more expensive to get the 51% than what you could make by exploiting the network).

with PRL there is no such cost, the PoW (proof of work) is not "useless". their version of PoW is performing matrix multiplications that are the basis of inference. miners/providers get paid to do this by the ai customer and the PRL mined are just a byproduct / the cherry on top. they call this "duplex mining" and sell it as an upgrade to pure PoW because the work (in proof-of-work) is not wasted and is instead serving inference demand from ai customers.

this has a huge flaw.
a potential prl attacker gets most money spent on the attack back. because he gets paid for his inference work. whereas an attacker for a pure pow chain gets zero money spent on the attack back. the result is that attacking prl is much cheaper than attacking a similar sized pure pow network. pure PoW chains utilize 100% of the hash because the work is useless. whereas Pearl and other PoUW chains only utilize some small % of the hash. if we put this % at 5% (as an example) then it would be 20x cheaper to attack PRL than it would be to attack a pure PoW network of similar size / similar TAM. 

- team ethics are questionable 
they championed the claim of "no VC, no pre-mine" and simultaneously raised two funds, one for equity in the lab and one for mining PRL tokens early on. this was not properly disclosed (talked about this in my channel a couple months back, it has been leaked since). i view this as a negative. 

- potentially some cabal activity going on
multiple VCs and entities were parading around SG saying they want to buy more / double their position but it would just be so hard to source coins. from a game theory standpoint it would make zero sense to telegraph your move and allow others to frontrun yourself if you really had the intention to buy a large quantity of coins. they only possible scenario where this would make sense (from a game theory pov) is when you would be fully allocated already and want to drum up liquidity. 
another entity wrote in an article that "Pearl might actually achieve negative overhead – in other words, building kernels that are faster than the ones inference providers already use." thats straight up Fugazi, there is no world in which i believe a crypto team will produce better kernels than NVIDIA and Google. there is zero shot this becomes a reality, and if it would then it would further weaken network security as outlined in the first point of this post. just remember, these people are not your friends and they have their own agenda and motives for what they say what they say.

on the positive side:
that said, the narrative for PRL is elite. positioning itself as an AI-winner in times where most of crypto is labelled an AI-loser. it also addresses many problems of established SoVs, like quantum resistance. also maybe there is a way duplex mining can scale 20x faster than traditional PoW and therefore secure the network against malicious actors with access to compute. i have my doubts, but worth exploring this possibility.

on the "hard money / SOV" narrative i think it is currently lacking a lot. you cannot come out and label smth "money" that has not even existed 6 months before. (crypto) money properties come from the ability to not be controlled by a single entity and a decentralized network (PRL is controlled by a private company), lindy effect and having stood the test of time (PRL is a couple months old) and provable scarcity. i also think network security is most crucial in any attempt of labelling smth a store-of-value. 

curious to hear your opinions on this subject in the comments.

As a PL designer building a high-level language with a rich type system, a core goal is reducing the need for low-level escape hatches like inline asm.

In glm-vx(GLM-5.3 serving engine with kernels in Vx, checkpoint loading, and streaming HTTP), we replaced most inline PTX with MLIR ops, cutting asm regions from 499 to 81 across 20 kernels.

When LLVM sees the surrounding code, it can simplify logic and cut spills thus generating better code.

But when hoisting/reordering hurts (like %laneid or mma scheduling on H200), we have no option to keep the asm.

text:
So the universe is harmonious and on this monumental day of history - the beauty of the primes has likely been proven. 

Today based on the Alpöge's @__alpoge__ + @AnthropicAI Riemann Hypothesis result claim (congratulations), I'm opening all my work I've been doing in private to a public repo + app so that the community can explore the map of the zeta function, primes and the universe together. 

I have been working on this for 17 months on and offline for the pure love and curiosity of it. Between walks, paper, terminal and dream work, here is what I have for the community.

Zeta App: https://t.co/MHXntQmVJ7
Zeta Repo: https://t.co/bpPS65uYN6

I used a large variety of methods, models, techniques and help from certain people that may not want their names mentioned yet. If this repo has useful results we can go into that later. As Tao said, we want to flesh out the map, so here is some of that map.

I didn't get to prove RH, but here's what myself and the AI fleet found instead over an intense 17 month period of non stop work (I have had to rush to release based on the high pace of the art):
0. Twin ladder model and bridge shear.
1. No-go theorem. No "soft" heat-flow hypothesis can prove RH. Arithmetic input is required. Machine-verified, resting on Rodgers–Tao.
2. Frozen-rung ⟺ Platt–Trudgian. Freezing the ladder rungs is exactly the Platt–Trudgian mechanism, capped at the verified zero height.
3. What really binds Λ ≤ 0.2. An audit, confirmed three ways: the limit is the verified zero height. Tightening the barrier can't beat it.
4. 44 routes to RH. Every one is either non-rigorous or equivalent to RH itself. 
5. Permutation atlas. Every rearrangement family classified. Isometries provably give no gain; one family can.
6. Two open conjectures are now theorems. The Ramanujan-reversal identity and the row sum R_n(1) = n^(n−1), kernel-verified in Lean.
7. 20 kernel-verified Lean 4 projects, including theory mathlib lacks: a general argument principle on rectangles, Abel's binomial theorem, tree-function ODE theory.
8. Exact closed forms for when zeros stop being isolated under heat flow, including c* = √(2+√3) − 1.
9. Candidate bounds on the de Bruijn–Newman constant.
10. The Λ ≤ 0.14 route reduced to one open family. It is a conditional contract, not a bound.
11. Zeta on a torus, sphere, Klein bottle and projective double cover, computed live in your browser, with heat flow you can scrub and fall lines draining into each zero. I have especially had fun with thinking in these realms personally.
12. A corrections ledger. Every caught (prepublish) overclaim is logged. Dead ends being logged for all to see.
13. And more much. 

Corrections, analysis, additions and PRs welcome. I have a lot of work in progress ideas, papers, proofs, etc. Some parts I'm racing to fix as I have some upgrades coming that are backed up 55 PRs at least.

Be patient with me while I figure out the release and prune the bonsai. I spent a lot of time on this and I expect there to be errors to fix and upgrades to do.

Hopefully there is something useful in there for us to learn/hack/explore/teach together in the open and add to the fantastic work through history of the best minds. 

We not only stand on the shoulders of giants, we took a leap into the air and started to flap our wings. 

There will be a lot more to do with the zeta and view this day as an opening to apply it elsewhere and explore more the beauty of nature...

text:
Prefill vs Decode: How SGLang Summit 2026 Explained Cheaper Inference

SGLang held its first summit on November 12 and 13, 2026, at Fort Mason in San Francisco, hosted by LMSYS and @sgl_project. Official page: https://t.co/stwOorQVo4. Selected sessions are supposed to come out later as edited clips. This is not a transcript.

What stuck with me is not another announcement. It is why inference still gets expensive, and which software tricks actually change the bill.

On November 12, @sgl_project announced v1.0: https://t.co/unAAUSUCga. The public pitch is faster inference, better use of memory, and splitting prefill from decode. They said the details of the release would come later, so I am not inventing official benchmark numbers. They also said the stack is used across 330+ organizations, with day-zero support for 217 models. That is their claim, not a count I audited.

LMSYS also announced a SGLang Consortium. The founding members, from the official November 12 blog (https://t.co/0kXUsSgizT), are NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Google, Meta, Cloudflare, Modal, and RadixArk. The same official pages associated Meta, Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Thinking Machines Lab, Cloudflare, Reflection, Modal, HeyGen, LinkedIn, Alibaba, and Tencent TACO with the stack, among others. Those names were on the official pages. That is not an audit of how large each deployment is.

The cost story was consistent across the two days: split prefill and decode, tier the KV cache, use speculative decoding, and run RL rollouts on a different class of GPUs than training. The project is clearly trying to run across hardware, not just one vendor. The agenda included AWS Trainium, NVIDIA NIM, AMD, Intel, and Google TPU sessions.

Prefill and decode are different jobs. Prefill reads the whole prompt at once and wants compute. Decode emits tokens one by one and wants memory bandwidth. Keep both on the same pool of cards, and you scale the expensive parts together. Split them, and you can scale each side on its own, even put them in different rooms or on different grades of hardware. Fireworks AI put it in a session title: "Prefill Here, Decode There: Disaggregating Inference Across Datacenters and Hardware Classes." Crossing rooms is not free. You pay for network latency and for moving the KV cache.

For long context and agent history, the KV cache (the model's reusable memory of what it has already seen) can get enormous. Leaving all of it in expensive GPU HBM is a good way to over-buy the most expensive memory in the rack. A layered cache keeps hot data on the GPU and moves colder data to host memory, or to a cheaper tier. That was the idea behind Alibaba's "From HiCache to Agentic KV Infrastructure" and Netpreme's "Don't Over-Buy HBM, Tier It!"

Netpreme also published its own research, which is not an official SGLang benchmark. In an October 19, 2026 post (https://t.co/AAhKsYnmeK), they reported that a faster, higher-capacity memory tier than host DRAM raised peak decode throughput by 2.09× to 3.04× across the 16K to 1M context lengths they tested, under their stated assumptions. Treat that as one company's result, not a league table.

Speculative decoding is simpler than it sounds. A small model guesses the next few tokens. The large model checks them in one pass. If the guess is right, you skip some full forward passes of the expensive model. Decagon had a production session on choosing between EAGLE and DFlash. SpecForge was on the agenda too, on training draft models the server will actually serve. I have not checked a speedup number I would want to put here.

Updating the weights can stay on top-tier GPUs. The many trial runs that generate trajectories (rollout) can move to cheaper cards, or to a different vendor. That was the idea in the ai& session "Train on One Chip, Roll Out on Any." I have not independently confirmed specific chip pairings from a primary source, so I am not putting model numbers here.

Official unified benchmarks are not out. A lot of the multiples around the event are vendor self-reports. The mechanism is the part worth remembering.

A marketplace like https://t.co/GmFquLEKMT should like the direction. The software makes it easier to use GPUs in different rooms, of different grades, and from different vendors. That is not the same as a finished global compute network. https://t.co/GmFquLEKMT is still a GPU rental marketplace, not an automatic compute federation. Reliability, data handling, and scheduling are still the marketplace's problems.

Sources:

SGLang Summit 2026: https://t.co/VUJXh8JK8c
SGLang Consortium blog, November 12, 2026: https://t.co/0kXUsSgizT
@sgl_project v1.0 announcement, November 12, 2026: https://t.co/unAAUSUCga
Netpreme, XM-Sparse, October 19, 2026: https://t.co/AAhKsYnmeK

Announcing SGLang v1.0 at SGLang Summit 🚀
High-performance inference for LLMs and multimodal models, built for production at scale.

v1.0 brings together:
⋅Faster inference: zero-overhead scheduling, performance-critical paths rewritten in Rust, speculative decoding, and megakernels.
⋅Better use of memory: unified memory for hybrid models, plus hierarchical caching to keep long agent histories reusable beyond GPU memory.
⋅Flexible scaling: prefill/decode disaggregation and flexible parallelism to match your serving setup to your workload.

With adoption across 330+ organizations and day-zero support for 217 models, SGLang has grown through the work of contributors and teams running it in production.

Thank you to everyone building with us. This milestone is yours, too.

text:
模型越来越强，Harness 迟早会被吃掉，这篇论文给了个相反的看法。

以前搭 Harness，更多是在给能力不够的模型兜底。alex zhang 他们的新论文认为，现在模型强了，Harness 的作用变成了把模型已有的能力组合起来，让它能处理更长、更复杂的任务，甚至是训练里没见过的任务。

我觉得最有意思的是这个思路：把长任务拆成很多次小调用，让每一次调用都落在模型熟悉的范围里。这样训练时就不用跑完整条很长的流程，用合成任务加模拟的工具调用和子 Agent，单独训练其中一次调用就行，省数据也省时间。

自己做 Agent 产品下来，感觉也差不多。模型升级以后，Harness 里确实有不少东西可以删掉，但怎么拆任务、怎么调度子 Agent，这些设计会更重要。

目前论文、代码和数据都开源了，做 Agent 的朋友可以去翻翻。

quoted_text:
Harnesses used to be a crutch for weak LLMs. In 2026 and onward, with stronger models, harnesses now offer a mechanism for composing an LLM’s existing and new capabilities to generalize well beyond their training environments.

In our new paper, LM Harnesses are Compositional Generalizers, we explore how various harness abstractions enable LM systems to generalize over task length, task strategies, recursive task depth, and more through composing existing LLM capabilities. These abstractions provide a means for more data-efficient training, especially over long tasks, by keeping trajectories locally in-distribution (LID) — i.e., shaping all individual LLM calls to be in-distribution.

For tasks that take a very long time to roll out, this implies that we can even perform surrogate harness training, meaning we train an individual LLM call instead of doing the very long harness rollout, using purely synthetic tasks, with fake tool calls + sub-agents!

A common idea floating around is that LLMs will absorb harnesses and make them obsolete. We disagree, and argue that we haven’t sufficiently explored what harnesses can provide.

The full paper, logs, codebase, and data are available: https://t.co/AXBjdoqmiz

text:
🚨 BREAKING: @thinkymachines just dropped Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weight model that loops.

RAM limits how large a model can be when running Local AI, but Looping allows models to trade compute time for improved reasoning capabilities, effectively making any model you already have access to smarter, but not necessarily larger.

It is their 26.4B parameter (3.4B active) Apache 2.0 licensed LLM. It has 24 transformer layers, but in inference the middle 12 layers are looped 3 times, effectively running 48 layers on each token. This looping allows more computation per token, enabling the model to often solve problems with fewer tokens generated. The model was trained natively in 4-bit precision and takes up only ~20 GB, so should run on any Mac with 32GB of RAM.

text:
I asked @Starcloud_'s @PhilipJohnston if satellites in orbit have to worry about collisions:

"You definitely have to think about it. The best case study right now is Starlink.

They have around 10,000 satellites in orbit. Every so often those satellites have to do collision avoidance maneuvers, where they slow down or speed up a little.

We're going to have to do much less of that because of the dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbit.

Where the Starlink satellites fly, they cross each other. We're trailing ourselves over the Earth in this horizontal band.

So it's much, much less prone to collisions."

quoted_text:
.@Starcloud_ was quoted $100M to build their first data center in space. They built it themselves for $2.5M.

That satellite put the first Nvidia H100 in space, 100x more GPU compute than anything done before.

And @PhilipJohnston thinks that's where all AI compute is eventually is going.

He walks me through why space will be the cheapest place to run AI, the physics behind operating a data center in space, why Nvidia invested even after one of their GPUs died, and the dynamic of competing with SpaceX while relying on their rockets to get up there.

We also get into what really happens in a tranched funding round, what @ycombinator is really backing, the importance of talent density and holding a high hiring bar, and his $15M probe to Alpha Centauri that won't arrive for 80,000 years.

text:
Anthropic 纳斯达克敲钟那张合影，把硅谷最不愿被看见的真相，赤裸裸地钉在了聚光灯下。

台上十八个人，十七张白人面孔，一张印度裔，没有一张华人。

他们站在那里，像在宣布：这场由华人垫底的革命，终于可以开始庆祝了。

2021年，七个人离开OpenAI，创立了Anthropic。几年后，他们打磨出Claude这把硅谷目前最锋利的刀。可真正把刀磨利的人，大多不在台上。

写代码、调模型、通宵打地基的，是Yanda Chen、Kathy Ko、Fiona Fan这些华裔工程师。他们一寸一寸把地基夯实，钟声却只为别人而响。

华人能造出全世界最好的引擎，却极少被允许坐上驾驶座。

黄仁勋亲手为整个AI时代浇筑了算力地基，把英伟达推到全球市值之巅。可在那张真正决定权力分配的圆桌上，他依然只是个被礼貌请进门的客人。

这和两百年前修铁路的华工，没有任何本质区别。

当年是华工修完铁路，昂撒人在铁轨上合影庆功；如今是华人熬完大业，昂撒人在纳斯达克敲钟上市。只不过这一次，修的是AI铁路。

这张合影一个字都没说，却把一条人人心里都懂的潜规则，彻底摆到了台面上：

华人负责把路修到终点，却永远不被允许站在终点的那张照片里。

一个真实存在的现象：Anthropic 创始团队与敲钟象征性舞台上缺乏华人，而硅谷 AI 技术人才中华人占比很高。

author: 0xSoju
quoted_text:
I watched all 8 episodes of The Altruists, the Netflix series about Sam Bankman-Fried, Caroline Ellison and the collapse of FTX.

Genuinely can’t believe how dirty they did CZ.

Netflix portrays CZ as someone who was jealous of FTX’s growth, stealing their developers, bribing VCs and trying to get Sam and Caroline to shut down their exchange.

(In reality, Binance was one of the earliest investors in FTX)

FTX eventually bought back Binance’s stake in 2021 for $2.1B in FTT, BNB and BUSD.

There’s a scene in episode 4 where CZ suggests that Sam should give Alameda access to FTX customer trading data so they can front-run their own users.

SBF is portrayed as the one who refuses to do something unethical.

There’s no publicly documented evidence that this conversation ever happened tho

Even Forbes questioned why Netflix included this scene.

The series makes it look like CZ had a personal vendetta against Sam and was waiting for the perfect opportunity to destroy FTX.

Keep in mind that CoinDesk published Alameda’s balance sheet on November 2, 2022.

CZ announced that Binance would liquidate its remaining FTT on November 6, citing risk management and what happened with LUNA.

Binance agreed to potentially acquire FTX on November 8 and pulled out a day later after conducting due diligence.

FTX filed for bankruptcy on November 11.

CZ didn’t create the $8.7B hole in FTX. 

His actions accelerated the collapse of a company that was already insolvent.

In July 2026, a Delaware court dismissed the FTX estate’s claims against Binance related to CZ’s tweets during the collapse, although the claims regarding the 2021 share buyback survived.

Yet Netflix decided to portray CZ as someone who never intended to save FTX and was purely interested in humiliating SBF.

I’m not saying CZ is a saint either don’t get me wrong here 

Meanwhile, millions of people had their money stuck on an exchange because its founder was using customer deposits to fund his other business.

The guy responsible for that was sentenced to 25 years in prison.

You don’t need to invent a villain when the story already has one.

投了上百个加密项目后，IOSG @IOSGVC 发现：Web3 投资最危险的坑，可能根本不在币价上。

IOSG Legal 公开 5 个投资实战案例，有些经历比 Rug Pull 还离谱：

▪ 投的公司突然「法律死亡」：一家美国母公司因长期未提交合规文件被行政注销，股权投资人的法律救济陷入困境。
▪ 项目换个壳，早期投资人被架空：投资人出钱养团队、做技术，创始人却另设实体发行 Token，原有股权权益无法直接覆盖。
▪ 熊市救命，牛市翻脸：项目濒临破产时获得救助融资，行情回暖、成功上所后，创始人却开始推诿此前的代币分配承诺。
▪ 大股东突然开除 CEO：投资人选择观望，半年多后基金会宣布清算，最终收回不到 20% 的本金。
▪ 华尔街精英拿融资款去赌博：一个链上赌场项目刚完成数百万美元融资，创始人便将资金转入个人钱包，随后在其他赌博平台输掉数百万美元。

这篇文章最值得记住的一句话：

「投资人真正怕的，从来不是去中心化，而是去责任化。」

从 SAFE、SAFT 到 Token Warrant，Web3 的投资协议越来越专业，但如果控制权、资产和法律责任被拆散，出事时投资人依然可能找不到能追责的人。

牛市看估值，熊市看人品，真正出事时，看的却是合同到底有没有执行力。

值得每个加密投资人和项目创始人读一遍。

text:
David Friedberg: Restricting Open Source AI is a Path to Tyranny

“Open source needs to be allowed and frankly encouraged to proliferate because the absence of that means that you're going to have tyrannical groups, ultimately, they become tyrannical.

They don't intend to be tyrannical, but every group that has the power to control what people see, what they're allowed to do, what they're allowed to access, how they're allowed to use things, what those specific weights are on ‘facts of history,’ on ‘proven science,’ on ‘the truth.’

That is where people become tyrannical because they have an opinion where they think they're right, and if they have the power, they will act on that opinion, and it will ultimately give them tyrannical force over a broader population.

That's what will happen if we limit the proliferation of open source software in AI.

And I've said it before, I'll say it again, ultimately, you can regulate, you can restrict, you can control, you can litigate, you can criminally penalize people for the outputs of what they use software to do.

But to limit software, to label software, to make it a point of restriction and control creates a regulated monopoly for the closed source products that are out there that ultimately, if aligned with certain government agencies, gives those government agencies and those individual corporations power and control over you, the individual, what you're allowed to do, what you're not allowed to do, and every business on Earth no longer operates freely.

None of us should want that. I don't care what your political affiliation is.”

text:
I'm in my autonomous car, which is driving me to Robot Fights in San Francisco.

I've seen enough startups now and enough papers to know that wondrous things are about to come. But we did open Pandora's box to a whole range of new human problems. For instance, misinformation: it is far more powerful in this new world that's about to come than it is in the current world. That's not me saying that; that's Jeremy Bailenson, who runs VR and AR at Stanford University.

And that's just one of the issues that we're going to have to face as humans. It leads to brain-computer interfaces, which you'll start using once you get into the glasses. You all will, because it's a far superior way to compute than looking at your phone, even if your idea of computing is watching YouTube videos all day long.

Lately, I've been meeting people who are like, "I'm using glasses to run my agents." Viture glasses give you a 50-inch screen, or maybe even a little bigger, in front of you. So imagine being in an autonomous car and having the entire visual field in front of you augmented.

In Silicon Valley, we have a millimeter-wave radar sensor company. I did a video with them two years ago at the Consumer Electronics Show. In smoke, fog, or driving snow, that sensor can see the road ahead for about 300 yards in 3D, even if the human eye can barely see the road. It costs $400 plus plus plus; let's say it turns into $1,600 once it gets to the retail level. But if Elon figures out he should have one of these in the Cybercabs in places where there could be snow, fog, smoke, or dust, he can make his Cybercab/robotaxi network far more reliable. That will make him more money and easily cover the $1,600 cost (or $5,000 if you include the software).

We're also about to get characters that can talk to us (you've seen me share quite a few of those). That'll be a big deal in the glasses, right next to your agents. That leads directly to robotics, where you can put that digital twin on top of your robot. Now you've just given your virtual being eyes, ears, touch, and pretty much everything else, because anything it can see, it can figure out. If Elon's team gets this all working, Optimus is going to be a bigger deal than I'm expecting.

But that's an aside. Wondrous things are about to come. Let's figure out how to keep from destroying humanity as well, please.

author: bread_
quoted_text:
Gemini won. 

I gave Astra, Carbon and Fable the same prompt for finding performance gains on the a codebase, with the only restrictions being:
→ Feature parity 
→ No UX degradation 
→ 12hr time limit

Astra basically didn't do anything, and stopped after 2hr. It's "big idea" brought key presses from 1.3ms to 0.5ms (lol).

It was really efficient though (193 loc).

Fable innovated on some responsiveness metrics, missed on the other metrics, and then spit out 3x the amount of code for test scripts. Definitely the "safest" to merge if I were to one shot it. It also reward hacked somewhat by showing a responsiveness metric hitting 250ms while the CPU finished on the backend over 2s so the "gains" were still felt on the system.

Gemini was the only model to take the guidance prompt to heart, which specifically said large structural changes are okay if nothing is lost. It achieved strong gains across the board, but also didn't test as thoroughly as Fable. This was apparent when it caught a few edge cases issues like 15min before submitting. 

It was also just very hard to track throughout its process. The text is much more code-dense than Fable or Astra and can be hard to follow (pictures at the end for comparison).

In the age of agentic coding, I want ambitious models so the win here goes to Gemini. I'll be giving it the job of reviewing all submissions and coming up with a merge plan to preserve as many gains from all 3 as possible. 

So far, really pleased with Google's new model.

text:
Fair points, and I'll concede that as a spam filter the gate works. Graduated coins survive far more often than the rest, and even buying your way through costs real money.

But I think we're answering two different questions. You're defending the gate. My post was about what's under it: who gets the supply, at what price, and what holders can actually collect.

The filter only needs the cap. It doesn't need 79% of supply sold for 85 SOL by arrival order, or holders marked at 326 SOL against a pool that pays out 67.

One nuance on the filter: it screens for capital, not for organic. A third of September's graduations were filled in 3 trades or fewer (Bitquery).

Where I do sadly agree: there may not be a better solution the market would actually use. Alternatives exist and haven't taken share. Traders are conditioned to expect charts that jump, and the thing that makes a chart jump is the same thing that makes the value uncollectable: very little SOL moves the price a long way. Fix that and price gets harder to move on the way up.

But no one would trade that. 

So I'll give you "best we have" right now, but still argue the "optimal" point.

Thanks for the reply.

text:
Rockstar Games 周三解雇了我。第二天 GTA 6 就发售了

我是 Rockstar North 的高级引擎工程师，从事 RAGE 性能优化。三个月前，我在遥测模块里发现了一条本不该存在的数据管道，而且我能证明它流向了哪里

此刻每一份正在运行的 GTA 6 都在收集玩家的行为数据。这部分不算新闻。每款游戏都会收集遥测数据。隐私政策里写的是"用于改进未来产品的匿名游戏数据分析"。我发现的不是这个

遥测模块的数据会汇入 Take-Two 内部的一个系统，名为 Lens。Lens 并不会把匿名使用统计数据发送到 Rockstar 开发人员的数据看板。它为每一位玩家建立一份个人行为画像。不是匿名的。与你的主机账号、你的平台 ID、你的 IP 绑定

我在8月14日向我的技术主管报告了这件事。他说这是"用于玩家体验研究的扩展分析"，让我别管这事。我要求提供数据处理协议。他说这是在 Take-Two 集团层面处理的，不在 Rockstar 的职责范围之内

我调取了 Lens 数据管道的完整文档。我发现的内容如下：

遥测的内容远远超出游戏时长和崩溃报告。Lens 以毫秒级精度记录每一次输入。按键时间点、摇杆动作、反应速度、PS5 自适应扳机上的扳机压力模式。它实时运行行为分析，并生成他们称之为"玩家行为签名"的东西 - 一份对每位玩家都独一无二的画像，就像指纹对每个人都独一无二一样

Lens 会从你的游戏过程中推导出：冲动控制评分、风险承受度指数、攻击性反应模式、耐心阈值、压力下的决策速度、消费冲动评级。这些不是调试指标。这些是心理行为类别

直到我找到了对外传输的管道，我才明白它们是用来做什么的

这些数据不会留在 Rockstar。也不会留在 Take-Two。Lens 通过内部 API 将行为画像传送给 Take-Two 旗下一家名为 Vantage Analytics 的子公司。Vantage 没有公开网站，没有新闻页面，没有招聘信息。它于2023年在特拉华州注册成立

Vantage 是一家行为 AI 公司。它用玩家画像训练预测模型，并把这些模型授权给商业客户。管道文档中包含一份不完整的客户清单。两家保险集团，一家信用风险建模公司，一个人力资源筛选平台，以及一家广告数据经纪商

你的 GTA 6 游戏过程此刻正在生成一份行为评分。没人追你的时候，你开得有多快。你会不会在红灯前停下。NPC 无端攻击你时，你怎么反应。你行动之前要想多久。你花游戏内的钱有多冲动。每一个选择都在喂养一个模型，企业正在付费查询这个模型，用来对真实的人做决定

text:
Arthur Hayes: Why Is Bitcoin Sold First When Markets Turn Risk-Off?

On November 17, 2026, Maelstrom CIO Arthur Hayes @CryptoHayes said on the New Era Finance podcast @new_era_finance that Bitcoin and crypto remain risk assets. Because crypto markets operate around the clock, investors facing losses elsewhere often sell their readily accessible crypto holdings first to meet margin calls or repay bank loans. 

This leaves Bitcoin exposed to selling during global risk-off events, particularly when stress is concentrated in technology stocks. Even if investors expect eventual bailouts to drive prices higher, they may still need cash now to avoid liquidation in less liquid positions.

WuBlockchain notes that Arthur Hayes has a mixed track record of market predictions and frequently revises his views. Readers should focus on his analytical framework rather than treating specific price targets or timelines as investment guidance.

text:
Silence Laboratories and @bureauidentity are working together to build a new foundation for private and collaborative fraud prevention. We were glad to have @ranjanready, Founder & CEO of Bureau, showcase it at DeCompute 2026 during Singapore FinTech Festival (@sgfintechfest) week.

Bureau's AI-powered platform connects identity, device, behavioural and transaction signals for more than 200 banks, fintechs and online businesses.

However, even with all of those signals connected, some fraud only becomes visible across institutions. Fraudsters often spread their activity over several, while the signals that could stop them stay scattered.

That’s where our privacy preserving solution comes in

Our encrypted computing layer enables institutions to securely compute across these fragmented signals and extract collective intelligence, without moving, sharing or exposing the underlying raw data. Only the resulting inferences are revealed.

This unlocks richer fraud signals, stronger cross-institutional detection and a more holistic understanding of risk, while preserving the privacy, control and trust of every participating institution.

Together, Bureau and Silence Laboratories aim to make collective fraud intelligence more accessible, actionable and privacy-preserving.

More on our collaboration: https://t.co/DHvYXwlb8a

text:
Arthur Hayes：为什么市场避险时，比特币先被卖掉？

2026 年 11 月 17 日，Maelstrom 首席投资官 Arthur Hayes @CryptoHayes 在 New Era Finance @new_era_finance 播客中表示，比特币和加密货币仍属于风险资产。由于加密市场全天候开放，当投资者的其他持仓出现亏损，需要补缴保证金或偿还银行欠款时，往往会先卖出随时能变现的加密资产。

因此，全球市场出现避险行情，尤其是科技板块承压时，比特币也会遭到抛售。即使预期未来救市会推动价格上涨，投资者眼下仍可能需要筹集现金，避免其他流动性更差的仓位被清算。

吴说提醒，Arthur Hayes 的市场预测历史准确率较低且观点常有调整，建议重点参考其分析框架，而非具体价格与时间预测。

text:
Sufficiently advanced interpolation is magic

> This is not theory-building in the usual sense. It is something much weirder and more alien. The best human mathematicians know how to build theory, painstakingly, to reach a goal. But no human brain, on its own, is capable of creating a wormhole that requires a 25,000 page long tour through existing infrastructure with no obvious or realistic connection to the goal.
author: krishnanrohit
quoted_text:
Like most mathematicians, I believed the Riemann Hypothesis to be completely out of reach at present (even with the best AI tools), because I expected it to require substantial theory-building, probably in arithmetic geometry. The kind of new theory-building that fills entire books, and that AI isn't so good at yet.

Mathematicians have a notion of how deep a problem is. A sufficiently deep problem is generally intractable until enough of the theory is in place. If difficult problems are like valuable mineral reserves buried miles underground, you first need to build the infrastructure to reach them.

What Levent's proof seems to have done instead is something completely different. It takes an incredibly complicated tour through the infrastructure built for a hundred other mineral reserves, situated far from the destination, and somehow create a wormhole to the original destination.

This is not theory-building in the usual sense. It is something much weirder and more alien. The best human mathematicians know how to build theory, painstakingly, to reach a goal. But no human brain, on its own, is capable of creating a wormhole that requires a 25,000 page long tour through existing infrastructure with no obvious or realistic connection to the goal. But huge credit to Levent here: I think no current AI, on its own, is capable of this either.

I had never worked on or thought too much about the Riemann Hypothesis: it seemed very far removed from my own area of number theory.

But the astonishing thing about Levent's claimed proof of RH (which I think has a very good chance of being correct) is that it uses a huge number of precisely the things that are central to my own corner of number theory:

- Theta functions and other automorphic forms on unitary groups
- Gan–Gross–Prasad period formulas
- Relative trace formulas

Etc., etc.

A problem that I had always assumed would require new theories in arithmetic geometry may instead turn out to be tractable through an inhuman chain of existing (deep) results in higher-rank automorphic forms (and a lot else).

text:
看到 bitcoin:native 这种跌法，突然有一种感觉：

过去几年，我们可能太习惯用资产价格来衡量经济好坏了。

标普不断创新高，AI 巨头市值一路膨胀，Crypto 也创造了无数财富故事。

但对于很多普通人来说，生活成本、就业压力、收入增长，似乎一直没跟上这场繁荣。

现在资产价格开始集体回撤，才让人重新思考一个问题：

过去的繁荣，到底有多少来自真实的经济增长，又有多少来自流动性、估值扩张和市场预期？

当然，资产下跌不等于经济危机。但我会特别关注，金融市场的压力会不会进一步传导到企业融资、就业和消费。

如果只是资金出清，市场可能很快修复；如果企业投资和居民收入也开始恶化，那才是更值得担心的事情。

或许是资产上涨时，普通人没有分享到多少繁荣；资产下跌时，却可能承担经济收缩的代价。

text:
这篇文章强烈推荐！

作者梳理了五个下跌原因：

•   大厂资本开支太高（单季 2,019 亿美元），压缩自由现金流。
•   中期选举后“特朗普看跌期权”失效，市场还在定价 AI 监管甚至禁令。
•   沃什领导的美联储在通胀连续 67 个月超标的背景下激进加息。
•   英伟达黄仁勋出走、AMD 被指控走私芯片。
•   ANT 的 IPO 抽走流动性，对冲基金集中撤离。

并给出无需过度悲观的依据：

•  标普三季度 EPS 同比 +31.9%，盈利已连续 13 个季度超预期。
•  英伟达远期市盈率只有 9 倍，科技板块估值是 2020 年 3 月以来最低。
•  油价本月跌约 22%，2027 年年中美联储有望放松。
•  他们判断美国不会真的禁止 AI。

最后的结论是：

现在风险回报比开始有吸引力，优先关注资产负债表强、盈利增长在加速的高质量科技股。他们预计，流动性回来后，抄底资金会像 2025 年 4 月那样很快回流。

-----------------------------

【全文翻译】
45天蒸发6万亿美元：这是“泡沫”，还是机会？

最近被问得最多的问题是：AI 是不是泡沫？泡沫是不是已经破了？美股已经连续 31 个交易日下跌，平均每天蒸发 2,250 亿美元市值。下面我们完整梳理一下：行情是怎么走到这一步的，现在发生了什么，接下来怎么看。

从 2022 年 11 月起，我们一直强烈看多 AI，称它为史上最大的技术革命。我们“持有资产，否则就被甩在后面”的观点，建立在两点之上：创新带来的回报，以及不断累积的通胀。

过去 6 周，AI 交易经历了诞生以来最大的考验之一，和 2025 年 4 月贸易战那次差不多。建议收藏这篇文章，未来几周可以回来对照。

现实是，AI 正在颠覆全球市场、经济乃至文明的现状。颠覆会让情绪走向两极，而资产价格的波动又会进一步加剧这种两极分化。我们现在看到的正是这样。

一、过去 45 天非常混乱
10 月 6 日是标普 500 最后一次创历史新高。从那以后的 45 天里，市场经历了数不清的伊朗战争头条、2026 年三季度财报季、对 AI 资本开支和自由现金流的担忧、10 月美联储议息会议、美国中期选举、英伟达风波，最终市值蒸发了 6 万亿美元。

此外，Anthropic 的 IPO 刚刚募资超过 1,000 亿美元，是史上最大的 IPO，过去几个交易日明显抽走了市场流动性。

在这种时候，投资者要退一步问自己一个关键问题：到底什么变了？哪些已经被定价了？

二、很多担忧已经被定价：资本开支与自由现金流
这轮抛售最早源于对美国大型科技公司 AI 资本开支的担忧，以及这对 2027、2028 年自由现金流和盈利能力的影响。这些担忧是真实存在的。

亚马逊、Alphabet、Meta 和微软四家的合计资本开支在 2026 年三季度增加 369 亿美元，达到创纪录的 2,019 亿美元。这个数字在过去 12 个月翻了一倍多，比 2024 年一季度高出 356%。过去 3 年，大型科技公司在资本开支上一共花了 1.6 万亿美元。

但也要承认，创纪录的基建支出是史上最大技术革命的必要条件。短期的负自由现金流，是长期建设的短期代价。很多恐惧已经反映在价格里了，但在这些资本开支的回报率变得更清楚之前，担忧还会持续，大概要到 2027 年一、二季度。

从来没有哪个市场像现在这样，恐惧这么多，增长也这么强。截至目前，标普 500 公司 2026 年三季度 EPS 同比增长 31.9%，是至少 4 年来最强的增速。实际盈利已经连续 13 个季度超出预期，AI 建设的力度比大多数人意识到的更强。

三、民主党“横扫”中期选举，“特朗普看跌期权”终结
我们认为，科技股近期回撤的很大一部分原因来自中期选举结果，它实际上终结了我们所说的“特朗普看跌期权”（Trump Put）。

无论是特朗普 2016–2020 年的第一个任期，还是第二个任期到现在，只要特朗普有能力左右市场，市场在波动中就会感到安心。“特朗普看跌期权”是一种对冲：大家相信行情一旦难看，特朗普就会出手干预，因为市场稳定一直是他的首要任务之一。

民主党“横扫”中期选举后，我们认为这份“看跌期权”已经实际失效。11 月 4 日的一条帖子进一步加速了这个托底的瓦解（原文配图）。参众两院易主，部分削弱了特朗普干预市场的能力。“禁止 AI”的呼声越来越大，市场已经在定价：2027 年 1 月民主党掌权后，会有激进的监管，甚至可能禁止 AI。

“特朗普看跌期权”的终结不会逆转，会让美股出现更剧烈的回撤。但我们认为对监管的担忧过头了。美国不会禁止 AI。这样的禁令就算能执行，也等于把全球 AI 竞赛的位置拱手让给中国。监管会更多，可能还会有新税，但市场假设的情况比我们认为会实际发生的要极端得多。说到底，不管谁执政，美国都应该想赢。

四、美联储在市场焦虑时加息
除了 AI 投资的担忧和政治格局的变化，美联储还在激进加息。伊朗战争快到第 300 天，美国通胀已经连续 67 个月高于美联储 2% 的目标。美联储主席沃什已经明确表示，首要任务是把通胀降到 2%，没有例外。

这意味着本来就很昂贵的 AI 建设会变得更贵，美国联邦债务的处境就更糟了。

11 月美国投资级公司债发行预计同比增加 370 亿美元（+27%），达到 1,750 亿美元，是有记录以来最高的 11 月。我们认为，在这种背景下加息进一步加剧了近期的动荡。这种情况会改变吗？

政治权力的转移和近期市场下跌，让油价本月下跌约 22%。再加上市场不稳，美联储对 2027 年的展望很可能会变，尤其是如果伊朗战争明显接近结束。

我们在 11 月 2 日发布过中期选举前的油价分析，预计油价会跌破 93 美元。之后油价跌到了 2026 年 8 月以来的最低点。周日我们会发布最新一期 The Kobeissi Letter，欢迎订阅。

即使油价下跌，“更高更久”的利率暂时还会持续，但我们认为到 2027 年年中，美联储政策变得没那么紧的可能性在上升。

五、英伟达、AMD 与中国芯片问题
过去两周，英伟达失去了 AI 革命的领袖黄仁勋，股价几周内跌了 40%；AMD 被指控走私芯片到中国。市场已经对这些事件的影响做了大幅悲观定价。

大家可能都看到了，我们对英伟达这件事表态很多，一开始就坚持黄仁勋在被证明有罪之前是无辜的。我们呼吁董事会在明确的独立调查查清事实之前，给黄仁勋留一扇门。这是因为黄仁勋对 AI 革命和美国的成功贡献巨大。现在英伟达的股价反映的是“黄仁勋几乎肯定不会回来”，而且基本把公司的前瞻指引全部当作不算数。

AMD 也一样。11 月 19 日一份做空报告指控它走私芯片到中国，但这个说法远远没有得到证实。

这些事件导致科技板块的远期市盈率跌到 2020 年 3 月以来最低。英伟达的远期市盈率降到 9 倍，是标普 500 里最便宜的股票之一；相对于它的盈利增速，更是便宜得多。

这说明什么？市场不相信远期市盈率里的“E”（盈利）。尽管英伟达给出的 2028 财年营收指引约 7,500 亿美元，而且这是在没有黄仁勋的情况下给出的，市场仍然不信。现在的市场里埋着大量超预期的空间。

六、情绪处于危机水平
10 月 15 日我们发表了《隐形熊市》一文，指出标普 500 表面之下已经出现熊市，尤其是在科技股里。那是情绪转变的开始，而不是从中期选举或英伟达事件才开始的。那些事件只是加速了情绪转变。

VIX 已经比 10 月低点上涨超过 100%，11 月 5 日录得 2018 年 2 月以来最大单日涨幅。在恐慌突然飙升的同时，Anthropic（ANT）的 IPO 又大幅抽走了市场流动性。周二簿记结束后，这次 IPO 的机构需求达到 4,000 亿美元，散户订单 1,000 亿美元，是当时预期募资额（每股 78 美元、644 亿美元）的近 8 倍。

情绪突变加上流动性大幅收缩，造成了本周的走势：股票、黄金、加密等几乎所有资产都在跌。对冲基金本月录得十多年来最大的 6 周滚动净流出，大家就是在夺门而逃。我们认为，流动性回来后，市场会企稳。

七、结论：接下来怎么走？
回到最初的问题：AI 是不是泡沫？泡沫破了吗？我们的答案是：不是。

毫无疑问，AI 革命正面临迄今最重大的考验之一。但我们认为，市场定价的结果比基本面显示的要悲观得多。我们认为市场处在一次正常的回调中。即使标普 500 从当前水平再跌 10%，也仍然在健康回调的范围内。

押注一个延续到 2027 年的长期熊市，等于押注上面这些因素不仅会兑现，还会继续恶化。当前估值里已经包含了大量负面情绪。对于正在迅速流行的“标普 500 跌 30% 以上”的说法，我们会保持谨慎。

现实是，情绪已经极度两极化，而我们相信这种两极化会像以往一样创造机会。

在当前水平，市场同时定价了几件事：利率持续高企、激进的 AI 监管、AI 基建投资回报令人失望，以及科技行业最重要的一些公司的长期不确定性。走向 2027 年，正面超预期的空间很大。

我们不是说市场一定已经见底。波动还会很高，流动性仍然受限，在不确定性持续的情况下，继续下跌完全可能。但风险回报比正变得越来越有吸引力，尤其是那些资产负债表强、盈利增长在加速、有持久竞争优势的高质量科技公司。

我们认为大量看空情绪已经被定价，而市场忽视了正面惊喜的可能。尘埃落定后，我们预计抄底资金会很快回到高质量科技股，就像 2025 年 4 月那样。长期来看，资产持有者会继续赢。

text:
the hottest job in tech right now is basically being good at hanging out

startups and vcs are hiring people with titles like ecosystem lead whose whole job is showing up in person. dinners, run clubs, coffee, the panel nobody wanted to go to. it sounds like a joke until you realize why

every company now has the same ai writing the same launch post, making the same video and sending the same cold email to the same inbox. marketing got infinitely cheap, which also made it kind of invisible. when everyone can automate the pitch, the pitch stops working

so the thing that cant be automated becomes the whole strategy. being in the room. remembering someones name. replying to a comment like a person and not like a growth tool

same thing is happening online. the accounts actually growing right now are weirdly manual. they answer people by hand, they show up in other peoples replies, they post things that clearly came from their actual week. its slower and it doesnt scale and thats exactly why it works

when i was building my old account to 5.3M, the internet mostly rewarded whoever could post the most. i think that era is ending. volume is free now. real attention to one specific person isnt

the funny part is sf spent a decade trying to automate every human interaction, and the most valuable skill in the city is turning out to be the one you learn at a dinner party

do the thing a bot could do. just do it yourself

author: AISafetyMemes
quoted_text:
The Riemann Hypothesis has fallen.  RH was the singular math result that had been named, in advance, as the obvious coal mine canary for dangerously advanced AI, over the last three decades.  The methods used should generalize to "make AI very good at anything you can definitely test", and unfortunately that category includes "make AI better at making AI".

This is like a private company announcing they have produced a million tons of 15% enriched uranium.  It's not 90% enriched weapons-grade uranium, so you could proclaim the company's output is not immediately deadly right now.  The concern is that the process line may generalize, to an extinction-level threat, within the unpredictably immediate future.  Forecasters still had Riemann at 2035 one week earlier.

This is distinct from earlier events in that earlier you could reasonably ask if AI was selectively picking off famous math problems that turned out to be easier for AI.  The Riemann Hypothesis was the single challenge most often named in advance as a warning sign.

quoted_text:
我的数学家朋友已经有一点精神不正常了。。。

大部分人看到AI可能证明了黎曼猜想，第一反应都是去检查证明有没有漏洞，代码是否正确，形式化验证能不能成立。

但这位朋友甚至根本不打算讨论证明的对错。

他直接从数学哲学的角度否定了这件事。

他说，根本不存在独立于人类理解的数学实体。
数学定理本质上是人类头脑中的概念，也是社会关系的凝结。
所以，如果一份证明长达几万页，根本没有人类能够完整理解，那么它就没有社会意义，自然也没有数学意义。

在这种情况下，所谓证明成立，实际上就等价于相信AI这个神谕机，以及提交证明的「祭司」没有欺骗你。

别人还在争论AI到底有没有证明黎曼猜想，他已经开始质疑：就算证明是真的，那又怎么样？

随着AI的数学能力继续发展，我们可能真的会遇到一种情况：AI能够证明的东西，已经超出了人类能够理解的范围。

到那个时候，数学究竟是谁的数学？

反正不是我的数学。

author: yangyue992125
quoted_text:
今晚抽了不少烟，对着屏幕敲下这些字的时候，感觉挺魔幻的。今年我30岁，96年生人。在这个圈子里摸爬滚打了整整十年，也算是老韭菜里的老韭菜了。

说真的，这十年就像一场大梦。从大学进入市场，还在玩比特币中国网，到后来转型去中币，结果中币直接倒闭，里面还锁着我70个ETH，这辈子估计都提不出来了。你懂那种感觉吗？就是市场拿走了你的钱，连声招呼都不打。

但那时候年轻，不信邪。2023年，我算是抓住了趋势，8000U滚仓做多大饼，那数字看着看着就飙升到了40万U。后来以太在4800的高点，我成功预判了顶，反手做空。那阵子真的是巅峰，账户里躺着145万U。我出金了190万人民币，买了车房，欧洲，非洲，东南亚，斐济，满世界旅游。哪怕剩下的100多万U回撤了60%以上，我当时的眼睛也是长在头顶上的。

bn.oke送的礼物，堆满了整整一个房间。在新加坡时我见过CZ，在香港的论坛上见过孙割和何一。那时候真觉得自己是个天才，以为自己早就把市场玩明白了。所谓的阶级跃迁，不就是账户数字多加几个零吗？

今年，我的高光时刻又来了。中期选举丢两院，AI科技存储半导体估值泡沫破裂，克劳德ipo，黄仁勋出轨，币安被盗……我顺势做空，又赚了130万U。得了千钱想万钱，当了皇帝想成仙。赚了这些，我不甘心啊，我想博一个彻底财富自由的机会。自己为市场到底了，在底部分别3倍、5倍建仓了多个板块和加密市场。结果呢？市场用最狠的方式把我按在地上摩擦，账户直接回撤90%，只剩12万U。

被市场教育得体无完肤之后，我反而清醒了。

我强制出金了90%，差不多70万人民币，丢进了年化只有2-4%的债基里，赎回期最少60天。我名下的房子，我妈有1%的产权，我不能变卖抵押；每年信用卡我固定逾期3次，硬生生把自己的借贷额度搞没。彻底断了我的退路，我太怕自己再上头去加杠杆了。

交易所里现在还剩1万7千U，这就是我留给这十年交易的最后子弹。最后一舞，不知道成败，但求一个体面的告别。

回看这十年，真的是应了那句：人老得太快，往往聪明得太晚。

以前我总喜欢带人赚钱，看到别人负债，我拉一把。结果呢？很多人靠着我的帮助赚到了钱，后来就因为我不带他们了，在背后疯狂中伤我。都是养不熟的白眼狼。你渡他人苦，自己得脱层皮。后来我算是明白了，永远不要去同情谁，也别去帮谁。大多数人懂感恩吗？不，他们只会觉得你有钱，你就该带着他们过一样的日子。

这就好比我以前理解不了的《红楼梦》。年轻时以为那是本爱情小说，后来真见过了所谓的豪门和世态炎凉，才发现那写的根本就是豪门兴衰实录。里面的人物就像现实里的各种人，王熙凤那么聪明，那么有手段，为什么救不了贾府？因为一个人能力再强，也救不了一个正在腐烂的系统。贾府真正的问题，不是没钱，而是人心散了。全是一帮想着算计的人，谁会真正关心这个家族还能走多远？

现在的社交也是一样，全是算计。就像鲁迅见了成年后的闰土，阶层不同了，身份不同了，你看着就心里难受。其实最好的朋友，就是那种酒肉朋友。你和他都没啥期待，待在一起就是舒服。喝罐可乐，扯扯当年在西安喝酒打架的破事，心一下就放下了。一旦人和人之间掺杂了太多利益，心就再也放不下来了。

那些所谓“爱情是对价值的反应”的毒鸡汤，我看多了。全世界大部分成功的企业家，另一半都是相貌平平。爱本质上是无条件的，精神上的共鸣才是硬道理。如果你过分执着于别人的反馈，最后肯定是一场空。

人这一生最大的误区，就是把“拥有”当成财富。真正的财富，其实是使用权，是流动能力。你能拥有一切，但不被这些东西绊住，这才是自由。总在找赚钱机会的人，一辈子都会卡在找机会的阶段。

其实这个世界，就是一场精心包装过的剧本，90%的人都照着剧本走完了一生。包括我以前去爱沙尼亚，看着那些每天能睡到自然醒的人，真的羡慕。现在想想，绝大多数人，包括我自己，要么熬夜，要么失眠，要么被闹钟强行叫醒，睡眠都成了一种奢侈品。

财富驾驭不住，就会铜臭外露；权力驾驭不住，就会盛气凌人。只有输过，只有痛过，人才会平静地思考。赢只会让人骄傲，从而放弃思考。

命运这玩意儿是有伏笔的。你相信什么，就会吸引什么。无数件事发生在你生命里，其实都是在铺垫你该走的路。

从伊斯坦布尔到成都，从暴富到回归生活。现在看着账户里那最后的1.7万U，我没那么多不甘心了。能被人看出来的聪明，其实是一种愚蠢。真正聪明的人，你看到的是真诚和自信。

市场不会安慰你，但它会告诉你答案。这十年，我交了太贵的学费，但也算买到了属于自己的清醒。

这最后一舞，跳完，我就彻底退场了。不用祝我暴富，祝我今晚能睡个好觉吧。

pearl-2:native's "useful work" has a fatal flaw: 

The system only checks whether the math was done, not whether it was actually needed by a real AI customer, so miners can earn the same rewards by submitting random numbers, and research has found that the dominant mining software doesn't even contain inference code. 

Data shows that fewer than 1% of Pearl's blocks match real AI models, with over 80% of computing power coming from consumer graphics cards just mining for rewards. Bitcoin's "useless" work is superior because its only goal is hard to produce, extremely easy to verify. 

This simple security model has held up for over a decade, while Pearl's "usefulness" remains mostly marketing.
author: DefiRatesNet
quoted_text:
Can anyone answer: Where is the demand side for Pearl? 

It seems the entire story of Pearl is that it has solved it's supply side. 

Pearl has merged PoW and AI inference, so that these are harmonized, rather than competitive with each-other. Great 👍. That's cool and novel.

They solved the supply side. 

As far as I understand it, Pearl has no answer for the demand side. Demand for Pearl is entirely speculative and reflexive. 

There is simply no reason to hold Pearl as a SoV, or spend Pearl as a commodity. Holding Pearl is simply subsidizing the AI buildout by allowing Pearl miners to sell at a higher price. 

While it's true that this is not fundamentally different than BTC or Gold ('there is no utility or commodity value to BTC"), saying this as a pro-Pearl argument feels incredibly vapid and borderline disingenuous. Just because we have Bitcoin as precedent to point to, doesn't mean that this precedent gets to be applied anywhere else.

Even at least ZEC is different in this regard, in that the utility value of holding ZEC is privacy. 

Unless I'm missing something, I have no interest in Pearl unless someone can tell me where sustained demand-side pressure comes from.

text:
中国科技公司过去最熟悉的一条上市路线，现在可能要重新走了。

路透独家报道，中国证监会近期向部分律师事务所传达了一个新的监管口径：2023 年境外上市新规实施之后搭建红筹架构的企业，必须先把注册地迁回中国境内，才能推进境外上市。

阶跃星辰就是一个例子。今年 4 月，它就被曝正在拆除离岸架构，为赴港 IPO 做准备。

这件事其实挺值得关注的。

过去很多中国科技创业公司，都是在开曼等地搭建控股架构，国内研发经营，海外融资，最后去香港或者美国上市。

但现在，这条走了很多年的路，可能没法再照搬了。

路透还披露了一个数字：去年证监会批准了 50 家红筹企业赴港上市，今年截至目前只有 6 家。

我觉得真正值得思考的，不只是几家公司上市可能推迟，而是中国科技创业公司的整个融资逻辑都可能发生变化。

毕竟红筹架构不是上市前一天才搭建的。从早期融资、美元基金进入，到员工期权、股权安排，很多东西从创业初期就已经确定。等到 IPO 前再拆掉重来，时间和成本都不是小事。

当然，这不是禁止中国公司去香港上市。目前也只是路透援引知情人士披露的监管指导，并非公开发布的新法规。

但有一个趋势越来越清楚：中国科技公司未来怎么融资、在哪里注册、最终去哪里上市，这三个问题恐怕不能再分开考虑了。

以前创业公司可以先把业务做起来，上市的问题以后再想。现在，资本路径可能从创业第一天起，就必须成为战略的一部分。

text:
四年周期规律被打破？比特币跌破 5.6 万美元，市场正在经历一场漫长的熊市。

11 月 21 日，加密市场再次遭遇全面抛售。

BTC 单日暴跌近 9%，接连失守 6 万、5.7 万、5.6 万美元关口；ZEC 24 小时跌超 21%，LIT 跌 16.8%，HYPE 跌 13.7%，NEAR 跌 13.6%，PUMP、UNI 等前期热门币种同样遭遇两位数跌幅。

随着价格持续下探，全网近 1 小时爆仓金额扩大至 6.36 亿美元，杠杆多头遭遇集中清算。

但比短期暴跌更值得关注的，是比特币正在经历的周期变化。

从 2025 年 10 月 7 日周期高点算起，至今已经过去 410 天。按照传统四年周期理论，比特币通常在减半后的约一年至一年半内见顶，随后进入熊市调整，再逐步迎来下一轮复苏。

然而，这一次市场并未按照部分交易者预期的节奏企稳。BTC 从去年高点持续回撤，现已跌去超过一半市值，连此前表现强势的山寨币也开始集体补跌。

过去，加密市场习惯用四年周期解释一切：减半、牛市、见顶、熊市、再减半。

如今，ETF、机构资金、美股流动性与宏观政策正在改变比特币的交易结构，传统周期理论的解释力也面临新的考验。

四年周期究竟已经失效，还是我们仍处在一轮尚未结束的熊市之中？
